class.name: Superior Monk
classFeatures: Tongue of the Sun and Moon|Monk||13

classFeature.name: Upgraded Martial Arts
entries: Here is an updated table for the Monk's Unarmed Strikes damage progression. Monks can use this damage in place of the normal damage for an unarmed strike or monk weapon.

classFeature.name: Advanced Ki Features
entries: Starting at 2nd level, your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points. Your monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Ki Points column of the Monk table.

You can spend these points to fuel various ki features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more ki features as you gain levels in this class.

When you spend a ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points.
Some of your ki features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

entries.classFeature: Advanced Step of the Wind|Superior Monk|DMSecretWeapon|2|DMSecretWeapon

classFeature.name: Advanced Patient Defense
entries: You can spend 1 ki point to take the {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action on your turn. If you do, you also regain hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier.

classFeature.name: Advanced Step of the Wind
entries: You can take the {@action Disengage} or {@action Dash} action as a bonus action on your turn. When you use this feature, you can choose to spend 1 ki point. If you do, your movement speed increases by 10 feet and your jump distance is tripled until the end of this turn.

classFeature.name: Advanced Deflect Missile
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your reaction to deflect or catch the missile when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by {@dice 1d10} + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can catch the missile if it is small enough for you to hold in one hand and you have at least one hand free. If you catch a missile in this way, you can spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack (range 20/60 feet) with the weapon or piece of ammunition you just caught, as part of the same reaction. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and the missile counts as a monk weapon for the attack.

Starting at 7th level, you can empower yourself with Ki to deflect or catch magical projectiles. When you are hit by a ranged spell attack, or the {@spell magic missile} spell, you can expend one ki point to use your reaction to reduce the damage you take from the attack by {@damage 1d10} + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level.
If you reduce the damage to 0, you capture that magic and dissipate it through your form. You regain 1 ki point.

classFeature.name: Font of Ki
entries: {@i This optional ability replaces the Stillness of Mind feature at 7th level, if the player chooses to take it.}
As an action, you regain spent ki points equal to your Wisdom modifier. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a rest short.

classFeature.name: Perfect Form
entries: {@i This optional ability replaces the Purity of Body feature at 10th level, if the player chooses to take it.}
You gain proficiency in {@skill Acrobatics} and {@skill Athletics}, or two other skills if you have proficiency in them already.
In addition, you can use your Wisdom modifier when calculating your {@skill Athletics} checks.
Finally, you gain expertise in {@skill Acrobatics} and {@skill Athletics}. Double your proficiency bonus for any ability checks you make with those skills.

classFeature.name: Upgraded Barbarian Rage
entries: Here is an updated table for the Barbarian's Rage damage progression. The Rage Damage scales at the same rate as a character's proficiency bonus, capping at +6, rather than the meagre +4 we have now.

classFeature.name: Improved Reckless Attack
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defence to attack with fierce desperation. When you make an attack roll with a weapon or unarmed strike, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

{@i Design Note: Reckless Attack now works on all Barbarian attacks (not only those made on the player's turn) and can be used on attacks made with ability scores other than Strength, opening new opportunities for Dexterity focused builds. Note that the Barbarian Rage damage bonus still only applies to Strength-based attacks.}

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one Fighting Style from the Fighter's Fighting Style options. You can't take the same Fighting Style more than once, even if you later get to choose one again.

classFeature.name: Crushing Might
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use your bonus action to attempt to shove that creature 5 feet away from you or grapple that creature.

classFluff.name: Superior Monk
entries: It seems widely accepted by the community that Monks are currently the weakest class in D&D 5e. Whether that is true or not, we can identify certain "problems" with the Monk, and do a little House Rules magic to correct them.
The aim of this section is to change as little as possible about the Monk, while bringing the flavour, power level and fun factor of the class to a level on par with the other classes.

Advanced Abilities will change a couple of the Monk's features slightly to give them a little "push". For example, altering Patient Defense to be comparable with the Rogue's 2nd level feature Cunning Action. It also introduces a couple of new class features at various levels.

Consider allowing your players to use this Monk in your games, or talking with your GM about including some or all of these changes to make the Monk just as strong as other classes, without needing to "power game" via restrictive race options and features. Enjoy!

classFluff.name: Superior Barbarian
entries: Alongside the Monk and Ranger, Barbarians are the class that are most often viewed as having "problems". Barbarians get some awesome early game features that scale poorly (like Rage), some great features that don't work as people think they should (like Reckless Attack), and a whole load of middling features after level 5.

These optional changes aim to improve on the base Barbarian and its most iconic subclass, the Berserker, without "breaking" them. These rules also aim to be simple and effortless to incorporate into existing builds and games.
Consider these changes as my answer to a self-imposed challenge: Improve the Barbarian while changing as little as possible. Enjoy!

subclassFeature.name: School of Hard Knocks
entries: Wizardry requires years of training and careful study to cultivate. Even then, most wizards only truly master a single discipline of magic. However, away from the universities and textbooks, there exist other, less refined ways to develop a connection with the arcane. Through diligent observation of the other more fortunate students, and the magic of the everyday world, self-taught Wizards have been known to emerge. These selfstarters are referred to scathingly by some and proudly by others as Wizards of the School of Hard Knocks.

subclassFeature.name: Observational Savant
entries: Starting at level 2, you have developed an incredible awareness and connection to magic after years of observation and personal study. Whenever you see a spell cast by another spellcaster, you may roll an arcana check (DC = 10+ that spell's level). On a success, if that spell is a Wizard spell, you may copy it into your spellbook within the next 48 hours, after which time you forget the details of the spell if it goes uncopied. The time and gold you spend to copy a spell in this manner is halved.

subclassFeature.name: Running on Empty
entries: Starting at 2nd level, when you cast a spell using your final spell slot, or cast a cantrip while you have no remaining spell slots, you can instantly recover any number of spell slots that have a combined level equal to or less than half your wizard level, rounded up.
Regaining spells in this way is extremely taxing. When you do so, you gain one point of {@condition exhaustion} and cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Hard Knock Life
entries: Beginning at 6th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning damage, your current hit point maximum increases by 6, and whenever you gain a wizard level, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 1 point.

subclassFeature.name: Streetwise
entries: Beginning at 10th level, you may add your intelligence modifier to wisdom checks and wisdom saving throws. In addition, when you take the help action, the creature you are helping may add your intelligence modifier to their check.

subclassFeature.name: Self-Made Mage
entries: Starting at 14th level, as an action, you can draw on your vast, worldly experience to produce a single, empowering burst of magic. Chose one of the following effects:

items: You gain immunity to a damage type of your choice for one minute.
You gain a flying speed, swimming speed, and burrow speed equal to your walking speed for 10 minutes.
You have advantage on all saving throws for one minute.
You have advantage on all ranged attack rolls for one minute.
When you next cast a spell that requires a creature to make a saving throw, treat that creature's result on the die as a 1.

entries: One you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Bloodline
entries: The innate magic that flows through your veins is Demonic in origin, a dark power that burns with a desire to be wielded in battle. Often, Sorcerers with this origin can trace their powers back to a dark bargain or blood pact made by an ancestor with a powerful Demon, or even claim a parent as one possessed by a Demon. Sometimes, these powers manifest in individuals seemingly at random, perhaps as a result of the unknowable machinations of a powerful Demon Lord in another realm of existence, or as an unpredictable, chaotic burst of Demonic energy latching onto a host.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Demonic Spellcasting table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be a {@filter conjuration or necromancy spell from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list|spells|class=sorcerer;warlock;wizard|school=C;N|level=1;2;3;4;5;6;7;8;9}.

subclassFeature.name: Dark Wanderer
entries: Starting at 1st level, you have {@sense Darkvision} at a range of 60ft, and you can read and write Abyssal or one other language of your choice. In addition, whenever you cast a spell that would create magical darkness, you and a number of creatures you designate equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) can treat that magical darkness as though it were non-magical darkness (allowing for creatures with {@sense Darkvision} to see in it, for example).
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Sorcerous Frenzy
entries: Starting at 6th level, whenever you kill a hostile enemy humanoid, celestial or fiend you regain 2 sorcery points.
Additionally, you can use your sorcery points to enhance yourself. As a bonus action, you can spend any number of sorcery points to grant yourself 5x that many temporary hit points.
Once you use this feature to gain temporary hit points, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Transformation
entries: Starting at 14th level, as a bonus action, you can unleash the chaotic, demonic energy within you, enhancing your abilities for the next 10 minutes. Roll twice on the table below to randomly determine the benefits you recieve, rerolling any duplicates.

items: You grow skeletal wings, have a fly speed of 40 ft, can hover, and your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

Your hands become long, sharp talons. Your reach increases by 5ft, and you can use your action to make two unarmed strikes, dealing {@damage 1d12} magical slashing damage on each hit. You can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity modifier, for the attack and damage rolls.
You turn {@condition invisible} and can communicate telepathically with any creature that speaks at least one language within 120ft of you.
You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Spells you cast cannot be counterspelled or dispelled, except by an {@spell antimagic field}.
Even if you cast a spell with a casting time of a bonus action, you can still cast a levelled spell as your action, as long as that spell has a casting time of one action.
Whenever you cast a spell, you may treat that spell as though it were cast at one level higher than you cast it.
You have resistance to all non-magical damage, and have advantage on all saving throws to maintain {@status concentration} on a spell.

entries: Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 6 sorcery points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Familiar
entries: Starting at 18th level, once per long rest, as an action, you can call forth a demon to aid you in battle. A {@creature Hezrou} appears at a point you choose within 60ft of you. You can command it as a free action, and it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your commands and is hostile to everyone except you and your allies. It lasts for 59 minutes, or until its hit points reach 0, at which point it vanishes.
In addition, the {@creature Hezrou} gains the following benefits:

items.entry: If the {@creature Hezrou} forces an enemy to make a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.
When summoned, the {@creature Hezrou} gains temporary hit points equal to your Sorcerer level + your charisma modifier.

You gain the damage immunities and resistances of the {@creature Hezrou}, and it gains any damage resistances and immunities you have, for as long as you are within 60ft of each other and neither of you are {@condition incapacitated}.

subclassFeature.name: The Deep Consciousness
entries: Your Patron is The Deep Consciousness, an enigmatic and mysterious presence, unknowable and unyielding, existing without form. It is a void, empty of both light and darkness. A vast, incredible, ancient mind untethered to flesh or machine, holding unfathomable knowledge and understanding beyond the limits of mortal comprehension.
The Deep Consciousness grants power to Warlocks, steadily spreading its influence across all planes of existence in the aim of furthering some unknowable agenda.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Deep Consciousness lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a Warlock Spell. The following spells are added to the Warlock spell list for you.

entries.caption: Expanded Spell List
rows: {@spell Disguise Self}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter||Hideous Laughter}
{@spell Modify Memory}, {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond||Telepathic Bond}

subclassFeature.name: Iron Mind
entries: The power of The Deep Consciousness has strengthened your mind. At 1st level, you gain resistance to psychic damage, and you can add your charisma modifier to your intelligence saving throws.

In addition, if you would drop {@status concentration} on a spell cast using your pact magic, you can choose to maintain {@status concentration} instead. You can use this ability an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Invasion
entries: Beginning at 6th level you can use a bonus action to strike at the mind of a target you can see within 60ft of you that has an intelligence score of 3 or higher. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your Warlock Spell Save DC. On a failed save it suffers one negative effect of your choice from the following list:

items: It is {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn
It is {@condition deafened} until the end of your next turn
Its base movement speed is reduced by 30ft until the end of your next turn
It falls {@condition prone}
It drops {@status concentration} on any spell it is concentrating on
The first time it takes damage each turn, it takes an additional {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. This effect ends at the end of your next turn.

entries: Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Fortress
entries: When you reach 10th level, your mental fortifications grow even more powerful. You are immune to the {@condition charmed} and {@condition frightened} conditions. In addition, whenever you cast a spell that would charm or frighten an enemy, or use your 6th level Mental Invasion ability, you may expend an additional Pact Magic spell slot to have the target make its saving throw to resist the effect with disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Mind Crush
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can expend your energies to open a doorway in a target's mind to allow a small vestige of your Patron's power to invade.

As an action, choose a creature you can see within 60ft of you. Both you and it are {@condition incapacitated} and your base movement speeds become 0 for the next minute, or until you chose to end the effect. At the end of each of its turns, or whenever it takes damage from another source, it takes {@damage 2d10} psychic damage and makes a wisdom saving throw, freeing itself from your control on a successful save. Creatures immune to psychic damage treat damage from this effect as though they were resistant to it, not immune.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Demon Fist
entries: Monks of the Way of the Demon Fist train ferociously in the art of martial combat. They learn ruthless techniques to grievously wound, {@condition incapacitated|incapacitate}, or kill their enemies with blinding speed, harnessing their ki as a deadly weapon to bolster their power or devastate their foe.

subclassFeature.name: The Hidden Demon Technique
entries: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate the flow of your ki to duplicate the effects of certain spells, cursing an enemy or empowering yourself.
As an action, you can spend 2 ki points to cast {@spell Hold Person}, {@spell Blur}, {@spell Alter Self}, or {@spell Blindness/Deafness} at their lowest level without providing material components.
Additionally, you gain the {@spell Thaumaturgy} cantrip if you don't already have it.

subclassFeature.name: Ferocious Strike
entries: At 6th level, your strikes become brutal, targeting pressure points, aiming to grievously wound or kill. You score a critical hit on a 19 or a 20, and any creature you strike with a melee attack can't regain hit points until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Fighting Spirit
entries: By 11th level, your fighting spirit has become so intense that pain only fuels your frenzy. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to instantly make two unarmed strikes against any creature within 5ft of you.

subclassFeature.name: Fury of the Demon
entries: At 17th level, you gain the ability to devastate a foe by swiftly striking at multiple pressure points. If you hit the same creature with four or more melee attacks in one turn, at the end of that turn, that creature takes an additional {@damage 8d10} force damage and falls {@condition prone}.

subclassFeature.name: Kingpin
entries: In a world of monsters and magic, there are many ways to get rich. Some rogues steal. It could be a coin purse here, or a gold necklace there, but you have your eyes set on a grander, less tangible goal. Organised crime is big business, and any business needs good management to enjoy the lion's share. You have the skills to protect yourself, but what is a leader without disposable goons to aid them in the dirty work? As you increase in power and notoriety, so too will your influence through the underbelly of society grow. Many Kingpins operate outside the law, but some are known to conduct operations on behalf of the state, in businesses such as bodyguarding, monster hunting, and debt collection.

subclassFeature.name: Unarmed and Dangerous
entries: You have trained in a manner that allows you to maintain an outward appearance of respectability and dignity. Openly carrying a weapon is uncouth and bound to attract the wrong type of attention. Fortunately, you are just as deadly without one.
Starting at 3rd level, you gain the following benefits.

items: You gain proficiency with improvised weapons, and you may apply your sneak attack bonus to your unarmed strikes and attacks with improvised weapons.
You may use your dexterity modifier instead of strength when calculating attack and damage rolls using unarmed strikes and improvised weapon attacks.
Your unarmed strikes use a d4 for damage. This increases to a d6 at level 11.

subclassFeature.name: Tough Guy
entries: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in {@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion} (your choice) and your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your rogue level + your charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Thug Dealer
entries: Starting at 9th level, your influence has grown to the extent that you can conscript a Thug to accompany you in your daily dealings. They are friendly to you and your companions, and obey your commands. Your Thug's loyalty is absolute, however they may disobey blatantly suicidal orders at your DM's discretion.
Find your Thug's game statistics in the {@creature Thug|DMSecretWeapon} stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.

In combat, the Thug shares your initiative count, but they take their turn immediately after yours. They can move and use their reaction on their own, but the only actions they can take on their turn are the help action or the dodge action, unless you use a bonus action on your turn to command them to take another action.
That action can be one in their stat block or some other action. If you are {@condition incapacitated}, the Thug can take any action their choice.

If your Thug dies, you must return their equipment and body to their loved ones (if possible) and also give the family 500 gold pieces as a mark of respect. If you do not, your reputation sours and you cannot conscript a replacement Thug.

subclassFeature.name: I'll Do It Myself
entries: Starting at 13th level, you can use a bonus action to crack your knuckles, menacingly. Add your charisma modifier to your next attack attack roll and your next damage roll this turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your charisma modifier per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Goon Platoon
entries: When you reach 17th level, you can now conscript up to two thugs with your Thug Dealer trait, and any Thugs under your command gain temporary hit points equal to your charisma modifier any time you roll for initiative.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Totem Avatar
entries: The Circle of the Totem Avatar is an ancient order of Druids that harness the spiritual energies of the earth and manifest them in the form of powerful, totem armor. They cloak themselves in a spiritual avatar, amplifying their size and power. The form a druid's Totem Avatar takes often reflects an aspect of their personality or beliefs. An aggressive, hard headed druid may form themselves a Beast Totem Avatar in the form of a mighty bull, whereas a contemplative and subtle druid's Beast Totem Avatar may take the shape of an owl.

subclassFeature.name: Totemic Transformation
entries: Starting at 2nd level, as a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape to conjure spectral Totem Armor around your body, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain temporary hit points equal to your Druid level x3 for as long as your Totem Armor remains.
Your size becomes large, if there is room to do so.
Your reach increases by 5ft.

entries: In addition, choose one of the following forms: Beast, Tree, or Golem. The form you choose confers additional benefits.

entries.name: Beast Form
entries: You can use your Wisdom modifier when calculating attack and damage rolls for your unarmed strikes.
When you take the attack action on your turn, you can make a number of totemic unarmed strikes equal to half your Wisdom Modifier (rounded down).
Your totemic unarmed strikes deal {@damage 1d6} force damage.

entries.name: Tree Form
entries: Whenever you cast a leveled spell, you can bless one creature within 30ft of you with temporary hit points equal to that spell's level + your wisdom modifier.
You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
You are immune to the {@condition Stunned}, {@condition Paralyzed} and {@condition Prone} conditions.

entries.name: Golem Form
entries: You resist Bludgeoning, Slashing and Piercing damage from weapon attacks.
You have advantage on Strength and Constitution Saving Throws.
Your Totem Armor lasts for 1 minute, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}, Wild Shape, or use your Totemic Activation feature again to shift forms.

subclassFeature.name: Guardian Soul
entries: From 6th level, your Totem Armor offers you a measure of protection against lethal damage. Whenever you would fall to 0 hit points or die while in your Totemic Transformation, you instead fall to 1 hit point and your Totemic Transformation ends.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Totemic Transformation
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can enhance your totem forms with a greater level of power. Your Totem transformations gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Beast
entries: Your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistances and immunities, and if you take the attack action on your turn, you can make a single totemic unarmed strike as a bonus action.

entries.name: Tree
entries: You have 30ft of Tremorsense, and you can cast spells with a range of touch targeting a creature up to 30 ft away from you, as long as both you and that target are touching the ground.

entries.name: Golem
entries: You are resistant to fire, cold and poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: Totem Unification
entries: By expending two uses of your Wild Shape, you can activate all forms of your Totem Armor simultaneously, gaining the benefits of all of the totem forms at once.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Calamity
entries: Calamity Barbarians draw upon the raw, primal energies of the material plane. They embrace the reality that the forces of nature rule above all. Earthquakes topple the mightiest of kingdoms; tidal waves decimate the greatest fleets.
Contrary to what the cruellest tyrants and noblest kings may wish to believe, there are no heights mortals can reach that cannot be torn asunder by natural disaster.

Embracing this chaotic power, a Calamity Barbarian's greataxe may be struck by lightning as it falls in a blast of power, or a javelin may ignite in flame as it soars through the air. When angered, they are a walking natural disaster, channelling the immeasurable wrath of a calamity.

subclassFeature.name: Imbued Calamity
entries: When you take this path at 3rd level, choose one calamity through which you channel your power. Each calamity has an associated damage type, which empowers some of your other abilities, and confers a special benefit to you.

subclassFeature.name: Earthquake
entries: Bludgeoning Damage - Your base your walking speed increases by 5ft.

subclassFeature.name: Volcano
entries: Fire Damage - You gain a resistance to fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Hurricane
entries: Lightning Damage - You gain a resistance to lightning damage.

subclassFeature.name: Tsunami
entries: Cold Damage - You gain a resistance to cold damage.

subclassFeature.name: Disaster Strike
entries: Also at level 3, while you are raging, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can channel a calamitous strike, dealing {@damage 4d4} additional damage of your associated calamity type.
You can only use this feature once per long rest, unless you expend one use of your rage to do it again.
The damage of your Disaster Strike increases to {@damage 4d6} at level 6, {@damage 4d8} at level 10, and {@damage 4d10} at level 14.

subclassFeature.name: Oncoming Calamity
entries: Beginning at 6th level, your calamitous power grows. You gain an additional power related to your associated calamity type.

entries.name: Earthquake
entries: You gain the ability to sense the vibrations and tremors in the earth around you. You have Tremorsense in a 10ft range.

entries.name: Volcano
entries: You glow red hot while raging. Any creature grappling or grappled by you takes fire damage at the start of each of its turns equal to twice your proficiency bonus. You have resistance to cold damage.

entries.name: Tsunami
entries: You are a devastating threat in water. You gain a swim speed equal to twice your walking speed, and can hold your breath for up to an hour below water. You have resistance to fire damage.

entries.name: Hurricane
entries: You are empowered by the force of winds. While raging, you can choose to hover 5ft above the ground. In addition, as a bonus action while raging, you can leap through the air supported by a conjured gale. You can leap a number of feet equal to 3x your proficiency bonus in this way. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Invoke Calamity
entries: Starting at 10th level, your connection with the forces of elemental chaos allows you to force calamities on others.

When a creature within 15ft of you makes an attack roll against a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that attack (before the roll). If that attack misses, the attacking creature takes magical damage of your associated calamity damage type equal to half your barbarian level.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Calamity Incarnate
entries: At 14th level, while raging, once per long rest, you use a bonus action to expend an additional use of your rage and transcend into a maelstrom of living elemental power; a natural disaster incarnate.
This transformation lasts for as long as you are raging. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you invoke this transformation, creatures of your choice within 10ft of you take {@damage 2d6} magical damage of your calamity damage type.
Your movement speed increases by 10ft.
The area in a 15ft radius of you becomes difficult terrain for any creature other than yourself.
Your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d6} magical damage of your calamity damage type.
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack, that creature must make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + Strength Modifier + Proficiency Bonus) or fall {@condition prone}.

subclassFeature.name: Sky Domain
entries: Sky Domain Clerics are devoted to the open heavens and believe in the ideals of freedom, trust, individualism and tranquility. Deities such as the Greek Titan Uranus, Goddess Hera, Roman God Jupiter, or Egyptian God Horus are example patrons of Sky Clerics. Gods of the sky can also embody the sun, air, righteous combat, personal potential, weather and freedom.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with {@filter Martial Weapons|items|type=martial weapon;!treasure (gemstone);!treasure (art object);!futuristic;!renaissance;!treasure (coinage);!modern} and {@item Navigator's Tools|PHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Sky Scout
entries: Also at first level, you learn the {@spell Find Familiar} spell and can cast it as a ritual, except no matter the form your familiar takes, it has a 30ft fly speed, can hover and gains appropriate anatomy to support flight. For example, a Weasel familiar might be granted a pair of spectral wings.

As a bonus action, you can grant your familiar immunity to all damage for the next minute, or until it deals damage to another creature. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Skystrider
entries: At 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to grant the power of flight to those around you.

As an action, you present your holy symbol, and a gentle beam of sunlight shines forth onto a creature within 5ft. They gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Cleric level, a flying speed equal to their walking speed and can hover. These abilities last until they finish a long rest, or you use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Sunlight Empowerment
entries: Starting at 6th level, while in sunlight, you have advantage on attack rolls and {@skill perception} checks that rely on sight.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to imbue your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon Attack, you can cause the Attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Breath of the Heavens
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you use your Skystrider Channel Divinity, you can impart the benefits to a number of creatures equal to your proficiency bonus. In addition, allied creatures within 60ft of you with a fly speed can dash as a bonus action, and their movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Tomb Raider
entries: Tomb Raiders are explorers. They are hunters of fantastical treasures and guardians of ancient relics. They seek to plum the depths of history by hand, protecting the historic artefacts of immemorial cultures. They strive to educate, discover and preserve; a tomb raider is far from a common thief.

Exploring long forgotten dungeons and deep burial sites is risky business. Foolish Tomb Raiders don't live long. Adventuring parties and expeditions will often seek the aid of a Tomb Raider to guide them through dangerous dungeons, disarming traps and removing curses. A combination of warrior, locksmith, cursebreaker and artist; a wise Tomb Raider is the difference between a party finding untold magical secrets and items, or finding certain death in the forgotten, dark tombs of the old world.

subclassFeature.name: Favoured Weapon
entries: At third level, choose a Favoured Weapon from the following list. You gain additional benefits while wielding your Favoured Weapon. You can swap a Favoured Weapon choice to another option any time you gain a Ranger Level:

items.name: Whip
entries: Your attacks with a whip deal {@damage 2d4} slashing damage. In addition, when you hit a creature with an attack using a whip, if they are large or smaller, you can use your bonus action to attempt to pull them off their balance. They make a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your Dex or Strength modifier+ Proficiency Bonus) or fall {@condition prone}.

items.name: Blowgun
entries: You ignore the loading property of the blowgun, and attacks at long range don't impose disadvantage.

In addition, as a bonus action, you can coat the tip of a number of blowgun darts equal to your proficiency bonus in a simple poison. You have the knowledge on how to harvest this poison from natural resources found in your favoured terrain. Poisoned darts remain venomous for one minute or until they strike a creature. On a hit, the target takes one point of piercing damage and makes a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus), taking an additional {@damage 2d6} poison damage on a failed save.

items.name: Net
entries: You ignore the restriction on nets preventing you from making multiple attacks in a turn. In addition, making an attack roll with a net while standing within 5ft of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your roll, and attacks at long range also don't impose disadvantage.

Finally, your skill with net craftsmanship allows you to create more sturdy and powerful nets. You can craft a sturdy net in one hour of work at the cost of 10 gold pieces. It has an AC of 15, requires 15 slashing damage to break, and requires a strength check ({@dc 15}) to escape from.

subclassFeature.name: Lost Knowledge
entries: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in either history, investigation, or thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make which uses that proficiency.

subclassFeature.name: Raider's Fortune
entries: From 6th level, you have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition poisoned} condition, and advantage on saving throws to avoid or resist the effects of curses and cursed magical items.

In addition, you can cast the spells {@spell Detect Magic}, {@spell Remove Curse} and {@spell Identify} once each per long rest without expending a spell slot. You can also cast these spells with any available spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

subclassFeature.name: Raider's Instinct
entries: Starting at 11th level, you can add your wisdom modifier to any {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Stealth}, or {@skill Investigation} check.
In addition, you may choose an additional weapon from the Favoured Weapon list to act as a second Favoured Weapon, and you gain a +1 to attack rolls with your Favoured Weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Unorthodox Weapon Master
entries: Starting at 15th level, the maximum number of magical items you can attune to increases by one. In addition, when you use the attack action to attack with a Favoured Weapon, you can use your bonus action to make a single attack with a Favoured Weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Spectre Knight
entries: Many warriors kill, but none harness the dread powers of death itself like the Spectre Knight. Forever walking the twilight expanse that stretches between the living and the dead, Spectre Knights are imbued with supernatural, unknowable forces from beyond the realms of natural magic.
Not all Spectre Knight's are agents of chaos and evil, but the inky blackness of death that haunts their journey can push even the most noble warriors down a cruel, dark path.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Magic
entries: At 3rd level, you learn to manifest the power of the dead within yourself. This power is represented in your Spectral Energy dice, which are a {@dice d6}. You have a number of these dice equal to 1 + your proficiency bonus, and they fuel the powers you have, which are detailed below.

Some of your powers expend the Spectral Energy die they use, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when your dice are all expended. You regain all your expended Spectral Energy dice when you finish a long rest.

In addition, when you reduce a hostile, enemy creature to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to channel their fleeting vitality into yourself, regaining one expended Spectral Energy die. You can regain a number of Spectral Energy dice this way equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.
When you reach certain levels in this class, the size of your Spectral Energy dice increases: at 5th level ({@dice d8}), 11th level ({@dice d10}), and 17th level ({@dice d12}).
The powers below use your Spectral Energy Dice.

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Slash
entries: When you make an attack roll against a creature, you can imbue your strike with ghastly necrotic energy. Expend one Spectral Energy die, and add the number you rolled to your attack and damage rolls of this attack. The extra damage dealt by this ability is necrotic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Ghost Barrier
entries: As a reaction, when you are hit by an attack, you can expend one Spectral Energy die and gain AC equal to that roll until the start of your next turn, potentially turning a hit into a miss.

subclassFeature.name: Invoke Terror
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend one Spectral Energy die to cause your form to crackle with necrotic energy. All creatures of your choice within 15ft must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + Proficiency Bonus) or become {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Merciless
entries: Also starting at 3rd level, you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures who are {@condition frightened}.

subclassFeature.name: One With The Fallen
entries: Starting at 7th level, you unlock new Spectral abilities.

subclassFeature.name: Vanishment
entries: You unlock the power to turn intangible for a short time. As an action, you and all objects you are wearing and carrying become spectral in form, and you can move through objects and other creatures as though they were difficult terrain. While in this form, you resist all damage except force damage. This transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you attack, cast a spell, or force a creature to make a saving throw. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again unless you expend one Spectral Energy die.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Guidance
entries: As a reaction, immediately after you fail a Strength, Constitution or Charisma saving throw, you can roll a Spectral Energy die and add that result to the total, potentially turning failure into success. If you still fail that saving throw, your Spectral Energy die is not expended by using this ability.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Command
entries: Starting at 10th level, you can cast the spell {@spell Animate Dead} without requiring material components, and its casting time is reduced to 1 action when you cast it using this feature.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Ectoplasmic
entries: At 15th level, you gain the strength to expand your necrotic powers beyond your form. As a bonus action, you cause your form to glow, shedding dim green light in a 30ft radius for the next minute.
Other creatures of your choice within the light have advantage on Constitution and Death saving throws, and gain temporary hit points equal to your constitution modifier at the start of their turns.
Once you take this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a Spectral Energy die to do it again.

subclassFeature.name: From Beyond
entries: At 18th level, when you fall to 0 hit points, your spirit can leave your unconscious form and continue to fight. You appear as a translucent, white shade of your living self, complete with your equipment.
While in this form your statistics remain the same, but the only actions you can take on your turn are the help action and the attack action.
In addition, whenever you make a Death saving throw, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
You cannot cast spells or manipulate objects in this form, and you are immune to poison, cold, and necrotic damage. In addition, your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage.
Any damage dealt to your spirit form or your unconscious body causes a failed death saving throw as usual.
You can remain in spirit form for upto 10 minutes, or until your body regains consciousness, or you die, at which time your spirit form instantly vanishes.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you complete a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: College of Mime
entries: Bards of the College of Mime are masters of motion, movement and physical performance. An unusual school of magic, Mime Bards seek to channel powerful magic through gesture, rather than words. Stealth, speed, enchantment and abjuration are the tools through which they weave spells.

The most powerful Mime Bards can form unbreakable structures from nothing, cure lethal curses with a touch, banish creatures with a wipe of the hand, and even make a semi-decent living as a performing street artist on the side

subclassFeature.name: Voiceless Whisper
entries: When you take this subclass at level 3, your training in the art of physical performance allows you to channel magic through gestures, rather than your words.

You can cast spells without performing the verbal components, as long as you aren't {@condition restrained} or {@condition incapacitated}, and you can inspire others with your Bardic Inspiration even if they can't hear you, as long as they can see you.

subclassFeature.name: Ensnaring Mimicry
entries: Also at level 3 you gain the power to form magical connections with other creatures through the art of mimicry.

As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. You spend your action and half of your movement speed mimicking its movements with uncanny accuracy, forming a magical connection. This link lasts for the next minute, or until you lose {@status concentration} (as if concentrating on a spell).
While linked with a creature this way, you can use your bonus action to influence its behaviour in one of the following ways:

entries.name: Comedic Mimicry
entries: The linked creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, both you and it fall {@condition prone}.

entries.name: Tragic Mimicry
entries: The linked creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, until the start of your next turn, it suffers a negative modifier to all Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Unified Motion
entries: The linked creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, its movement becomes tied to yours. Until the end of this turn, as you move using your movement speed, the creature also moves that number of feet in any direction that you choose. You can't force the creature to move through obviously dangerous ground, such as a fire or off a cliff.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Motion
entries: Beginning at 6th level, your growing mastery of movement and performance begin to intertwine, enhancing your body with incredible grace and speed.
Your movement speed increases by 10 feet, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check or saving throw you are proficient in that uses your Dexterity modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Gesticulated Manifestation
entries: When you reach 14th level, once per long rest, you can use this trait to cast any  {@filter Abjuration or Illusion|spells|source=|school=a;i}spell of a level for which you have a spell slot with a casting time of one action. You cast it without performing its verbal components and doing so consumes a spell slot of that level.

If that spell normally requires {@status concentration}, it doesn't when you cast it using this feature, and instead lasts for the full duration. The spell ends early if you are knocked {@condition unconscious} or audibly speak.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Merriment
entries: Many Paladins seek to protect the innocent, but those who take the Oath of Merriment seek more. They aim not to only save lives, but give them purpose and meaning; to spread merriment and joy.

The Oath of Merriment pledges equal worth to physical and emotional freedom. Paladins of this order spread goodwill and companionship to all those they meet. After all, what is the gift of life for but to be enjoyed?
Spreading this message, Merriment Paladins oppose agents of misery, cruelty and suffering wherever they find them, and take pride in finding reasons to live well, even in the darkest of times.

entries.name: Tenets of Merriment
entries: {@b Joy -} To live well means to live with joy. All sentient life has a right to happiness, and you strive to build a world where none are condemned to misery and hopelessness.
{@b Safety -} To live well means to feel secure. Protecting the innocent is paramount, and you protect others by being powerful yourself.
{@b Companionship -} To live well means to share life with others. You are a uniter of all peoples, and place great importance on bonds of friendship and family.

{@b Acceptance -} To live well means allowing all to live well. You need not understand the ways of people to respect them. As long as they don't spread misery or pain, you seek to defend the cultures and beliefs of all people.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the Paladin levels listed.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this Oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: The Right Path
entries: As an action, you place your hand on a non-hostile creature and bless them with divine energy. You have advantage on all Charisma (persuasion) checks against that creature for the next minute. In addition, if that creature was originally good-aligned and its alignment has changed, it is restored to its original alignment.

entries.name: Divine Gift
entries: As a bonus action, you conjure a number of tiny magic boxes equal to your charisma modifier, which appear in unoccupied spaces within 30 ft of you. Choose a creature within range when you conjure each box. That box can only be opened by the chosen creature.

As an action, the chosen creature can open a box to receive a benefit, and the box then vanishes. If unopened, the boxes disappear after 24 hours, or when you use this feature again. When you create each box, choose one of the following benefits to store within:

entries.name: Soul
entries: The creature gains temporary hit points equal to half your paladin level (rounded up) + Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Spirit
entries: The creature gains a point of inspiration.

entries.name: Heart
entries: Opening the gift cures one of the following conditions affecting a creature (their choice when they open it): {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Poisoned}, {@condition Blinded}, or {@condition Deafened}.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Miracles
entries: Starting at 7th level, your spirit hums with a magical aura of fortune and jollity, heartening all those around you. Whenever you or an ally within 10 feet of you rolls a natural 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction to let that creature reroll the die. They must use the new roll.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Festivities
entries: Starting at 15th level, you can cast the spell {@spell Heroes' Feast}, without expending a spell slot.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Miracle Strike
entries: At 20th level, your fervent embrace of life grants you moments of spectacular fortune. You can use an action to gain the following benefits for one hour.

items: Once, when you make a death saving throw, you can treat any roll on the die as a natural 20.
Once, when you hit a creature with an attack roll while you have only 1 hit point, you can treat the number rolled on the die for that attack roll as a natural 20.

Once, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you falls to zero hit points, you can use your reaction to expend a spell slot. That creature regains hit points equal to twice the level of the spell slot you expended + your charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: School of Reverberation
entries: Wizards of the School of Reverberation are masters of sound, echo, and vibration magic, commanding oscillating pulses of magical force to produce devastating effects. From calamitous booming shockwaves, to gentle whispers that grow to a furious hurricane, their spells echo across time, rebounding on their targets for brutal damage.

subclassFeature.name: Cacophonous Savant
entries: When you select this school at 2nd level, you gain a resistance to Thunder damage. Any time and gold you spend to copy a spell that deals {@filter Thunder|spells|damage type=thunder} damage or causes the {@condition Deafened} condition into your spellbook is halved.

subclassFeature.name: Reverberant Echo
entries: From 2nd level, when you cast a non-concentration, levelled spell that deals damage, you can overcharge it with reverberant magic, creating a spell echo.

The echo lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1+ the spell's level, or until you lose {@status concentration} (as if concentrating on a spell). While it is active, the sound of the spell can be heard bouncing and shimmering in the air.
As a bonus action on each of your turns, you can choose one creature within 60 feet and unleash the force of the echoed spell upon them.

The target makes a constitution saving throw. Roll a number of d8s equal to the level of the echoed spell. The target takes that much damage of the spell's damage type, or half as much on a successful save.
You can create a spell echo in this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Tune Up
entries: Starting at 6th level, you gain the power to synchronise your own magical energy with the area around you. By focusing for 10 minutes, you gain one of the following benefits:

items: You gain the benefits of a short rest.
You have advantage on initiative rolls and perception checks that rely on sound for the next 4 hours.

You become acutely aware of the ripples of magic that resonate around this location. For the next 30 minutes, you can sense the presence of magic within 60 feet of you. If you sense magic in this way, you can use your action to see a faint aura around any visible creature or object in the area that bears magic, and you learn its school of magic, if any. This effect can penetrate most barriers, but it is blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

entries: Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Tremor Resonance
entries: Starting at 10th level, you gain {@sense Tremorsense|MM} in a 30 foot radius.

In addition, you gain the power to channel magic through vibrations in materials. If you cast a spell with the range of touch, you can increase its range to target a creature or object within 30 feet, as long as both you and the target are touching the same surface.

subclassFeature.name: Power Word Mastery
entries: Starting at 14th level, your words echo with incredible power and force.

When you cast a spell with "Power Word" in its name, the hit point threshold required for that spell to affect a creature is increased by 50%. For example, when you cast {@spell Power Word Stun}, it can affect a creature with 225 hit points or fewer.
In addition, you become immune to harmful "Power Word" spells and Thunder damage.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Coven
entries: Druids within the Circle of the Witch understand and uphold the cycle of life and death. Both are essential, beautiful, and powerful forces, and form the cycle that drives all existence in the multiverse. They are also adept healers and brewers of magic. Many Druids are isolationist, but "Witch Druids" have been known to gather and travel together in small covens, typically numbering thirteen.

Their ability to exert influence over the undead has led many to fear them; the word "witch" is a whispered slur on the lips of many commoners. However, although they can command powerful necromancy magic, they are not inherently "evil", and some are widely known and beloved as respected healers, shamans and counselors.

subclassFeature.name: Circle Spells
entries: When you join this circle at 2nd level, you receive secret knowledge on necromantic and conjuration magics. This grants you access to some spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circle of the Witch Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

subclassFeature.name: Deadly Potionier
entries: Also at 2nd level, at the end of a long rest, you can use natural materials you have foraged from an area of wilderness you are familiar with to brew dangerous, volatile potions.
You can create enough potions to fill a number of vials equal to your proficiency bonus. These potions harbor fleeting magic, and lose all abilities after 24 hours.
A creature can use an action to hurl a potion vial up to 30 feet, which shatters on contact with the ground or an object or creature.
All creatures in a 5-foot radius of that point must succeed on a saving throw against your Spell Save DC, or suffer a negative effect, dictated by the potion you brewed.
These effects are also activated if a creature ingests the potion. If a creature drinks one, they make any saving throw to resist its effects at disadvantage.

rows: You take {@damage 2d10} poison damage. This damage increases to {@damage 3d10} at level 5, {@damage 4d10} at level 11, and {@damage 5d10} at level 17.

You have disadvantage on all Strength checks, Strength saving throws, and your movement speed is reduced by 15 feet for one minute. A creature suffering this effect can use its action to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, ending the effect on a success.
You fall {@condition unconscious} for the next minute, or until you take next damage, or a creature uses an action to shake or slap you awake.

You become entangled in grasping vines that sprout from the area the potion spilled. You are {@condition restrained}. A creature {@condition restrained} by the plants can use its action to make a Strength check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself. The vines wither away after 1 minute.
You become befuddled. Words and thoughts are difficult to articulate. You have disadvantage on all Charisma and Intelligence checks for the next minute.

You are engulfed in flame. You take {@damage 1d6} fire damage at the start of each of your turns for the next minute. A creature can end this damage by using its Action to make a Dexterity check to extinguish the flames, or by fully submerging themselves in water. The damage dealt by this potion increases to {@damage 2d6} at level 5, {@damage 3d6} at level 11, and {@damage 4d6} at level 17.

subclassFeature.name: Vile Shape
entries: Also at 2nd level, when you wild shape, you retain the ability to talk.
In addition, if you choose, you can wild shape into an undead, zombified or skeletal form of the beast you change into.
While in that form you gain proficiency in the {@skill intimidation} skill, and your creature type becomes undead, not beast.

subclassFeature.name: One With The Azure
entries: At 6th level, you can choose a small, inanimate object that you own, like a broomstick, hat, or cloak, and infuse it with magic.
As a bonus action, if you are carrying or wearing that object on your person, you can invoke the magic stored within to gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed for the next 10 minutes.
You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Gift of Life and Death
entries: At 10th level, you gain the power to infuse your spells with necromantic powers. Whenever you cast a spell that targets only one creature, choose one of the following effects:

items: That spell deals an additional {@damage 1d12} necrotic damage.
The spell grants the target a number of temporary hit points equal to {@dice 1d12} + their constitution modifier.

entries: You can only use this feature once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Coven
entries: Starting at 14th level, when you finish a long rest, you can choose a number of creatures within 60 feet of you up to your Wisdom modifier. They gain the following benefits for the next 12 hours as long as they are within 30 feet of you or another creature you choose with this feature:

items: You gain +1 to your AC.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
You can add {@dice 1d12} to an attack roll or ability check. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add that bonus to the damage.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Wild Magic
entries: The Oath of Wild Magic is sworn to embrace and uphold the fundamental forces of magic. Becoming in tune with the gentle hum of magic that permeates all realms, allowing the chaos of unpredictable forces to guide you, and, in turn, guiding them without demanding control; these are the ideals of Wild Magic Paladins.

This philosophy manifests as ideals revolving around freedom, honesty, and impermanence. Many Wild Magic Paladins serve as councillors and ambassadors to powerful, magical beings like dragons and archmages, or as guardians of significant, magical places.
Many Paladins who swear this oath do so to unite themselves with the fundamental, divine magic that permeates all things.

entries.name: Tenets of Wild Magic
entries: The Tenets of Wild Magic are less rigid than those of other paladin orders, serving as philosophical guidelines rather than an immutable code.

entries.name: Impermanence
entries: Nothing lasts forever. One day everything will end, and no-one will remember. Seek not to preserve the ways of old, embrace change and spontaneity.

entries.name: Freedom
entries: Bare not shackles of iron or philosophy. The magic of the world cannot truly be captured or owned. The same applies to all living things, we are manifestations of magic.

entries.name: Honesty
entries: Divine Magic is a fundamental force of existence. Like gravity, it cannot lie. You should be the same. Hide nothing, speak openly, seek not to control others with deception.

entries.name: Humility
entries: Stake no claim to the forces or form you wield. Your strength of body and magic are temporary gifts, not rights. They will fade in time. Be thankful. Command them with respect.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain Oath Spells at the Paladin Levels listed.

entries.caption: Oath of Wild Magic Spells
rows: {@spell Disguise Self}, one randomly determined 1st level spell from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}
{@spell Levitate}, one randomly determined 2nd level spell from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}
{@spell Major Image}, one randomly determined 3rd level spell from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}
{@spell Hallucinatory Terrain}, one randomly determined 4th level spell from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}
{@spell Legend Lore}, one randomly determined 5th level spell from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}

entries: {@i Editor's note: there are many helpful tables of class spells online. To randomly determine a spell, you can go to these tables and use a random number generator to select one}.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Well of Magic
entries: You draw upon the latent magic of the world to empower yourself. Over the course of a short rest, you regain expended spell slots. The spell slots can have a combined level of up to your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Chaos Channeler
entries: When you use your Divine Smite ability, choose one: Light or Darkness. Roll on the corresponding Wild Magic Table and apply that effect. Once you use this Channel Divinity, you can activate this effect again when you Divine Smite a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short rest, but never more than once per turn.

entries.caption: Wild Magic of Light
rows: You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your charisma modifier at the start of each of your turns for the next minute.
You regain one expended spell slot of 3rd level or below.
Choose a damage type. You have resistance to that type for the next minute.

You grow one size category larger for the next minute, if there is room. Your reach is increased by 5 feet, your weapon attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d4} damage, and you have advantage on strength checks and strength saving throws for this time.
For the next minute, you can take the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} actions as a bonus action.
For the next minute, you can use your reaction when you make an attack roll or saving throw to roll {@dice 1d6} and add the result to your roll.
For the next minute, when you use your Lay on Hands feature, the creature you heal recovers five hit points for each point you expend.

A creature you can see within 30 feet of you is {@condition charmed} by you for the next minute, or until you or one of your allies deals damage to them. At the end of each of their turns, they make Wisdom saving throw, ending this effect early on a success.

entries.caption: Wild Magic of Darkness
rows: For the next minute, you have advantage on all attack rolls, and attack rolls against you are made at advantage.
For the next minute, your weapon attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage.
For the next minute, you can teleport a number of feet equal to half your walking speed to an unoccupied space you can see as a bonus action.
Choose up to two creatures you can see within 30 feet. For the next minute, they must roll a {@dice d4} and subtract the result from all their attack rolls and saving throws.
Your form becomes wreathed in shadows, making your movements difficult to track. Attack rolls against you have disadvantage for the next minute.

For the next minute, when you hit a creature with an attack roll, they must make a Charisma saving throw or be {@condition blinded} until the start of your next turn. You can only use this ability once per turn.
You can immediately take one additional action.
All creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you lose hit points equal to your Paladin level. You gain temporary hit points equal to the total number hit points other creatures lost by this effect.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Chaos
entries: Starting at 7th level, you exude an aura of chaotic, magical energy, influencing the world in unpredictable ways.

When a hostile creature within 10 feet of you rolls a natural 20 on an attack roll or ability check, you can use your reaction to chaotically influence fate. They reroll the die, and must use the new roll.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Darkness From Light
entries: At 15th level, you can manipulate the magic of your Lay on Hands feature to inflict harm as well as healing.
When you use your Lay on Hands feature, you can choose to inflict necrotic damage equal to the number of Hit Points you expend, rather than healing that amount.
If you do this, the target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a success, any damage dealt by this feature is halved.
This feature has no effect on undead or constructs.

subclassFeature.name: Chaos Incarnate
entries: At 20th level, you can enter a state of total connection to magic, letting you exert some degree of control over your Wild Magic surges. As a bonus action, you gain the following effects for one minute:

items: When you use your Chaos Channeler ability, you can choose one effect from either table to apply. Then roll on the other table and apply that effect as well.

You can use your Chaos Channeler ability once per round when you hit a creature with an attack. This use does not count against the amount of times you can use your Chaos Channeler ability or Channel Divinity per short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Wilds
entries: As one with the roaring tempest and charging ram, Barbarians of the Path of the Wilds are empowered with the raw, primal magic of the material plane. As dangerous with their bare hands as when swinging a colossal greathammer, they make for terrifying close quarter combatants, leveraging incredible strength and skill to overwhelm their foe.

subclassFeature.name: Bare Fist Brawler
entries: You are an adept hand-to-hand combatant. Your unarmed strikes can deal {@damage 1d8} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage. This damage increases to {@damage 1d10} at level 10.
In addition, if you successfully grapple, shove, or disarm a creature on your turn, you can make a single unarmed strike as a bonus action.

subclassFeature.name: One With The Wilds
entries: You have mastered surviving and moving through the wilderness. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Animal Handling} and {@skill Survival} skills, and have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

subclassFeature.name: Furious Onslaught
entries: While you are raging, your attacks are treated as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage.

In addition, when you score a critical hit against a creature that is no more than one size larger than you and is within your reach, you can use your reaction to barrel into them. That creature becomes grappled by you or is shoved {@condition prone} (your choice).

subclassFeature.name: Rugged Survivalist
entries: You can add your Constitution modifier to your Wisdom Saving Throws.
In addition, when you enter a rage, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Barbarian level + your Constitution modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Dizzying Blow
entries: Your blows are imbued with ruinous force. Once on your turn, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, choose one of the following effects:

items: That attack deals an extra {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage.

The target must succeed on a Constitution Saving Throw (DC = 8 + your Strength Modifier + your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, they have disadvantage on all attack rolls and Dexterity Saving Throws until the start of your next turn.
The target cannot make opportunity attacks until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Champion
entries: The archetypal Champion focuses on the development of raw physical power honed to deadly perfection. Those who model themselves on this archetype combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows.

subclassFeature.name: Devastating Critical
entries: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.
In addition, when you score a critical hit, you can choose to forgo the extra damage to instead choose one of the following effects.

items: The target is {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn.
The target falls {@condition prone}.
You push the target up to 15 feet horizontally to an unoccupied space you can see.
You can take the {@action Disengage} or {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action on this turn.
A surge of adrenaline rushes through your body. You gain temporary hit points equal to {@damage 1d10} + your Constitution modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Remarkable Athlete
entries: You can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check or saving throw you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus.
In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

subclassFeature.name: Ultimate Fighter
entries: You can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature or an additional feat.
In addition, the maximum threshold for your Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity scores increases by 2.

subclassFeature.name: Ruinous Critical
entries: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.
In addition, when you score a critical hit, you can forgo dealing damage to choose two options from your Devestating Critical feature, not just one.

subclassFeature.name: Ultimate Survivor
entries: You have attained the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain Hit Points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your Hit Points left.
You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 Hit Points.

subclassFeature.name: Monstrous Bloodline
entries: Through dangerous, magical experimentation, the meddling of a powerful deity, or some other means, your bloodline is twisted with the blood of monstrosities. You draw a vivid and brutal magic from the savage energy that courses through your veins, manifesting itself in powerful and unpredictable ways.

Some Sorcerers of the Monstrous Bloodline are cursed to bear the physical attributes of their heritage, drawing ire and suspicion wherever they roam. Others appear ordinary, able to manifest their power in battle and then slip back into society, anxiously guarding the secret origin of their power, a slumbering well of monstrous force simmering within.

subclassFeature.name: Monstrous Spells
entries: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Monstrous Spellcasting table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be an evocation or transmutation spell from the {@filter sorcerer, warlock, or druid spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer;Warlock;Druid}.

entries.caption: Monstrous Spellcasting
rows: {@spell Poison Spray}, {@spell Faerie Fire}, {@spell Speak With Animals}

subclassFeature.name: Monstrous Heritage
entries: Monstrous power runs through your bloodline. Choose one of the following monsters from which you draw power and gain that feature:

subclassFeature.name: Mimic
entries: You can cast the spell {@spell Disguise Self} at will without a spell slot or components. When you cast it in this way, any creature that makes an investigation checks to perceive through the illusion makes that check at disadvantage.
In addition, you are immune to acid damage. You may also choose to have your skin become slightly sticky and acidic to the touch when you gain this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Drider
entries: You have darkvision out to a range of 120 feet, and you can add your Charisma modifier to your Stealth and Perception checks.
You may also choose to have your limbs lengthen slightly and grow an additional pair of eyes directly above your current ones when you gain this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Hydra
entries: You gain a bonus to any saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition deafened}, or {@condition stunned} conditions, or to maintain {@status concentration} on a spell. This bonus is equal to half your sorcerer level (rounded up).
You may also choose to grow a second head when you gain this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Gift of the Bloodline
entries: Choose another benefit from the options below. The monster you inherit this power from can be the same as the one you chose for your 1st-level feature, or a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Mimic
entries: As an action, you can alter your body on a molecular level to gain an immunity to one damage type for the next 10 minutes. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short rest.

subclassFeature.name: Drider
entries: Your base movement speed increases by 10 feet, and you gain the ability to move up, down, and across vertical surfaces upside down while leaving your hands free. You also gain a climb speed equal to your walking speed.

subclassFeature.name: Hydra
entries: By dividing your focus as a dual mind, you can take one additional reaction per round (but never more than once on a single turn).

subclassFeature.name: Monstrous Connection
entries: You have an innate connection with monstrosities. Once per turn, if a spell you cast forces a monstrosity to make a saving throw, that monster rolls {@dice 1d6} and subtracts the result from its save.
In addition, spells you cast that can normally target only beasts ({@spell Speak With Animals}, {@spell Dominate Beast}, etc.) can also target monstrosities when you cast them.

subclassFeature.name: Monstrous Manifestation
entries: Choose a final, monstrous benefit from the options below. The monster you inherit this power from can be the same as the one you chose for a previous feature, or a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Mimic
entries: You learn the {@spell Shapechange} spell, and if you cast it, you automatically succeed on any Constitution saving throws to maintain {@status concentration} on that spell that are triggered by taking damage.

subclassFeature.name: Drider
entries: As a bonus action, can sprout four more limbs. This transformation lasts for the next 10 minutes, unless you extend duration by using this feature again. You can end the transformation early by using an action to retract your extra limbs into your body.

While in this form, your movement speed increases by 30 feet, you gain a climb speed equal to your walking speed, you ignore difficult terrain created by spells, your AC increases by 3, and you can cast the spell {@spell Web} as a bonus action without expending a spell slot. If cast {@spell Web} using this feature, it does not require {@status concentration}, and lasts for the full duration.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma Modifier per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Hydra
entries: As long as you have at least 1 hit point, you regain 10 hit points at the start of each of your turns. If you took fire damage since the end of your last turn, this ability does not trigger.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Path of the Berserker
entries: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end – that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammelled fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker's rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.

subclassFeature.name: Frenzy
entries: You can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, you can immediately make a weapon attack as a part of the bonus action you used to rage on this turn. In addition, for the next minute, as long as you are raging, you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend one additional use of your rage to activate it again.

{@i Design Note: You can now attack the turn you activate your frenzy, and it does not give a point of exhaustion as a penalty for use. However, it is limited to only once per day, unless a player expends an additional use of rage to activate it again. This functionally limits Frenzy to once per day until level 6, and only three times per day upon reaching level 15.}

subclassFeature.name: Mindless Rage
