entries: You can't be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened} while raging. If you are {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened} when you enter your rage, the effect ends.

subclassFeature.name: Intimidating Presence
entries: When you take the attack action, you can substitute one of those attacks with an attempt to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be {@condition frightened} of you for the next minute or until your rage ends or you use this feature again. This effect ends early if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.
{@i Design Note: Intimidating Presence now replaces only one attack, not your entire action, and lasts for a minute.}

subclassFeature.name: Retaliation
entries: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within your reach, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Flame Weaver Conclave
entries: With hearts and magic inflamed with passion, Flame Weavers wield fire as a living weapon, directing its destructive energy to incinerate foes. Rangers of this conclave seek to command the most raw, explosive force of nature, and prioritise offensive magic and high-risk battle strategies. However, the conclave is not mindless. They understand the devastating potential of a flame unchecked, wielding fire magic with respect, caution, and subtlety when such virtues are called for. Flame Weavers are highly sought after as professional assassins, as a master of the technique can reduce a target to ashes while leaving the surrounding area unblemished.

subclassFeature.name: Flame Weaver Magic
entries: You learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Flame Weaver Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Flame Infusion
entries: Fire magic ripples through your body and bursts when you strike. The first time you hit a creature each turn with a weapon attack, the creature takes an additional {@damage 1d6} fire damage. When you reach 11th level in this class, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Incineration Specialist
entries: Your mastery of fire magic grants your spells extra potency, and offers some guard against flames. Your weapon attacks, spells, and abilities that deal damage to other creatures ignore any resistance to fire damage, and you have a resistance to fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Jet of Flame
entries: As a bonus action, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see in a burst of flame. Other creatures within 5 feet of you when you appear must succeed on a Dexterity Saving Throw (DC = your Ranger spellcasting DC), or take {@damage 1d8} fire damage. When you reach 11th level in this class, the damage increases to {@damage 2d8}. You can use this feature once per long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 2nd level or above to do it again.

subclassFeature.name: Burning Form
entries: Your blistering reactions and blazing magic serve to protect you at a moment's notice. You learn the {@spell fire shield} spell. In addition, when you roll initiative, you can use a reaction to cast the spell {@spell fire shield} on yourself, without expending a spell slot.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Heart of Flame
entries: You are one with flame, and your command over fire is absolute and devastating. Your weapon attacks, spells, and abilities that deal fire damage ignore any target's immunity to fire damage.

In addition, when you cast a spell or use an ability that deals fire damage and forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can choose a number of those creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one). You bend the spell in such a manner as to avoid harming the chosen creatures, and they take no fire damage from that spell or ability.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Iron Mind
entries: With willpower as inflexible and sturdy as plate mail, Monks of the Way of the Iron Mind are masters of both physical and mental durability. Able to manifest their ki as mighty, spectral armor, they shield themselves from harm whilst channelling a flow of power that enhances their combat capabilities. Monks who walk this path are typically unflinching and resolute, rarely changing their mind or shifting their perspective. They dedicate themselves to a singular purpose and see it done, wielding ki as a mighty shield and crushing weapon to smash through any who stand in their way.

subclassFeature.name: Martial Dedication
entries: You gain proficiency with light and medium armor, and you retain the benefits of your Martial Arts and Unarmored Movement features even if you are wearing armor.

subclassFeature.name: Armor of Ki
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend two ki points to manifest magnificent, spectral armor. You decide what your armor looks like; for some monks, it may appear as a gleaming sheen of plate mail, for others, a writhing fortification of darkness.

When you manifest the armor, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to 5 + your Wisdom modifier + your Monk level. The armor lasts for 1 minute, or until you have no more temporary hit points remaining. While the armor is active, you also gain the following benefits.

items: You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your half proficiency bonus rounded up.
You can use your Flurry of Blows, Step of the Wind, and Patient Defense features without expending a ki point.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Will of Iron
entries: While your Armor of Ki is manifested, you resist Bludgeoning, Slashing, and Piercing damage, and can add your Wisdom modifier to Intelligence and Charisma saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Ki-Fuelled Strike
entries: While your Armor of Ki is manifested, your damage rolls deal additional force damage equal to half your proficiency bonus rounded up.

subclassFeature.name: Ki Detonation
entries: When the temporary hit points granted by your Armor of Ki feature are depleted, you can expend 5 ki points to detonate your armor with explosive force. Creatures of your choice within 15 feet must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 10d10} force damage on failed save, or half as much on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Superior School of Evocation
entries: What's more iconic than making things explode? Wizards are all about big booms, and yet the Evocation subclass is, regrettably, pretty mid. In fact, it's arguably broken, seeing as its best trait is one that exploits a curious interaction between the spell magic missile and the 10th level feature Empowered Evocation that was absolutely not intended.

So, please accept this offering as a revised Evocation Wizard, one that aims to give its underpowered (or just straight up boring) features a boost, and its "problematic" features a slight tweaking to prevent the cheese that is the {@damage 7d4+42} force damage that cannot miss.
If you'd like, you can treat this variant School of Evocation as a related but separate discipline, perhaps hailing from another continent or rival order of magic to the original.

You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar. Others use their spectacular power to protect the weak, while some seek their own gain as bandits, adventurers, or aspiring tyrants.

subclassFeature.name: Evocation Savant
entries: The gold and time you must spend to copy an {@filter evocation|spells|class=Wizard|school=V} spell into your spellbook is halved.

subclassFeature.name: Sculpt Spells
entries: You have unrivalled command over the destructive force of your spells. Once per turn, when you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose to sculpt the spell to maximise its potency or protect those caught in the blast. Choose one of the following effects:

items: Choose a number of creatures equal to 1 + the level of the spell. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
Choose one creature affected by the spell, it has disadvantage on its saving throw against this spell.

entries: {@i Sculpt Spells Design Note: This feature adds the ability to sculpt your evocation spells for increased damage rather than only for defence. In playtesting, we have found that an intelligently played spellcaster rarely, if ever, needs to position their spells in a manner that damages their allies. This feature also covers much of the design intent of the original Potent Cantrip feature, allowing for room to unify the old Potent Cantrip and Empowered Evocation features into a single, streamlined 6th-level ability.}

subclassFeature.name: Empowered Evocation
entries: Once per turn, when you deal damage to a creature with an Evocation spell, that creature takes additional force damage equal to 1 + your Intelligence modifier.

{@i Empowered Evocation Design Note: Sadly, the old Potent Cantrip feature only applied to cantrips that forced saving throws, while the primary damage cantrip Wizards prefer to use is Fire Bolt. This new feature corrects that issue, applying a small boost to all spells, while preventing the "magic missile cheese" effect present in the old Empowered Evocation feature.})

subclassFeature.name: Detonate
entries: When you drop {@status concentration} on an Evocation spell, you can detonate the fleeting magical focus as a blast of elemental power. Choose a number of creatures within 60 feet equal to your proficiency bonus. Each must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or take Xd4 acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder damage (your choice), where X is the level of the spell you were concentrating on.

{@i Detonate Design Note: This feature is entirely new to the Evocation wizard, and aims to give an appropriately explosive conclusion to the iconic Evocation concentration spells such as arcane hand, wall of fire, and sunbeam.}

subclassFeature.name: Overchannel
entries: Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take {@damage 2d12} necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by {@damage 1d12}. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

subclassFeature.name: The Greatwyrm
entries: Your patron is an ancient greatwyrm: a gargantuan dragon of godlike power. That primal power now flows through you, enhancing your body with the strength and fortitude of dragons, and granting you the ability to unleash your spells as a devastating wave of dragon's breath.
Often, the true nature of a draconic patron, their colour, motivations, and goals, are a mystery even to those who wield their strength.

In rarer cases, a greatwyrm may seek a more active role in the lives of a warlock, conversing with them regularly and directing them as emissaries through which the greatwyrm can interact with the world. In any case, the towering might of dragonkind slumbers within you, and the ancient fury of the greatwyrm is yours to command.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Gift
entries: Your draconic patron enhances your physiology and strength. You gain proficiency with medium armour, and you have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're {@condition blinded} or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an {@condition invisible} creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Greatwyrm lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The Greatwyrm Expanded Spells table shows the spells that are added to the warlock spell list for you.

subclassFeature.name: Spellbreath
entries: Your pact magic bubbles and simmers in a well of power within your body, and you have been granted the ability to expel that magic in a terrible burst of draconic breath. If you make an attack roll as part of a spell, such as one of the attacks made when casting {@spell eldritch blast}, {@spell scorching ray}, or {@spell vampiric touch}, you can replace that attack roll with a 15-foot-cone breath weapon attack. Creatures in that cone must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or take damage equal to the damage that would be dealt by that attack roll on a hit, or half as much on a successful save.

Alternatively, if you cast a spell that restores hit points to a single target, you can instead expel that rejuvenating magic in a 15-foot-cone of invigorating breath. Creatures of your choice within the area of your breath regain hit points equal to the hit points that would be bestowed to a single target of that spell.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier. You regain all expended uses of this feature upon finishing a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Form of the Dragon
entries: As a bonus action, you can sprout spectral, draconic wings. You gain a fly speed equal to your walking speed for 10 minutes, during which time you can also hover, and you have advantage on Intimidation checks and Strength saving throws.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Spellbreath
entries: The well of power inside you has grown. When you use your Spellbreath feature, the size of the cone increases to 30 feet. In addition, any creature you damage with it takes additional damage equal to your Charisma modifier, and any creature you heal with this feature gains temporary hit points equal to twice your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Fortitude
entries: You are blessed with a fragment of your patron's incredible fortitude. Your maximum hit points increases by an amount equal to your Warlock level, and you gain one Legendary Resistance. If you fail a saving throw, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Plague Doctor
entries: The pulse of life beats fast in dark, winding city streets all across Avestros. Millions of lives crammed into ramshackle homes and united in poverty— the city is a breeding ground for desperation and disease. However, in some districts, there are streets where none fall ill— areas of respite where the plague doctors operate.

These holy physicians are masters of medicine, running clinics across the nation that save countless lives. Some roam, following the grim footsteps of plague and curing those afflicted in its wake, others are conscripted in the nation's army, combating the infection and sickness that runs deadly in war. Many also work as midwives, educators, and city planners.

They use their divine powers to combat the invisible, bacterial horrors of the world, with gods such as Asclepius, Dian Cécht, Sekhmet, Serket, and Eir common among those worshiped by such clerics. Although loved and respected for their great powers of healing, many are wary of the plague doctors, for one with the power to battle necrosis and poison also has the power to wield it.

subclassFeature.name: Plague Medic
entries: You have proficiency with martial weapons and in the Medicine skill, and you have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition poisoned} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Humor Manipulation
entries: Your magic can manipulate the humors of the body, causing healing or harm. Once on your turn, you can use one of the following effects:

items.name: Respite
entries: When you cast a spell or use an item that restores hit points to one or more creatures, choose one target of that spell or item. That creature is also cured of one of the following conditions: {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition deafened}, or {@condition poisoned}.

items.name: Necrosis
entries: When you damage one or more creatures with a levelled spell or weapon attack, choose one creature damaged by that spell or attack. That creature takes an additional {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition poisoned} until the end of its next turn. The damage dealt by this feature increases by {@damage 1d4} at levels 5 ({@damage 2d4}), 11 ({@damage 3d4}), and 17 ({@damage 4d4}).

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Aura of Purification
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to create a sanctuary of purity and asepsis for those you choose.

As a bonus action, you present your holy symbol, and a sphere of cool, blue light emanates from you. The sphere is centered on you, has a 30-foot radius, and shines dim light. The sphere moves with you, and it lasts for 1 minute or until you are {@condition incapacitated} or die. Creatures of your choice in the sphere gain the following benefits:

items: It has immunity to poison damage and the {@condition poisoned} condition.
If it is suffering from a nonmagical illness, the symptoms of that illness are repressed.
It can add {@dice 1d6} to saving throws made to resist or end the {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition paralyzed}, and {@condition stunned} conditions.

subclassFeature.name: Psychosomatic Assault
entries: When you use the necrosis effect of your Humor Manipulation feature, you can also expend a spell slot. Instead of making a Constitution saving throw to resist the {@condition poisoned} condition, the target of your necrosis effect must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or suffer one of the following effects until the end of its next turn, depending on the level of the spell slot you expend:

subclassFeature.name: Divine Strike
entries: You gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Putrefaction
entries: When you use your Aura of Purification Channel Divinity, you choose to radiate a potent, magical toxin. Creatures that start their turn in the sphere take {@damage 5d8} poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: College of Battle

entries: To whom it may concern,

I was roused from my slumber AGAIN last night by the raucous union of cymbals, drums, and bugle. Once more, riff-raff spewing forth from the Bardic College of Battle disrupted the city's tranquil, evening peace. Let it be known that if these "musicians" trouble my sleep once more, I will confront them personally, and show them some damn manners.
Yours in great irritation,
To whom it may concern,

Scarcely had laid my aching head to rest when the ungodly ruckus of college musicians burst on to my street once more. I have no recourse left unto me other than violence. I will not be held accountable for my actions; I will club these damn ruffians about the head!!
Yours in righteous fury,
To whom it may concern,
I wish to withdraw my previous complaint. I'd also like to kindly request a doctor to attend to my quarters immediately, for I have had my baton lodged in my posterior.
Yours in humility,
entries.by: This can also be an array

entries: Bards of the College of Battle train for positions on the front lines. They are the trumpeters, drummers, and bagpipers of war—performers whose songs radiate over the chaos of battle to inspire hope and signal changes in strategy and fortune. Far from mere harbingers of combat, "Battle Bards" are capable, armoured warriors, wielding instruments of song as their instruments of war.

subclassFeature.name: Basic Training
entries: You have proficiency with Medium Armour. In addition, you can treat a musical instrument you are carrying as a simple melee weapon, which deals bludgeoning damage equal to your bardic inspiration die on a hit.

subclassFeature.name: War March
entries: As a bonus action, you can begin a War March—a performance of music and motion which lasts for 1 minute. While performing in this way, you can incorporate attacks and the Verbal and Somatic components of your Bardic spells into the War March, allowing you to synchronise spellcasting and song. The War March ends early if you are {@condition restrained}, or you choose to end it (no action required).

When you begin your War March, you and a number of creatures of your choice up to your proficiency bonus within 30 feet of you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + half your Bard level (rounded up).

In addition, while in your War March, when you cast a Bard spell with a casting time of one action, you can cast it as a bonus action instead. If you do, the only action you can take on that turn is the Attack action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest.

You can begin a War March a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest. If you have no use remaining, you can begin a War March by expending two uses of your Bardic Inspiration instead.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. In addition, you can replace one of those attacks with a use of your Bardic Inspiration.

subclassFeature.name: Inspiring Chorus
entries: While you are performing your War March, creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you gain a bonus equal to your Charisma modifier on their first attack roll, ability check, or saving throw each turn.

subclassFeature.name: The Unseen
entries: Unburdened by mortality, morality, and fear, ever rising and falling in the dark and hopeless places of the world, exists an idea. It is a gnawing concept; a thought as invisible and infectious as a virus. It is called The Unseen.

Followers of The Unseen answer not to a dark god or monstrosity. Instead, they draw power from an ideology, and a community of fellow believers. The Unseen is a philosophy of unity and destruction; a call to the downtrodden and unwanted to band together and set the world alight. Members of The Unseen operate in the shadows, an ever growing collective seeking the ruination of modern society. Under the cover of nightfall, ordinary men and women–teachers, doctors, beggars, and merchants, don masks and perform rituals to beckon in the coming chaos.

The motivations of individuals may vary wildly. Some believe the current rule of the world is corrupt and wicked, and seek to reverse the fortunes of the tyrannised and build a new order for the benefit of the people. Others seek personal power, eager to spread carnage and rise like smoke through its chaos. In all cases, The Unseen draw strength from one another, empowered by a vision of a new world. To the mighty and powerful, there is no threat more terrifying.

The Unseen is labelled as an anarchistic cult and outlawed in most empires, and membership is punishable by death. However, no matter the brutal retribution of the state, The Unseen seem to grow ever more numerous, harbingers of a new order that will rise from the ashes of the world they burn. If you dare dream of a better world, and are willing to do whatever it takes to bring it to bear, seek out The Unseen.

subclassFeature.name: Shared Malice
entries: When a creature you can see within 20 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction to choose a number of allied creatures within 20 feet of you up to your proficiency bonus, and draw on your collective willpower to impose a negative modifier to that attack roll, ability check, or saving throw equal to 1 + the number of creatures you chose. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Unseen Idealogue
entries: You know the spell {@spell charm person}, and can cast it a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Collective Knowledge
entries: You learn three additional Eldritch Invocations of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Thought Dominator
entries: You learn the spell {@spell dominate person}, and can cast it once per long rest without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Legion
entries: Your power is magnified when allies stand together. You generate an aura of power which extends in a 20-foot radius while conscious. You, and friendly creatures within the aura, gain a bonus to saving throws equal to the number of friendly creatures within 20 feet of you (maximum +5).

subclassFeature.name: School of Petrification
entries: Before advancements in magical understanding and experimentation ushered in the contemporary, academic age of spellcasters, disciplines of wizardry existed in a looser, flexible form. Few among these ancient traditions exist today, with one notable exception: The School of Petrification. As belligerent as a rock, this primal doctrine of magic resisted all attempts at innovation and is practised today by wizards across the world in much the same way it was practised millenia ago. Petrification wizards are famous for their labyrinthine, stunningly carved temples—structures of stark beauty and vibrant magic that runs through the stone like blood through veins. There is wisdom in the ancient ways, and wizards of this school understand that no matter how the people of the world evolve in philosophy and habit, the primal power of the earth remains unchangingly supreme.

subclassFeature.name: Fortification of Stone
entries: As a bonus action, you can you can fortify yourself or one willing creature you are touching with the endurance of stone for one minute, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}. While fortified in this way, if the target isn't wearing Heavy Armour, it can calculate its AC as 10 + your Intelligence modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use your Fortification of Stone a number of times equal your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Whispers of Stone
entries: You have proficiency with {@item mason's tools|PHB}. You also you learn the {@spell petrificus|DMSecretWeapon} cantrip and can add your Intelligence modifier to the damage dealt by it. It doesn't count your number of cantrips known.

In addition, over the course of a one hour ritual, you can cast the spell {@spell glyph of warding} without material components or expending a spell slot, but you must inscribe the glyph on a stone surface. You can perform this ritual twice, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Curse of Petrification
entries: When you cast the {@spell petrificus|DMSecretWeapon} cantrip, you can expend a spell slot as part of the casting. If you do, the target has disadvantage on their Constitution save made to avoid the effects of the spell. In addition, you can choose from one of the following effects to add to the spell as you cast it:

items: The target takes additional damage equal to 5 x the level of the spell slot expended.
You gain temporary hit points equal to 5 x the level of the spell slot expended.
You can target additional creatures with the spell equal to the level of the spell slot expended.
The target has a penalty to Dexterity saving throws equal to the 2 x the level of the spell slot expended until the end of its next turn.

The target's movement speed is reduced by an additional 5 feet x the level of the spell slot expended until the end of its next turn. If this effect reduces the target's movement to 0, it falls {@condition prone}.

subclassFeature.name: Gift of the Stone
entries: A creature under the effect of your Fortification of Stone feature also resists bludgeoning, slashing, and piercing damage, has advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws, and has tremorsense out to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Stoneshaper
entries: Over the course of a long rest, you can imbue a non-magical pebble with incredible power. The pebble gains the properties of any {@item ioun stone} of your choice. The pebble remains magical in this way until it is destroyed, or you use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Vigilante
entries: The world is dangerous. Every shadow hides thieves, murderers, devils, and monsters, lurking in wait to prey on the weak. Kings, generals, and priests speak of their power to protect from such evils, but you know they are just as cruel and oppressive as the monsters they claim to oppose. No matter where you look, the vulnerable are deceived, exploited, and thrown aside. In such a world, where corruption and greed rule, the only way to stand up for the innocent is to stand against the system.

You are a vigilante. You operate outside the law, governed by nothing but your own moral compass. You act in anonymity, living in the shadows and striking against wrongdoers. Noble folk call you a common criminal—a thug no better than the monsters you seek to destroy. To the evildoers you punish, you are a phantom—a nightmare of vengeance that haunts their every step. To the downtrodden, the helpless, and the desperate, you are a hero—a symbol of their discontent and righteous fury. Your methods may be frightening, perhaps even savage, but you act in the hope that when your work is done, and the darkness of night gives way to the delicate rays of dawn, the sun rises on a safer, virtuous world.

subclassFeature.name: One With Shadow
entries: Anonymity, stealth, and surprise are vital to your survival. You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured (such as by dim light, heavy rain, light smoke, or other such effects).

subclassFeature.name: Frightful Strike
entries: If you score a critical hit against a creature, or hit a creature with an attack roll while hidden from it, that creature is {@condition frightened} by you for the next minute. A creature can make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Chilling Presence
entries: You wield shadows as both a shield and a weapon, misdirecting and terrifying your enemies. If a creature is {@condition frightened} of you and cannot see you, it has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls and it moves cautiously, expending 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves.

subclassFeature.name: Street Tactics
entries: Hardened by brutal experience, you have learned there is no tactic too dirty to grant you an edge in battle. When you make a melee attack roll against a creature, you can choose to enhance that strike with a burst of sand, glass, or acidic fumes. If your attack hits, that creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or be {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Swift Vengeance
entries: Your retribution is swift and fierce against those who harm others. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against the attacking creature.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Fear
entries: Once per turn, when you take the attack action and hit a creature that is {@condition frightened} of you with an attack roll, that creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) to avoid being totally overcome with fear. On a failed save, the target is {@condition paralyzed} for as long as it is {@condition frightened} of you.

subclassFeature.name: Portal Knight
entries: Portal Knights are an elite order of warriors who blend martial virtuosity with conjuration magic— their most revered and mysterious power is the ability to summon portals. In battle, they wield this magic as unpredictable and deadly combatants, a legendary force of trickery and versatility. Their unique magical gifts serve Portal Knights well in many subtler facets of warfare and adventuring. Far from crude, brute warriors, they excel in the arts of infiltration, assassination, and espionage.

subclassFeature.name: Create Portal
entries: As a bonus action you can create two intangible, linked portals. They remain for 1 minute, or until you dismiss them as a bonus action, or you use this feature again. Choose two points that you can see within 60 feet of you. A circular portal, 10 feet in diameter, opens at each point. You cannot open a portal in a space occupied by another creature.

The portals are glowing rings that shed dim light in a 10-foot radius and float perpendicular to the ground. They are magically linked in space—each portal acts as a window that you can look, move, or pass objects through. A Large or smaller willing creature or an object that moves through a portal is teleported, exiting from the other portal's space as though the two portals were adjacent to one another.

Creatures within 5 feet of a portal can make melee attacks through it, striking at a target within 5 feet of the linked portal. Ammunition from a ranged weapon that passes through the portal's space is teleported, allowing ranged weapons to target creatures on the other side of the linked portal. Magical effects, such as the ranged attack roll from the {@spell fire bolt} cantrip or the damaging area of effect of a {@spell fireball} spell do not pass through the portals.
Huge or larger creatures and objects, creatures who do not wish to teleport, or creatures that are unable to teleport can move through a portal's space without teleporting to its counterpart.
Once a creature has teleported through a portal, it cannot teleport through a portal again until the start of its next turn.
You can create portals in this way a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Astral Gift
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}. Charisma is the spellcasting modifier you use for these cantrips. You can exchange one chosen cantrip for another applicable choice any time you gain a level in this subclass.

subclassFeature.name: Portal Guardian
entries: If a creature you can see attempts to teleport through a portal you have created, you can use a reaction to try and shut it out. The triggering creature must make a Charisma saving throw (DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, it cannot teleport through the portal until the start of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Energy of the Ethereal
entries: Whenever you teleport through a portal you have created, you gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Portal Trickster
entries: Your portals are now powerful enough to teleport unwilling creatures who pass through their space. An unwilling creature that enters a portal's space can attempt a Charisma saving throw (Save DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) to avoid being teleported. On a successful save, that creature moves through the portal's space without being teleported, and is immune to the effects of the portal until the start of its next turn. On a failed save, it is teleported.

subclassFeature.name: Portal Warrior
entries: You have advantage on attack rolls you make through a portal, and your attacks made through portals deal additional damage equal to your Charisma modifier on a hit. In addition, attack rolls made against you through your portals have disadvantage.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Nine Hells
entries: Forged in fire and desperation, far from the golden skies and stifling tranquility of the higher planes, warriors battle endlessly for the fate of all realms. Devils, demons, and other unimaginable creatures run rampant across the underworlds, each faction a world-devouring force, like a great colossal hydra, ready to conquer all if not for the interference of each other.

In this eternal battleground, some warriors find meaning. Those who take the Oath of the Nine Hells pledge themselves to the underworld, wielding the strength of devils. Some do this for selfish reasons, eager to harness the fiery power of hell, while others see it as the lesser of two evils, fighting fire with hellfire. In all cases, Oath of the Nine Hells Paladins are ferocious, brave, and blessed with devilish ambition and cunning. They despise demons, recognising the threat they pose to the entire multiverse, and channel infernal magic to utterly incinerate any foe who stands in their way.

entries.name: Tenets of the Nine Hells
entries: {@b Ambition.} It is every creature's duty to seek power, be it for the good of others, or only themselves.
{@b Hierarchy.} The universe spins around a static pillar of ultimate authority. There will always be a top and a bottom of society, and only those too weak to climb it complain.
{@b Law.} The word of the law is paramount and must be upheld. Without it, chaos reigns.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain the following oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

entries.caption: Oath of the Nine Hells Spells

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

items.name: Hellish Strike
entries: As a bonus action, you imbue a weapon you are holding with the living inferno of the nine hells. The next time you make an attack roll against a creature with that weapon within the next minute, the weapon lets loose a burst of unholy flame, and the target takes additional fire damage equal to 10 + your Paladin level (whether the attack hits or misses).

items.name: Turn Fiend
entries: As an action, you present your holy symbol and utter a ferocious battlecry. Each Fiend that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. Creatures that are the Fiend (Demon) type or are of a CR or Level lower than your paladin level have disadvantage on this Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the {@action Dash} action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the {@action Dodge} action.

subclassFeature.name: Devilish Aura
entries: You radiate an aura of spiteful, living fire magic. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you take an additional {@damage 1d4} fire damage when hit by a weapon attack.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Hellish Gifts
entries: You are immune to fire damage and the {@condition frightened} condition.

In addition, you learn one Eldritch Invocation of your choice from the Warlock class. You must still meet the prerequisites to learn it (if any). You can swap the Eldritch Invocation you gained from this feature for another by performing a 1 hour ritual. Once you perform this ritual, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Infernal Transformation
entries: As an action on your turn, you can cast the {@spell shapechange} spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the creature you shapechange into must be a Fiend (Devil).
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Infinite Heavens
entries: Oath of the Infinite Heavens is a Celestial seasoning of the Oath of the Nine Hells subclass.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain the following oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

entries.caption: Oath of the Infinite Heavens Spells

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

items.name: Divine Strike
entries: As a bonus action, you imbue a weapon you are holding with the burning radiance of the nine hells. The next time you make an attack roll against a creature with that weapon within the next minute, the weapon lets loose a burst of divine light, and the target takes additional radiant damage equal to 10 + your Paladin level (whether the attack hits or misses).

items.name: Turn Fiend
entries: As an action, you present your holy symbol and utter a ferocious battlecry. Each Fiend that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. Creatures that are the Fiend (Devil) type or are of a CR or Level lower than your paladin level have disadvantage on this Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the {@action Dash} action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the {@action Dodge} action.

subclassFeature.name: Smiting Aura
entries: You radiate an aura of vengeful, radiant magic. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you take an additional {@damage 1d4} radiant damage when hit by a weapon attack.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Gifts
entries: You are immune to radiant damage and the {@condition charmed} condition, and you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed.

subclassFeature.name: Holy Transformation
entries: As an action on your turn, you can cast the {@spell shapechange} spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the creature you shapechange into must be a Celestial.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Endless Abyss
entries: Oath of the Endless Abyss is a Demonic seasoning of the Oath of the Nine Hells subclass

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain the following oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

entries.caption: Oath of the Endless Abyss Spells

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

items.name: Abyssal Strike
entries: As a bonus action, you imbue a weapon you are holding with the roiling fury of the abyss. The next time you make an attack roll against a creature with that weapon within the next minute, the weapon lets loose a burst of clawing shadow, and the target takes additional necrotic damage equal to 10 + your Paladin level (whether the attack hits or misses).

items.name: Terrorize
entries: As an action, you present your holy symbol and utter a ferocious battlecry. Each Humanoid that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the {@action Dash} action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the {@action Dodge} action.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Aura
entries: You radiate an aura of chaotic, cruel magic. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you take an additional {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage when hit by a weapon attack.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Demonic Gifts
entries: You are immune to necrotic damage and the {@condition frightened} condition.

In addition, you learn one Eldritch Invocation of your choice from the Warlock class. You must still meet the prerequisites to learn it (if any). You can swap the Eldritch Invocation you gained from this feature for another by performing a 1 hour ritual. Once you perform this ritual, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Abyssal Transformation
entries: As an action on your turn, you can cast the {@spell shapechange} spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the creature you shapechange into must be a Fiend (Demon).
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Death Caller
entries: Every living person likes to dance, but the dead love it. Death Caller bards are magical performers with the power to commune with the departed—weaving music so vibrant it warms lost spirits, and invites them to move within the corporeal world, for a time. They are often seen performing at funerals, or memorial services in remembrance of terrible battles and bloodshed. But art with the power to move the dead can have terrible effects on the living.

Death Callers are widely respected, but rarely welcomed, with a repertoire of terrifying dirges and murder ballads that falls far from the breezy folk songs of popular traveling minstrels and troubadours. The magic such music spins is cruel and lethal if turned to nefarious ends, and many tales tell of evil Death Callers spreading dancing plagues and deadly fevers through villages. Armed with naught but a haunting, dissonant, irresistible melody, they compel victims to dance in a desperate frenzy until they die on their aching feet... and then compel their corpses to dance still further.

subclassFeature.name: Dirge Dancer
entries: As an action, you can begin a magical performance of death, which lasts for one minute or until you end it as a bonus action. As part of the action when you begin this performance, and as a bonus action on subsequent turns, you can choose one creature of your choice that can hear you within 30 feet as the focus of your magical performance. That target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn. Undead creatures have disadvantage on this saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Death Rattler
entries: Creatures {@condition frightened} of you have disadvantage on saving throws while you're within 30 feet of them and you aren't {@condition incapacitated}.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Guidance
entries: You are guided by the spirits of those who have died. You learn the {@spell guidance} cantrip or one cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric}.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Caller
entries: You learn the spells {@spell animate dead}, {@spell phantom steed}, {@spell revivify}, and {@spell speak with dead}, and you can cast them without expending a spell slot by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration instead. If you do, the spell's casting time becomes 1 action. Once you cast a spell in this way, you cannot cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Dance of Death
entries: You learn the spell {@spell Otto's irresistible dance|PHB|irresistible dance}. When you cast it, a target affected by the spell takes {@damage 4d10} necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns

subclassFeature.name: Spell Rager
entries: The fury of a Spell Rager is unlike that of any other warrior. Rather than the chaotic, unordered mind of sizzling aggression typical of a barbarian, the spell rager's Rage ushers in absolute mental focus and magical connection to the energies of the earth. As such, they are the only known path of barbarians able to augment their destructive fury with spellcasting.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Your fury ignites your soul with magic, granting you the ability to cast spells. You can concentrate on spells and cast spells while raging.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You learn three cantrips: {@spell thaumaturgy} and two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}. You learn another druid cantrip of your choice at 10th level. By meditating over the course of a long rest, you can change one chosen cantrip to another from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}.

entries.name: Raging Magic
entries: You have a number of Raging Magic Points equal to twice your Rage Damage bonus. You can spend these points to cast spells from your Raging Magic feature, and you regain all expended Raging Magic Points upon finishing a long rest.
You learn spells at the barbarian levels listed:

Any time you gain a Barbarian level, you can swap out one spell from the Subclass Spell table for a spell from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid} of the same level from the abjuration or transmutation school of magic.

entries.name: Spellcasting Modifier
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your barbarian spells. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a barbarian spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Recovery
entries: Over the course of a short rest, you can expend a single use of your Rage to regain a number of expended Raging Magic Points equal to your Barbarian level divided by 3 (rounded down).
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Ignition
entries: When you enter your Rage as a bonus action, you can cast one spell you know with a casting time of 1 action as a part of that same bonus action. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Frenzy
entries: When you use an action to cast a spell while raging, you can use a bonus action that turn to make a single weapon attack. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Magical Resistance
entries: You resist damage from spells, and you gain a bonus to saving throws made to resist the effects of spells equal to your Rage damage bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Striker
entries: You can add your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage rolls of your weapon attacks that use Strength while Raging.

subclassFeature.name: Primordial Soul
entries: The churning, writhing power of the elements bubbles in your veins. Be it by blood, bond, or gift, your body harbours the power of primordials — ancient incarnations of the raw, natural magic of the multiverse

subclassFeature.name: Primordial Ancestry
entries: Your primordial lineage grants you power. You gain one of the following elemental boons of your choice. When you finish a long rest, you can change your choice. Your current elemental boon also impacts the abilities you receive at later levels.

items.name: Earth
entries: Your skin is as hardy and durable as stone. Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your Sorcerer level. In addition, while you aren't wearing armour, you can calculate your AC as 12+ your Constitution modifier.

items.name: Water
entries: You gain a swim speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe underwater. In addition, the first time you hit a creature with a spell attack roll each turn, you can push that creature up to 15 feet away from you.

items.name: Fire
entries: You resist cold damage. In addition, when you cast a spell that deals acid, cold, lightning, poison, or thunder damage, you can change the damage type of that spell to fire damage. Finally, spells you cast that deal fire damage ignore damage resistance.

items.name: Air
entries: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet and your AC increases by 1 while you aren't wearing medium or heavy armour. In addition, whenever you cast a spell that targets only yourself, or you take the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} action, you gain a fly speed equal to your walking speed until the end of the turn. If you end that turn in the air, you fall.

subclassFeature.name: Primordial Bonds
entries: You gain proficiency in two of the following skills, and whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Charisma check even if it normally uses a different ability: {@skill Animal Handling}, {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, {@skill Religion}, {@skill Survival}.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Sorcery
entries: When you use a bonus action to convert a spell slot into sorcery points, you can cast a cantrip as part of that same bonus action.
In addition, the elemental boon you choose for your Primordial Ancestry feature confers one additional benefit.

items.name: Earth
entries: Whenever you fail a Strength or Constitution saving throw, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll that save at advantage. You must use the new result.

items.name: Water
entries: As a reaction when hit by an attack roll, you can spend 1 sorcery point to conjure a shield of ice to protect yourself. You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Charisma modifier against that attack, potentially turning a hit into a miss. The ice then shatters, dealing {@damage 1d8} cold damage to the attacker if they are within 5 feet of you.

items.name: Fire
entries: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you in a jet of flame. When you do, you can choose to deal {@damage 1d10} fire damage to all creatures within 10 feet of the space you teleported from.

items.name: Air
entries: As a bonus action, you can spend 1 sorcery point to take the {@action Dash} action and the {@action Disengage} action.

subclassFeature.name: Primordial Ally
entries: You can cast the spell {@spell conjure elemental} without a spell slot or components. Once you do so, you cannot cast it again using this feature until you finish a long rest. When you cast {@spell conjure elemental} using this feature, it does not require {@status concentration}, and lasts for the full duration.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Transformation
entries: At the start of your turn, you can spend 5 sorcery points to alter your body, becoming one with your elemental ancestors. This transformation lasts for 1 minute, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}. The benefits you gain depend on the elemental boon you have chosen for your Primordial Ancestry feature.

items.name: Earth
entries: You have tremorsense out to 30 feet, and a burrow speed equal to your walking speed. When you burrow, you don't disturb the material you move through. You take {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage if you end your turn inside the ground while burrowing.

items.name: Water
entries: When a creature starts its turn within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction attempt to ensnare that creature in a coiling vortex of conjured water. That creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be {@condition incapacitated} until the start of your next turn. Creatures that are Large or smaller have disadvantage on this save.

items.name: Fire
entries: You are immune to cold damage. In addition, if you would take fire damage, such as from the spell {@spell fireball}, you instead gain temporary hit points equal to the damage you would have taken.

items.name: Air
entries: When you take the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} action, or cast a spell that targets only yourself, you can turn {@condition invisible} until the end of your next turn. In addition, while {@condition invisible}, you resist bludgeoning, slashing, and piercing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Skyrider
entries: As one with the wind, skyriders are a legendary conclave of rangers that roam the globe, defending the birds and beasts of the sky. As you grow, your connection with the primordial energy of air enhances your movement, magic, and combat prowess with the bite, speed, and untethered fury of a hurricane. Skyriders are renowned for their powers of flight, and tales of a lone, skyborne warrior defending innocents from pirates and dragons are found in cultures across the multiverse.

subclassFeature.name: Blade of the North Wind
entries: The bitter chill and whirling gusts of the north wind empowers your strikes. Once per turn, on your turn, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll, you can enhance that strike with one of the following effects:

items.name: Concussive Blast
entries: You move the target 10 feet directly towards or away from you.

items.name: Fleet Foot
entries: You can take the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} action as a bonus action this turn.

items.name: Whirling Eddies
entries: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or have disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Skyrider Magic
entries: You learn the {@spell true strike} cantrip, or another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Druid or Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer;Druid}. At the end of a short or long rest, you can swap your chosen cantrip for another applicable choice.

You also learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Skyrider Spells table. Each spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Heart of the West Wind
entries: The gifts of the west wind amplify your every step with dancing, rising magic. At the start of your turn, you can choose to gain a fly speed equal to walking speed for 10 minutes. In addition, if you are mounted, your mount shares your fly speed. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Breath of the East Wind
entries: The magic of the east wind shimmers through your every strike. When you use your Blade of the North Wind feature, you can also choose from the following options:

items.name: Teleport
entries: Expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher. You and up to 5 willing creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

items.name: Swift Casting
entries: Expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher. You can cast a cantrip with the casting time of 1 action using your bonus action this turn.

items.name: Whirlwind
entries: You can take the {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action this turn. If you are mounted, your mount also gains the benefits of the {@action Dodge} action until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Shield of the South Wind
entries: The blessing of the south wind guards you from harm. You resist bludgeoning, slashing, and piecing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Machines
entries: Oft labeled as iconoclasts and mavericks, Druids of the Circle of Machines are fascinated with the malleable essence of the natural world, and the myriad of shapes it can take. A tree is a tree, but in the paws of a beaver it becomes a dam—bowerbirds build structures for courtship, and octopi crack and customise coconuts for shelter. Druids of this order believe the essence of the natural world is giving, not immutable. The raw materials of the earth and sky are sacred, no matter the shape they are born with, or the form they become. Guided by this philosophy, druids of this circle are the ultimate artisans of creation, crafting the magical from the mundane.

The creations of such druids are prized - exquisitely crafted magical objects that enhance the abilities of the wielder. It's easy to spot a village home to a circle of machines druid; every hunter wields a spear blessed with the sting of a wasp and every scout carries an eyepiece granting the sight of a hawk. Druids of this order even pass their own magic into automaton creations, blessing crafted creatures with a brief breath of life. Mavericks among druids they may be, but none question the communal benefit of a kindly circle of machines druid, and none doubt the danger of an angered one.

subclassFeature.name: Circle Spells
entries: When you join this circle, you gain knowledge of arcane secrets, granting access to spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Circle of Machines spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.
Your study also grants you proficiency with two artisan's tools of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Clockwork Companion
entries: Over the course of a long rest, you can construct a {@creature Clockwork Companion|DMSecretWeapon}. Once constructed, you can animate it for up to 1 hour by expanding a use of your Wild Shape (no action required). While unanimated, the companion folds into a tiny sphere that can be carried. Once you have crafted a {@creature Clockwork Companion|DMSecretWeapon}, you cannot create another unless your current one is destroyed, or you disassemble it to craft a new one over the course of a long rest.

The animated {@creature Clockwork Companion|DMSecretWeapon} is friendly to you and your companions and obeys your commands. See this creature's game statistics in the {@creature Clockwork Companion|DMSecretWeapon} stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.

You determine the construct's appearance and size (Tiny or Small) when you build it. {@creature Clockwork Companion|DMSecretWeapon} are magical - some fly with the aid of stunningly crafted, articulated wings, others through magic.

In combat, the companion shares your initiative count, but takes its turn immediately after yours. The only action it takes on its turn is the {@action Dodge} action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are {@condition incapacitated}, the companion can take any action of its choice, not just {@action Dodge}.

subclassFeature.name: Clockwork Enhancements
entries: Over the course of a long rest, you can create a number of clockwork enhancements equal to your Proficiency Bonus. These are magic items that require attunement. You determine their appearance - some druids craft exquisite, complex magical contraptions, others simple, magically infused rings that impart power to their wearer. Blessed with eager but fleeting nature magic, a willing creature can attune to one by focusing on it for 1 minute. These magic items disintegrate when you finish your next long rest.

When you craft your clockwork enhancements, choose from the options in your Clockwork Enhancements table. Some of the enhancements reference Proficiency Bonus (P.B.), in these cases, use your proficiency bonus, not the Proficiency Bonus of the creature attuned to the item.

entries.caption: Clockwork Enhancements
rows: You have a +P.B. bonus to initiative rolls
You have darkvision out to 120 feet
Once per turn, you can jump up to 30 feet using only 10 feet of movement
Your walking speed increases by 20 feet
Choose one skill when you attune to this item. You have a +P.B. bonus to any checks using that skill
You have a bonus to attack and damage rolls equal to half P.B. (rounded down)
You have a swim speed equal to your walking speed
You have a climb speed equal to your walking speed

subclassFeature.name: Clockwork Casting
entries: When you animate your {@creature Clockwork Companion|DMSecretWeapon}, choose one 1st level spell you can cast. Your companion can cast that spell once without a spell slot while animated for the next hour. You can expend a 1st-level spell slot (no action required) to allow it to cast that spell again.

subclassFeature.name: Mechanist's Blessing
entries: You gain one additional attunement slot, but this attunement slot can only be used to attune to one of your Clockwork Enhancements.

subclassFeature.name: Clockwork Masterwork
entries: The following options are added to your Clockwork Enhancements table:

rows: You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed
You have a bonus to saving throws rolls equal to half P.B. (rounded down)
You have tremorsense out to 30 feet
While you aren't wearing heavy armour, you have a bonus to your AC equal to half P.B. (rounded down)
Your spell save DC increases by 1

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Radiant Soul
entries: Across all times and cultures, warriors have fought and died in the name of the gods. There are few, however, who can truly claim to be chosen by them. Monks of the Radiant Soul infuse their blistering agility and technique with the divine power of the Higher Planes. Some such warriors are chosen from birth, while others find relationships with Higher Beings through deep, transcendent meditation. In all cases, they are fearsome in battle, fortified and bolstered by the holy power of the gods.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Shelter
entries: Once per turn, when you deal damage to a creature with an unarmed strike or Monk weapon, you can shield yourself in an aura of divine light. If you do, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Retribution
entries: Once per turn, if a creature within 60 feet of you hits you with an attack while you have temporary hit points, you can use a reaction to retaliate with a bolt of fiery radiance. Choose one or more of the following effects:

items: That creature takes radiant damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.
Expend 1 Ki point, your AC increases by an amount equal to your Wisdom modifier, potentially turning a hit into a miss. This AC increase lasts until the end of this turn.
Expend 2 Ki points, that creature is {@condition Blinded} until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Shining Soul
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Religion} and {@skill Nature} skills, and when you make an ability check using either skill, you can make it as a Wisdom check, rather than Intelligence.

subclassFeature.name: Transcendent Wings
entries: While you have temporary hit points, you have a fly speed equal to your walking speed, and you can hover.

subclassFeature.name: Shared Blessing
entries: Once per turn, when you gain Temporary Hit Points, you can choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. They gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

subclassFeature.name: Rapturous Surge
entries: On your turn, when you use your Divine Shelter feature, you can forgo gaining Temporary Hit Points to take an additional bonus action this turn instead. Once you use this feature, it cannot be used again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Eternal Blessing
entries: When you would gain Temporary Hit Points, you gain that many plus your Wisdom Modifier instead.
While you have Temporary Hit Points, you can add your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Darkness Domain
entries: It is curious how often the laws of the physical world parallel those of the magical. Just as every action has its equal and opposite force, so too does every faith, every god, every instance of magic. Clerics who serve deities of darkness represent the balance to those who worship the gods of light. While others see darkness as terrifying - a blinding shadow of death and nothingness, clerics of this domain see darkness as the truest form of the universe. Once, all things were darkness. One day, they will be again.

Such clerics have a saying: "even followers of the brightest light cast shadows". They often reject the rigid dogma of traditional religious orders, seeing them as inflexible and open to corruption. Typically, clerics of this domain are neutral and chaotic-good in alignment, and almost never lawful. They are at home in the darkness and do not fear it, though they respect its power. They seek to protect allies from the great terrors that dwell in the shadows, and weild its horror as a weapon against foes.

subclassFeature.name: Priest of Darkness
entries: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armour. Additionally, you gain darkvision out to a range of 30 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Ally of Shadow
entries: You resist bludgeoning, slashing, and piercing damage from nonmagical, nonsilvered weapons while in darkness. When you start your turn in darkness, your movement speed increases by 10 feet until the end of that turn.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Aura of Darkness
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to cast the spell {@spell darkness} without expending a spell slot and without material components. When you cast it in this way, it does not require {@status concentration} and lasts for the full duration or until you choose to end it as a bonus action. Additionally, the point you choose for the darkness to emenate from must be an object you are wearing or carrying, and you can see through the magical darkness created by this effect.
On the turn you use this Channel Divinity, you can cast one Cleric cantrip or make a single weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclassFeature.name: Blessing of the Shadows
entries: If you cast a spell with a spell slot of 1st level or higher that targets a creature, you can infuse an additional fragment of divine power into that spell. Choose one bonus effect from the following list to add to that spell's effect as you cast it:

items: The target can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a range of 30 feet for the next minute.
The target gains a resistance to radiant and necrotic damage for the next minute.
The target takes {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d8} when you reach 10th level.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. If the spell targets multiple creatures, you can choose any number of them to affect, expending a use of this ability for each one.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Endless Darkness
entries: When you cast the spell {@spell darkness} it doesn't require {@status concentration} and its radius increases to 30 feet. Additionally, allied creatures within magical darkness that you create share your damage resistances.

subclassFeature.name: Wayfinder
entries: In a sprawling, infinite multiverse, there are infinite sprawling paths. Wayfinders are the conclave of rangers dedicated to setting out into the unknown, charting the first maps and breaching the boundaries of untouched planes of existence.

Such rangers are true explorers, ever seeking new magic, knowledge, and cultures across the multiverse. A wayfinder must truly be ready for anything, for stepping into the unknown means risking horrors and dangers as yet unimagined. Adaptability and cunning are at the heart of the conclave; without them, no ranger will last long in the uncharted depths of wild and mysterious lands. Despite the dangers, heroes of this conclave are drawn ever onward by the spirit of adventure. To the wayfinder, there is no path more tempting than the path yet untravelled.

subclassFeature.name: Wayfinder Magic
entries: You learn the {@spell guidance} cantrip if you don't already know it. You also learn an additional spell of 1st level or higher when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Wayfinder Spells table. Each spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

subclassFeature.name: Wayfinder's Preparation
entries: When you finish a long rest, you can choose one damage type from among acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, radiant, or thunder. You resist that damage type until you use this feature again.
Additionally, the first time each turn you deal damage to a creature marked by your {@spell hunter's mark}, that creature takes an additional {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen damage type.

subclassFeature.name: Virtuosic Explorer
entries: You know the spell {@spell comprehend languages}, and can cast it without a spell slot or components, and you have proficiency in the {@skill Survival} skill or one other skill of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Branching Magic
entries: While concentrating on a spell from your Wayfinder Magic table, you can cast {@spell hunter's mark} using a spell slot of 2nd level or above. When you do, it does not require {@status concentration}, and it lasts for the duration or until the spell you are currently concentrating on ends.

subclassFeature.name: Wayfinder's Instinct
entries: Your honed instincts give you a split second advantage when facing danger. When you roll for initiative or for a saving throw, you can give yourself and creatures of your choice within 5 feet that make the same check or saving throw a bonus to that roll equal to your Wisdom modifier.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Dimension Hopper
entries: When you take damage or cast {@spell hunter's mark}, you can use a reaction to teleport up to 90 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can make a single weapon attack before or after you teleport as part of the same reaction. You can use this feature once. You regain a use of it upon finishing a short or long rest, or upon expending a spell slot of 3rd level or higher (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: The Unspeakable
entries: Deep beneath the crust of the material plane, the end of the world slumbers. In dreamless sleep waits a monstrosity with power not to rival Gods, but devour them. The true name of the creature is lost to time, but its strength persists. Those who syphon this strength refer to the creature as the Unspeakable.

Warlocks of the Unspeakable are beings infused with primal fury and might, who draw magical power from a sleeping monstrosity. Such power is not meant for mortal beings, and those who channel it heedlessly undergo painful transformations; the bones thicken like aged oak trunks, the skin hardens and cracks like volcanic rock, and the voice drops and rasps like grinding stone. The reward is primal magic pulled from an infinite well of power.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Unspeakable lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

subclassFeature.name: Guard of the Unspeakable
entries: Your connection to the Unspeakable lets you draw upon its mighty fortitude, hardening your flesh against harm. While you are not wearing any armour, your armour class equals 10 + your Constitution modifier + your Charisma modifier. If you have proficiency with shields, a shield's benefit applies as normal.

subclassFeature.name: Strength of the Unspeakable
entries: The incalculable strength of the Unspeakable courses through your body, grantinting you the following benefits:

items: You can add your Charisma modifier to Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
When you score a critical hit against a creature, that creature falls {@condition prone}.

Once per turn, when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal additional force damage to that target equal to your Proficiency Bonus, or you can move it 5 feet to an unoccupied space.

subclassFeature.name: Roar of the Unspeakable
entries: As an action, you can let out a deafening, monstrous cry, drawing breath from the lungs of the Unspeakable. Creatures of your choice within 60 feet that can hear you make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your Proficiency Bonus).

Creatures who succeed have disadvantage on attack rolls against you until the end of your next turn. Creature's who fail are {@condition frightened} of you for the next minute, and suffer additional penalties depending on the result of their saving throw:

items: A result of 5 or more below the save DC: the creature takes {@damage 2d10} psychic damage.
A result of 10 or more below the DC: the creature is {@condition Stunned} until the end of its next turn.
A result of 15 or more below DC: the creature falls to 0 hit points.
A result of 20 or more below DC: the creature dies.

entries: A creature {@condition frightened} by this effect can repeat the Wisdom save at the end of each of its turns, ending the {@condition frightened} condition on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Offering to the Unspeakable
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll on your turn, you can banish the target to the belly of your patron, slumbering deep in the centre of the world. The target vanishes as it is hurled into the gut of the Unspeakable. While there, it is {@condition blinded}, {@condition restrained}, {@condition incapacitated}, and takes {@damage 16d6} acid damage at the start of its turn. At the end of your next turn it reapers in the space it left, covered in stinking bile and blistering slime.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Tranquility
entries: The primal force of Rage is as unwieldy as it is powerful. Warriors who harness it are called barbarians, known for their brutal savagery and blinding fury in battle. In you however, Rage is no master— it is a force under your command. It steadies your mind and enhances your senses.
