That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d8} poison damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d8} at level 5, {@damage 3d8} at level 11, and {@damage 4d8} at level 17. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries.name: Kinetic
entries: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and your jump distance is increased by a number of feet equal to your Constitution modifier. In addition, you can take the {@action Dash}, {@action Dodge}, or {@action Disengage} action as a bonus action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short rest.

entries.name: Human Lineage
entries: You gain proficiency in one skill and one tool of your choice, and you speak one additional language you and your GM agree is appropriate for your character.

entries.name: High Elf Lineage
entries: You know one cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Wizard spell list|spells|class=Wizard}. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting modifier for this spell (choose when you select this race).

entries.name: Halfling Lineage
entries: When you roll a 1 on the d20 for an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

entries.name: Gnome Lineage
entries: If you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you can reroll that saving throw. You must use the new roll. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest.

entries.name: Tiefling Lineage
entries: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: {@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Persuasion}, or {@skill Religion}.
You have a resistance to fire damage.

entries.name: Dwarf Lineage
entries: You have advantage on saving throws to avoid the harmful effects of poisons, and you have a resistance to poison damage.

entries.name: Dragonborn Lineage
entries: You have a tough, scaly hide. When you aren't wearing armour, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier (a shield's benefits apply as normal).

When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can deal additional damage equal to twice your proficiency bonus. This additional damage is acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage (choose when you select this race). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest.

entries.name: Centaur Lineage
entries: You have hooves, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you hit with them, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier bludgeoning damage, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.

entries.name: Frost Gnome Lineage
entries: You resist cold damage.

In addition, whenever you cast a spell that deals acid, fire, lightning, or poison damage, you can change the damage type of that spell to cold. You know the {@spell fire bolt} cantrip. In addition, you always have the {@spell burning hands} spell prepared and can cast it without a spell slot a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a long rest. You can also use any spell slots you have to cast the spell.

entries.name: Shadow Gnome Lineage
entries: The range of your darkvision increases to 120 feet, and you can take the {@action Hide} action while only lightly obscured by dim light or shadow. You know the {@spell minor illusion} cantrip. In addition, you always have the {@spell pass without trace} spell prepared and can cast it without a spell slot once per long rest. You can also use any spell slots you have to cast the spell.

entries.name: Woodland Dryad Lineage
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Nature} skill.

Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell cure wounds} spell with this trait. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast {@spell enhance ability} with this trait. Once you cast {@spell cure wounds} or {@spell enhance ability} with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this species).

entries.name: Desert Dryad Lineage
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Stealth} skill.

Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell silent image} spell with this trait. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast {@spell heat metal} with this trait. Once you cast {@spell silent image} or {@spell heat metal} with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this species).

entries.name: Coastline Dryad Lineage
entries: You have a swim speed equal to your walking speed.

Starting at 3rd level, you can cast the {@spell fog cloud} spell with this trait. Starting at 5th level, you can also cast {@spell lesser restoration} with this trait. Once you cast {@spell fog cloud} or {@spell lesser restoration} with this trait, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast either of those spells using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this species).

entries.name: Class S
entries: Your Strength score increases by 2, as does your maximum for that score.

Additionally, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift, and you can grapple and shove creatures that are no more than two sizes larger than you.

walk.condition: Upir crawling speed is equal to your walking speed

entries.name: Class D
entries: Your Dexterity score increases by 2, as does your maximum for that score.
Additionally, your base walking speed increases by 5 feet, and you have a climbing and crawling speed equal to your walking speed.

entries.name: Class C
entries: Your Constitution score increases by 2, as does your maximum for that score.
Additionally, you are immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition, and you have resistance to poison damage.

entries.name: Class I
entries: Your Intelligence score increases by 2, as does your maximum for that score.
Additionally, you are immune to any magical effect that aims to sense your emotions or read your thoughts, and you are immune to the {@condition charmed} condition.

entries.name: Class W
entries: Your Wisdom score increases by 2, as does your maximum for that score.
Additionally, you are immune to the {@condition frightened} condition and you have advantage on ability checks made to peacefully interact with Beasts.

entries.name: Class Z
entries: Your Charisma score increases by 2, as does your maximum for that score.

Additionally, if you fail a Charisma ({@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, or {@skill Persuasion}) check, or Charisma saving throw, you may choose to reroll, but you must use the new roll. If the new roll turns failure into success, you cannot use this trait again until you finish a short or long rest.

raceFluff.name: Castanoot
entries: Castanoot are a race of small, fey creatures native to the feywild who are notable for their thick, spined shells. An ancient and deeply solitary peoples, Castanoot are famously distrustful of outsiders and seek to avoid interaction with others if they can. However, they have been known to trade and associate with other races on occasion. Trust is hard earned however, and easily lost. Castanoot have a strong distrust of Fairies for an insult dealt unto them long ago that none remember, aside from the fact it came from the tongue of a Fairy.

Although Castanoot can burrow, they typically live in woodland areas, building homes inside trees. They age rapidly from birth, reaching adulthood in just 5 years, and then go on to live for around a century.

items.name: Caescean
entries: Caescean Castanoot are the most traditionally focused of all Castanoot races. They live in tight knit, matriarchal societies on lands claimed long ago. They take great pride in their heritage, and resist change fiercely.

items.name: Dentata
entries: The Dentata Castanoot are a warrior people. They find great joy in hunting as a tribe and combative sports. To the Dentata, a Castanoot's shell is of the utmost importance, and many hours each day are devoted to the cleaning, decoration and preservation of one's shell. It is their first line of defence, and most trusted weapon.

items.name: Sativan
entries: The Sativan Castanoot are a nomadic people who long ago cast off their spiky shells and the traditions of the old ways in favour of physical and social mobility. They shirk the isolationist philosophies of other Castanoot and traverse the feywild, delighting in meeting new creatures. They are famous for living in open, polyamerous societies, although finding two Sativan committed exclusively to one another is not uncommon.

raceFluff.name: Zu-Zoi
entries: The Zu-Zoi are a jungle dwelling species of sentient, insectoid humanoids. Once a slave-race, Zu-Zoi are intensely aggressive and territorial, having learned to fear and despise outsiders.

They trade with other species only as a necessity, as they lack the resources and knowledge to produce complex mechanical or magical objects. However, they are not primitive. Zu-Zoi are beyond virtuosic in the fields of agriculture, survivalism and combat.
It's said Zu-Zoi can turn a barren wasteland to a thriving, luscious forest in a single generation.
There are two primary subraces which co-exist peacefully: the {@race Zu-Zoi (Zat)|DMSecretWeapon|Zu-Zoi-Zat} and {@race Zu-Zoi (Zen)|DMSecretWeapon|Zu-Zoi-Zen}.

raceFluff.name: Feytroll
entries: Feytroll are a race of small, solitary creatures native to the forests of the material plane. Zealous collectors, most Feytroll adore shiny objects, regardless of their financial worth, and use them to decorate their nests and clothing. Usually fearful of larger creatures, Feytroll typically protect themselves with illusion magic, choosing to hide away rather than engage with other beings. Brave or curious Feytroll who seek to explore the world and socialise are not unheard of, however.

All Feytroll feel a deep connection with the sun and moon, with many choosing to actively worship the heavenly spheres. Names such as Solus, Dusk, Dawn, Luna, Fireborn, Brightborn, Wolfmoon, and Helios are common among Feytroll.

raceFluff.name: Lostanta
entries: Lostanta are fallen humans native to the Ethereal Plane. Originally a nation of proud and ambitious people, the Lostanta sought to replicate the long life of elves, infusing themselves with youth, power and beauty beyond their natural limitations.

In punishment for transgressions against their true nature, they were banished from the material plane, left in a timeless void where they barely age or tire. Some have found ways back to their ancient home, and wander the material plane mourning that which their people left behind in pursuit of immortality.

raceFluff.name: Cyclod
entries: The Cyclod are a reclusive race of fey, distant descendants of the mighty Titans. Easily identifiable by the single, large eye in the center of their head and their large tusks, their imposing appearance and scarcity have led to Cyclods being vilified in many cultures as bestial monsters that consume humanoid flesh.

In actuality, they are a gentle and timid people, forming small, nomadic communities of roughly a dozen families who wander the mountains of the material plane. No two Cyclods share the same colouration of skin, each born with their own unique coloration and patterns. Cyclod elders traditionally interpret these patterns to predict a newborn's future.

raceFluff.name: Clagborne Lineage
entries: A peculiar species of subterranean magical ooze, Clagborne are a deeply mysterious race. Unique in that they are fully amorphous and brainless until they find a host, almost nothing is known of a Clagborne's early life or origin, as even they remember nothing of it.

What is known is that these brainless oozes slime their way through caverns and dungeons on instinct, until they come upon a humanoid corpse. At this point, the Clagborne strips the body of its flesh and tissue, magically absorbing all chemical and electrical information, and is "born" as a new entity, complete with all the memories of its fallen host.
The ooze wraps around the skeleton, forming a new body in the model of the old. A Clagborne can alter the transparency and colour of its slime flesh to suit its wishes.

Although a Clagborne retains the memories their original form had in life and are functionally identical in personality, desires and ability, they are a distinct creature. The soul of the departed does not return to the Clagborne, and many struggle coming to terms with their identity.
Are they the same person as they were in life? Or an abominable walking undead, host to a parasitic, brainless monster?

raceFluff.name: Westurai
entries: Created by Celestial Gods to articulate their designs on the material plane, Westurai are a mysterious, enigmatic race devoted entirely to their divine purpose.

Each is magically hewn from stone with a fully formed mind and impetus. Be it to guard a temple, gather information, destroy evil, or explore the world, most Westurai have their actions dictated to the letter by the god who created them. They obey these orders unthinkingly and without passion.

However, should their orders cease to arrive, perhaps through the death of a god or a severing of the divine connection, a Westurai becomes free to act independently, forging their own destiny as a living being.

raceFluff.name: Aemyr
entries: Ancient legends tell that the first Aemyr were created by a powerful, empathetic archfey who sought to create guardians for the natural world across all planes of existence. Aemyr have been found on many planes, uniquely adapted to suit their environment. There are two primary subraces that exist on the Material Plane: The {@race Aemyr (Flaxfoot)|DMSecretWeapon|Flaxfoot Aemyr} and The {@race Aemyr (Lowstone)|DMSecretWeapon|Lowstone Aemyr}.

items.name: Flaxfoot
entries: Flaxfoot Aemyr usually dwell in forests, and by natural disposition are playful and merry. They have an unfortunate reputation for gluttony, and overindulgence in fine food and drink, however this is largely unfounded. Flaxfoot enjoy the bounties of their forest home to the fullest, but they are no more greedy or gluttonous than any other race. Still, rarely do travellers who come upon a Flaxfoot town leave the next morning without a full belly and ringing hangover.

items.name: Lowstone
entries: Lowstone Aemyr are mountain dwellers. Acclimated to life at the very peak of the tallest mountains, they are a rare sight on the lands below. Many Mountain Dwarf legends feature Lowstone as invisible protectors or guardians to those who fall foul of the mountain. They are rumoured to have the power to sense volcanic eruptions and earthquakes before they happen, and have long aided Dwarves building mighty mountain fortresses in ways that will not provoke the mountain's wrath.

raceFluff.name: Ichorborne
entries: Legends tell of the Ichorborne, a cursed race hewn from dark magic. Walking abominations, held together without skin or sinew; a swirling mist of blood and terror. They take humanoid form, with crimson flesh and scent of iron. The air about them ripples with the taste of blood. These are the tales the people tell.

As sentient and capable of goodness as any other race, the Ichorborne are so rare, and so feared, they struggle to find acceptance in the wider world. Formed from the memories of innocents whose blood has been shed, they emerge into the world fully formed and sentient. A chaotic amalgamation of personalities bound to a single mind.

Many Ichorborne isolate themselves entirely, or disguise themselves as hooded, masked travellers, attempting to live a quiet existence among the rest of the world. Some seek vengeance on those who harm the innocent. Unless an individual can somehow prove themselves to a community and receive acceptance, the life of the Ichorborne is forever one of suspicion, persecution, and secrecy.

raceFluff.name: Augmegnome
entries: Augmegnome are an unusual subspecies of gnomes that have grown accustomed to the dense, highland jungles of Avestros. Over centuries, they have adapted to grow tall and lithe, able to move swiftly through the jungle and protect themselves from the more physically magical dangers that surround them.

Augmegnome are sometimes stereotyped as flighty, stupid and naive by other gnomes, but they are no less wise or inquisitive than their cousins. Instead of relying on tools and intellect, they prefer to take matters into their own hands, facing danger head on with panache and style.

raceFluff.name: Firmakin
entries: Firmakin are sentient elementals found in the rich, unclaimed territories of the material plane. Anywhere unconquered by human, elven or dwarven hand, Firmakin can be found.

They are typically solitary, rarely meeting or interacting with other Firmakin save for times of great crisis. They form close bonds with plants and beasts, and often wander their vast territory talking to themselves and the natural life around them.

Many legends of nature spirits and invisible fey creatures can find their origin in the Firmakin walking the woods; their gentle, deep voices rumbling through the earth and frightening unwitting travellers in their lands.

raceFluff.name: Caridae
entries: Caridae are an amphibious, jungle dwelling race. They come in four main types: Fire-Belly, Galvanic, Poison Dart and Kinetic. Caridae grow into their type upon reaching adulthood.

These types seem to have no genetic bearing. For example, two parent Fire-Belly Caridae might produce an offspring that grows into a Galvanic. As such, many myths and legends exist in Caridae folklore attempting to explain where Caridae powers come from, and what they mean.

Caridae live relatively short lives and are innately curious and trusting. This naivety is sometimes attributed as stupidity to cynical outsiders, but Caridae are as intelligent as any other sentient race. They simply have a natural inclination to take words and people at face value.

raceFluff.name: Pelaggion
entries: Pelaggion are an amphibious, mammalian race of humanoids native to the shores and islands of Avestros. A common sight on the continent, Pelaggion are rarely found outside its borders.
With powerful bodies well adapted for swift motion across both land and ocean, Pelaggion society is wholly structured around the sanctity of The Hunt and an individual's personal value to the tribe.

Each Pelaggion has a niche, and they take great pride in their area of expertise. To be rendered "useless" through injury or superior competition is a terrible fate to a Pelaggion. Many leave the tribe and oceans to seek fortune or die alone if they feel they can no longer provide a tangible contribution to their community.
They are often sought out as fortune-tellers or advisors, due to their ability to see glimpses of the near future.

raceFluff.name: Pooka
entries: A compound race, Pooka are unlike any other humanoid in that their brain (known as The Gnute) exists separately from their body. The Gnute is housed in the centre of a living, symbiotic "shell" organism (known as The Ultat). The two creatures are born together, sharing the same thoughts, desires and sensory information. Together, they form a Pooka.

In very rare, tragic cases, the connection between the Gnute and the Ultat can be severed. At this time, the Ultat ceases to hear the commands of the Gnute, and is driven by instinct. This leaves the Gnute to wither, existing as a prisoner inside a body they cannot command, impotently observing its actions. In this form, the Pooka is dangerously aggressive and primal.

Pooka who's Gnute and Ultat are not working in unison are referred to as being "desynchronised" by others of their kind. Although the condition is treatable, once the Gnute and Ultat have been disconnected, the Pooka is forever changed. Pooka who are saved and reunited return altered by the magical trauma of the experience.

raceFluff.name: Powgarfoot
entries: Making their home in the temperate, mountainous forests of Avestros, Powgarfoot are an ursine race of humanoids. Hulking, sociable, and independant, they typically prefer to keep out of conflict, unfettered by the politics and warfare of other races. All are welcome in a Powgarfoot village, free to stay as long as they wish, and to take as much food as they desire.

Powgarfoot take enormous pleasure in food. Eating, cooking, sharing, and storing it are acts of delight and great cultural significance. All events, be they funerals, weddings, birthdays, weekends, or weekdays, are marked with a great feast. Their cuisine is famous across the land as delicious and eclectic. There is no dish a Powgarfoot will not sample, and very few meals they will not enjoy.

raceFluff.name: Chookardian
entries: In a bustling, ancient, criss-cross network of caverns and tunnels, the Chookardian build homes, raise livestock, and thrive beneath the notice of most surface dwellers.

Happily beating a peaceful existence largely removed from the rest of the world, only rarely do Chookardian meet with surface dwellers to trade materials, knowledge, and stories. These cultural exchanges are deeply significant, with the Chookardian sending an honoured expedition party to the surface world, resplendent with the finest works of Chookardian craft to barter for supplies for the tribe.
Occasionally, a Chookardian may choose to stay above ground, either to fulfil a personal goal or to embark a self-imposed mission to obtain wondrous resources to improve the life of their kin.

raceFluff.name: Spectrakin Ancestry
entries: Souls fraught with fury or inflamed with passion can resist the call of the grave. Such cases are rare, but when the body dies and the spirit lives on, a new, crude being is created: a spectrakin.

Ghastly in appearance, possessing a rudimentary body hewn from necrotic, spectral force, spectrakin retain the memories and personality they had in life. They cling to the material world through sheer force of will, and though they do not age, rarely do spectrakin remain for long, often passing from existence when their task is complete or their vengeance sated.

raceFluff.name: Mollopod
entries: A humanoid race of shelled molluscs, mollopod are an artful, amiable, spiritual folk who live and thrive in the freshwater swamps of Avestros. Renowned for their eccentric and idiosyncratic beliefs (each mollopod has their own theory on the nature of the cosmos that they're pretty darn sure is the right one), mollopod often find themselves acting as spiritual guides, fortune tellers, and advisors on the mystical to folk of all races. They share similar gifts of foresight to the mountain dwelling cyclod, and have an innate flair for the theatrical and storytelling.

A mollopod's most distinctive feature is, of course, its shell, which begins growing on its back from childhood. A mollopod is considered an adult from the day its shell "manifests", at which point a connection between the material plane and the immaterial plane is created. From this point on, the mollopod carries an extra-dimensional gateway on its back, and is able to store any number of objects safely there. No matter the situation, a well travelled mollopod will likely carry the answer somewhere on its back.

raceFluff.name: Gree
entries: Across the lands of Avestros, there is no community of people so naturally dispossessed to cheer and playful mischief as the gree. A nocturnal, hatchling race, born from mysterious eggs which magically appear where gree gather together, they are famous across the land for their highly idiosyncratic and, at times, baffling fashion sense. Each gree crafts their own unique costume upon reaching adulthood, a magical garment designed to aid them in whatever path they choose to take in life.

A gree's costume is sacred and personal, a reflection of that which they are and that which they hope to be. Simultaneously, the gree are a race that takes being silly very seriously, and so an individual's costume will often celebrate their playful nature with outlandish design philosophy. They often take inspiration from mighty creatures, terrifying folktales, or tasty foods, and costumes feature heavily in their many cultural traditions, festivals, and rituals.

raceFluff.name: Chiropine
entries: Chiropine are among the newest known races, emerging in the material world after the Great Convergence synchronised several overlapping planes. As such, their unique customs and "quirky" behaviour are regarded with interest and bemusement by many. Of course, the chiropine view other races as "quirky" instead, their own society having no interest in conquest, wealth, or territorial expansion. They operate at night if possible, relying on echolocation to get by in the dark, and have a preferred diet of fruit, devoting large swathes of land to its production.
Chiropine are also known for vivacious explosions of energy—few creatures are as fast, on land or air, as a spriting chiropine.

raceFluff.name: Lamnite
entries: Beneath eternal, inky skies and over bitter, icy wastes, a race of nomads beat a weary trail. These people are the lamnites, perhaps the most mysterious beings native to Avestros. In a magical continent of microclimates, where blistering desert borders verdant forest, the lamnite call the endless tundra that devours the south of Avestors their home. Trembling rays of sunlight reach their territory for only minutes each day, with the rest of a native lamnite's existence spent in aching dark and cold. It is a hard life, but one for which lamnites are well adapted. They are weavers of darkness—able to command, conjure, and dispel it. Some folk view lamnites with suspicion, as few of them venture north of their icy territory and still fewer care to dispel fearful notions of their shadowy magic. Lamnite, however, view their shadow magic and cruel home quite differently. Rather than a people that celebrate darkness and isolation, they view their very existence as the ultimate rebellion against it. For if they can stride through darkness and call its power for their own, then they are living proof that no creeping shadow or biting tundra can quench the breath and light of life.

raceFluff.name: Centovis
entries: Joyously peeling back and forth on a winding journey down Abrax, the tallest mountain in Avestros, flows the Pathis River. Along its banks from icy crest to gentle foothill live the centovium: a wool-coated, hooved, quadruped race, cousins of the famous centaurs. While alike their distant kin in stature and physique, centovium could not differ more from centaurs in attitude to outsiders. While few centaurs would ever suffer the indignity of bearing another on their back, a typical centovis takes delight in acting as a mount for others. In centovis culture, the mount, bearing the wounded or weary on their body, is a position of bravery and dominance, and a powerful protection magic is woven between rider and bearer when the centovium charge.

raceFluff.name: Dyenoia
entries: Running across the centre of the world, stretched as a band dividing north from south like a colossal, emerald serpent, is the Ouroboros Jungle. Scarcely 50 miles wide at its broadest, this incredibly fragile ecosystem can only survive in the perfect, seasonless equilibrium maintained at the equator. It is home to many incredible fauna and flora, but none so curious as the plant-folk dyenoia.

A rigidly defined life awaits every new-born dyenoia. Every child is raised by the community and is given no name until they reach adulthood. Concepts of individuality and personal ambition are foreign; from first gasping breath to last, each dyenoia is trained to think only of the needs of the collective, and to fill their place within the system that maintains it. Though dyenoia have rulers and priests, such roles in society offer no more personal wealth or status than that of a labourer, scholar, nurse, or merchant. To distant outsiders, this is seen as admirable; scholars write of the nobility of dyenoia—a utopian society where greed and ambition has been vanquished for the good of all.

To local outsiders however, the dyenoia are terrifying. Their commitment to each other is matched only by their utter indifference to sufferings of others. The ferocity with which they defend the Ouroborus Jungle is legendary, and swiftly puts paid to any attempt by outsiders to barter, conquer, or connect with them. The fearful reputation of dyenoia is not aided by the imposing, acidic maw that crowns each individual's head, capable of crushing bone and devouring creatures whole. Fortunately, the dyenoia lack ambitions of conquest or domination, and trouble none who do not trouble them. The greatest fear of any who live or travel near the Ouroboros Jungle is that they accidentally tread on dyenoia land and face swift and lethal retribution.

raceFluff.name: Dragonborn (Variant)
entries: The magic of dragons is ancient, mysterious, and tenacious. Eons ago it is said dragons took on humanoid forms and lived among the other races of the world. Other tales speak of ancient wizards and sorcerers conducting dangerous experiments to harness draconic magic. Whatever the origin of their heritage, some humanoids carry draconic blood in their veins.

The power of dragons can manifest in any number of incredible ways. Some dragonborn appear as ordinary humans, orcs, elves, and dwarves, blessed with invisible but potent draconic power. For others, a draconic heritage is evident, with dragonborn appearing as lizard-like humanoids with scales, tails, and razor-sharp fangs. No two dragonborn are alike, but all are powerful.
When creating your dragonborn character, you can use the following traits, which replace all dragonborn traits.

raceFluff.name: Half-Orc (Variant)
entries: In the distant past, orcs were feared and despised as a brutish, cruel people. Labelled as savage and murderous, orcs were often isolated, slaughtered, and enslaved by races who called themselves "noble". Thankfully, such times have passed, and today orcs are accepted as equals to other beings, as capable of art, magic, diplomacy, and empathy as any group of people. As a consequence of this shift toward a more cosmopolitan world, half-orcs became commonplace; children blessed with orcish ancestry from one parent alongside the ancestry of the other.

Half-orcs can be born with any number of physical traits from either ancestry. Some appear identical to orcs, naturally tall, broad, and muscular, with green or purple skin. Others are born with a mixture of physical traits. A half-orc, half-centaur may have an orcish torso and head with a horse's body. Another might have a typically orcish body, but a horse's tail and hooves in place of their feet. A half-orc, half-dragonborn may have the scales and horns of a dragon, but the build and tusks of an orc. When you select this race, you choose your physical appearance.

raceFluff.name: Cloudian
entries: The breath of creation reverberates through all things, even natural phenomena. In rare instances, where the breath of life sings deep and loud, conscious thought is born, forming a body from the fundamental force it once was. Cloudians are one such race of people, born eons ago from clouds who sought to live among the creatures they gazed down upon.

A typically affable and peaceful folk, cloudians claim no region or country as their own, effortlessly integrating among other peoples all across the globe as they see fit. This "open borders'' approach to territory has been known to vex more isolationist countries where cloudians settle, but the soporific speech and affable character of cloudians is so disarming that even the most hardline separatist societies have come to accept their presence without protest. As such, with only a gentle smile and spectacular inability to comprehend they might not be welcome, many cloudians have peacefully settled in lands that armies have failed to conquer for millenia.

raceFluff.name: Myod

entries: Myods-y lives under the oceans,
Myods-y lives under the sea,
With his tentacles, he knows the motions,
So bring back myods-y to me!

Although rarely seen on land, beneath the spitting, churning black tides that slap at the golden sands of the Autumn Coast live an enormous society of tentacle headed humanoids - the myods. The Under, their submerged capital, is the most densely populated city in Avestros, with an approximate population of 500,000 myods in permanent residence. It is a city of intellectuals, universities, high culture, and scientific experimentation.

Myods are relentlessly curious and naturally intelligent, measuring maturity not in years, but in mental acuity. A myod becomes an adult when they are capable of solving a gauntlet of complex mathematical and philosophical questions in under 1 minute, whilst juggling using at least three tentacles. As such, precocious myods as young as four can be found occupying senior positions in society such as lawyers, doctors, and professors. This hasty induction into society is necessary, however, as even the longest-lived myods never reach 30 years of age. It's been said they could conquer the world if they had the time, but myods are not, by nature, aggressive folk. Though able to move and live on land, they typically prefer the ocean, and often act as emissaries between land folk and other, less docile sea dwelling races.

raceFluff.name: Avestrosian Gnoll
entries: Legends speak of gnolls spread across the all planes of existence: demonic, snarling, bloodthirsty creatures under the command of a terrifying demon lord. The first gnolls to fall through the Shimmering Veil into Avestros might have been of such savage and mindless character, but after millenia apart from the rest of the multiverse, and the oversight and influence of their vicious creator, Avestrosian gnolls have grown to overcome their feral instinct and craft their own destiny.

Similar in appearance and power to the gnolls feared on other planes, the life of an Avestrosian gnoll is one of restless temperance—an eternal balancing act between an ancient, clawing instinct for destruction and a blossoming desire for freedom, kinship, and peace. A great deal of gnoll art and contemporary philosophy explores this discordance at the heart of each individual's soul, and the journey of each gnoll is one of self-discovery and exploration--- a quest to turn a killer instinct to the pursuit of a life beyond mayhem and revelry. Those who succeed rise to greatness as true masters of themselves and their own destiny. The few gnoll who fail are as deadly as they are tragic—fallen monstrosities who roam the lands as slaves to their own monstrous instinct.

raceFluff.name: Aggrataurian
entries: "Flightless and frightful" was the description given by famed gnoll explorer Ignobious Riot upon discovering a roaming band of aggrataurian in the Craggy Mountains of western Avestros. Aggrataurian are towering, highly aggressive, flightless bird-folk, widely known as "jerks" by most outsiders. At first, it was believed that aggrataurian were isolationists, viewing any non-aggrataurian as a threat worthy of fierce assault. However, as time passed and outsiders saw aggrataurian they treated one another with the same ferocity as any other species, it came to be understood that these people were just "kind of like that".

Aggrataurian are highly aggressive. They live to brawl, and solve problems with direct physical confrontation where possible. They are not actively murderous, however, merely viewing hand-to-beak combat as the most efficient way to solve problems. Aggrataurians believe that all hierarchy is ultimately dictated by force, so why not cut the nonsense and work out who's top of the pecking order right here and now?

In recent years, through repeated efforts from various species to develop trade and bonds with the aggrataurian, some individuals have learned to quell their fighting tendencies long enough to hold a conversation with others. However, even the most habituated aggratuarian is always down for a scrap, and are known to be swift in misreading anything from a friendly wave to a passing compliment as an invitation to fight.

raceFluff.name: Arcardae
entries: Across the infinite multiverse, life blooms in every imaginable biome, and in every imaginable shape. Of all the sentient forms life takes, there is perhaps no greater mismatch in disposition and physiology than the terrifying arcardae. Gruesomely ugly spider-folk, arcardae have the upper torso of a humanoid sat atop the bulbous, bloated abdomen of a colossal spider. Similar in appearance to the demonic driders of the underworld, arcardae inspire understandable revulsion and terror in the eyes of most they meet.

Fortunately, however, arcardae prove the old adage correct: one cannot judge a book by its cover. A gentle, herbivorous species, these spider-folk are well regarded by those who know them as naturally thoughtful, tolerant, and open-minded people. Though their monstrous form provides them ample power to defend themselves if attacked, arcardae philosophy touts the virtues of nonviolence. Their society boasts very few soldiers and no war industry, and yet history carries few accounts of aggression from other species aiming to exploit their pacifistic ways. Many scholars posit that the arcardae's hideous appearance acts as a natural deterrent to potential invaders, who assume the spider-folk to be mighty, flesh-eating monsters not worth tangling with.

raceFluff.name: Avestrosian Gnome
entries: There are few species as wily and bafflingly resilient as the gnome. No matter the form they take (and across the infinite worlds of the multiverse, they take every form imaginable), gnomes exist and flourish in spite of their surroundings. In Avestros, there are two primary types - Shadow and Frost. Each share the immutable gnomish trait of fortitude, although it manifests differently in this world to how it is known to manifest in others.

items.name: Frost Gnomes
entries: Frost gnomes live in the icy south of the continent, able to survive the harsh conditions through a combination of iron tenacity and innate elemental magic. These gnomes operate in enormous groups—thousands of individuals living, working, and moving together. Amongst their kin, there is little concept of personal space, property, or private family. Every gnome elder sees every child as their responsibility; every frost gnome is kin to be loved and cared for. Interestingly, this often leaves frost gnomes hazy on parentage and direct relations. Bloodlines and other such concerns mean little-to-nothing. To frost gnomes, every other frost gnome is family.

items.name: Shadow Gnomes
entries: Shadow gnomes are the most populous species of the Soul Mountains, though you could travel those vertant peaks for years and never see one. In actuality, the real marvel of Soul is the brilliant network of tunnels that twist and burrow beneath the surface, the domain of the shadow gnomes. Well adapted to live in the dark, shadow gnomes live almost entirely in tight, family units. Upon falling in love, two gnomes will descend into the labyrinthine passages below Soul and live out a quiet life together in perpetual darkness. If blessed with children, the pair will return to the surface to raise them, before retreating once again into the solitude of the mountain's depths and each other's company. Few shadow gnomes leave Soul, and most who do plan upon sating their thirst for adventure to one day return to the gentle mountain with a true partner to treasure in isolation for their remaining tranquil years.

raceFluff.name: Dryad
entries: From tempestuous ocean, to trembling forest, to stark, belligerent mountainside, anywhere the natural world breathes freely, dryads call home. Typically solitary folk, dryads are most content among the company of one another and the solace of nature.

Throughout history, most clashes between dryads and other species have been in response to the other's aspirations of conquest and domination negatively impacting the natural world. Dryads have a reputation for civility and patience, but it swiftly veers into ruinous fury and retribution when harm is done to nature. Many dryads proudly declare themselves as protectors of The World, and value the lives of simple beasts, plants, and even mountains as equal to those of "intelligent" beings.

raceFluff.name: Avestrosian Tiefling
entries: Across the multiverse, there is no land where things are quite so different whilst being the same as Avestros. Tieflings exist on many worlds and planes, with many forms and powers granted by a fiendish lineage. In Avestros, they appear much the same as their brothers and sisters on other worlds, complete with horns, tails and humanoid stature. There is, however, one key difference.

In Avestros, intent matters more than bloodline. It doesn't matter what type of creature the ancestor that grants you power is. What matters is their alignment. Descendants of magical chaotic beings live with a spark of that chaos within. The ambition and iron will of lawful beings can manifest in a creature's family years down the line, and so too can the virtue of good and the vice of evil. Avestrosian tieflings have unique powers based on the alignment of the ancestor through whom they draw magic.

This isn't to say every tiefling shares the alignment and beliefs of their ancestors. It's common for tieflings blessed with power of chaos and evil to be lawfulgood alligned in themselves. Sadly, the inverse is often also true, with some wielding the magic of order and goodness passed down across generations for their own devious ends.

raceFluff.name: Spellforged
entries: Either through chaotic, explosive interactions of latent magic, or through the meticulous design of a powerful spellcaster, Spellforged are the very essence of the weave forged into consciousness. Spellforged created by spellcasters like liches and dracomages are often mindless servants who only gain control of their mind and destiny upon their master's destruction. Even while thralls to a greater being, however, these beings of pure magical energy feel emotion, pain and pleasure the same as any other creature.

The life of a free spellforged is often as chaotic as the explosive interactions that brought about their birth. Lacking any parents, culture, heritage, or purpose, they often wander the world, seeking fulfillment in any way they can find it. This may mean helping the vulnerable, forming communities with other spellforged, or gathering personal power. Their unstable ties to the weave tend spellforged toward Chaotic alignments.

raceFluff.name: Legionite
entries: A ruthlessly efficient species hewn from the earth and imbued with magic, the legionite were crafted to toil and mine in the vast network of glittering caves beneath the continent of Sniips. Although the earliest generation were viewed as a basic and expendable race of mindless automatons, soon more complex variations were created, each with different optimised properties to oversee all elements of the Levestros mining operation. Unbeknownst to their creators, legionite began to find sentience within a body of earthen and organic machinery. Far from mere "robots" they are Humanoid constructs.

With the power of the legionite, Sniips grew to be an indomitable powerhouse of industry. When the legionite rebelled, it was that same power that crushed Sniips under heavy, steel feet. The continent fell to chaos in a brutal and bloody civil war, known as Pandemonium. To this day the war continues, with many legionite fighting for their freedom while others flee to avestros across the churning ocean as refugees, seeking only to be free of Pandemonium.
Six known variations of legionite exist, each optimised to a singular function at the expense of all else.

raceFluff.name: Spherian
entries: As mysterious and beautiful as the trembling twilight sky, spherian are a species of humanoids imbued with divine starlight. Long-lived and deeply reclusive, spherian are believed to be mythological by some creatures, or alien visitors to the material plane by others. In truth, they are as terrestrial as a mountain dwarf, but hold such little interest in the affairs of others that they find no reason to engage with the tussles and tantrums that shape the modern world. Spherian do not require food or water to survive, and care little of earthly possessions, and so have no impetus to exploit or dominate other creatures. They prefer the solace of nighttime, although curious individuals have been known to venture out under the light of day to pursue the call of adventure.

Every spherian is born with a unique astrological marking on their body, as distinct as a fingerprint, which relates to a constellation of stars somewhere in the infinite universe. These marks contain divine power, which manifests differently in individuals depending on the resonance of the mark. Spellcasting spherian often work these patterns into their spellbooks and sigils, and many spherian spend long, meditative hours at night staring into the sky, searching for their constellation in the twinkling darkness.

raceFluff.name: Lumbrinth
entries: The humble lumbrinth are an innocuous folk descended from the mighty worms native to the material plane. In terms of temperament, however, they could not be further from their monstrous ancestors; they are every bit as cautious and shy as their purple worm progenitors are chaotic and destructive. That said, lumbrinth are not cowards. Their impressive natural armour and fierce tail stingers make them potent warriors even when stripped of all weaponry, and many tyrants and warlords have met a painful end upon mistaking the lumbrinth as easy pickings for domination and exploitation.

Their long, wormlike bodies can strike an impressive figure, though many lumbrinth hang their heads low and fidget instinctively, conscious not to appear confrontational or intimidating. Lumbrinth are deeply unusual among sentient species in that they do not eat meat, able to sustain themselves by devouring vegetation and earth. Their natural carapace also provides sufficient protection from the elements, meaning lumbrinth struggle not for food or shelter, and so have little reason to engage in trade or industry. Some lumbrinth do seek wealth in pursuit of status or pleasure, but for most, all the tools necessary for a comfortable life are granted by their own unique physiology and the earth at their feet.

spell.name: Hyperfocus
entries: Your touch imbues a target with energy, increasing their awareness. They have advantage on dexterity saving throws and initiative rolls, and can't be surprised for the duration of the spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot above 2nd.

spell.name: Mark of Vulnerability
entries: You weave a cursed, spectral mark onto a creature you can see within range. Choose a damage type from among Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder.
The target creature loses any resistance to that damage type for the duration of the spell.

spell.name: Wrecking Bolt
entries: You fire a vivid bolt of energy towards an object that isn't being worn or carried or a construct within range, rippling through the structure and targeting any vulnerabilities in its construction.
The target takes {@damage 4d10} force damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Energy Transfer
entries: Choose one creature within range. It gains {@dice 1d8} temporary hit points, and can use its reaction to make a single weapon attack; or cast a spell with a casting time of one action that is of a lower level than the level of this spell; or move up to its movement speed. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the target creature gains an additional {@dice 1d8} temporary hit points for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Moonburst
entries: Make a ranged spell attack against a creature within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d8} necrotic or radiant damage (your choice) and makes a constitution save. On a failed save, the target is blinded until the start of your next turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Lunar Touch

components.m: A diamond or crystal worth at least 600gp

entries: You imbue a creature with lunar energy, granting it certain benefits that reflect its true nature:

entries.caption: Lunar Touch Benefits
rows: Target gains advantage on all wisdom checks, resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, and +2 AC for the duration.
Target gains {@dice 4d10} temporary hit points, its movement increases by 10 ft, and adds a +2 to its attack rolls for the duration.
Target can use an action to glow with a faint, silvery light until they use an action to dismiss the effect.
The target randomly grows or shrinks {@dice 1d6} inches for the duration.
Target gains advantage on all saving throws against spells and other magical effects for the duration.

spell.name: Rise of the Blood Moon

components.m: Several seeds of any moonseed plant, a vial of the caster's blood, and a spherical, crystal orb worth at least 2,000gp, which the spell consumes

entries: Crimson light shines down in a mile-radius sphere centred at a point you can see within range, penetrating magical darkness and walls and objects less than 12 inches thick. Every humanoid and beast with an intelligence score of 3 or higher illuminated by the crimson light makes a wisdom saving throw (they can choose to fail).

On a failed save they gain immunity to all non-magical, non-silvered weapons; their alignment shifts to match yours; they gain {@dice 5d10} temporary hit points; their base walking speed increases by 10ft; and their AC increases by 1.

If you choose to do so, you can issue a simple command to all those under the effect of the Blood Moon as you cast it. An example could be "Protect the city", "Loot and burn", or "Kill my enemies". Affected creatures will follow the command to the best of their ability, even risking their life, but will not actively harm themselves.
If no command is given, those affected act according to their new alignment for the duration of the spell.
If this spell is cast on the night of a full moon, unwilling creatures make their wisdom saves with disadvantage.
The effect of this spell on an individual can be dispelled with a Dispel Magic spell cast at 9th level.

spell.name: Berserk
entries: Choose a creature you can see within range, that target makes a Charisma saving throw (it can choose to fail), or is affected by this spell. Until the spell ends, the target gains {@dice 1d12} temporary hit points; it gains resistance to bludgeoning, slashing, and piercing damage; it makes all strength checks, strength saving throws and melee attack rolls with advantage; it deals an additional +2 damage on all melee attacks; attacks against it have advantage; and it cannot concentrate on spells or cast spells.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the target gains an additional {@dice 1d12} temporary hit points for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Weave Drain

time.condition: which you take when you see a creature within 90 feet of you casting a spell

entries: You attempt to interrupt a creature in the process of casting a spell. If the creature is casting a spell of 6th level or lower, its spell fails and has no effect. If it is casting a spell of 7th level or higher, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spells level. On a success, the creature's spell fails and has no effect.
If the spell fails as a result of you countering it with this spell, you regain a spent spell slot of a level equal to or less than half the level of the spell you countered (rounded down).

spell.name: Spiritual Interposition

time.condition: which you take when you see a creature within 30 feet of you take damage

entries: You magically intervene in an act of self sacrifice when a creature you can see within range takes damage from an attack. Instead, they take no damage, you take the amount of damage they would have taken, and your hit point total is reduced by the same amount. This damage cannot be resisted or redirected in any way. Your hit point total returns to normal after a short or long rest.

spell.name: Invoke Gobbledegook
entries: Choose a creature you can see within range. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or else uncontrollably babble incessant, meaningless nonsense. Creatures that speak a language say gobbledegook phrases. Creatures that do not speak a language instead make a constant stream of grunts, howls and whines. While babbling in this way, the target cannot speak anything other than gobbledegook, perform the verbal components of spells, or do anything that requires the articulation of its mouth other than babble.
At the end of each of its turns, the target can make another Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target.

spell.name: Cascading Impact
entries: Make a ranged spell attack roll at a target within range. On a hit, that creature takes {@damage 3d8} force damage and, if it is Large or smaller, you push it up to 10ft in any direction.
If you push the creature into a space occupied by another creature it stops moving and both creatures take {@damage 1d8} force damage, are pushed 5ft away from each other, and fall prone.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, it deals an extra {@dice 1d8} damage to each creature you damage with this spell for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Episquee
entries: You place a hand on a creature and imbue it with reactive, defensive magic. The next time the target takes damage, as long as they are conscious, they immediately gain temporary hit points equal to twice the damage they took. These hit points last for the duration of the spell, or until the target regains any hit points.

spell.name: Ocular Pat Down
entries: Choose a creature you can see within 60ft. You instantly determine its strength score, dexterity score, and if it is carrying any weapons that aren't concealed by magic.
For the duration of the spell, you also have advantage on any insight checks to detect whether the target is lying, and advantage on any intimidation checks made against the creature.

spell.name: Jelly Legs
entries: A burst of vivid yellow energy engulfs a target creature within range. That creature makes a constitution saving throw.

On a failed save, its equilibrium is thrown off balance. Its walking speed is reduced by 10 feet, it cannot take the dash action, and it has disadvantage on dexterity checks and saving throws until the spell ends.
At the end of each of its turns, the creature can make a constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Mushroom Cloud
entries: A devastating explosion of spores instantly erupts from a point of your choosing within range. Each creature in a 30ft-radius-sphere must make a Constitution saving throw. A target takes {@damage 6d6} poison and {@damage 6d6} acid damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
The area struck by this effect becomes heavily obscured by thick clouds of dust and spores for as long as the spell lasts.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, you can increase the radius of the sphere this spell impacts by 10ft for each level above 6th.

spell.name: Into Shadow
entries: Target creature within range makes a Charisma saving throw (it can choose to fail). On a failed save, it is instantly teleported up to 30ft to an unoccupied space you can see. The chosen space must be on a surface or liquid that can support the target without the target having to squeeze.
When the target is teleported, it takes {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the target takes an additional {@dice 1d6} damage for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Price of Empathy

time.condition: which you take when a creature within range takes damage

entries: When a creature you can see within range takes damage, you attempt to form a link between that creature and another, sharing its pain. Choose another creature within range, that target must make a Wisdom saving throw, or take psychic damage equal to half the amount of damage the first creature took.

spell.name: Obsolescence
entries: You invoke the power of shadow to cause a creature's spirit to fade from the living world. When you cast this spell, and at the start of each of your turns, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On every failed save, their movement speed is reduced by 10ft, their AC decreases by 1, and their weapon and spell attacks deal {@dice 1d4} less damage (but no less than 1).
If you concentrate on this spell for the full duration, the target suffers the changes to its stats for the next 7 days.

spell.name: Flaming Binds
entries: Choose a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition restrained} for the duration as they are bound in flaming, spectral chains.

When it fails this saving throw and at the start of each of its turns, the creature takes {@damage 1d8} fire damage. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make another Dexterity saving throw. On a success, the spell ends on the target.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level about 3rd.

spell.name: Bide
entries: When you cast this spell, increase your AC by 1.
The first time each round you are hit by an attack, while you are concentrating on this spell, your AC increases by 1.

When this spell ends, you unleash a violent burst of captured kinetic energy at a creature within 30ft of you. That creature takes {@damage 2d8} force damage for each point of AC you gained from this spell's effect while concentrating on it.

spell.name: Precision Bombardment
entries: You let loose a devastating barrage of magical bolts, striking at a creature you can see within range.
Make a ranged spell attack roll. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d8} force damage. This attack scores a critical hit on an 18, 19, or 20.
If you cast Precision Bombardment on your previous turn and scored a critical hit, you can cast it again this turn at the same level without expending a spell slot as a bonus action.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or above, make the attack roll at advantage.

spell.name: Siphon Essence
entries: You become wreathed in purple, spectral flames.

The next time you inflict damage to a creature with a spell or weapon attack, you deal an extra {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage as the flames surrounding you are channeled into the attack. You then gain temporary hit points equal to half the total damage you inflicted.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each slot level about 1st.

spell.name: Six Hundred Needles
entries: When you cast this spell, and as an action on each of your turns, you can weave a cursed needle mark onto a creature you can see within range, which lasts until the spell ends.

After cursing a target in this way, that creature takes {@damage 1d10 + 1} piercing damage for each needle mark you have cursed them with, as spectral needles fly from your outstretched hand and home in on the target.

spell.name: Wall of Slime

components.m: a pinch of powdered snail shell

entries: An opaque wall of dense green slime springs into existence on a solid surface at an unoccupied point you choose in range. You can choose to make this wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, and 10 feet thick or in a circle that has a 20-foot diameter and is up to 20ft high and 10 feet thick.

A creature can move through the wall, albeit extremely slowly. For every 1 foot the creature moves through the wall, it must spend 10 feet of movement. For as long as a creature is in the wall, it is {@condition blinded} and {@condition deafened}, and cannot breathe, speak, or perform the verbal components of spells. It also cannot stand up from being {@condition prone}, take the {@action Dodge} or {@action Dash} action, and has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. A creature has resistance to all damage types except psychic while it is in the wall of slime.
Non-magical weapon attacks cannot pass through the wall, instead getting caught in the slime.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you may increase the thickness of the wall by 5ft for each slot level above 5th.

spell.name: Bubble Prison
entries: You attempt to conjure a bubble of water around a Huge or smaller creature within range. That creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or become encased in a bubble of water. The bubble moves with them as they move.
While in the bubble, they are completely submerged in water. They can't breathe, speak, and have a resistance to all fire damage.

In addition, they have disadvantage on all attack rolls, their movement speed is reduced by 10ft, and the first time each turn they take lightning damage, they take an additional {@damage 1d8} lightning damage.
A creature can use its action to attempt a Dexterity saving throw, escaping the Bubble Prison on a success. When the creature escapes, the bubble breaks and the spell ends.

spell.name: Rainfall
entries: Gentle rain falls in a 120ft radius from a point you choose within range. The water is pure, clean and drinkable.

While concentrating on this spell, you can influence the rainfall, such as limiting the rain to fall only in certain areas, or use an action to create a simple, sensory effect like a rumble of thunder or flash of lightning.
If you concentrate on this spell for the full duration, the rain continues for the next hour before ending.

spell.name: Ranineamorphosis
entries: This spell transforms a creature with at least 1 hit point that you can see within range into a frog or toad. An unwilling creature must make a Constitution saving throw to avoid the effect. A shapechanger automatically succeeds on this saving throw.
The transformation lasts for the duration, or until the target drops to 0 hit points or dies. The target assumes the form of either a {@creature frog} or a {@creature giant toad} (your choice).
Their game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the beast, but they retain their alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma scores.

The target assumes the Hit Points of its new form. When it reverts to its normal form, the creature returns to the number of Hit Points it had before it transformed. If it reverts as a result of dropping to 0 Hit Points, any excess damage carries over to its normal form. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce the creature's normal form to 0 Hit Points, it isn't knocked {@condition unconscious}.

The creature cannot cast spells, speak, or take any action that would be limited by the capabilities of their frog or toad form. Transforming does not break {@status concentration} on a spell they have already cast, however, or prevent them from taking actions that are part of a spell, such as {@spell Call Lightning}, that they have already cast.
The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't activate, use, wield, or otherwise benefit from any of its Equipment.

spell.name: Blood Bend
entries: You attempt to manipulate the life flow of energy within one Huge or smaller creature you can see within range. If the target has 100 hit points or fewer, you take control of its body until the end of the turn.

While you control a creature in this way, it cannot move in any way that you do not allow. You can use your bonus action to take total and precise control of the target, during which time you can force the creature to move up to its movement speed and take an action, but you cannot force the creature to cast a spell.
For example, you might force an {@creature adult red dragon} to fly 40 feet, use its breath weapon attack, and then fall {@condition prone}.
And any damage the creature takes while under your control is also dealt to you, as your life force intertwines with its own. At the end of the turn, the creature is freed of your influence.

spell.name: Bloodblade
entries: You evoke a glistening crimson blade of living blood in your hand. Roll a number of hit dice equal to the spell slot level you cast this spell at. Your maximum hit point total is reduced by that many hit points until the spell ends.

The blade lasts until the spell ends. It counts as a simple melee weapon with which you are proficient. On a hit, it deals {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage for each hit die you rolled to create it, and has the finesse, light, and reach properties.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you may use your spellcasting modifier for attack and damage rolls with the blade.

spell.name: Insatiable Fury
entries: You attempt to stir an unquenchable fiery fury in a creature you can see within range. Creatures that can't be {@condition charmed} are immune to this effect.

The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it instantly takes {@damage 4d8} necrotic damage and flies into an uncontrollable fury. It has advantage on all weapon attacks made against you, but disadvantage on all other attack rolls and ability checks, and has disadvantage on saving throws to maintain {@status concentration} for the duration of this spell. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and suffers no other effects.
A creature can use an action to attempt to overcome its fury, repeating the Wisdom saving throw, ending the effects on a success.

spell.name: Curse of Dehydration
entries: You weave a vicious curse of dehydration on a target within range, subjecting them to a savage, painful thirst.
The target has disadvantage on all Strength, Dexterity and Intelligence saving throws and can't concentrate on spells.

At the start of each of its turns, a creature can make a Constitution saving throw, ending the effect on a success. If the target uses an action to drink something after being targeted by this spell, it makes all subsequent saves to end its effects at advantage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 6th.

spell.name: Divine Flavour
entries: You lay your hands on one small piece of food, imbuing it with healing magic and incredible flavour.
When you cast this spell, choose one condition from the following list: {@condition Blinded}, {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Deafened}, {@condition Frightened}, or {@condition Poisoned}.
Using an action to eat the food cures that condition, and grants the eater advantage on saving throws against that condition for the next 24 hours.
They also gain temporary hit points equal to your spellcasting modifier.
After 24 hours, if uneaten, the food loses all magical properties.
Once a creature gains the benefits of eating a food imbued with Divine Flavour, that creature cannot benefit from the spell again until it completes a long rest.

spell.name: Curse of Famine
entries: You weave a vicious curse of famine on a target within range, subjecting them to a terrible, aching hunger.
The target has disadvantage on all attack rolls and ability checks.

At the start of each of its turns, the creature can make a Constitution saving throw, ending the effect on a success. If the target uses an action to eat something after being targeted by this spell, it makes all subsequent saves to end its effects at advantage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Gumdack's Falling Elephant
entries: An elephant thunders into existence 30 feet above the point you choose and plummets to earth. All creatures within 10 feet of the point you chose must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 7d4} bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.
The elephant vanishes after the damage is dealt.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When Gumdack casts this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Elisleo's Invisible Space Hoppers
entries: Up to four creatures within range have their jump distance doubled until this spell ends, and they take no fall damage.
In addition, if they fall more than 10 feet, they can use their reaction to immediately bounce a number of feet equal to half the distance they fell in any direction.

If a creature bounces into another creature using this effect, they stop moving, and if the creature they hit is not under the effect of Elisleo's Invisible Space Hoppers, they must make a Strength Saving Throw or be knocked {@condition prone}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Miracle Explosion

time.condition: which you take when a creature within 10 feet of you misses with a melee attack roll

entries: As a reaction, when a creature within 10 feet of you misses with a melee attack roll, you can exploit their momentary vulnerability with a blast of force.
The creature takes {@damage 3d8} force damage and is knocked 10 feet away from you.

spell.name: Three-for-One
entries: The next time you cast a cantrip this turn that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can target three creatures in range with that spell instead of only one.
To be eligible, the cantrip must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the spell's current level. For example, {@spell Acid Splash} isn't eligible, but {@spell Fire Bolt} is.

spell.name: Elisleo's Screaming Bat-Nado
entries: A screeching sphere of spectral bats bursts into existence, forming a dark cloud, striking at all creatures within 30 feet of a point you choose within range.

Each creature inside the sphere when you cast this spell, or who enter it for the first time on their turn, must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be {@condition blinded} and take {@damage 5d8} magical piercing damage at the end of each of their turns. A creature can repeat this save at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.
As a bonus action on each of your turns, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet in any direction.

spell.name: Fury of the Raging Tarrasque
entries: The earth erupts with a calamitous, seismic tear. Each creature on the ground in a 60-foot radius centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A target takes {@damage 4d20} bludgeoning damage and {@damage 4d20} force damage and falls {@condition prone} on a failed save, or half as much damage and doesn't fall prone on a successful one.

In addition, you are surrounded by a spectral, scaled carapace. Any time you are targeted by a {@spell Magic Missile} spell, a line spell, or a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll a d6. On a 1 to 5, you are unaffected. On a 6, you are unaffected, and the effect is reflected back at the caster as though it originated from you, turning the caster into the target.
This carapace lasts until the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a 9th level spell slot, the duration of the spell is increased to 10 minutes.

spell.name: Fury of the Black Dragon
entries: A hissing geyser of boiling acid erupts at a point you choose in range. Each creature in a 30-foot radius centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A target takes {@damage 3d12} acid damage and {@damage 3d12} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.
In addition, you gain a resistance to acid damage for the duration of this spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, increase the acid damage by {@dice 1d12} for each level above 5th.

spell.name: Fury of the Frost Giant
entries: A deafening burst of ice and stone erupts at a point you choose in range. Each creature in a 10-foot radius centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. A target takes {@damage 3d8} cold damage and {@damage 3d8} bludgeoning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.
In addition, you gain a resistance to cold damage for the duration of this spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, increase the cold damage by {@dice 1d8} for each level above 3rd.

spell.name: Superior Blade Ward
entries: You extend your hand and trace a sigil of warding while touching a creature (you can target yourself). Until the end of your next turn, that creature has resistance against bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage dealt by weapon attacks.

spell.name: Superior Druidcraft
entries: Whispering to the spirits of nature, you create one of the following effects within range:

items: You create a tiny, harmless sensory effect that predicts what the weather will be at your location for the next 24 hours. The effect might manifest as a golden orb for clear skies, a cloud for rain, falling snowflakes for snow, and so on. This effect persists for 1 minute. Once created, you can use your action to influence the sensory effect, turning a golden orb into falling snow, etc. If you do, make a Nature skill check (DC 20). On a success, the weather at your location shifts over the course of the next 24 hours to reflect the effect you created. You cannot create weather of an intensity that would threaten life in the area. Once you use this feature to attempt to change the weather in your location, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
You instantly make a flower blossom, a seed pod open, or a leaf bud bloom.
You create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect, such as falling leaves, a puff of wind, the sound of a small animal, or the faint odor of skunk. The effect must fit in a 5-foot cube.
You instantly light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire.
You instantly know the location of all edible, poisonous, or sentient plants in a 300-foot radius.

spell.name: Superior Color Spray
entries: A dazzling array of flashing, colored light springs into existence at a point you choose in range. Roll {@dice 6d10}; the total is how many hit points of creatures this spell can effect.

Creatures in a 30 foot radius originating from the point you choose are affected in ascending order of their current hit points (ignoring {@condition unconscious} creatures and creatures that can't see). Starting with the creature that has the lowest current hit points, each creature affected by this spell is {@condition blinded} until the spell ends. Subtract each creature's hit points from the total before moving on to the creature with the next lowest hit points. A creature's hit points must be equal to or less than the remaining total for that creature to be affected.
At the end of each of their turns, a creature affected by this spell can make a Constitution saving throw, ending the effect on themselves on a success.

spell.name: Superior Water Walk
entries: This spell grants the ability to swiftly move across any liquid surface—such as water, acid, mud, snow, quicksand, or lava—as if it were harmless solid ground (creatures crossing molten lava can still take damage from the heat).

A creature moving across a liquid surface this way must only expend one foot of movement for every two feet it moves, and does not provoke opportunity attacks while moving on a liquid surface. Up to ten willing creatures you can see within range gain this ability for the duration.
If you target a creature submerged in a liquid, the spell carries the target to the surface of the liquid at a rate of 60 feet per round.

spell.name: Superior Jump
entries: You touch a creature. The creature's jump distance is tripled until the spell ends and it takes no fall damage if it falls a number of feet fewer than 9 + 3x its Strength modifier.
In addition, if that creature runs out of movement mid-jump, they complete the jump as normal, but land {@condition prone}.

spell.name: Ground Rotation
entries: Choose up to three points on the ground within range. You can cause the earth in a 5-foot radius of that point to shift to another position on the ground within 15 feet.

If a creature is standing on an area of earth you choose, they make a Dexterity saving throw (they can choose to fail). On a success, they manage to step off the moving ground and remain where they are.
On a failed save, they move with the ground up to 15 feet to another point of ground or fall {@condition prone} where they are (your choice).

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can choose an additional point on the ground for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Rock Bombardment

m.text: a rare stone worth at least 100gp

entries: You conjure 4 rocks or wrench them from the earth, which hover and rotate in the air around you. Each rock is roughly 1 cubic foot in size.

As a bonus action, you can hurl one of the rocks at a creature within 60 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack roll against that target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage.
While you have at least 2 of the rocks hovering around you, you have half cover.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can conjure an additional rock for each slot level above 3rd.
