The beast is friendly to you and your companions, and obeys your commands. It disappears after 1 hour, or when it falls to 0 hit points. Once this property of the Ioun Stone of Superior Beastcalling has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Redundancy
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.
While this jet black sphere orbits your head, your maximum attunement slots increase by 1.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Flight
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.
While this biconcave crystal orbits your head, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Teleportation
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.
While this flat, pink disc orbits your head, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Ferocity
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.

While this jagged hunk of graphite orbits your head, your unarmed strikes deal {@damage 1d8} force damage, and when you take the {@action Attack} action, you can make a single unarmed strike as a bonus action that turn.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Rejuvenation
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.

While this perfectly spherical blue stone orbits your head, you can use an action to gain the full benefits of a short rest. Once this property of the Ioun Stone of Rejuvenation has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Obstinance
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.
While this translucent gem orbits your head, the first time you would fall to 0 hit points, you fall to 1 instead and take no further damage for the rest of this turn.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Energy
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.

While this bright yellow gem orbits your head, you don't need to sleep, magic can't put you to sleep, and you can gain the benefits of a long rest by spending 4 hours doing light activity, such as meditating, reading, writing, or keeping watch.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Resistance (Rare)
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.

This stone was created with powerful abjuration magic, made to counter a specific type of damage, such as thunder or slashing. While this heavy, silver pebble orbits your head, you have resistance to the damage type it was created to protect against.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Self
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.
While this shining, silver stone orbits your head, you can always see yourself reflected in its body, and you are immune to the {@condition charmed} and {@condition frightened} conditions.

item.name: Ioun Stone of Duplication
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.

This stone orbits your head alongside an intangible, illusory duplicate. While attuned to the Ioun Stone of Duplication, you create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 10 minutes. The illusion appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. On your turn, you can use your movement speed to move the illusion instead, dividing your movement between the two of you as you choose. When you speak, you can choose to speak through yourself or the illusion.

The illusion can't attack, cast spells, or physically interact with objects or creatures. As an action, you can see and hear from your illusion as if you were located where it is, until the start of your next turn. While you are using your senses at the illusion's location, you are {@condition blinded} and {@condition deafened} in regard to your own surroundings. Once you create an illusory duplicate with the Ioun Stone of Duplication, it can't be used to do so again until the next dawn.

item.name: Pyrotechnician's Gloves
entries: While wearing these gloves, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls, and resist fire damage from the {@condition burning|DMSecretWeapon} condition.
In addition, whenever you score a critical hit with a spell attack that deals fire damage, the target of that spell ignites in flame and suffers the {@condition burning|DMSecretWeapon} condition.

item.name: Alchemist's Blue Flame (flask)
entries: This sticky, adhesive fluid ignites when exposed to air. As an action, you can throw this flask up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the alchemist's blue flame as an improvised weapon.
On a hit, the target ignites in flame, and suffers the {@condition burning|DMSecretWeapon} condition.
Alchemist's Blue Flame is magical, and can burn underwater. Being submerged in water does not end the {@condition burning|DMSecretWeapon} condition imparted by this flask.

item.name: Petrified Hand
entries: This petrified hand is clenched into a fist with the middle finger raised, and bubbles with antagonising magic.

As a bonus action, you brandish the hand to take the {@condition Goaded|DMSecretWeapon|Goad} action, targeting a creature within 30 feet that can see you. Once you use this feature of the Petrified Hand, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Backarmour (2nd)
entries: A set of magical Light Armour, known as barkarmour. The barkarmour you create is tailored specifically to connect with your druidic power; only you can wield it. As you advance in levels, the potency of your barkarmour increases, as shown in the {@subclassFeature Druidic Armourcraft|Druid||Barkarmour|DMSecretWeapon|2|DMSecretWeapon|Druidic Armourcraft table} below.

item.name: Backarmour (6th)
entries: A set of magical Light Armour, known as barkarmour. The barkarmour you create is tailored specifically to connect with your druidic power; only you can wield it. As you advance in levels, the potency of your barkarmour increases, as shown in the {@subclassFeature Druidic Armourcraft|Druid||Barkarmour|DMSecretWeapon|2|DMSecretWeapon|Druidic Armourcraft table} below.

item.name: Backarmour (10th)
entries: A set of magical Light Armour, known as barkarmour. The barkarmour you create is tailored specifically to connect with your druidic power; only you can wield it. As you advance in levels, the potency of your barkarmour increases, as shown in the {@subclassFeature Druidic Armourcraft|Druid||Barkarmour|DMSecretWeapon|2|DMSecretWeapon|Druidic Armourcraft table} below.

item.name: Backarmour (14th)
entries: A set of magical Light Armour, known as barkarmour. The barkarmour you create is tailored specifically to connect with your druidic power; only you can wield it. As you advance in levels, the potency of your barkarmour increases, as shown in the {@subclassFeature Druidic Armourcraft|Druid||Barkarmour|DMSecretWeapon|2|DMSecretWeapon|Druidic Armourcraft table} below.

item.name: Backarmour (18th)
entries: A set of magical Light Armour, known as barkarmour. The barkarmour you create is tailored specifically to connect with your druidic power; only you can wield it. As you advance in levels, the potency of your barkarmour increases, as shown in the {@subclassFeature Druidic Armourcraft|Druid||Barkarmour|DMSecretWeapon|2|DMSecretWeapon|Druidic Armourcraft table} below.

item.name: Artillerist's Shield
entries: This mighty shield is fortified with abjuration magic... and a big freaking gun. While attuned to it, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC.

The Artillerist's Shield has 7 charges, and regains {@dice 1d6} expended charges each dawn. As an action, you can expend 1 charge to fire the magical cannon built into the shield, choosing from one of the options below:

items.name: Cannonshot
entries: The cannon magically generates a weighty, iron cannonball before firing. Make a ranged attack roll against a creature within 120 feet. On a hit, the cannonshot deals {@damage 3d10} bludgeoning damage, and the creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength saving throw or fall {@condition prone}.

items.name: Flametongue
entries: The cannon expels a jet of flame in a 15-foot cone. Creatures in that area must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

item.name: Mask of the Greatwyrm
entries: This mask bears the visage of a snarling dragon. While wearing it, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks, and you have darkvision out to 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range is extended by 60 feet instead.

entries.name: Special Property: Greatwyrm Assembled
entries: While attuned to the Mask of the Greatwyrm, {@item Sword of the Greatwyrm|DMSecretWeapon}, and {@item Shield of the Greatwyrm|DMSecretWeapon}, you can use an action to cast {@spell draconic soul|DMSecretWeapon}, without a spell slot or components. When you cast it in this way, you can use Constitution for your spellcasting ability, it doesn't require {@status concentration}, and it lasts for the duration.
Once this property of the mask has been used, it cannot be used again for {@dice 1d4} days.

item.name: Shield of the Greatwyrm
entries: This shield was forged in dragonfire, and bears the gilded crest of a dragon.

When you take fire damage, you can use a reaction to draw upon the draconic magic of this shield. Until the end of your next turn: you resist fire damage (including against the triggering damage), and any creature within 10 feet of you that makes an attack roll against you takes {@damage 1d6} fire damage.

item.name: Lantern of the Crimson Drake
entries: This ornate lantern bears the head of a dragon atop its case. A creature can use an action to light the lantern, upon which the magical fire within the lantern burns indefinitely, even when starved of oxygen or underwater. While the lantern is uncovered, it sheds bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for a further 15 feet.

A creature attuned to the lantern can use an action to blow the flame out. When it does so, the light is extinguished as a jet of flame issues from the mouth of the dragon atop the lantern in a 15-foot cone. Creatures in that area must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

item.name: Helm of the Fathomless
entries: This helm is adorned with interlocking tentacles. While attuned to it, you have a +1 bonus to your AC, you have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed, and you can breathe underwater.

Additionally, you can speak telepathically with any creature within 300 feet that has a swimming speed, granting them the ability to understand your language and telepathically communicate with you in return. As long as you have not dealt damage to a creature with a swimming speed, you also have advantage on Charisma checks made to interact with it.

entries.name: Special Property: Fathomless Call
entries: This helm has 8 charges. While attuned to the Helm of the Fathomless, {@item Trident of the Fathomless|DMSecretWeapon}, and {@item Shield of the Fathomless|DMSecretWeapon}, you can use a bonus action and expend 1 charge to summon a Huge, spectral tentacle in an unoccupied space within 60 feet of you. When the tentacle appears, and as a bonus action on each of your turns, you can telepathically command it to ensnare or bludgeon a Huge or smaller creature within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a {@dc 18} Strength saving throw or take {@damage 4d10} bludgeoning damage if you choose bludgeon, or become {@condition grappled} by the tentacle for the next minute if you choose ensnare. The tentacle can only grapple one creature at a time. A grappled creature can use its action to reattempt the saving throw, escaping on a success. The tentacle remains for 1 minute, after which time it vanishes.
When the last charge of the helm has been expended, it must be submerged in seawater for 8 days, after which time it regains all expended charges.

item.name: Trident of the Fathomless
entries: While attuned to this magical trident, you can speak a command word (no action required) to have it dissolve into seawater and reappear in your empty hand. The trident must be on the same plane of existence for you to use this effect.
You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the Trident of the Fathomless.

Additionally, when you take the {@action Attack} action, you can stamp the trident into the ground at your feet in place of one attack. If you do, choose a 10-foot square within 60 feet of you. That area becomes coated in slippery seaweed for the next minute. The area is difficult terrain, and the first time on a turn a creature enters that area or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition prone}.

If you are underwater, you can raise the trident over your head in place of one attack. If you do, a 5-foot cube of water centered on a point you choose within 60 feet boils, dealing {@damage 3d10} fire damage to all creatures within that area. This damage ignores fire resistance.

item.name: Shield of the Fathomless
entries: This shield bears the crest of a kraken. While underwater, it has the properties of an {@item animated shield}.

Additionally, if a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use a reaction to conjure a torrent of water that blasts from the shield. The triggering creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength saving throw or take {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage and be pushed back 20 feet.

item.name: Vial of Kraken's Ink
entries: This vial contains a jet-black, alchemical mixture known as Kraken's Ink, which has several unique properties. The vial has enough ink for 8 uses. As a bonus action, you can uncork the vial and use it in one of the following ways:

items.name: Body Paint
entries: A creature painted with Kraken's Ink gains a swimming speed equal to their walking speed and can breathe underwater for the next 8 hours.

items.name: Poison
entries: You can apply the Kraken's Ink to food or drink. It is odorless and tasteless, but jet-black in colour. A creature who ingests the Kraken's Ink must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be unable to breathe outside of water for next 8 hours.

items.name: Upturn
entries: While underwater, upturning the vial causes it to form a cloud of black ink in a 20-foot radius. That area is heavily obscured to all creatures, except those painted with Kraken's Ink (see Body Paint). A strong current disperses the cloud, which otherwise disappears at the end of your next turn.

item.name: Rune of Explosive Damage
entries: This magical rune can be applied to any weapon with a damage die of {@dice 2d4}, {@dice 1d10}, {@dice 2d6}, or {@dice 1d12}.

When a weapon blessed with this magical rune rolls maximum damage for its damage roll (for example, when you roll a 12 on the die using a {@dice 1d12} weapon), you can roll one additional weapon damage die and add the result to the damage dealt by that attack.

item.name: Rune of Spiral Criticals
entries: This magical rune has 6 charges, and regains all 6 charges each dawn. It can be applied to any weapon.

When a weapon blessed with this magical rune rolls maximum damage for any damage roll (for example, when you roll two 4s on the dice using a {@dice 2d4} weapon), you can expend 1 charge to roll the damage again, adding the result to the damage dealt by that attack. If the damage roll triggered by expending a charge of this rune also rolls maximum damage, you can expend a further charge to repeat the process.

item.name: Rune of Critical Savagery
entries: This magical rune can be applied to any spellcasting focus.

When a creature rolls a natural 1 on their saving throw against a spell you cast, they take additional force damage equal to thrice the level of the spell slot you expended to cast that spell + your proficiency bonus.

item.name: Rune of Critical Salvation
entries: This magical rune can be applied to any spellcasting focus.

When you roll maximum when rolling dice to restore hit points to a creature, this rune vitalises them still further. You can choose to grant the target temporary hit points equal to the total rolled on the dice, or end up to two conditions of your choice affecting that target.

item.name: Rune of Critical Hope
entries: This magical rune can be tattooed onto one's body. It has 4 charges, and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges each dawn.
Whenever you roll a natural 1 on an attack roll or saving throw, you can expend 1 charge from this rune to gain a point of heroic inspiration.

item.name: Rune of the Critical Counter
entries: This magical rune can be applied to any armor or shield. It has 4 charges, and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges each dawn.
When a creature scores a critical hit against you, you can use a reaction to expend 1 charge from this rune and grant yourself resistance to the damage of that attack.

item.name: Islander Hat
entries: While attuned to this item, the wearer gains advantage on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks and a bonus to any initiative roll equal to their Charisma modifier (maximum of +3).

item.name: Islander's Sacrificial Sword
entries: This ancient longsword glimmers with fiery magic.
On the first successful hit against an object or enemy creature each turn, this weapon deals an additional {@damage 1d4} fire damage.
In addition, while attuned to this blade, the wielder has advantage on Constitution saving throws to resist extreme cold.

item.name: Potion of Water's Welcome
entries: It lasts for 24 hours. The Water's Welcome Potion gives each player a swim speed equal to their walking speed, 60 feet of {@sense darkvision}, the ability to speak and breathe underwater, and an immunity to the crushing pressure of the depths.

item.name: Tidal Trident
entries: The Tidal Trident flows with a strange magic, eager to be wielded. You gain proficiency with this weapon once attuned to it.

item.name: Immortal Raven's Feather
entries: This feather has three charges. After the last charge has been expended, the feather ceases to be magical.

A creature holding the feather can use a bonus action and expend one charge to gain a fly speed equal to their walking speed for 10 minutes. A creature holding the feather that makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw can use a reaction and expend one charge to add {@dice 1d6} to their result.

item.name: Superior Ring of Spell Storing
entries: This ring stores spells cast into it, holding them until the attuned wearer uses them. The ring can store up to 5 levels worth of spells at a time. When found, it contains {@dice 1d6 - 1} levels of stored spells chosen by the DM.

Any creature can cast a spell of 1st through 9th level into the ring by touching the ring as the spell is cast. The spell has no effect, other than to be stored in the ring. If the ring can't hold the spell, the spell is expended without effect. The level of the slot used to cast the spell determines how much space it uses.

While wearing this ring, you can cast any spell stored in it. The spell uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster, but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell. The spell cast from the ring is no longer stored in it, freeing up space.

item.name: Aria's Music Box
entries: As an action, you can open this music box, which generates a soothing, magical song that lasts for 1 minute, or until you close the box as a bonus action. While the song plays, creatures within a 10-foot radius of the box have advantage on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws. Once opened, the box cannot be opened again until the following dawn.

itemProperty.name: Trial
entries: These magic items have one baseline ability and one hidden ability. In order to access the hidden ability, the wielder must complete a trial over the course of the campaign. Attuning to the weapon instantly makes the wielder aware of the trial.

Several trial items make reference to "worthy" enemies. These weapons do not recognise mindless, challengeless slaughter as counting towards completing their trials. For example, hunting common rats with the weapon would not count towards completing a trial, defending oneself from a hostile kobold would.

itemGroup.name: Bracers of Unyielding Fury
entries: To attune to these bracers, you must rage while wearing them. The bracers then painlessly bind to your flesh, and cannot be parted from you without your consent.
While attuned to the bracers, your unarmed strikes deal {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage and you gain a bonus to your melee attack and damage rolls. This bonus is determined by the bracer's rarity.
In addition, if you would be killed or reduced to 0 hit points while raging, your rage ends and you fall to 1 hit point instead. This property of the bracers can't be used again until the next dawn.
items: Bracers of Unyielding Fury (+1)|DMSecretWeapon
Bracers of Unyielding Fury (+2)|DMSecretWeapon
Bracers of Unyielding Fury (+3)|DMSecretWeapon

itemGroup.name: Ioun Stone
entries: An {@i Ioun stone} is named after Ioun, a god of knowledge and prophecy revered on some worlds. Many types of {@i Ioun stone} exist, each type a distinct combination of shape and color.

When you use an action to toss one of these stones into the air, the stone orbits your head at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet and confers a benefit to you. Thereafter, another creature must use an action to grasp or net the stone to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful {@dc 24} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and stow the stone, ending its effect.
A stone has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. It is considered to be an object that is being worn while it orbits your head.

Ioun Stone of Resistance (Legendary)|DMSecretWeapon
Ioun Stone of Beastcalling|DMSecretWeapon
Ioun Stone of Superior Beastcalling|DMSecretWeapon

Ioun Stone of Rejuvenation|DMSecretWeapon
Ioun Stone of Obstinance|DMSecretWeapon

Ioun Stone of Resistance (Rare)|DMSecretWeapon
