adventure.name: Issue #42: Pirates on the Azure Skies

entries.name: Introduction
entries: This is an adventure designed for 4–6 Level 4 player characters using the Dungeons and Dragons 5e system. The player characters are travelling from the continent of Leeestros to Havernackle across the sea, when their ship is destroyed in a freak, terrifying storm. After being knocked unconscious, they wake up alone but for each other on an island and look up to find a group of over 40 heavily armed natives standing over them (Fig. 1).
One native wearing an extremely large hat and carrying an impressive, clearly magical sword approaches them, and speaks in perfect {@language Common}:

"Hello there chaps! I'm fairly happy to see you alive. You've washed up on my island here, and as such, you are technically my property. You see, we're cannibals, we like to eat people (love it, actually) and you are people so... that's probably going to be a thing. I understand it might seem frightening or strange to you, but I do ask that you please respect our customs and don't judge or resist!

However, tonight is the night of our great festival, Bakeoffia, and our chef recently poisoned himself by accident. As such, I'm open to cutting you a deal; if you accept, we'll agree not to eat you for at least the next 24 hours!"
The cannibal leader will explain that the party must prepare the traditional Bakeoffia meal themselves (a stew called Squibnumbs) for the whole village, or be eaten.

The party has until nightfall to prepare the stew. The Islanders will not harm them until that time, and if the meal is satisfactory, will even help make a raft for the party to leave the island on. Should the party fail to make Squibnumbs, or produce an unsatisfactory version of the stew, they will be devoured as punishment.

The island leader will give the party directions to the three places the ingredients can be harvested from, wish them luck, and ask that they try not to eat anything too fattening themselves across the day, in case the islanders need to eat them later, as his husband is aiming to avoid "empty calories".
To prepare Squibnumbs, the party will need 3 ingredients:
Red Hot Chilli Peppers from The Mountaintop Temple ({@adventure Fig. 3|CannibalCookoff|2|Fig 3: Mountaintop Temple})
Fresh Seaweed from the Shores of the Bay ({@adventure Fig. 4|CannibalCookoff|2|Fig 4: Shore of the Bay})
Sweet, Sweet Plumbs of the Havoc Tree, located in the Open Glade ({@adventure Fig. 5|CannibalCookoff|2|Fig 5: The Open Glade})

entries.name: The Village
entries: The tribe leader will guide the party members to his community's village. ({@adventure Fig. 2|CannibalCookoff|2|Fig 2: The Village})

From here, the players are within one hour's brisk walk from The Open Glade (see {@adventure Chapter 2|CannibalCookoff|0|The Open Glade}), Shores of the Bay (see {@adventure Chapter 3|CannibalCookoff|0|The Shore of the Box}), and The Mountaintop Temple (see {@adventure Chapter 4|CannibalCookoff|0|Mountaintop Temple}). These are the three locations of the ingredients they must gather for Squibnumbs. They may gather the ingredients in any order they choose. Once the players have chosen a location to head to, navigate to the relevant chapter to continue the story. After completing each chapter, the party returns to the village where the ingredients can be stored in preparation for the cooking of Squibnumbs that night.

Upon arriving in the village, the players will see locals going about their business. In particular, their attention is drawn to three different groups of villagers with problems. The players may attempt to help in each instance, and if they do, the villagers will reward the players with information. The problems are:

entries.name: Lost Lizard
entries: A villager's pet Lizard is caught up in a baby Havoc Tree. A {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check is needed to climb up and grab the lizard as the tree flails around. Alternatively, a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check may be able to coax the lizard down. On a failed check the player will be unsuccessful and the lizard will scuttle further up the tree, becoming lost in the foliage. From here it will be unreachable for hours until the tree calms down. If the players pass the check, the villager will thank them, and tell them that the best Sweet, Sweet Plumbs of the Havoc Tree are the smaller, darker purple ones, not the larger, brighter ones.

entries.name: Spice Ain't Nice!
entries: A gruff, grumpy elder villager is complaining loudly of an upset stomach. He says that he'd have eaten the party already were he not feeling so bad. If a party member does any action that causes him to regain a hit point ({@spell Cure Wounds}, Lay on Hands, {@spell Healing Word}, or {@spell Goodberry} for example), it will ease his stomach. He will thank the party, and tell them he had stomach pains from harvesting Red Hot Chilli Peppers too early in the morning. They are best plucked in the early evening, so getting those last would be a good idea!

entries.name: Pro-Gamer Move
entries: Two younger islanders are playing a spirited game that looks not unlike chess, except the pieces are made from lobster and crab meat, and the pieces are eaten when taken. A {@dc 14} Intelligence check is needed to win a game. They will each play one game, after which all the pieces will have been eaten. If the players should win, the Islanders will share a secret that the best meals are always cooked in one of the old shells of the Fussy Hermit Crab (who goes through several shells a day), so picking one of his old shells from the beach to use as a pot might be a good idea.

entries.name: The Open Glade
entries: The journey to the Open Glade is gentle and pleasant. There are no difficult obstacles to navigate, no monsters to avoid and the path seems well worn and safe. That is, until the players come to a surging river, beyond which lies a wide, open glade. ({@adventure Fig. 5|CannibalCookoff|2|Fig 5: The Open Glade}) Here, the path abruptly turns left, but the quarry the party seeks lies beyond the stream. Large rocks and boulders litter the glade, each with a titanic impact crater around them, indicating that they struck the earth with incredible force. Besides the grass itself, not a single thing lives in the field aside from a huge, animated {@creature Havoc Tree|DMSecretWeapon}.

Even from this distance, the party can see it writhing and twisting, as if it were caught in the midst of a hurricane. They see too, hanging from its higher branches, dozens of thick, juicy Sweet, Sweet Plumbs of all hues and sizes.

entries.name: The Havoc Tree
entries: The moment the players enter The Open Glade, the Havoc Tree will become aware of their presence. Roll Initiative. The {@creature Havoc Tree|DMSecretWeapon} will use its actions to attack the party as soon as it is dealt damage, or the moment a party member steps within 90 ft. of it. Otherwise, it will Ready its action to use Casting Rock the moment a party member steps within 90 ft.
Upon reducing the Havoc Tree to 0 Hit Points, it becomes {@condition Paralyzed} for {@dice 1d4} hours.

The party may now gather its Sweet, Sweet Plumbs. If they so choose, the party may climb further up the tree to access the smaller, darker fruit. If the party does not specify what Plumbs they take, it is assumed they gather the easier to access, larger Plumbs nearer the bottom.

entries.name: The Shore of the Box
entries: The journey to The Shores of the Bay is taxing, no matter the route taken. It requires either crossing many stagnant, waterlogged marshes, or taking a coastal route and traversing rocky coves with sharp, slippery rocks.

If the players take the marsh route, they each must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 1d8} Poison damage and have Disadvantage on saves to resist the {@condition Poisoned} condition for the next 24 hours.
If the players take the coastal route, they each must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw while crossing the coves, or else slip and take {@damage 2d8} Slashing damage.

Upon reaching The Shores of the Bay (Fig. 4), the players will be greeted with the sight of the precious Fresh Seaweed, alongside some hulking, crustacean monsters feeding on it. They also see many discarded Shells of the Old, Fussy Hermit Crab scattered along the sands, some of which are large enough to fit the whole party inside, others as small as a frying pan.

entries.name: Of Moisters and Men
entries: The {@creature Moisters|DMSecretWeapon} feasting on the seaweed seem very preoccupied with their meal. Periodically one will stop and raise its hideous maw to the breeze, before diving back into the feast. The party may attempt to steal some of the Fresh Seaweed without the Moisters noticing. Alternatively, they may choose to engage the Moisters in combat. It's likely that an all-out attack will take the creatures by surprise.

If the party attempts to steal the Fresh Seaweed via {@skill Stealth}, have the entire party roll a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, taking the average of all rolls as their stealth result. If the party take appropriate measures to conceal themselves (such as hiding in one of the large, vacant shells), you may have them add {@dice 1d4} to the final roll. On a successful group roll ({@dc 14}), the party successfully sneak up to the Fresh Seaweed and collect some. They then must make another collective Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) roll ({@dc 14}) to retreat from the area without drawing the attention of the Moisters. If either check fails, the Moisters will immediately detect the player characters and attack.

If the players choose to engage the Moisters directly in combat without stealth, the Moisters are surprised. The number of Moisters in this battle is equal to the number of player characters divided by two (rounded down).

entries.name: Mountaintop Temple
entries: The climb to the Mountaintop Temple is a potentially deadly task in its own right. The heat is intense, thick, hazy fumes linger in the air, and clambering up the sheer rock face is arduous. As the climb continues, the billowing fumes become so dark and thick that the area grows shrouded in permanent Dim Light. Each player must make a {@dc 9} Constitution saving throw, taking 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion} on a failed save while climbing. At last the party reaches a mountainside plateau, where they come to the temple where the Red Hot Chilli Peppers grow. However, many things besides the Red Hot Chilli Peppers grow and live in this long abandoned temple.

entries.name: You've Got To Be Kitten Me...
entries: Immediately after reaching the temple ({@adventure Fig. 3|CannibalCookoff|2|Fig 3: Mountaintop Temple}), the party come face to face with a {@creature Spice Leopard|DMSecretWeaponAdventures}, and a swarm of {@creature Giant Buzzer|Giant Buzzer|Giant Buzzers}. The number of Giant Buzzers is equal to the number of player characters minus 1. The party can see some Red Hot Chilli Peppers growing in the heart of the temple, but there's no way of reaching them without a fight. Roll Initiative.
The return trip with the peppers is a little easier than the climb up the volcano, and the party manages to find a way down without requiring another Constitution save against the heat.

entries.name: The Meal
entries: After gathering all the ingredients, the party returns to the village to cook Squibnumbs. As the party all help cook, they roll a {@dice d20} as a collective with Advantage, using the highest Wisdom modifier of the group to give them their final result.
Extra modifiers:

items: If the party harvested the smaller, dark purple Sweet, Sweet Plumbs of the Havoc Tree, they may add {@dice 1d6} to the cooking check.
If the party cooked the meal in an old shell of the Old, Fussy Hermit Crab, they may add {@dice 1d6} to the cooking check.
If the party harvested the Red Hot Chilli Peppers as the final ingredient, they may add {@dice 1d6} to the cooking check.
If any player is proficient in {@item Cook's Utensils|PHB}, the party may add their proficiency bonus to the cooking check.

At the DM's discretion, extra modifiers may be added to reward party creativity. Any intuitive thinking by the party may add a further {@dice 1d4} to the check. For example, using the spell {@spell Goodberry} to add a tasty additional ingredient, or {@spell Prestidigitation} to flavour the final product may justify this bonus.

entries: No matter what the final score is, the meal is sufficient to stop the party being eaten. If they get a 10 or below, the cannibal leader will thank them for the meal, and quietly remark to himself that in future, he'd be better off just eating the prisoners immediately.
On an 11–20, the cannibal leader will thank the party honestly, and offer them a very stylish {@item Islander Hat|DMSecretWeapon}.

On a 20+, the leader and the entire community will thank the players, and swear off humanoid meat forever, instead setting up an expedition party among their numbers to make the Squibnumbs in the same way every night. He will give the party the {@item Islander's Sacrificial Sword|DMSecretWeapon}, a magical {@item Longsword|PHB} that deals an additional {@damage 1d4} Fire damage on the first hit each turn: "Cooks the meal as you carve it!"

The next day, the Islanders present the party with a raft and sails with which to escape the island. They set off with a strong following wind, and reach the continent of Havernackle by sunfall, no worse for wear. Nobody believes their story.
The End.

data.name: The Trapmaker's Garden Puzzles
entries: These puzzles were recovered from an old, haunted music store, {@i The Lonesome Tromboner}! Dragon Tier supporters may remember the full notes on that little adventure from a few months ago. Luckily the team that went in made it out alive, and brought details of the malevolent spirit's deadly game of riddles back to us for use in our own death traps. For science, of course.

entries.name: The Riddle of Inspiration
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Medium
I seek she who inspires my sound,
Or to think on a question,
where an answer might be found...

entries.name: Solution
entries: The solution to the puzzle is option 3, spelling out the word "Muse".

entries.name: Suggested Puzzle Encounter
entries: Have the runes and the riddle words appear on a wall that the party must pass in order to move forward.
Accompanying the puzzle is some eerie, ethereal music, which plays in a sinister but enchanting melody, making the party feel a little drowsy...

Every 60 seconds (real time) the party gains a point of {@condition Exhaustion}. If available, a minute timer or hourglass on the table to visually show the passage of time can be very effective in heightening the pressure on your players. An incorrect guess adds a point of {@condition Exhaustion}, unless the PCs have 4 or more points of {@condition Exhaustion}, in which case nothing happens.

Upon completing the riddle, the music stops. The party loses any points of {@condition Exhaustion} they have accrued, and the runes glow a blinding, blue light. In a burst of luminous energy, the wall shutters, and the way forward is revealed.

entries.name: Hints
entries: Good ways to deliver hints to a party include via an NPC, through successful Intelligence checks their characters make, or through Intelligence ({@skill Investigation})/Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks to find notes or carvings left by other, long dead adventurers.

entries.name: Hint 1:
entries: Can you hear that music play? It's dangerous, but it's tied to the riddle. The answer may have something to do with music.

entries.name: Hint 2:
entries: The runes on the wall almost look like letters within boxes! What could they be spelling?

entries.name: The Riddle of Foresight
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Easy
The following riddle might adorn a door, or chest, or be given by an NPC. In any case, the party must offer the correct answer in order to progress.
Pronounced With One Letter But Written With Three
Two Different Letters Are Used To Write Me.
I Can Be Many Colours; Black, Blue, Brown, Or Green.
What am I?

entries.name: Solution
entries: The answer to this puzzle is "Eye".

You may wish to give an alternate route around a puzzle, or a forfeit if the party fails to answer it. One simple but effective forfeit is that the party must make an offering of gold to progress instead. Another is that, upon failure to solve, they suffer the effects of a hex until the next dawn, reducing their hit point maximum by {@dice 2d8}.

data.name: The Stalking Death
entries: This is an adventure for 4–6 Level 7–8 Player Characters. It should take 1–2 sessions to complete, depending on player choices, efficiency, and optional encounters.

entries.name: Premise
entries: The party has arrived in Haversham ({@adventure Map 1|TheStalkingDeath|2|Adventure Map 1}), a small and famously beautiful farming town on the edge of a dense, forest wilderness. However, the usually charming and cheerful area has been upturned. Many wealthy families are packing up all their possessions and evacuating, panicked guards run back and forth, and the poorer families with nowhere to go wander the streets, desperately praying to their gods.
After 600 years of tranquillity, the dreaded {@creature The Chucabyrant|DMSecretWeapon|Chucabyrant}, "The Stalking Death", has returned.
Possible hooks to involve the party in the adventure include:

items: A PC with the {@background Soldier} background is recognised by Glothful, a grizzled and elderly dwarf soldier who retired to manage the guard at Haversham.

A PC with the {@background Noble} background would be familiar with Prospero, the famously extravagant noble who owns property in the town. His usually hearty demeanour has drained away, and he is afraid.
A PC with the {@background Folk Hero} background is approached by the town Mayor, Bronzeback, who desperately requests their help.

entries: The familiar PC will give the party the following information.

Until now, the village of Haversham has been protected by The Temple of the Four Elements, a shrine to the Gods that closes the gap between the Material Plane and other planes of existence. However, recently the temple has fallen into darkness, its great magical energy sapped away, and nobody has been able to get in through its ancient protections to investigate.

Without its protection, Fiends have begun to creep back into the world, slaughtering livestock and murdering those who venture beyond the walls. The {@creature The Chucabyrant|DMSecretWeapon|Chucabyrant}, "The Stalking Death", has been spotted, and the villagers have taken it as an omen that the village will soon fall to destruction.
The party is tasked with investigating the temple to try and rekindle its magic and in doing so banish the Chucabyrant from the Material Plane.

entries.name: Journey to the Temple
entries: The journey to the Temple of the Four Elements from Haversham is a harsh trek through the dense wilderness. A successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check is needed to not lose oneself in the dark forest. If the party gets lost, the journey takes an additional 4 hours, and the prolonged exposure to the magical forest weighs on their spirits, reducing their movement speed by 10 feet until they complete a Long Rest.

If you choose, you may have the party face a {@creature Grizzlowl|DMSecretWeapon} en route. Should the party fight and defeat it, they will find the wreckage of an old caravan the beast had raided, containing three {@item Potion of Greater Healing||Potions of Greater Healing} and 1,000 gold's worth of rare gems.

entries.name: The Locked Door
entries: Upon reaching the temple, the party finds the entrance barred by an impassable stone door. On it are carved various letters, and as they approach, they see words etched into the stone around the door.
This puzzle is discussed in greater detail in the {@adventure The Rune Door|TheStalkingDeath|1|The Rune Door} section, which includes hints to offer the party assistance in solving the puzzle.
Upon giving the correct answer to the puzzle, "Zenith", the door will open, and the party can enter the ancient shrine.

entries.name: What Lies Within...
entries: Inside, the party finds a truly ancient sight. The foundations are crudely hewn from the earth; it is a structure closer to a cavern than a shrine, save for peculiar markings dotted around, and a colossal, intricate structure hanging from the ceiling ({@adventure Map 2|TheStalkingDeath|2|Adventure Map 2}).

On each of the four walls the PCs see a symbol: the elemental insignias of Fire, Water, Earth, and Air. At the far end of the room they see a pit, and on the floor, there is a grid, with many symbols scattered upon it. The cavernous roof above them twists into a great mechanism, with four huge, stone turbines hanging down. They are not moving.

entries.name: DM Note
entries: See the {@adventure Four Elements Floor Puzzle|TheStalkingDeath|1|Four Elements Floor Puzzle} for more information on running this floor puzzle and the behaviour of the elemental tiles.
Before the party has time to act, the door slams shut behind them, and three twisted, hideous fiends pull themselves forward from the shadows.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: DM Note
entries: When running this encounter, be sure to pay attention to where the party stands, and note the relevant magical effect that takes place should at any point all four tiles of one element be stood upon.

entries.name: Igniting the Spark
entries: Upon defeating the last of the fiends, the party are left alone in the temple. The door behind them remains closed, and the only clues to progress are the symbols on the walls and floor.
The following effects take place if all four tiles of one element are stepped on at once:

rows: A flame ignites in a pit at the front of the room.
A torrent of water falls into the pit below.
Gusts of wind blow upwards from the floor, over the pit.
A great clay dome falls from the ceiling on top of the pit. It strikes the ground with a deafening crash and instantly shatters.

entries: These symbols need to be activated in the correct order for the temple to activate: Fire, Air, Earth, Water.
See {@adventure Four Elements Floor Puzzle|TheStalkingDeath|1|Four Elements Floor Puzzle} for more information on running this puzzle, and detailed descriptions of how the mechanism operates.

entries.name: The Stalking Death
entries: Upon completing the puzzle, the water boils in the great stone basin, and the magical steam rises up and slowly begins to turn the turbines. The temple begins to hum with ancient magic, but just as it does so, a blood-curdling screech echoes from outside.

The doors of the temple are smashed open from outside, and before the party stands a hideous, four-legged fiend. Horns protrude from its head, bristling hair extends down its back, and its eyes glow a vicious, hateful red. From its nostrils an unending, poisonous, purple haze billows forth.
The {@creature The Chucabyrant|DMSecretWeapon|Chucabyrant} lets out another screech, and charges toward the party.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: The Temple of the Four Elements
entries: As the {@creature The Chucabyrant|DMSecretWeapon|Chucabyrant} is defeated it dissolves into a cloud of hideous, purple smoke. As the hum of the temple grows more powerful, the cloud is whisked upward towards the twirling stone turbines, and with a final, haunting screech the Chucabyrant is banished by the powerful, ancient magic.

With the temple activated, the bridge to the spirit world that had been opened is closed again. As its powerful Abjuration magic weaves through the forest once more, the Temple of the Four Elements stands guard over the people of Haversham.

Upon returning to the village with the news, the party are greeted with rapturous praise and thanks. They receive 6,000 gold in donations from the townsfolk, but their work is surely not over. Other fiends may have slipped through the crack between the realms while it was open, and the mystery of how the temple came to be disrupted in the first place is yet to be solved...

data.name: The Trapmaker's Garden Puzzles
entries: These puzzles were recovered and studied by our clean-up squad who went in and dealt with the aftermath of a party of adventurers and their dealings at The Temple of Four Elements in Haversham. You can find more details on that little escapade in {@adventure The Stalking Death|TheStalkingDeath|0}.

entries.name: The Rune Door
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Medium

This puzzle adorns a door, barring entry to all those who cannot find the answer. On a failed guess, the door will let loose a blast of Psychic energy, forcing all those within 60 feet to make a {@dc 13} Intelligence saving throw, taking {@damage 3d6} Psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: DM Note
entries: You may wish to increase the damage and difficulty check to avoid the Psychic damage when running this puzzle for higher-level player characters.
On the door, letters are written in the following pattern:
As the party approaches, a {@spell Magic Mouth} appears on the door, and speaks the following words:
The first letter is the last of the top,
The second falls, and back two,
Continue like this to find my answer, six letters true
If you move past the beginning, rise up to the end and keep going,
Answer my riddle: I'm the Apex, All-knowing.
Give up? Never fear, clues may be near,
Search far and wide, and find the key to inside
Alternatively, the words of the riddle may be hewn into the wall around the doorframe.

entries.name: Solution
entries: The answer to this riddle is the word {@i Zenith}, meaning apex, or pinnacle.

The first letter is the last letter on the first line. To find the second letter, fall down a line and move back two spaces, and so forth. If you would move beyond the "start" of a line by moving backwards, you continue through the end of the line above.
Following this pattern you get the letters: Z, E, N, I, T, H.

entries.name: Player Hints
entries: If your party is struggling, consider giving these hints through an NPC, or through successful Intelligence checks.

Alternatively, following on from the puzzle's closing lines, you can deliver hints in the form of scrawled notes left behind by previous adventurers that the party can find with successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks.

items.name: Hint 1:
entries: The 3rd line says "six letters true"; perhaps the answer is a six-letter word, formed from the letters on the door?

items.name: Hint 2:
entries: "The first letter is the last of the top"... Could that be a reference to the last letter of the top line on the door?

items.name: Hint 3:
entries: "The second falls, and back two"... Could that mean to find the second letter you fall down a line and move back two spaces?

entries.name: Four Elements Floor Puzzle
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Easy
This is a great puzzle for when PCs need to activate or unlock something. On each of the four walls a symbol is etched, representing Fire, Earth, Water, and Air.
These symbols match symbols on the floor, as shown below.
When all four symbols are stood on at once, an elemental effect takes place.

In this puzzle, the elements need to be activated in a specific order to activate the magical mechanisms of the Temple of the Four Elements. At the very top of the room, hanging from the ceiling are great, stone turbines. They need to be turned to activate the temple's ancient magic.
The following effects take place if all four tiles of one element are stepped on at once:

rows: A flame ignites in a pit at the front of the room.
A torrent of water falls into the pit below.
Gusts of wind blow upwards from the floor, over the pit.
A great clay dome falls from the ceiling on top of the pit. It strikes the ground with a deafening crash and instantly shatters.

entries.name: Solution
entries: First, Fire needs to be activated by having all four player characters standing on the Fire tiles on the floor. This ignites the flame in the pit.
Next, Air needs to be activated, which fans the existing fire and creates a cushion of air above it. If Air is activated before Fire, the fire will be unable to light in the gale.

Third is Earth. If Air has been activated, the dome falls but is caught in the cushion of air, levitating and forming a great, clay bowl. If Earth is activated before Air, it will fall to the ground and shatter.

Finally, Water, which is collected in the dome, fills it. If Fire is active, the water boils, producing steam and turning the turbines at the top. If Water is activated before the clay dome conjured by Earth is hovering above the fire, the water will douse the flames below. If the puzzle is activated in the incorrect order but the conditions don't lead it to automatically reset, it will magically reset after 30 seconds.

entries.name: Combined Challenge
entries: This puzzle works well when combined with a combat encounter. Forcing the party to battle against an infinitely recurring onslaught of monsters will force them to solve the riddle as they fight. By positioning themselves intelligently while fighting, they can activate the floor and cause the encounter to end.

data.name: The Dead Tavern
entries: A non-linear, role play focused one shot of drinking, gambling, bar fights and thievery designed for 4–6 level 10 PCs!

Due to the non-linear nature of this story, I recommend you read this adventure in full and familiarize yourself with the layout of The Dead Tavern and the locations of key NPCs, potential combat encounters and objects. For your convenience, all important areas and objects are marked on the DM's Treasure Map on the following page for quick reference!

entries.name: Premise
entries: The party has set out to steal from the hoard of the Dread Pirate Captain Old Tom!

Before the session begins, give each party member an object they seek to claim from the table below, or have them invent one of their own (the object should be small enough to carry in their arms). The table also contains the suggested location for each item, and the recommended method to steal it.

The party will need to discover these locations and methods by exploring the Tavern and interacting with NPCs. As always, feel free to adapt the adventure as it progresses to reward your player's creativity and good dice rolls.

entries.caption: Table of Old Tom's Treasures
rows: The Crystal Urn of the Pirate Ghost Bronzebeard
Pick the lock ({@dc 15}), Enter, and Trick/Defeat Old Tom
The Hidden Storage Base (Entrance on Floor 2)
Find the entrance to the Storage passage.
Defeat/Placate the Ghost Pirate Bronzeback in the Cellar
Cause a distraction in the bar and make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check ({@dc 11}) to take it in the confusion.
A Parrot That Knows Too Much
Trick/Defeat Old Tom and make a Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check ({@dc 12})
Just, Like, a REALLY Nice Pirate Hat
Get Magni so drunk he falls asleep and take the hat.

entries.name: The DM's Treasure Map
entries: This adventure takes place in a tavern which has three floors. Here are the maps annotated with key locations, NPCs and Items, which may be useful to you as you run this adventure. You can find printable, gridded maps to use for your players at the end of this adventure.

entries.name: Old Tom's Dead Tavern
entries: Old Tom's Dead Tavern is a watering hole for pirates, criminals and undead. Human, Dwarf, Orc, and Zombie gather to drink, gamble and brawl. As the party enters the Tavern, they see numerous characters scattered all across the bar ({@adventure Dead Tavern - Map Layer 1|TheDeadTavern|0|The DM's Treasure Map}). They will also instantly see First Mate Magni, wearing a splendid pirate hat, and also spot a beautiful, jewel-encrusted cutlass hanging from the wall above the bar.

From here, the party's actions will dictate the flow of this adventure. They must interact with the occupants of the tavern to gather information and open up avenues to enable their heist. Other objects they may need to search for the old fashioned way.

In all social encounters, the party must make a skill check. A successful check will lead the NPC to reveal some information that will aid the party in claiming their desired object. Here is a list of suggested social encounters and hints to offer the party.

rows: A couple of pirates are having a tense arm wrestling match. (Floor 1)
The PC enters the arm wrestling contest. Strength ({@skill Athletics}) ({@dc 15})
"You got lucky this time, punk. Try boasting about this and I'll grab that Blunderbuss from the cellar and blow your head off with it, curse be damned!"
A skeleton is happily singing to himself with a flagon of ale. (Floor 1)
The PCs join the skeleton for a drink, and ask for information. Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) ({@dc 11})
"You think I can't handle my ale? First Mate Magni is far worse! Two drinks and he's out cold!"
A shifty looking Dwarven Pirate and Undead are having a quiet conversation (Floor 1)
Eavesdrop on them! (Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) {@dc 12})
"The Egg is down the hidden passage at the top right of the downstairs bar. If we can get it, we can escape through the hidden exit in the cellar!"
A group of pirates are betting on a game of darts (Floor 2)
Win a game of darts (Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) {@dc 14})
"You might even be better than Old Tom! Too bad he's always shut up in his cabin with that parrot."
A group of Pirates are betting on who can last the longest on a Mechanical Bull (Floor 2)
Ride the Mechanical Bull for the longest! (Strength ({@skill Athletics}) {@dc 14})

"You might have stuck the mechanical bull, but you wouldn't last 2 minutes if the band went on. This place turns into chaos when they do; it's a free for all brawl to music! You can't see or hear a thing going on for all shouting and dancing!"
A band is missing a few members so can't go on stage. (Floor 1)
A PC or two join the band (Charisma ({@skill Performance}) {@dc 15})
"With skills like that you'd make the Ghost of Bronzebeard dance! That is, if his urn wasn't locked up in Old Tom's Cabin!"
First Mate Magni is looking solemn. (Floor 2)
The party interacts with Magni and probes for any information on the Captain. (Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) {@dc 17})

"Old Tom ain't the pirate he used to be. A cold killer sure, but he just stays shut up with his gold. I reckon the only thing that would get him outta there would be if this tavern came under attack by an Ancient Black Dragon!"

entries.name: Optional Combat Encounters
entries: If the party antagonize drunken pirates they may be drawn into a fight. If so, have four {@creature Zombie Pirate|DMSecretWeapon|Zombie Pirates} attack.
Fights are not unusual at The Dead Tavern. After the party deals with the threat, the atmosphere quickly returns to normal and they can progress without drawing suspicion.

entries.name: The Hidden Storage Base
entries: Accessing this Storage Base requires a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check while in the Downstairs Bar ({@adventure Dead Tavern - Map Layer 2|TheDeadTavern|0|The DM's Treasure Map}). If the party successfully eavesdropped on the two pirates above, they instead find the entrance with no check needed. After following the passage and descending a layer, they find the Fossilized Black Dragon Egg.

entries.name: The Haunted Cellar
entries: As the party enters The Dark Cellar ({@adventure Dead Tavern - Map Layer 3|TheDeadTavern|0|The DM's Treasure Map}) the sounds of the tavern fade behind them. The darkness feels oppressive, almost painful. A foul, haunting voice calls out in the darkness.
"Show me my resting place... Or die"

This is the Pirate Ghost Bronzebeard. The party can show him his Crystal Urn, if they have it, and he will let them pass. Otherwise, they must retreat, or roll initiative. Pirate Ghost Bronzebeard uses the {@creature Spectral Pirate Captain|DMSecretWeapon} stat block.
After defeating/placating Bronzebeard, he vanishes, and the Blunderbuss lies in the Dark Cellar ready to be claimed.

Once in the Dark Cellar, the party can make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check ({@dc 14}) to find the hidden exit. If the party received the hint from the whispering pirate thieves, they instead find the exit without needing a check.

entries.name: Old Tom's Cabin
entries: Entering Old Tom's Cabin stealthily requires a successful lock picking check ({@dc 15}), the party must then make a collective Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check ({@dc 22}) to enter and retrieve their items without waking a sleeping Old Tom and his parrot.
Alternatively, they may knock, and Old Tom will open the door and accost them.
"How Dare Ye?!"

The party may attempt to lie to Old Tom to convince him to vacate the cabin. If so, they must make a {@dc 21} Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check, inventing a plausible reason to draw him away. If the party received and act upon the hint from First Mate Magni, they make this check with Advantage. If the party woke Old Tom while in his cabin, they make this check with Disadvantage. On a failed check, Old Tom will attack immediately. On a success, he will storm off, giving the party a few moments to rob the cabin.

If Old Tom is tricked into leaving, he will attack the party if he encounters them again. Old Tom will stay on the top floor of the Dead Tavern and ambush them if they return there. If the party wishes to avoid him, they must find a way to escape without returning to the surface.
Old Tom uses the {@creature Dread Pirate King|DMSecretWeapon} stat block.

entries.name: Into the Night!
entries: After stealing all the objects they can, the party escapes into the night. If everyone managed to successfully get their desired object and escape, they can choose to sell them on the black market for 5,000 gold a piece, or turn them in to the authorities for a 4,500 gold reward a piece and an improved reputation. You may also wish to reward the party with XP for any fights they managed to avoid through cunning gameplay and successful skill checks.
With the heist a success, tonight is a night for celebration. Come the dawn however, a dark sense of foreboding settles upon the party; stealing from a King of Thieves is unlikely to go unpunished.
Old Tom's crew will already be hunting them down, blades thirsting for a bloody revenge...

entries.name: The Chromatic Door
entries: Before you stands an impassable door, wreathed in flame. If a player or creature physically interacts with the door or attempts to pass through it they are pushed 5 ft. back, fall {@condition Prone} and take {@damage 2d6} Force damage.
Etched into the stone beside the door is the following riddle:
First of Flame,
Second of Thunder,
Third of Ice,
Fourth, your Plunder,
Fifth of Poison,
Sixth of Lightning,
Step forth, be brave,
Embrace the Frightening

entries.name: Solution
entries: To unlock the door, the party must complete a series of tasks, as hinted at by the riddle. The door's appearance changes after each task is completed. Below is the order of actions that must be taken to unlock the door.

items: Deal any amount of Fire damage to the door. The door begins to crackle and booms with thunder.
Deal any amount of Thunder damage to the door. The door begins to freeze.
Deal any amount of Cold damage to the door. The door turns bright gold.
Throw 10 gp or an object of equivalent or higher worth through the door. The object vanishes, and the door turns a sickly green.
Deal any amount of Poison damage to the door. The door begins to crackle with electricity.
Deal any amount of Lightning damage to the door. The door opens to reveal a terrifying black hole of spiraling death, teeth, darkness and flame.
Step through the door. The door frame becomes solid stone, and the path through is unlocked.

entries.name: DM's Recommendation
entries: For low level parties who may have limited damage options, you may wish to include this puzzle in an area where the party can be creative in accessing different sources of damage. For example, you could have the puzzle exist in a location where various native creatures with the power to inflict different damage types can be captured or harvested to inflict damage to the door.

entries.name: Talons of the Devil
entries: Before the party stands a grotesque statue of a devil. It is immune to all damage and status conditions, and cannot be moved against its will. It has sharp talons and terrible, clamping jaws. The party must destroy it to move onward.
At the base of the statue are carved the words:
Hatred Consumes All. In The End, Even Itself.
Any damage a player deals to the devil has no effect, and instead the devil deals the attacker {@damage 1d10} of that damage type back.

entries.name: Solution
entries: The devil statue works by inverting damage. Damage dealt to it by a PC is reflected back upon them. In order to damage the devil, the party must use the statue to damage themselves. Impaling themselves upon its talons, or smashing their heads into its stone form will deal no damage to them. Instead, that damage is reflected back, harming the statue, which will crack, shattering after a few successful reflected damage attacks.

entries.name: Clues
entries: Asking for an Intelligence check from the party is an easy way to impart clues. Alternatively, they may search the area for clues, finding scrawled notes nearby from fallen heroes who tried to pass before them.

entries.name: Hint 1:
entries: The Devil seems to reflect all damage we deal to it back to us. "Hatred Consumes All... Even Itself" what could that mean?

entries.name: Hint 2:
entries: Perhaps there is some way of using the Devil's damage reflection ability against it?

entries.name: Hint 3:
entries: Maybe if it hurts us when we hit the devil, it'll hurt the devil if we can get it to hit us?

This puzzle works best when the party is put under some type of time pressure. A simple and exciting way to do this is to have a stream of weak enemies pouring forth from the statue that will only cease once it is destroyed. These enemies could also be interrogated by the party as an organic way to deliver hints, if they are struggling.

data.name: Dinobattle
entries: Dinobattle is a light hearted, one-shot adventure of time-magic and dinosaurs for a group of four level 7 Player Characters.
This adventure is framed inside a deep forest, but feel free to adapt the location to suit your story or integrate this into an existing campaign.

entries.name: Premise
entries: After a hard day of adventuring, the party has chosen to set up camp in the midst of a deep forest.

Night is falling. A local stream softly babbles. Insects chirp, small animals scuttle through dry leaves, and the wind dances a quiet lullaby through the trees. A gentle night's sleep, a rare luxury in a busy and frightful world, comes easily to all who rest on this night.
It does not last.

The players are roused from their sleep in the early hours of the morning by the cataclysmic roar of a beast that has not walked the material plane in eons. Out of the darkness, toward the party, charge two enormous, bipedal reptiles: {@creature Iratasaur|DMSecretWeapon|Iratasaurs}. In front of them sprints a terrified {@creature Feytroll|DMSecretWeapon|feytroll}. She dives behind the party, covers her eyes with her hands and shrieks: "Protect me, big folk!!"

The dinosaurs crackle with latent Chrono-Magical power. The vegetation crushed beneath their feet withers and rots, only to burst into life once more as the beasts charge onward. Wherever they came from, these monsters have brought a fearsome magic along for the ride.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Round 1 - Dinobattle
entries: Use {@adventure Battlemap 1|Dinobattle|2|Adventure Map 1} for this encounter.

The Iratasaurs' connection to this time and place is unstable, and they are prone to bursts of chaotic Chronomagic. At your discretion, you may roll on the Wild Magic Table of Time and Space on initiative count 20 (losing any initiative ties) and apply the effect to the Iratasaurs until the start of the next round.
After the Iratasaurs are defeated, the feytroll ceases to quiver. She removes her hands from her eyes, rubs her enormous, bulbous nose and offers an outstretched hand to the party.

entries.name: Flooky and the Forest
entries: The Feytroll, named Flooky, will thank the party sincerely. A jumpy but enthusiastic creature, Flooky will be torn between gratitude toward the adventurers and a natural inclination to avoid "big folk".
If questioned about the dinosaurs, she will reveal they attacked her while she was scavenging for food deep in the forest.
An Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check on the defeated Iratasaurs will reveal another object of interest; the magic that crackled around them still remains.

A successful {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check will allow the player character to drain a small fragment of chronomancy from the beast into themselves. If the party defeated an Iratasuar without slaying it, they instead automatically succeed in this endeavor, with no Arcana check needed.

The player making a successful check obtains a {@b Mote of Chronomancy}, a small, glowing mote of scarlet light that gently orbits their head. Once, when they fail a saving throw or miss an attack, they can channel the mote to undo an isolated moment of time, allowing them to reroll their saving throw or attack roll. They must use the new roll. When the mote is used in this way, it vanishes. A player can only have one Mote of Chronomancy at a time.

A successful {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}), Intelligence ({@skill Nature}), or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will allow the party to track the route the beasts took through the forest to their place of origin.

Should the party fail the Investigation check, Flooky will instead offer to guide them as best she can to where she was first attacked. From there, closer to the dinosaur's origin, the party will be able to investigate to follow their tracks without difficulty.

entries.name: Lair of the Long Forgotten
entries: The dinosaur tracks lead deep into the forest. Eventually, they come to an opening at a vast, artificial tunnel, seemingly carved outwards from the earth. It burrows down at a sharp angle, with the darkness inside illuminated by a curious, green, glowing plant life. The air around here is sharp, bristling with magic.

If she accompanied the players, Flooky stops here and insists she cannot proceed any further. Trembling and looking into the tunnel, she will announce that it is her intent to bravely stay outside as a lookout until the party returns.

As the party descends into the tunnel, they will feel the space around them shift and stretch. Time slinks by at an imperceptible speed. It is impossible to tell how long the players spend marching onward; a second or an hour seem of equal worth here.
Eventually, the floor evens out, and the green hue emanating from the weeds and vines bursting from the tunnel's walls grows as bright as day.

entries.name: A Riddle of Time and Space
entries: The party is met by an intricate, magical tiling hewn into the tunnel floor. A series of tablets, each bearing the sigil of a sword, are all pointing in different directions. It looks like something one might find in a temple. Either way, the party must cross this floor in order to move onward.

See {@adventure Riddle of the Sword|Dinobattle|1|Riddle of the Sword} for the full details on running this puzzle. You may find it helpful to print out the puzzle and cut up the sword tiles for rotation, or give your players the access to rotate the tiles themselves if running the adventure online.

If the party fails to reach the end of the floor after three rotations, they are teleported back to the start and the puzzle resets. At this point, choose a random saving throw and roll on the Wild Magic Table of Time and Space. The DC for the save is {@dc 13}. On a failed saving throw, the player characters are subjected to that effect.

entries.name: Temple or Tomb?
entries: After escaping the puzzle room, the party emerges into a dark, glowing room ({@adventure Map 2|Dinobattle|2|Adventure Map 2}). The luminous plant life here grows up the walls and over the floor, cultivated into a conscious pattern, illuminating the room. Somewhere, the tunnel earth has hardened into stone, and it draws to a halt at the far side of the room, like the plank of a ship leading to a chasm of void below. There are also small offerings of gold and gems stacked around the place; approximately {@dice 2d10} thousand gold pieces in total value.

A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will lead to the party finding an old, faded tome left open at the end of the path. Rotten and broken with age, some small fragment of writing can still be made out, written in {@language Common}:
Death. Decay. Rot. Rust.
Such things are beautiful.
The greed of the chronomancers shattered the temple's once stable power.
Time has run wild.
I, the Final Guardian, have failed.
The temple summons its own guardians now. Torn through time, those who would desecrate this sacred place will be torn limb from limb in those fierce jaws.
I feel their presence drawing nearer, the hot breath creeping over my flesh.
I won't stay for such an end. I choose to fall.

entries.name: Round 2 - Ultimate Dinobattle
entries: Suddenly, the party feels the earth around them rumble. A hiss of wind, somehow conjured far below the earth, rips up from the void. Dust at the party's feet is pulled up and stings their eyes. The air buzzes with magic. No voice speaks. No words are heard. But the party receives an overwhelming feeling that they are not welcome.

At that same moment, four crimson vortexes burst into the room, emitting a dazzling light. Through each one steps a {@creature Terraraptor|DMSecretWeapon}, their feathered heads twitching, teeth bared, eyes wild. Two {@creature Iratasaur|DMSecretWeapon|Iratasaurs} join them, stepping through an even larger vortex of light. The first lets loose an earth shattering roar, the sound echoing from its mouth even as it materializes into the room. The dinosaurs charge towards the party.

As they do, the party feels a peculiar sensation pulse through them. The chronomancy and transmutation power of this area seems excited to be wielded. Each player makes a {@dc 8} Wisdom saving throw (they can choose to fail), allowing the magic to ripple through themselves on a failed save.

Harnessing the magic allows the player to undergo a sudden transformation. The spell {@spell Polymorph} is cast on them by the Temple. The player character is polymorphed into a {@creature Terraraptor|DMSecretWeapon}.

Use the {@creature Terraraptor|DMSecretWeapon} stat block for the player character's new stats. Their alignment remains the same in dinosaur form, and they recognize friend from foe. When they reach 0 hit points in this form, they revert back to their normal form and any remaining damage is carried over.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Time's Up
entries: Upon defeating the final dinosaur, turbulent chronomancy magic erupts in the chamber. The bodies of the dinosaurs disintegrate as eons upon eons of time are poured into their bodies. The stone crumbles to dusty sand beneath the party's feet. The open void closes as the dense earth reclaims its territory. Any player characters affected by the magic of the temple revert back to their normal form. The glowing plants on the walls and floor rot and crumble to dust, plunging all into darkness. Then, as suddenly as it began, the magic ends.

Returning to the surface, after a short journey, the party will find Flooky quivering with her eyes clamped tightly shut. Startled to see the party return alive, she will delightedly thank them for stopping the source of the dinosaur attacks, and present each player with an incredibly shiny copper piece, with the air of one imparting a gift of incredible value.
Flooky thanks the players once more before vanishing into the forest before their eyes in a flurry of illusion magic.
The forest around the party seems to breathe a gentle sigh of relief.

Night is falling. A local stream softly babbles. Insects chirp, small animals scuttle through dry leaves, and the wind dances a quiet lullaby through the trees. A gentle night's sleep, a rare luxury in a busy and frightful world, comes easily to all who rest on this night.
This time, it lasts.

entries.name: Riddle of the Sword
entries: This is a simple floor puzzle which uses the following rules.

items: The party starts on the top left square of the floor.
They can only move in the direction that the sword tile they are standing on is facing.
The aim is for the party to rotate the swords in order to make a path from the top left square to the bottom right so they can escape.
They can only rotate three swords (you can rotate them up to 360 degrees in one move).

If they attempt to rotate a fourth sword, or cannot progress without rotating another sword, they are instantly teleported back to the start of the maze, the floor resets, and each party member is blasted with a surge of powerful magic.
Have each party member roll on the Time and Space Wild Magic Table ("Time and Space Magic Surge") to determine the magical effect that takes place when the puzzle resets.

You may wish to also implement a timed element to this puzzle. If so, I recommend a visible timer that resets the floor, teleports the party back to the start of the maze and blasts each party member with magic every 90 seconds.

entries.name: Solution
entries: There are multiple solutions to this puzzle. The simplest is to rotate the following squares:

items: Row 1, column 1: Rotate to face down
Row 4, column 1: Rotate to face right
Row 5, column 3: Rotate to face right

entries.name: Riddles of the Mimiking
entries: These riddles are spoken aloud by a treasure chest whenever a creature moves within 10 ft. of it. To answer the riddle, a player must place their hand on the chest and speak the answer aloud.
On a correct guess, the chest opens, and its valuable contents are free to be plundered.
On an incorrect guess, the chest transforms into a {@creature mimic}, the treasure is lost, and the player character is {@condition grappled}.
Here are two riddles of increasing difficulty.

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #1
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Easy
"Red of blood, Grey of cloud,
Blue of sky, royal Purple, proud,
Brown of Earth, Green of meadow,
Pink of flesh, dandelion Yellow,
All colours, all light, that can be seen by the eye,
Mixed all together, that colour, am I."
The answer to this riddle is the colour white.

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #2
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Medium
Hard as a rock, yet light as a feather,
We travel the world, and gather together,
Innumerable brothers, we number so much,
Yet as soft as fine linen, is the caress of our touch,
We form mighty castles, can drag men to their doom,
We are the plaything of children, on a hot afternoon,
I can be found close to water,
Or counting time, flowing fine,
We can form a sea of our own,
But no water, you'll find.
What am I?
The answer to this riddle is Sand.

data.name: The Fallen Angel's First Rite
entries: The Fallen Angel's First Rite is a one-shot adventure designed for a party of four level 11 player characters featuring a healthy mix of combat, roleplay, and multiple, player-choice-dependent endings.

entries.name: The Fallen Angel
entries: The party have found themselves in Slumpkin City, a bustling city with a famously devoted religious quarter and powerful military presence.

Unbeknownst to the majority of the town's people, an excavation in the hilltops beyond the outskirts of the city has uncovered the fragile remains of a fallen {@creature Planetar}. Seen as a terrible omen by the religious elite, and a potential source of incredible power by the military, its discovery has led to a desperate race between the two powerful factions to claim the remains for themselves before word spreads to the townsfolk.
Possible hooks to involve the party in the adventure include:

items: A PC with the {@background Soldier} background is contacted by Honurth, a no-nonsense military captain stationed in Slumpkin. She will request the party oversee the extraction and recommend they connect with Carven Sansparke, a powerful war mage and magical weaponsmith representing the military interest in the excavation.

A PC with a background tied to religion is contacted by Pious, an elderly but energetic Cleric. He will request the party oversee the excavation without bloodshed, and recommend they connect with Evelyn Noire, a fiercely devout battle cleric representing the religious interest in the excavation.

A PC once did a job for Brushbeard, the pompous but amiable dwarven mayor. He is concerned about both of the representatives overseeing the excavation, and has requested the players go as an independent party to oversee the activity there.

entries: In all cases, the party will act as final adjudicators in what becomes of the Planetar remains. Guided by their contact, the party navigate their way out of the city and to the Planetar excavation site.

entries.name: Curses and Conflict
entries: Upon reaching the excavation site ({@adventure Map 1|TheFallenAngelsFirstRite|2|Adventure Map 1}), the party come upon two NPCs embroiled in fierce open debate. A dwarf, clad in complex, magical armour stands on one side, roaring and gesticulating wildly. On the other, a human cleric towers over him, hand on the hilt of her sword, armour glistening in the afternoon sun.

Behind them is a colossal pit, within which lie the bones of the fallen Planetar. Despite the distance, the party can feel a bubbling, celestial magic darting through the air. Even in death, the magic of this once mighty creature whispers on the breeze.
As the party approaches, the arguing pair turn to face them.

Suddenly, an explosion sends dust and debris hurtling through the air. A cloud of thick smoke billows out from behind the two representatives, and they both collapse to the floor, choking and spluttering before swiftly falling {@condition unconscious}.
Out of the smoke stride four cloaked figures, weapons drawn. They cast a swift glance over the two fallen representatives, and then look towards the party.
"The Planetar is ours. Flee with your lives, or face the consequences!"
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Addressing the Situation
entries: Just as the last of the bandits fall, the cleric and wizard begin to regain consciousness.

If the party didn't kill the bandits in the fight, the cleric will immediately call out for the bandits' execution for transgressions against a holy site. Swiftly, the wizard will counter this proposal, insisting they be taken alive.
The party's companion turns to face the players:

"Looks like it's up to you where we go from here. Make a decision on these bandits, and then decide who takes charge of these blasted bones. These bandits will be the first of many; word must be spreading of the power that lies here. We need this dealt with, quick!"

items: The bandits (if alive) sit tied up and beaten at the front of the pit.
Carven Sansparke, the war wizard, stands on the right of the pit, looking over the Planetar excavation.
Evelyn Noire stands on the left of the pit, her eyes shifting furiously between Carven and the restrained bandits, her hand never leaving the hilt of her sword.

entries: From here, the party is free to chat with each representative (and the bandits if they choose) to come to a decision on what happens with the fallen Planetar.
In the table below you'll find the NPCs, their primary motivation for wanting the remains, and a secret that the party may uncover over the course of their investigation.

rows: Carven Sansparke seeks the bones of the Planetar to construct powerful magical weapons for the army (and a tidy profit for himself). He argues that to not use them would be tantamount to treason, that a gift such as this must be wielded to destroy the enemies of the state. Powerful weapons save lives, ending conflict quickly and decisively, and making it so no-one ever dares challenge the might of the empire. He wants the Bandits kept alive.
Carven was the one who hired the bandits to take the bones. Contracted by the military, they sought to incapacitate Noire and take them under the guise of petty thieves.

Evelyn Noire sees the discovery of the bones as a terrible omen sent by the Gods. She is certain that to disturb them further would incur the wrath of deities that could lead to the outright destruction of the city. She seeks to ritualistically destroy the bones as an offering, and to never tell anyone what was discovered here. She wants the bandits killed immediately for disturbing this holy site.

Evelyn is aware that the planetar remains still hold a connection to the celestial realm. She hopes that in offering the bones, she will receive personal favour with the gods. This isn't about the military, the church, or Slumpkin. Evelyn is here seeking personal connection to the divine through the remains.
The bandits want to live, and will plead for their lives. They are aware the bones are worth incredible money, and sought to steal them to later sell on.
The bandits were hired by Sansparke and the military in a subtle attempt to take the bones without the religious quarter knowing.

items: Upon hearing both sides, the party must make a decision.
If the party decides to side with Carven Sansparke, proceed to {@adventure Ending 1|TheFallenAngelsFirstRite|0|Ending 1 - Siding with Carven}.
If the party decides to side with Evelyn Noire, proceed to {@adventure Ending 2|TheFallenAngelsFirstRite|0|Ending 2 - Siding with Evelyn}.

entries.name: Ending 1 - Siding with Carven
entries: As the party announce their intent to oversee the Planetar being handed over to the military, Evelyn Noire lets out a cry of rage!

"You fools! The wrath of the gods will surely descend upon this city! All will be doomed! You are the murderers of your own children! In the name of that which is holy, I will not allow heathens to wield this power! I will channel the celestial powers myself! Witness the consequences to all who would betray God!"

At these words, Evelyn draws her weapon and slams it into the earth. A burst of Radiant and Necrotic energy deafens and blinds all those present, and the party feel a huge tremor as the ground beneath their feet begins to shift.

Evelyn's body shimmers and glows, her form dissolving into motes of pure, golden light. The Planetar bones in the earth do the same, evaporating to dust and rising up toward the sky. Carven Sansparke lets out a scream of fury and fear as the light forms into the terrible, nightmare visage of undeath. A ghostly, black shade of the once living Planetar stands tall over the pit. Two vast, spectral wings unfurl behind it. The being lets out a low rumble of laughter. It speaks with Evelyn's voice:
"Witness me! The untethered power of the divine!"
Roll Initiative, using the {@creature Necro-Planetar (Ghost Form)|DMSecretWeapon|Necro-Planetar: Ghost Form} stat block.

entries.name: Evelyn's End
entries: Upon defeating the Necro-Planetar, it bursts into motes of rainbow light, vanishing into the sky with a final scream. The party hears something of Evelyn's voice in that dying wail, echoing with fury, fear and... triumph?

Carven will spit on the ground furiously. For all his efforts, the Planetar was destroyed. He will curse Evelyn and curse the party for their ineptitude in stopping her. Furious, he storms off towards the city, leading the bandits (if they are alive) behind him to face trial by the military.

The party are thanked by their contact, who believes the players made the right choice. They offer each party member a reward in the form of a magical rune. This rune can be applied to any weapon. When applied in this manner, the weapon gains one random property from the {@table Major Weapon Boons|DMSecretWeapon} table.
With their mission completed, the party returns to Slumpkin, its people never knowing how the actions of the party that day have changed the course of the city's destiny forever...

entries.name: Ending 2 - Siding with Evelyn
entries: As the party announce their intent to oversee the Planetar being destroyed, Carven Sansparke lets out a cry of rage.

"You fools! The wrath of our enemies will descend upon this city! You are the murderers of your own children! In the name of the crown, I will not allow traitors to destroy our future! Behold, the first test of the force I shall wield to destroy those who would betray the kingdom!"

At these words, Carven draws his staff and slams it into the earth. A burst of Radiant and Necrotic energy deafens and blinds all those present, and the party feel a huge tremor as the ground beneath their feet begins to shift.

The fallen planetar bones course with the energy of the mighty spell. The ancient bones begin to rattle a ghastly cacophony as they wrench themselves from the earth. A black mist descends on the being, cloaking it in a veil of darkness as it tears itself from the binds of the pit. It draws itself to its full height as two black, spectral wings unfurl from behind it. The force of his spell leaves Carven breathless and shaking. He collapses to the floor as the Necro-Planetar steps over him to face the party. As it does so, Carven lets out a mad cackle of laughter:
"The domain of the Gods is no more! Witness the harnessed power of the divine!"
Roll Initiative, using the {@creature Necro-Planetar (Zombie Form)|DMSecretWeapon|Necro-Planetar: Zombie Form} stat block.

entries.name: Carven's End
entries: Upon defeating the Necro-Planetar, it crumbles to dust. The magical energy that pulsed through the air fades, and a sudden silence falls over the area.
Carven will raise himself from the floor and spit bitterly at the party:

"You blasted fools. In time, I could have shaped this being into an even greater guardian of hope for the whole kingdom. I would have ended all wars and saved countless lives. It would have been a new era of peace and prosperity for our people. Instead you have cut the thread of hope at its very conception. Do with me as you will, and may the mothers who weep for their slaughtered children on the battlefield haunt your conscience evermore!"

Evelyn will thank the party sincerely, and request permission to execute Carven immediately for transgressions against the Gods. If the party does not allow her to do so, she will humbly acquiesce and return to the city, but not before openly blessing each of the party with the favour of the Gods.

The party are thanked by their contact, who believes the players made the right choice. They then take charge of escorting Carven to face trial in the city if he is still alive, and offer each party member a reward in the form of a magical rune. This rune can be applied to any weapon. When applied in this manner, the weapon gains one random property from the {@table Major Weapon Boons|DMSecretWeapon} table.
With their mission completed, the party returns to Slumpkin, its people never knowing how the actions of the party that day have changed the course of the city's destiny forever...

entries.name: Puzzle of the Five Doors
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Easy
The party enters a room with five doors standing side by side before them.
All have keys sticking out of their locks. The far right, centre and far left doors are unlocked. The remaining two doors are locked.
From here, it is down to the party to explore and work out the puzzle to progress.

entries.name: Rules of the Puzzle
entries: Walking through any unlocked door will teleport the party back to the entrance of the room, unless all doors are unlocked.
The aim is to unlock all the doors so the party can progress.

A player can use an action to turn a single key to lock or unlock a door. When they do so, the door on the immediate left and right of that door also shifts from being locked to unlocked, or vice versa.

entries.name: Solution
entries: The trick to this puzzle is to get three doors next to each other that are all locked, and have the remaining two doors unlocked. That way the final central door can be unlocked, which will also unlock the two doors either side. Here is a guide demonstrating one path to solve this puzzle.

entries.name: Running the Puzzle
entries: When running this puzzle in person, I recommend creating double sided doors with the locked and unlocked variation on each side. Then when a player unlocks a door, you can flip that door over, along with the doors directly on either side.

entries.name: Riddles of the Mimiking
entries: This riddle is spoken aloud by a treasure chest whenever a creature moves within 10 ft. of it.
To answer the riddle, a player must place their hand on the chest and speak the answer aloud.
On a correct guess, the chest opens, and its valuable contents are free to be plundered.
On an incorrect guess, the chest transforms into a {@creature mimic}, the treasure is lost, and the player character is {@condition grappled}.

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #3
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Medium
I can race, but not run,
I can break without tearing,
You have only one,
But you hope for a pairing.
I can beat, I can thump,
But can't punch or pummel,
I can skip, but not jump,
And if I stop you're in trouble.
What am I?
The answer to this riddle is: The Heart

data.name: Invader from Beyond
entries: Invader from Beyond is a science-fantasy inspired one shot adventure for a party of four level 4 characters, featuring a mix of problem-solving combat and roleplay.

entries.name: Deep Impact
entries: The party have taken rest for the night in a spare building owned by a kindly middle aged farmer (Sven) and his wife (Hilga).

As the party is chatting around the hearth late in the evening they hear a deafening boom, so loud it shatters all the windows and shakes the walls. Outside they will be met with a colossal cloud of black smoke streaming through the sky, a pale green glow at its center, trailing pieces of falling metal debris.

The cloud billows directly towards the party, the object at the center colliding with the ground, requiring a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw from each player to dodge out of the way or be knocked {@condition prone}.
The crashed flying saucer will continue to spew thick smoke for 8 hours after the crash ({@adventure Map 1|InvaderFromBeyond|2|Invader from Beyond Map 1}).
Simultaneously, metallic spider constructs emerge from the places where the other smaller pieces of debris fell from the ship, causing panic among the local farm hands and families.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Metal Legs
entries: Five {@creature Mechanical Spider|DMSecretWeapon|Mechanical Spiders} will move in, two from behind the crashed saucer and one from each of the rooftops of the nearby buildings. They will attempt to ensnare anyone within reach with their synthetic web to be carried away and vivisected by {@creature Invader from Beyond|DMSecretWeapon|The Invader} once the area is clear. They will attempt to kill any creature that breaks out of the web, passes the save against it or attempts to free another creature.
Four civilians will have been rendered {@condition unconscious} by the blast from the crash landing and cannot flee, including Sven and Hilga.
When only two mechanical spiders remain, any party member with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) 14 or higher will notice a small figure emerging from the crashed saucer through the smoke.

The Invader will take a quick look around, then leap into the air on a plume of dark smoke, seemingly propelled by the pack on its back. A shower of sparks bursts from the device, and the figure drops significantly in altitude; perhaps this propulsion pack is damaged in some way? The figure's eventual destination will be hidden as it becomes fully obscured by smoke.

entries.name: Aftermath
entries: If both Sven and Hilga survive they will thank the party for their aid in resisting the onslaught and offer them an heirloom belonging to Sven's great grandfather; a {@item Ring of Fire Resistance}.

The party will be approached by three of the surviving farmhands who will tell them a group of mechanical spiders were seen heading into a nearby valley, carrying bits of flashing metal from the saucer.

A {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check on the saucer will reveal that some of the internal parts seem to have been removed. A {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check on the mechanical spiders will reveal that they are seemingly powered by a glass sphere in a metal frame that glows a deep red in the center of their abdomen. A {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check around the site will reveal deep, narrow tracks that can be followed to a nearby valley.

entries.name: Ashes
entries: As the party enters the valley, they will see destroyed {@creature Kobold} traps and several piles of ash. Following the tracks and carnage, they will arrive at a cave entrance.

A {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal the discarded Jetpack lodged in a crevice above the mouth of the cave, requiring a {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to climb to. Once retrieved, any player character can attempt a {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to deduce how it works. A player who wears the broken jetpack can use their bonus action to jump up to 30 ft.

As the party descends into the cave they come upon an eerie scene. A kobold settlement lies seemingly abandoned, aside from dozens of ash piles scattered about the place. Lukewarm food is laid out in a communal area alongside several half-completed traps.
A player who makes a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will hear a faint shuffling sound coming from within a pile of food sacks; a surviving {@creature kobold} is hiding within.
The kobold will scream and beg for mercy. If granted, it will nervously tell the party of the "small, big headed" creature that had a weapon "like dragon breath" that turned anything it hit to ash.

entries.name: First Contact
entries: The party passes through the entryway into the Elders' Cavern, a very large room dedicated to the tribe's draconic ancestry. It is empty save for several dead kobolds, each of whom suffered a different degree of vivisection ({@adventure Map 2|InvaderFromBeyond|2|Invader from Beyond Map 2}).
A green glow emits from the top left corner of the room, concealed by a protruding wall. The party must pass a {@dc 17} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to approach unnoticed.

If they succeed on the check they will be able to approach {@creature Invader from Beyond|DMSecretWeapon|The Invader} unnoticed. It is at work constructing a titanic machine, seemingly made of the parts missing from the Crashed Saucer.

Should the party attack or be spotted by the Invader, it will immediately turn to face them. Alien though its face is, the disdain The Invader has for these primitive animals is plain to see. It unhooks a sinister, handheld device from its belt.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Earth Is Closed
entries: On initiative count 20 the alien machine emits an extremely loud, high pitched noise. Any creature within 30 ft. of the machine must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition deafened} for 1 minute.

A mechanical spider has been converted into an immobile turret (HP 20, AC 12). On initiative count 10, it will fire a web at a player character. That target must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition restrained} by webbing. A restrained target can use an action to make a {@dc 12} Strength check to break the webbing and free itself. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; hp 5; vulnerability to Fire damage; immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage).

entries.name: Epilogue
entries: Once the Invader has been defeated the party will still need to deactivate the machine. It has an AC of 18 and 45 hit points. Alternatively, the party can attempt to shut it down with a {@dc 19} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to identify the shutdown sequence. It will continue sending out shockwaves each turn, growing increasingly unstable. After 10 rounds, if not destroyed or deactivated, the machine will detonate, dealing {@damage 20d10} Fire damage to all creatures within 60 ft.

With the threat eliminated, the party will return to the farm. The crashed saucer has already begun to rust, swiftly decomposing at a rate far beyond any known metal. The danger has seemingly passed, but the question of from where this machine and its pilot came, and whether they were but the harbingers of more to come, remains a mystery.

data.name: The Trapmaker's Garden Weighted Floor Puzzles
entries: Weighted floor puzzles make for simple and fun logic challenges for a party to face.

entries.name: The Rules
entries: The party begins on the tile marked START.
There is a portal on the tile marked END, but it is not active.
In order to activate the portal to move forward in the dungeon, the party must step on every weighted tile to trigger them, and power up the portal.

If the party steps on the same tile more than once, the magical contraption overloads. When this happens, each player character takes a number of d10 Force damage equal to their proficiency bonus, and are teleported back to the starting tile. The puzzle then resets.
The aim is to step on every tile only once, finishing on the tile marked END to step through the activated portal.
The party must move as a unit, and cannot split up to complete the puzzle.
Any tiles blocked by Rocks cannot be stepped on, and do not need to be stepped on to activate the portal.

entries.name: The Puzzles
entries: The first puzzle is very simple, intended to introduce the concept to a new party. Puzzles #2–#4 may require a degree of planning or trial and error to complete.
