data.name: Curse of the Desert Queen
entries: The Curse of the Desert Queen is an adventure of exploration, mystery and horror designed for a party of four level 8 player characters.
Be warned, this adventure carries a higher than usual possibility of player character death!

entries.name: Just Deserts
entries: The party are making their way through the vast, harsh desert wasteland of Molkesh, passing from oasis to oasis. The battle against the elements is brutal, but spirits are high. The party are approaching civilization for the first time in weeks as they make their way toward the oasis village of Sheshet.

A creeping sense of unease sets over them as they close in on the village however. Though they have encountered no adverse weather in their travels, the village appears as if it has been struck by a powerful sandstorm. Buildings lie half buried and abandoned, and the oasis has dried up.

While walking through the village, any player who makes a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will notice a glint of light out of the corner of their eye; the sun reflecting from a gold ring lying just barely above the sand. An attempt to retrieve the ring will reveal the corpse it is attached to. A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will reveal the corpse to be that of a merchant, not native to these lands.

entries.name: Survivors
entries: As the party continues onward, they hear a faint thud from the far side of the village. The sound continues rhythmically, and grows louder as the party approaches a small courtyard ({@adventure Map 1|CurseOfTheDesertQueen|2|Curse of the Desert Queen Map 1}).
There, they see a skeletal giant in ornate armour slamming its mace onto the roof of a building, crumpling the structure and breaking its way in.
The skeletal giant is not alone; it is surrounded by four figures in the dress of local guards, standing eerily still (use the {@creature Undead Guard|DMSecretWeapon|Undead Guards} stat block).

A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal the guards are desiccated, as if they were killed weeks ago. A subsequent {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check will reveal that they had the life force drained from them before they were reanimated.
If the party waits too long before engaging with the giant it will break into the building. Cries of terror and the sound of slaughter will then be heard from within.

If the party does not engage the undead creatures before they have killed the survivors inside the building, they will remain motionless for a short time before the faint sound of whispered words slink through the air. From this point onward, all the undead in the town know the location of the party and will hunt them to the death.
The undead cannot be surprised, but if the party elects to attack without first being seen, they may roll for initiative at Advantage.

entries.name: The Tale
entries: After the battle, if the undead were destroyed before they could smash their way into the building, three survivors will emerge. They wear the same style of foreign clothing as the dead merchant found earlier.

The merchant survivors will share with the party the tale of what they saw the previous night. A vicious sandstorm struck without warning, forcing them to shelter in the abandoned town. The lethal storm battered the buildings, and yet, in the darkness, the merchants heard wails and screams. Through a high window, they saw figures moving unhindered through the storm, walking out from the village and into the desert.
When the dawn broke, two of their number set out to explore the village, each identifiable by an ornate golden ring. Neither have returned. Then the undead attacked.
In return for saving their lives they will give the party their stock of 1 {@item Potion of Greater Healing||potion of healing (greater)} and 4 {@item Potion of Healing||potions of healing}.

entries.name: The Wastes
entries: Any Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check in the area the villagers were last seen will reveal a loose string of items: buttons, copper coins and scraps of cloth, spaced roughly every dozen metres. They provide a trail, leading into the wastes. Following it for approximately one hour at walking pace, the party will come to a small pyramid of smooth gold, around 20 ft. tall in the sand.

As the party draws within 10 ft. of the structure, the sands about their feet begin to shift. The pyramid rises up from the desert. Each player must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw or be thrown back, tumbling into the sands and falling {@condition prone}.
When the pyramid reaches its full height, it stands at an incredible 500 ft.
Once the pyramid reaches its full height a fell wind blows from within. With it echoes three foul, whispered words:
"The way is shut."

entries.name: Curse of Scarabs
entries: The pyramid's main door is locked, with only one small opening visible, just large enough to place one's hand inside. In order to open the door, an adventurer must place their hand inside to activate the mechanism that lies within. It must be held for three rounds to successfully open the pyramid, the door sliding slowly open with each round.

Once every round the player with their hand in the opening will take {@damage 1d4} magical Piercing damage and feel something crawl under their skin and up the inside of their arm. The mechanism imparts a curse of scarabs on the player.

Once the player removes their hand from the mechanism, the scarabs bite from within their body, {@condition paralyzed||paralysing} the victim and dealing {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage each round. To remove the scarabs and end the curse, they must be cut out by the other party members.

Each scarab has an AC of 18 and 1 hit point. If a party member attempts to attack a scarab and misses, the cursed player will take {@damage 1d4} damage from the blow. An adventurer with proficiency in Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) can make their attacks at Advantage to cut out the cursed scarabs. The curse ends when three cursed scarabs have been cut out.

entries.name: What Lies Within
entries: Inside the pyramid food instantly moulders and water evaporates. Other non-magical drinks are spoiled — wine turning to vinegar, for instance. The door behind the party closes the moment they step inside ({@adventure Map 2|CurseOfTheDesertQueen|2|Curse of the Desert Queen Map 2}).

The only way forward is a narrow corridor, leading the party ever deeper into the pyramid. Eventually, they approach an open gateway, and a dark whispering and muffled screams can be heard from beyond.

Within the room, there is a ruined dais that sits on a floor of sand, and beside it, an undead woman dressed in opulent golden jewellery. The chamber is largely empty otherwise, save for two {@creature Poison Mummy|DMSecretWeapon|poison mummies} standing beside the dais and six incredible, stone serpentine heads pulsing with magical energy.

As the party looks on, they see the woman drain the life of a terrified merchant, held in place by two poison mummies. The energy is sapped from his body and drawn into her own. The merchant falls, a desiccated husk, to the floor.
Two corpses already lie on the ground. After the merchant falls, a powerful voice emanates through the chamber. It speaks as a whisper yet echoes terrifyingly loud, shaking the room:
"Rise. Serve."
The corpses are struck by green light. They then claw themselves from the earth and stand to attention. If the party chooses to attack before this occurs, it instead happens on initiative count 20.
After hearing the voice, the priestess walks to the dais at the centre of the chamber and turns as she speaks, her eyes lovingly passing over each serpentine head.
"It is almost time, my Queen."
Then the voice speaks once more. A vicious, agitated hiss.
"Intruders! At the gateway!"
Roll initiative.

entries.name: Mummy Mayhem
entries: The party are facing two {@creature Poison Mummy|DMSecretWeapon|mummies}, three {@creature Undead Guard|DMSecretWeapon|undead guards} and {@creature The High Priestess|DMSecretWeapon}.
On initiative count 20 if there are no undead guards remaining, {@dice 1d4} {@creature skeleton||skeletons} rise from the sand as green energy pulses from the serpent heads.

entries.name: Escape!
entries: Once the High Priestess and two Mummies are defeated a dreadful scream echoes through the chamber. Sand begins to pour into the room through the mouths of the serpents as the pyramid starts to sink back beneath the sands. The scream rips through the chamber again, a mix of fury and anguish, as the serpent eyes grow a deadly red.

Any remaining skeletons freeze in a trance-like state and will not move, their souls already claimed by the Queen of the Desert Sands. "We will serve you Nabirah, Queen of Queens" they chant, over and over as the sand claims them.
The tunnel the party entered through is already overflowing with sand; the only way out is up.
As the sand rises, a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw must be made to climb atop the sand. A character that fails this save will sink up to their waist in sand and have their speed reduced to 0.

To escape they must make a {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or another player must use an action to pull them free. If a player is stuck in this manner for two full rounds, the sand claims them and they become {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition incapacitated}, and begin suffocating. They will drown if not rescued.
All the while, the sand rises.
After successfully managing to stay above the sand, the party members are pushed to the very tip of the pyramid. The risk now is being crushed against the ceiling.

However, towards the very tip, a distant light can be seen at the end of a hallway built into the wall; an exit! There is another open door to the side of this hallway, one that leads to a huge room filled with fabulous treasures.

entries.name: A Final Test
entries: Piles of gold, chests full of gems, ancient artefacts and magical weapons call out to the party from the room. The party may also see other treasures relevant to their own character. A vial of legendary potion that could revive a dead family member for example.

Should the party enter the room, any object they touch turns to sand. In order to leave, they must use an action and succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or be unable to do so. A fellow player character not in the cursed treasure room can attempt to assist them in escaping by calling out to them. If they do so, the player makes any Wisdom save to escape at Advantage.

If a player spends more than three full rounds in the treasure room, they will become buried in sand. They become {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition incapacitated}, and begin suffocating. They will drown if not rescued.
Passing by the treasure room, the party escapes through a slowly shrinking opening at the peak of the pyramid.
They are dropped back into the harsh desert, the pyramid sinking into the sands behind them.

Each player character must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the player is cursed. No matter how far they travel, no matter where they go, in quiet moments, they hear a haunting, echoed whisper of hatred and vengeance; the Curse of the Desert Queen.

data.name: The Trapmaker's Garden Weighted Floor Puzzles
entries: Back by popular demand! Weighted floor puzzles make for simple and fun logic challenges for a party to face.

items: The party begins on the tile marked START. There is a portal on the tile marked END, but it is not active.
In order to activate the portal to move forward in the dungeon, the party must step on every weighted tile to trigger them, and power up the portal.

If the party steps on the same tile more than once, the magical contraption overloads. When this happens, each player character takes a number of d10 Force damage equal to their proficiency bonus, and are teleported back to the starting tile. The puzzle then resets.
The aim is to step on every tile only once, finishing on the tile marked END to step through the activated portal.
The party must move as a unit, and cannot split up to complete the puzzle.
Any tiles blocked by Rocks cannot be stepped on, and do not need to be stepped on to activate the portal.

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #4
entries: This riddle is spoken aloud by a treasure chest whenever a creature moves within 10 ft. of it. To answer the riddle, a player must place their hand on the chest and speak the answer aloud.
On a correct guess, the chest opens, and its valuable contents are free to be plundered.
On an incorrect guess, the chest transforms into a {@creature mimic}, the treasure is lost, and the player character is {@condition grappled}.
You might see me in the nighttime waters,
But no matter how deep you dive,
I'll not be caught.
I've outlived all living things,
Yet am forever reborn and dying,
Vanishing to naught.
I run miles and miles each day,
And yet I never tire.
I am cold and stand in darkness,
But beam with the light of the one great fire.
What am I?
{@b Answer:} The Moon

data.name: Demon Chase
entries: Demon Chase is a one-shot adventure of combat and mystery for a party of four level 10 player characters.

entries.name: Premise
entries: The party has been recruited by Paladin Nyssa, commander of an order of knights known as the Order of Agathon.

Their founder, Saint Agathon, slew the demon lord Xer'Gaal and locked it away forever. The order is planning to assault the stronghold of a demon cult who have stolen their most prized artefact, the Sword of Agathon.

entries.name: The Plan
entries: The party begin the night before the assault in the camp of Paladin Nyssa. Sat around the fire, Nyssa lays out the plan ({@adventure Map 1|DemonChase|2|Demon Chase Map 1}).
She will first explain the details of the sword. It is an immensely powerful holy weapon, capable of channelling various radiant magics, including {@spell Greater Restoration}.
She will lead an attack on the cathedral where the Sword is believed to be held, commanding a unit of 50 knights.

The party is to follow in the aftermath, preventing any cultists from escaping and covering the main forces' rear from attack. The rest of the army will breach the walls and capture the rest of the stronghold.
The party may ask any questions or use this time to strategise. As soon as she is confident they are familiar with their role in the plan, Nyssa will bid them adieu and retire to bed.

entries.name: Storming the Gates
entries: The following day, the party follow the knights at a safe distance, entering the Demon stronghold after the initial battle has been won.
A path has been cleared, and following the spearhead charge of Nyssa's knights, the party approaches a cathedral; the colossal building that forms the centerpiece of the cultists' stronghold.

The party encounter no resistance; it is clear the attack went well. However, distant sounds of battle indicate that the fight is still raging in some areas of the stronghold, and the fallen bodies of many cultists lie strewn about the compound.

Through the main doors of the cathedral Nyssa can be seen standing, flanked by a company of six knights. They stand in a half circle around an altar, above which a resplendent longsword is hovering. The Knights are bloody, their armor and weapons crimson in the ichor of their fallen foes.
Nyssa reaches a trembling hand out to the sword.
"At last, we have returned the Swo..." she cuts off mid-sentence and stops moving, before violently jerking forward into a hunched position.
An awful crunching sound can be heard as two leathery wings burst from the back of her armour. She then turns, her form shifting into a void of fire and darkness as she becomes possessed by Xer'Gaal.
Simultaneously, the demon uses its blood storm ability, killing the surrounding knights whose bodies also begin to transform into demonic versions of themselves.
The demonic figure turns to the party, a maelstrom of fire and shadow, and a rich, charismatic voice booms forth:
"Finally free of that wretched blade, thanks to the slaughter my own enemies wrought upon those dwelling here. These sycophants didn't put up much of a fight. I don't imagine you will either."
Xer'Gaal then takes the Sword of Agathon and flies up to the higher level, shifting into an incorporeal form as it passes through the ceiling.
The {@creature Blood Demon|DMSecretWeapon|demonic knights} step forward.
Roll Initiative ({@adventure Map 2|DemonChase|2|Demon Chase Map 2}).

entries.name: Chests and Choices
entries: Once the demons have been defeated, the knights' corpses will return to their true form.

There are two spiral staircases on either side of the room. As the party ascends to the next floor they come to three ornate treasure chests on a small landing. Each one is marked with a crudely hewn, demonic scrawl carved into the stone above them.
The first chest contains a {@creature Hezrou}. An {@spell Identify} spell reveals that a creature is inside the chest, but the only way to determine the type of creature is to open it.

The second chest contains 5 {@item Potion of Healing||potions of healing}, 3 {@item Potion of Greater Healing||potions of healing (greater)}, a scroll of {@spell Greater Restoration}, a {@item +2 Weapon||+2 weapon} and a suit of {@item Elven Chain} armour.
The last chest is empty; if a player attempts to open it they will be magically pulled inside, and the chest will slam closed.

It instantly fills with gas. At the start of their turn any creature within the chest must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 5d8} Poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Creatures are affected even if they hold their breath or don't need to breathe. A {@dc 18} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check from a player either inside or outside the chest will break it, allowing the trapped player to escape.
If any chest is opened, the other two immediately meld together and transform into a single {@creature Mimiking|DMSecretWeapon}.
Upon defeating the Mimiking, the centre chest's contents are left for the party to take, if they did not grab them already.

entries.name: Dying to Meet You
entries: The spiral stairs lead to the second floor of the cathedral which houses the grand organ. Blood streaks can be seen along the floor. There is no sign of the demon.

The party feel uncomfortable, like something is crawling over their skin. As they move into the room, {@creature Aspect of Xer'Gaal|DMSecretWeapon|Xer'Gaal} will begin playing the organ badly, sitting, invisible, at the keys.
The demon bursts into view as the dreadful music reaches a crescendo, slamming its fists down on the organ as fire erupts from the pipes.
Flame bursts from the floor below, climbing up the balcony of the cathedral. The stench of burned flesh fills the air from the corpses below ({@adventure Map 3|DemonChase|2|Demon Chase Map 3}).
Xer'Gaal turns to face the party. He clutches the Sword of Agathon in one hand.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Battle!
entries: Upon being defeated, Xer'Gaal will let out a cackle of derisive, echoing laughter.

"I appreciate you slaying me here, and sending me home! I'll be sure to pay you all a visit again sometime to thank you in person, your families and friends too! I did enjoy the paladin, and although she was a weak vessel, I think I'll take her soul with me. A Demon's gotta eat, right?"

Nyssa returns to her true form as the Demonic presence leaves her body. She is {@condition paralyzed||paralysed} and at 1 hit point. The Sword of Agathon lies on the floor at her side. She will die unless the spell {@spell Greater Restoration} or similar magic is cast on her within the next minute. While in the presence of such hateful demonic energy, the Sword of Agathon will offer its power to any player who seeks to wield it, without requiring attunement.

If Nyssa survives, she will fall {@condition unconscious} but with her soul intact. The Sword is saved, a great artifact in the battle for all that is good, but the multiverse trembles at the return of another mighty Demon lord.

entries.name: Rising Water Puzzle
entries: Rising Water is a classic dungeon trap scenario. In this puzzle, the player characters must shut off the valves in the correct order to stop the water from rising and so they can escape drowning.
The rules are as follows:

items: Each character can turn only one valve per turn.
When the puzzle begins, all the valves are off.
There are 6 valves which must all be turned on.

entries: The valves must be turned in the correct order, to prevent the pressure from overloading the mechanism.
If a player shuts off an incorrect valve, the system overloads and all the valves spring back open.

In order to minimise the pressure, the players must never turn a valve within two spaces of the previous valve that was turned. The only exception to this rule is that the final valve can be turned on no matter where it is, as long as all the others have been turned on correctly to balance the pressure.
The players have 12 turns to find the correct order to shut off the valves before the water reaches the top of the room and they begin to drown.

You can choose to tell the players these rules in full, or let them discover it through trial and error. If you choose to let them explore the trap through trial and error, remember to give them extra time to compensate for the restricted information.

{@b Example:} after Player One turns valve 1, Player Two cannot turn valves 2 or 3, as that will overload the pressure and cause the mechanism to reset. Player Two chooses to turn valve 6. Now Player Three cannot turn valves 4 or 5. If they do, the system will overload. They choose to turn valve 2. Now the only available valve to turn is valve 5, as valves 3 and 4 will overload the pressure.

Player Four turns valve 5. Now the only remaining valves are numbers 3 and 4. However, both are within two spaces of valve 5, so no matter which one is turned, the system will overload! This is going to be trickier than the players first thought, and the water is rising...

entries.name: Solution
entries: One correct order to switch on the valves is as follows:
Valve 1, Valve 5, Valve 2, Valve 6, Valve 3, Valve 4.

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #5
entries: This riddle is spoken aloud by a treasure chest whenever a creature moves within 10 ft. of it. To answer the riddle, a player must place their hand on the chest and speak the answer aloud.
On a correct guess, the chest opens, and its valuable contents are free to be plundered.
On an incorrect guess, the chest transforms into a {@creature mimic}, the treasure is lost, and the player character is {@condition grappled}.
I come to all, in darkest night,
In name of peace, or name of fright,
A sweet embrace, with gentle hand,
A crushing force none can withstand.
A boundless world; your peaceful isle,
A taste of death, just for a while.
What am I?

entries.name: Solution
entries: Sleep

data.name: Mary Had a Little Dracolich
entries: When a prize winning lamb goes missing, a plucky adventuring party must venture into the Dracolich Dungeon to find the lost sheep, braving portal mazes, deadly monsters, draconic magic and psychedelic mushrooms on the way.
Mary Had a Little Dracolich is a one-shot adventure for a party of four level 1 player characters.

entries.name: A Woolly Sheep
entries: The village's prize winning lamb, "Ramsey", has gone missing, after being seen wandering in the direction of Dracolich Lake. Ramsey's shepherd, Mary, is distraught, and requests the help of the party in tracking the lamb down.

Dracolich Lake is a mystical pond found deep in the Mushroom forest, wherein the colossal skull of an Ancient Green Dracolich lies. Some say the skull may grant unearthly powers, or even twist reality itself. Many cruel and terrible creatures are rumoured to have spawned from those ancient, wicked bones.

entries.name: Mush-a-room About Nothing
entries: Ramsey was last seen trotting towards the Mushroom Forest ({@adventure Map 1|MaryHadALittleDracolich|2|Adventure Map 1}), a place home to many strange creatures and fungi. Upon entering the forest, the players can make a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to pick up Ramsey's trail. On a failed check, the players find mega-mushrooms instead.

If a player eats a mega-mushroom, they must make a {@dc 9} Constitution saving throw. On a fail, they are {@condition poisoned} for the next 10 minutes. On a success, they gain Advantage on {@skill Perception}, {@skill Insight}, and {@skill Survival} checks for the next two hours.

A player can spend 10 minutes coating a piercing weapon or up to three pieces of piercing ammunition with the juices of the mega-mushroom, which remains potent for the next 12 hours. When that weapon strikes another creature, that creature must make a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Pixie Mix
entries: After picking up Ramsey's trail, as the party moves through the forest, they are ambushed by two {@creature Vicious Shroomsprite|DMSecretWeapon|Vicious Shroomsprites} and two {@creature Psychatrunk|DMSecretWeapon|Psychatrunks}.
Roll initiative.

After the party defeats the two Psychatrunks, the Vicious Shroomsprites will flee, and the party can progress, reaching a clearing in the forest: Dracolich Lake ({@adventure Map 2|MaryHadALittleDracolich|2|Adventure Map 2}).

If the party falls to the Psychatrunks, they will awaken with 1 hit point left in the clearing beside Dracolich Lake. The Psychatrunks appear to have brought them to the area for an unknown purpose, at the behest of an unknown force.

In the centre of the water lies the colossal skull. A successful Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will reveal a small quantity of {@spell Goodberry||Goodberries} growing nearby (5 Goodberries per player). Consuming one restores 1 hit point.
The players also see lamb tracks leading through the mud and between the deceased Dracolich jaws, into the horned skull.

entries.name: Portals and Puzzles
entries: Inside the skull, the air fizzles with draconic magic. The floor has been hewn into a grid formation. The players must complete two Portal Puzzles to pass through the maze and follow Ramsey's trail.
The Rules:

items: The party begins on the tile marked START. There is a portal on the tile marked END, but it is not active.
In order to activate the portal to move forward in the dungeon, the party must step on every weighted tile to trigger them, and power up the portal.

If the party steps on the same tile more than once, the magical contraption overloads. When this happens, each player character takes a number of d10 Force damage equal to their proficiency bonus, and are teleported back to the starting tile. The puzzle then resets.
The aim is to step on every tile only once, finishing on the tile marked END to step through the activated portal.
The party must move as a unit, and cannot split up to complete the puzzle.
Any tiles blocked by Rocks cannot be stepped on, and do not need to be stepped on to activate the portal.

entries: Upon passing through the first portal, the party feels a wave of draconic magic sweep through them. Each player gains a breath weapon attack for the next 24 hours.

It costs an action to use, and spews forth elemental damage in a 30 ft. line. All creatures in that line must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d6} damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. Once used, it cannot be used again until the players finish a short rest. Players can choose the damage type of their breath weapon from among Fire, Lightning, Acid, Cold, or Poison when they receive this boon.

entries.name: Curse of the Dracolich
entries: Upon passing through the second portal, the party emerge in a fey clearing ({@adventure Map 3|MaryHadALittleDracolich|2|Adventure Map 3}). Ramsey, the lamb, stands trembling and bleating at the centre of the glade. His body has begun to mutate due to the magical influence of the fallen Dracolich. The party hear a hiss as a hideous creature, a beast enthralled and twisted with the Draconic magic of the dungeon, leaps towards them. Roll initiative.
On initiative count 1, Ramsey will open his mouth and let loose a jet of flame towards the {@creature Dragon Cursed Feral|DMSecretWeapon}, dealing {@damage 1d4} Fire damage to the monster.
After defeating the monster, Ramsey will run towards the party and leap, quivering into their arms. He is ready to be taken home. He is pleasantly warm to the touch.

entries.name: Ramsey's Return
entries: Mary weeps with joy upon Ramsey's safe return. She fusses over his physical changes, but Ramsey seems happy and content, and swiftly trots into his field and begins grazing, occasionally raising his head from the earth to belch a small jet of flame.

Mary thanks the party, and gives them 50 gold pieces each. Word of their heroics swiftly spread across the county, and the party can expect to find more requests for their services in the nearby town of Slumpkin, their reputation as adventurers swiftly growing.
At the DM's discretion, the party levels up.

data.name: The Trapmaker's Garden Puzzles
entries: One of the most common D&D problems is boring combat. As such, some of the best puzzles are ones that mesh cleanly into combat, demanding players think carefully about their actions and movement. The Elements Battle Puzzle is a fantastic, easy to implement puzzle that can be tweaked for different combat encounters.

entries.name: Four Elements Battle Puzzle: Basic Rules
entries: The combat encounter takes place on this grid, with at least four player characters.
The grid is marked with four elemental symbols on various tiles: Fire, Water, Air and Earth.
Each symbol corresponds to a damage type:

items: Fire = Fire Damage
Water = Cold Damage
Air = Thunder Damage
Earth = Bludgeoning Damage

entries: An elemental effect is activated by having each tile with that Elemental symbol on it occupied by a player character.
For example, if all four Fire tiles are stood on at once, the Fire elemental effect activates.
Using this simple mechanism, complex and interactive fights can be implemented! Here are two examples of encounters using the Elements Battle Puzzle.

entries.name: Variation #1: The Telegraphed Damage Boss Puzzle
entries: In this puzzle, activating all the tiles of one damage type grants the players resistance to that damage type for as long as all the tiles are occupied by player characters. For example, if all the Fire tiles are occupied by player characters, all players resist Fire damage, until one of them moves.

In this boss fight, the players are fighting an elemental creature that has a devastating area of effect elemental attack. On the turn before unleashing the effect, the elemental glows a certain colour. Red for Fire, Blue for Water, White for Air, and Green for Earth.

The puzzle requires the players work out what the glowing colours mean, and then move themselves to the correct tiles to give themselves resistance to that attack. This can be made more difficult by giving the elemental other attacks that forcibly move players, or having it attempt to shove them on its turn.
This puzzle allows the DM to present a dangerous threat to the players that demands careful strategy and positioning to survive.

entries.name: Variation #2: Exploiting the Weakness Puzzle
entries: In this puzzle, activating all the tiles of one damage type removes that damage immunity from the monster the party is fighting. For example, they may be facing an elemental demon that is immune to all damage. However, by positioning each party member on the Earth tiles, the demon loses its immunity to Bludgeoning damage.

After being sufficiently damaged, the demon may then destroy a Bludgeoning tile, forcing the player characters to shift tactics and exploit a different damage type to damage the monster. It may be the case that players need to pay attention to their turn order, holding actions and moving in a way that allows the Barbarian to strike with Bludgeoning damage, and then quickly shifting to let the Warlock strike with Cold damage on the turn immediately after.
This puzzle allows the DM to present a seemingly unbeatable foe that demands teamwork and creativity to overcome.

entries.name: Spectral Knight's Tour
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Extreme
The Spectral Knight's Tour is a puzzle that is at once very challenging but simple when you know how. I recommend presenting this puzzle to players who really want a challenge.

It makes for a great "homework" puzzle. Present this to the party at the end of a session, and give them the week to play around with it. If they complete it by the start of the following session, they get some awesome loot! If not, a friendly NPC can guide them (give hints from "The Method" section) and they should be able to get through!

entries.name: Rules
entries: The aim is to start at the square marked one, and move around the grid, landing on every square, while never ending on the same square more than once.

However, you must move as a knight would move in chess: Two squares in any direction vertically, followed by 1 square horizontally, or, two squares in any direction horizontally, followed by one square vertically, in an "L" shape.
Here's the map with the first move taken. It will take 20 moves to complete The Eldritch Knight's Tour.

entries.name: The Method
entries: It quickly becomes apparent when attempting this puzzle that you can give yourself the best chance of success by maximising the amount of available space for later moves.
Upon recognising this, we can see that it makes sense to always stay as close to the sides of the grid as possible with our moves, leaving the most room possible in the middle of the grid for later.

From here, we want to ideally find a way to "loop", going round and round reaching new squares in a pattern. To do this, we choose a direction (in the puzzle, the direction is picked for us: clockwise). By moving clockwise around the grid, and always choosing the square as close to the edge as possible, it becomes very simple to complete the Eldritch Knight's Tour in several ways!
Here is the most natural solution using the premade first move, moving clockwise around the grid, staying as close to the edges as we can.
Here is another particularly beautiful solution where the puzzle ends on the exact opposite side of the grid to where it began. In this approach, we begin by moving counterclockwise.

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #6
entries: This riddle is spoken aloud by a treasure chest whenever a creature moves within 10 ft. of it. To answer the riddle, a player must place their hand on the chest and speak the answer aloud.
On a correct guess, the chest opens, and its valuable contents are free to be plundered.
On an incorrect guess, the chest transforms into a {@creature mimic}, the treasure is lost, and the player character is {@condition grappled}.
The falling tears, like leaves of autumn,
The crimson swords, the gold that bought them,
That does not rust to my hand touched,
But in my name doth take so much,
The final hope to the great tormented,
The greatest gift, too oft resented,
Spurn me not, 'stead think on this,
The aching pain spared by my kiss
What am I?

entries.name: Solution
entries: Death

data.name: Tusk and Claw
entries: Tusk and Claw is an underwater adventure designed for a party of four level 5 characters, featuring a healthy mix of combat and puzzles.

entries.name: Premise
entries: The party are on a mission to acquire a fragment of tusk from the ferocious Tidal Mammoth. There is only one kink in the plan, the creature is long extinct, and was believed to have dwelled many leagues beneath the ocean.
Hearing of their quest, wealthy socialite and "collector", Cornelius Claw, has requested their attendance at his laboratory, Claw Blacksmiths, on the southern coast of the continent.

entries.name: Shaking the Claw
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|TuskAndClaw|2|Adventure Map 1})
The party reach Claw Blacksmiths in the early afternoon. They are at once greeted and ushered inside by an elderly Sea Elf, Cornelius Claw. He speaks in a pompous, whispery voice.
"So, I hear you're seeking the Tusk of a Tidal Mammoth? Something I too have long had my Elf eyes on. What a treasure that would be!
But, alas, my years have at last caught up with me. But you, I think, have just the right motivations and... je ne sais quoi to get this done.

Take my advice and magic, and we'll share the spoils of this quest! You take the Tusk, I just need confirmation that what's rumoured to be down there is actually down there, and then I can send in my people."

Cornelius will offer each party member a {@item Potion of Water's Welcome|DMSecretWeaponAdventures}. It lasts for 24 hours. The Water's Welcome Potion gives each player a swim speed equal to their walking speed, 60 feet of {@sense darkvision}, the ability to speak and breathe underwater, and an immunity to the crushing pressure of the depths.
Cornelius will also give the party an ancient, battered map, tattooed on Kraken hide, and then lift the watery forge in the centre of the room, opening a route in the ocean.
"Follow the map, it's mostly straight down anyway, and start hunting for the Temple of Ancient Things... Assuming it even exists that is.
Once there, find a way in, and there is, so the legends say, the Graveyard of the Tidal Mammoths. Good luck."
The party plunges into the deep, and the adventure truly begins as Cornelius rolls the forge back in place above them.

entries.name: The Endless Dark
entries: As the party descends, an eerie tranquillity falls over them. No life seems to exist in these waters.
The depths here are cruel and ache with a seeping poison. Each party member must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} for the next 24 hours.
After several hours of continuous diving, the inky grey that the {@sense darkvision} affords the party begins to bleed with colour ({@adventure Map 2|TuskAndClaw|2|Adventure Map 2}).

Luminescent algae grows, and as indicated by the map, all over the long dead Aquatiquities civilization. A mysterious, territorial people, they were hunted to extinction below the waters by... something.

If a party member has a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) greater than 15, they catch movement out of the corner of their eye, just in time to shout a warning to the group. If not, the party are caught {@status surprised} as two huge, multi-limbed creatures dart through the waters and strike.
If a player character has completed the Morty Viper's Sinking Circus Adventure, they will recognise them as {@creature Black Beast of Argh!|DMSecretWeapon}
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Riddles in the Deep
entries: After dispatching the beasts, the party are left alone in the ruined city to hunt for the Temple undisturbed.

A successful {@dc 11} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will lead the way; if a player rolls Investigation above a 16, they will also find 1,000 gold pieces worth of rare plants and magical ingredients.
Upon reaching the temple, the party comes face to face with a great, stone Tidal Mammoth Statue. This statue hides a secret, and bars the way forward.
Show the following image to the party, with the accompanying text.
100 cuts, no more, no less, are needed to bring her down.
{@i *The full rules and solution to this puzzle can be found in {@adventure Puzzle Room|TuskAndClaw|1|Balance of the Tidal Mammoth}.}

entries.name: The Temple
entries: ({@adventure Map 3|TuskAndClaw|2|Adventure Map 3})
After correctly solving the riddle, the great statue bows its head, and sinks slowly into the stone floor. Behind it is a tunnel, leading to the Graveyard of the Tidal Mammoths.
In the black depths of the ocean, silence is the norm. Yet here, the silence feels heavier, stronger, but not unpleasant. There is a sense of grandeur and dignity in the temple.

The party swims on, emerging at the ceiling of a cavernous, open chamber. At the base lies an enormous Tidal Mammoth Skeleton, half buried in sand. It is perfectly preserved, a slumbering giant, peaceful in solitude. In life, these beasts must have been truly awe inspiring.

However, the tranquillity is short-lived. As the party descends, they feel a shock wave pulse through the water. Something slithers down below. A jet of bubbles spiral upwards as a subtle, hateful voice echoes in the minds of the players.
"Prey? Here? Lucky me!"

"Can you feel the power here, brave little monkeys? Did you swim all the way here for the succulent death magic this forgotten Titan still holds? I've feasted endlessly for centuries. My strength is bursting, a change of diet is just what I needed. You'll die in the dark, little monkeys, and I'll feast on your decay for centuries more!"
The sands shift, and from the depths emerges an enormous, serpentine body: A {@creature Kenisiswyrm|DMSecretWeapon}. Psychic predators that feed on the necrotic energy of death and decay.
The serpent's psychic torment continues as it rises through the water. It is joined by two hideous, undead sharks. Rotting flesh hangs from their bones.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: After slaying the {@creature Great Wight Shark|DMSecretWeapon|Great Wights} and the {@creature Kenisiswyrm|DMSecretWeapon}, it falls with a scream into the sands below. The party is free to swim down and harvest materials from the Tidal Mammoth skeleton. Some scraps of ivory have been chipped and broken from the main tusk, making it possible for the party to gather all they need without disturbing the colossal skeleton itself.

Upon returning to the surface, they find Cornelius anxiously awaiting them. He immediately presses them for information on what they found, declaring he'll send a team in at once to "pick the place dry, if we can".

Should the party tell him the truth, he will thank them graciously, cheerfully handing over 2,000 gold pieces and giving each of them an additional bottle of {@item Potion of Water's Welcome|DMSecretWeapon|Water's Welcome Potion}. The magic contained within the bones of the Tidal Mammoth will soon be harvested for the benefit of the locals, and at a tidy profit for Cornelius Claw.

If the party lies, and says there is nothing to be found, he will sigh ruefully, and thank them for their bravery in the exploration. He will hand over 1,000 gold pieces for the party's trouble, and tear up the map when it is returned to him, vowing this to be the last time he chases legends and fairy tales for profit.
The Tidal Mammoth and its temple will be left, preserved in tranquillity and dignity, at the bottom of the ocean, free from parasitic aberrations and looting surface dwellers.

entries.name: Balance of the Tidal Mammoth
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Easy
Before the players stands a large statue of a Tidal Mammoth. Below it is carved the simple instruction: 100 cuts, no more, no less, are needed to bring her down.
On the wall beside the statue are numerous buttons, each with strange letters on them. In the centre is one large button: "Twinned Spell!" is written on it.

entries.name: How It Works
entries: The players can push the buttons. Once a button is pressed, it sinks into the wall and cannot be pressed again until the riddle is completed, or resets.
Each button deals "damage" to the statue of the Tidal Mammoth. The amount of damage is equivalent to the number given in Roman numerals on the button.
The only way to damage the Tidal Mammoth statue is by using the buttons. Conventional damage sources do nothing.
The twinned spell button will double the damage dealt by the next button.
The aim is to deal exactly 100 damage to the statue.
If the damage dealt exceeds 100, all the buttons instantly reset, any damage marked on the statue is reset, and the players take Psychic damage equal to 3x their character level.

entries.name: Solution
entries: To deal exactly 100 damage, the players must push the buttons shown below. The order doesn't matter, except that the Twinned Spell button must immediately precede XXVII.
{@b III, XII, TWINNED SPELL, XXVII, XXXI}

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #7
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Medium
I can beat you black and blue,
But speaking's something I can't do,
You might find me, in a game,
But not diamond, nor heart of flame,
'Stead black as coal, but I'm not found,
In that which hews coal from the ground,
I can beat you black and blue,
When held in hands stronger than you.
What am I?

entries.name: Solution
entries: CLUB

data.name: The Prince and the Bandit
entries: The Prince and the Bandit is a thrilling, classic-pulp inspired adventure of roleplay and combat designed for four level 9 player characters.

entries.name: Premise
entries: Prince Hugo Aster has been captured by the villainous Kalgan, a notorious bandit leader! The party have been summoned to the hand of the king, who seeks a desperate rescue of his son, and bloody vengeance on the bandit lord.

entries.name: King's Council
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|ThePrinceAndTheBandit|2|Adventure Map 1})
King Albert Aster sits defeated on his throne, drinking endless mugs of hot tea, a broken man. He speaks in a rasping, weary voice, a voice that has gone many days and nights without rest.
The king will implore the party for help, with the following rewards on offer:

items: 8,000 gold for the safe return of Prince Hugo Aster, wherever he is.
3,000 gold for the capture of Kalgan alive.
1,000 gold for Kalgan's head as proof of his destruction.

entries: The king will also share what information the crown has on Kalgan.
He is a notorious bandit lord, leader of a band of raiders named the Red Reavers. It is believed this band ambushed the Prince's retinue and kidnapped him.
The Reavers move in small groups, and one of these groups has been active near the party's current location, on the road towards the Leaky Casque Tavern.
Kalgan is described as a tall, well-built man with a weathered face, red hair and fierce beard.
Prince Hugo Aster is lean, soft-featured and tall, with light brown hair.

entries.name: The Road and The Red Reavers
entries: ({@adventure Map 2|ThePrinceAndTheBandit|2|Adventure Map 2})

The quest begins with the party approaching the next settlement in the path of the Red Reavers, a roadside tavern named the Leaky Casque, as indicated by the king. Successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks will reveal a small plume of smoke, likely from a campfire, rising above the trees, indicating that the tavern is still occupied.
Upon noticing this, the party can attempt to sneak closer to the flames. A collective {@dc 16} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check will allow them to approach unnoticed.
If the Stealth check fails, the bandits hear them coming, and hail them directly as soon as they are within earshot, inviting them round the fire.
If successfully stealthy, the party can roll for initiative at Advantage should they start a fight before being noticed.

There are three {@creature Raider|DMSecretWeapon|reavers} around the fire, none of whom fit the description of Kalgan. There is no sign of their having been an attack and the Reavers are not hostile, unless attacked.

Initially, they will try to convince the party to enter the inn with promises of free drink and food and will deny any knowledge of who Kalgan is, or their involvement with the Red Reavers. A successful {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check will reveal this to be a lie. They will also deny any knowledge of the Prince. A {@dc 21} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check will reveal this to be truthful.

There are three more {@creature Raider|DMSecretWeapon|raiders} inside the inn, alongside two {@creature Raider Sorcerer|DMSecretWeapon|raider sorcerers}. If the party enter peacefully, while the drinks are being poured a player with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 16 or above will see the three reavers entering behind them locking the door.

The raiders will attack when the door is locked and they have positioned themselves to roughly surround the party. If the party refuse to enter the inn or initiate a fight outside, those inside the inn will burst out and attack them in the open as combat begins.

entries.name: Bed and Breakfast
entries: Once the combat has ended the party can question one of the raiders or sorcerers by making a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check.
On a success, the raider will tell them Kalgan is in a hidden stronghold in the hills to the northeast and describes the location of one of its entrances.
Each raider has 150 gp in addition to their equipment.
The owners of the Leaky Casque and its patrons can be found tied up in the basement, grateful for the rescue. They offer the party free food, drink and beds until they move on.

If the party were unable to find information from the raiders, or they killed them all before questioning them, one of the owners will pass them the information, having overheard the raiders talking the night before.

entries.name: Arresting Development
entries: The party arrives at the location they were told the stronghold would be only to be met with an illusion hiding the door. All the party sees is a boulder in place of the door that the bandit told them should have been here.

{@spell Dispel Magic} will remove the illusion, or if a character states their intention to physically interact with the boulder they can make a {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to detect the illusion and find the mechanism to open the door behind it.
({@adventure Map 3|ThePrinceAndTheBandit|2|Adventure Map 3})
Advancing inside the stronghold (starting at the bottom left), the party are confronted with crackling golden sparks, arcing through the tight corridors.

Any creature that enters the golden light (any square on the map that contains the sparks) that is of a chaotic or neutral alignment must make a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw or become {@condition paralyzed||paralysed}.

A player can repeat this save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. If another player moves them out of the sparks, the paralysis also ends. Once a player has succeeded on a saving throw against the sparks, they are immune to their effect for the next 24 hours.
As the party moves through the corridors, they see two paralysed reavers with weapons drawn, brutally beaten, their bloodshot eyes darting from person to person as the party stands before them.
At that very moment, a commanding voice echoes from the path leading to the large chamber with the glowing sigil in the centre, calling the party to come forward into the light.

Entering the chamber at the top of the map, the party see five knights in ornate silver armour standing in a half circle around two paralysed figures. As the party draw closer, they can see the trapped prisoners are Prince Aster and the bandit lord Kalgan.

entries.name: By Order of Alise
entries: The leader of the five knights steps forward, and announces herself as Confessor Alise.
She will reveal that it was her knights who captured the prince, and then stormed Kalgan's stronghold to have a safehouse to hold him for long enough to draw the attention of the king.

It is their intent to murder both the Prince and Kalgan, framing the bandit lord for the kidnapping, and then bring both corpses to the King. They will be handsomely rewarded for the destruction of the kidnapper, all while ridding the king of his only heir, and earning the favour of the crown.
Through this political influence, and the king left without an heir, their order will be perfectly placed to seize power when the king finally dies.
Now the party has arrived, confirming the crown are aware of the kidnapping, all that is left to do is murder the Prince, bandits and any remaining witnesses.
Alise draws her sword as she speaks.
Roll initiative.

entries.name: Endgame
entries: The party are fighting {@creature Confessor Alise|DMSecretWeapon} and four {@creature Confessor Knight|DMSecretWeapon|Confessor Knights}.
During the fight, if a party member shoves Kalgan out of the paralysing light, he will join the fight on their side. He uses a normal {@creature Raider|DMSecretWeapon} stat block.

After defeating the knights, Kalgan will thank the party and offer them 4,000 gold for his freedom. The party are free to take his offer, or arrest him. Should they choose to do the latter, he will surrender without a fight.
Basic loot can be found in the stronghold, totalling 2,300 gold, various mundane weapons, and armour, supplies and casting components worth up to a total of 900 gold.
From here, the party return the prince to the royal family and are free to claim their reward.
If the party released Kalgan, the prince will make no mention of it upon being joyfully reunited with his father.

If they present the bandit to the king, the prince will explain Kalgan had no hand in the kidnapping. The party are rewarded as promised, and Kalgan is sentenced to act as the prince's personal bodyguard for 900 days to repay his debt to the realm.
In any instance, the king is grateful, and the party have earned favour with a powerful ally.

entries.name: The Riddle Door
entries: The party's way forward is barred by a door with no keyhole. When a creature moves within 20 feet of the door, a loud voice speaks the following riddle.
I must eat to stay alive,
But if I drink I'll surely die.
What am I?
(Hint: if the party investigates, the door feels warm to the touch)
{@b Solution:} Fire.
To open this door, you must damage it with specific damage types. To find the damage type, the party must answer each riddle.
To progress, the party must first damage the door with Fire. The door will then speak again, this time with the following riddle.
I crack but do not break,
I may rumble but never shake,
I can clap with no hands,
As a cantrip spell to command.
What am I?
(Hint: if the party investigates, they receive a slight static shock from the door).
{@b Solution:} Thunder.
Upon dealing Thunder damage to the door, it speaks a final riddle:
What can you catch, but never throw?
(Hint: The door sneezes)
{@b Solution:} A Cold.
Upon dealing the third and final damage type to the door (Cold), it swings open, and the party may pass.

entries.name: Riddle of the Mimiking #8
entries: {@b Difficulty:} Easy
Howling, 'neath the midnight moon,
With no mouth, nor lungs to sing my tune,
Crying with wolf, soaring with hawk,
Falling with rain, with panther, I stalk
I move a burning, freezing dance,
Without feet, nor legs, nor shadow to glance,
Felt by all, and seen by none,
Call my name, and this riddle be done.
What am I?

entries.name: Solution
entries: WIND
