entries.name: Introduction
entries: This adventure is designed for a party of four to six adventurers at level 3. It can be introduced at any time the player characters have an evening free, and are near a large river or the coast.
The party have come across an explosively colourful notice board in the center of town, which reads in enormous, neon capital letters:
ONE NIGHT ONLY, TONIGHT, BY THE WATER, SEE THE INCREDIBLE MORTY VIPER'S SINKING CIRCUS!! FREE ADMISSION TO ALL!
The sign post is surrounded by excited, chattering locals and children.
The party decide to check it out, little knowing they have taken their first step into the jaws of murder, mystery and magic.

entries.name: The Sinking Circus
entries: As night descends the party reaches the waterside, you find yourself dazzled by an incredible sight. Anchored in the water is an enormous, beautiful ship. It appears to be a converted galleon, painted in luminous colours, with a wide, open deck complete with a large assortment of tables, games, and attractions in the night air. Beside the vessel you see numerous smaller boats that likely serve as the workers' living quarters. To look upon the sinking circus is to have one's eyes drawn to a titanic big top tent, or at least, the top half of one, tethered to the front of the vessel, presumably holding an enormous circus ring within the water below.

Various humanoid workers of many races scuttle up and down the Galleon, lighting torches, playing music, selling food or doing rudimentary but exciting magical displays of light and sound. People are filing up the gangplank, and greeting them there is a Sea Elf in a large top hat, brandishing a scepter and making full use of his grand, booming voice. This man is Morty Viper, the ringmaster of Morty Viper's Sinking Circus.

entries.name: Morty Viper & Don Cheese
entries: As the party approaches the ship, Morty Viper catches sight of them and calls out. (Morty has a theatrical, booming voice, and somehow upon hearing him speak, you're aware every line is punctuated with at least one exclamation mark)

"Ahhh!!! Come forward dear friends, come forward! Ready yourself to board the great Sinking Circus!! Marvel and magic await, for you stand in the company of Morty Viper, greatest showman and wizard the world has ever known! Make haste!! The games await, and should you desire to see a display of my REAL POWER, the true show starts in the Sinking Big Top!"
Should the party stop and speak with Morty, take the opportunity to drop tantalizing hints about his "great show!" and how he has "fantastic, magical powers of the deep!!"

Beside Viper stands a fierce looking man, wearing dark clothing offset by a brilliantly luminescent name tag that reads "DON CHEESE, FIRST MATE", and an attractive, green pendant that hangs down over his clothes. He limply holds an ornate Trident by his side, a marked difference from Morty brandishing his scepter with every word he speaks. You also notice a few short daggers hanging down from his belt, that you recognise as the circus type performers might juggle as part of a show. Don Cheese seems to be the one actually keeping things going, occasionally barking orders to the crew, and wincing every time Morty shouts salutations at potential patrons right beside his ear.
As the party ascends the gangplank and steps onto the ship, you get a clear view of the deck and all the attractions and games.
[See {@adventure Fig. A|MortyVipersSinkingCircus|1|Fig. A} in the Map Pack for a map of the ship]

entries.name: The Games
entries: There are various games available for the party to play at the Sinking Circus.

entries.name: Hook-a-Kraken
entries: An excited gnome stands beside a wide table on which a small pool is set up, many floating Kraken with small hook rings fastened to them float on the water.
{@b How to play:} The PC makes a {@dc 11} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check to pull up a Kraken.
On a success, the player rolls a {@dice d20} to determine their prize:

rows: Giant Inflatable Kraken* (can only be won once).
footnotes: {@i *(While equipped, PC automatically succeeds Constitution saves against drowning, and can swim for twice as long without provoking {@condition exhaustion}).}

entries.name: The Kissing Booth
entries: An attractive, muscular half-orc woman stands behind a booth, with the words: NOT QUITE LOVE, BUT A DECENT APPROXIMATION! ANY HUMANOID FORM AVAILABLE!

As the players watch, the attendant will shift form into a broad, bearded male dwarf, then an androgynous-looking elf with crimson hair, then back to the half-orc woman form. The only physical characteristic all forms share is their startling beauty. The booth owner will call out to any player who moves within 15 feet of the booth, and the PC must make a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw or approach the booth and pay 1 gold for a kiss. They may request a form for the shapechanger to take should they desire a particular one.

If the player succeeds on the Wisdom saving throw, and approaches the booth anyway, they can make a {@dc 15} Charisma check when interacting with the attendant. On a success, the booth attendant will offer a kiss for free.

entries.name: Rope Ladder Climb
entries: A young human female mans a stand that has four ropes side by side.
{@b How to play:} One PC plays against 3 NPCs. The PC may choose to roll for either Dexterity or Strength to attempt the climb.

As they climb, the player feels a strange buzzing run through the rope, and it suddenly begins swinging wildly around. They notice the ropes are attached to mechanical contraptions at the top designed to throw climbers off. They must make either a {@dc 14} Dexterity or Strength saving throw. If they have attempted this game before, they make the save with Advantage. On a success they reach the top first and win the game. On a failure they fall to the deck of the ship.
{@b Prize:} One {@item potion of climbing||potion of climbing speed}. (Climbing speed is doubled for one hour after consumption).

entries.name: Test Your Might
entries: A bored minotaur sits beside a simple high striker. An impressive warhammer sits by the side.
{@b How to play:} The PC makes a Strength check to use the hammer to hit the high striker. Players without proficiency in heavy weapons make the roll with Disadvantage.

rows: The minotaur worker chuckles to himself and the puck barely moves. No prize.
The puck shoots up to below the halfway point. No prize.
The puck shoots ¾ of the way up the tower. The minotaur will offer the PC another go.
The bell rings. The PC receives a tarrasque plushie.
The puck knocks the bell off the tower, and the puck flies out into the water. The player receives a giant plushy Tarrasque.

entries.name: Surf the Seal-Irons
entries: Four large, barking seal-like creatures stand in a line by the edge of the ship. They sound and move like seals, but with very flat, glowing bellies that seem to be hissing out steam, and look hot to the touch. Looking off the deck of the ship, the players see a rudimentary obstacle course set up on the water. Tending the game is an elderly, cheerful dwarf; he introduces the seal-like creatures as "Seal-Irons".

{@b How to play:} The PC plays against 3 NPCs. They first make a {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check to ride a {@creature Seal-Iron|DMSecretWeapon} as the race begins. The PC realises the Seal-Irons are very familiar with the route, and enthusiastic to race; the difficulty here will come from staying on!
As the race continues, the PC must make another {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check to avoid being thrown from the Seal-Iron as it races round the final corner.
{@b Results:} If either check fails, the PC is thrown into the ocean, and the Seal-Iron will circle them, barking loudly and affectionately splashing in the water.
If both checks succeed, add the results together:

rows: The PC comes in a narrow second place.
The PC wins, and receives a Seal-Iron plushie.
The PC sets a new record, and receives a giant inflatable Killer Whale.*
footnotes: {@i *(While equipped, PC automatically succeeds Constitution saves against drowning, and can swim for twice as long without provoking {@condition exhaustion}).}

entries.name: Lil Lightnin' Bolt
entries: Four expensive looking, clockwork contraptions named "Lil Lightnin'" are set up in front of a shooting range, within which many inflated balloons are moving around swiftly on a system of ropes.

{@b How to play:} One PC plays against 3 NPCs. They make a ranged attack roll (+5) using the Lil Lightnin', which fires out a brilliant bolt of light toward the balloons. A roll of 15 or higher is needed to pop a balloon. If the PC is a spellcaster, they can add their proficiency bonus to the attack roll.

The winner is the first to pop 3 balloons. If you pop 3 balloons within 5 attacks you win, and get a single {@spell Lil Lightnin' Bolt|DMSecretWeapon|scroll of Lil Lightnin' Bolt}. After making 5 attack rolls and not winning, an NPC is declared the winner and the game ends.

entries.name: Here Comes Trouble
entries: At any point after a PC wins a game, one of the losing NPCs will accost them. They will accuse the player of cheating, and loudly call a friend over to them for back-up. The pair are clearly drunk, and also alarmingly seem armed. Even with no provocation, they will swiftly launch into a combat stance: it's a fight!
[Use {@adventure Fig. A|MortyVipersSinkingCircus|1|Fig. A} for the battlemap]

After successfully taking down the drunkards, Morty Viper will appear out of the crowd. He will thank the players for taking care of business, and offer them free front row tickets to the show in the Big Top.

He tells the players he will start when they're ready, but in no longer than an hour, should they desire to take a short rest and look around the circus a little more first. As soon as they're ready, the players should make their way to the lower deck to access the Big Top, and prepare for the greatest show on the continent!

entries.name: The Big Top
entries: The party descends down one layer in the ship, and sees there is a second set of doors down here, built into the side of the vessel. They're open; beyond them the party sees a slit in some thick, striped fabric that they realise is the opening to the submerged Big Top they saw from outside.
[See {@adventure Fig. B|MortyVipersSinkingCircus|1|Fig. B} for the submerged arena]

Don Cheese now stands by the door, taking admission for the "Big Show". His face is expressionless, and one-by-one patrons hand over 30 gold each, at which point he hands over a small bottle and instructs them to drink it. When the party draws to the door, he waves them in irritably for free, hands each of them a bottle, and tells them to "drink this, if you want to breathe that is".
The bottle contains a small amount of bubbling potion. It grants the user a swimming speed equal to their walking speed for one hour, and the ability to breathe underwater.

Inside the tent are descending stairs, leading into the water. Inside, the tent opens up to reveal a beautiful arena, totally submerged in water, with luminescent, glowing algae illuminating the arena. In the centre of the ring is a pit, which appears to hold a cage, although what is inside can't be seen from here. Morty Viper spots the party, and ushers them excitedly down to the front of the ring. The crowd fills the stands behind the party, Morty Viper moves onto the stage, and a hush falls over all in attendance.

entries.name: The Greatest Show
entries: The show begins with Morty Viper's speech. Read the following:

"Ladies, Gentlemen! All peoples of all walks of life, you are about to bear witness to the greatest show on the continent! Behold this magical artifact I hold in my hand! The wise and travelled among you may already have guessed, the jewel atop my mighty scepter was indeed harvested from the heart of the Kraken itself! It requires incredible magical power to use, but in the right hands, it offers extraordinary abilities! Yes, indeed, the power to command all life that dwells below the waters! Know only that nothing will harm you while in my domain, I am in total control! But be dazzled, be terrified, be amazed, as I command, the ALMIGHTY BLACK BEAST OF ARGH!"

Morty conducts his own words with his scepter as he speaks, and at the apex of his words, a terrible roar echoes around the ring, and in the depths and the darkness, you see Don Cheese crank a metal handle, as the bars of a cage are raised, and the ALMIGHTY {@creature Black Beast of Argh!|DMSecretWeapon|BLACK BEAST OF ARGH} swims forward into the ring.
The Black Beast of Argh is a terrifying sight:

Its size is astounding; its mammoth body is propelled by huge, insectoid limbs which pulse and claw, carving the water around it. Deep, yellow, sunken eyes gleam out above a titanic maw of dagger teeth and rippling tentacles. Yet despite the beast's terrifying form, it moves with an undeniable grace beneath the water. Bubbles escape from its gills as it drifts almost lazily around the ring, emitting an aura of casual, restrained power felt by all in attendance. It makes no noise as it moves.

entries.name: So That's Why They Called It "Argh!"
entries: Morty will command the beast to do several tricks, including swimming in circles, through some rings, and performing flips. The crowd that was once anxious cheer delightedly, the menacing creature obeying Morty's every command. Until... (read the following)

Suddenly, you see a flash of green fill the Black Beast's eyes. It lets loose a terrible roar, begins to violently thrash around, sending powerful tremors through the waters. The excited atmosphere of the room is sliced open. The audience stops laughing and cheering, perhaps uncertain of whether this is part of the show or not. Then the Black Beast turns to Morty Viper, who looks on, clearly terrified. Something has gone horribly wrong. He holds the scepter out in his hands, stares at it for a second, shakes it, looks back at the beast, and then flings it in the water above him and begins swimming as fast as he can toward the back of the stage. Once more the beast roars and charges after him, just as Morty sandwiches himself between two large metal boxes, barely out of reach of the terrible creature. Behind the party, you hear a scream—and chaos descends as people begin wildly scrambling upward towards the exit. The Beast hears the commotion and turns back to face the crowd. Its teeth are bared, its eyes wild—it lunges at the fleeing circus patrons, with the party at the very front. It's a fight!
At the start of the Black Beast of Argh's turn, if it has less than half hit points (48), read the following, and proceed to the next chapter.

Clearly wounded, the Black Beast of Argh lets out a terrible roar, and as it does so, unfurls scaly, thick black fins. Each party member is pushed back by the force of the water, and it swims high above them, smashing one of the support beams of the Big Top as it does so. It makes straight for the only one left in the room besides the party and Morty: Don Cheese, who is floating far above near the entrance, apparently frozen in shock. The party look on in horror as the beast opens its mighty maw and closes it around Don Cheese's body, swallowing him whole. You then hear a tearing sound as it forces itself out of the water, onto the ship.

entries.name: The Show Goes On
entries: The party hears a terrified yelp from Morty, still cowering between the metal boxes, begging for help. He is stuck.

If the party choose to help Morty, they will be able to pull him free of the boxes he has lodged himself between with a successful {@dc 12} Strength check. Morty's voice is considerably whimpier, and less grandiose. He will confess he has no magical powers, and the scepter he carries is simply for show. He merely assumed the beast did what he said because it "responded well to authority", and he assumed it had already been trained, and perhaps was lost or ran away from another circus when he found it.
Should the party speak with Morty further, he will request that they go up on deck and see if they can stop the beast.
"Heavens, the beast is still out there. It's probably feasting on my patrons! Oh, my, this will be terrible for business!"

Upon following the beast onto the ship ({@adventure Fig. A|MortyVipersSinkingCircus|1|Fig. A}), the party sees a gaping hole in the ceiling where the monster has forced its way onto the deck. Climbing the stairs, they will see the once bustling circus deserted; the stalls have been tipped over and scattered across the deck.

The Black Beast will be standing atop the highest level of the Galleon. A cursory glance will see some of the crowd still fleeing into the night from the circus, but the beast seems uninterested in following them. It stares at the party, before a voice calls out to them, emanating from the beast itself.
"You should not have interfered! This plan was in the making too long for me to let it collapse now. Too bad, for now you die alongside that ridiculous circus clown, Viper!"

The beast opens its mouth, and out steps {@creature Don Cheese|DMSecretWeaponAdventures}, unharmed. Around his neck burns a glowing green pendant, the same shade of green you see echo behind the Black Beast's eyes. The ceremonial Trident Cheese was carrying doesn't look nearly so ceremonial as he holds it out before him, an open challenge to the party.
"Any final words?"

Don Cheese is beyond all reason. A successful {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will allow a PC to notice the same green hue that burns behind the Black Beast's eyes shines behind Don's own. Perhaps the power of the Jewel in Don's possession is affecting him somehow.

Should the party question Cheese's motives, he will confess to attempting to kill Viper in furious vengeance for a lifetime of humiliation. He does all the work, yet Morty takes all the money. He will also confess to controlling the Black Beast of Argh all along, after obtaining a jewel which allows him to freely dominate the will of a single monster. Morty was never in control; Cheese only let him believe as much.
Don will not back down, and will attack alongside the Black Beast without warning if he gets the impression the party is stalling for time.

If a party member won a game of Surf the Seal-Irons earlier, their winning mount will leap on deck as combat begins and join them in the battle. It will follow instructions from its rider, or otherwise attempt to protect them by attacking either Don or the Black Beast, whichever is closer or appears the bigger threat at the time.

If the party participated in the game Lil Lightnin' Bolt earlier, they will spot one of the clockwork guns, broken from its stall, with two charges of Lil Lightnin' left in it on the deck. Firing the Lil Lightnin' Bolt gun takes one action.
When attacking Don, a party member may choose to attack the jewel hanging from his neck instead. The jewel shares Don's AC, but has its own Hit Points (34).
{@b Battle Outcomes:}

items: If the Jewel is destroyed while the Black Beast is still alive, the monster will be freed of Don's control, and instantly attack him, ignoring everything else. Don will beg for the party to save his life, and use his actions only to {@action Disengage} or {@action Dash} away from the beast. Should Don be killed, rendered {@condition unconscious}, or escape to over 1,000 feet away after the Jewel is destroyed, the beast will ignore the party and attempt to flee into the waters beyond the ship.
If the Jewel is destroyed after the Black Beast has been slain, Don will surrender immediately.

If Don is killed or rendered {@condition unconscious}, the Jewel will shatter immediately. If the Black Beast is still alive as Don is killed, it will go into a frenzy and attack the party wildly and at random until destroyed.

If the beast is killed and Don is below half hit points, he will attempt to flee by using the jewel to command a Seal-Iron, and then riding it into the night (he will not command the party's allied Seal-Iron).

entries.name: The End
entries: After victory, Morty will approach the party and thank them tearfully for saving his life.

He will look over the wreckage of his ship ruefully, declare the Sinking Circus to be over, and offer the party 8,000 gp (+800 gp if the party helped him escape from between the metal boxes) in thanks for his life.
If Don is still alive, Morty will hand the disgraced First Mate over to the local town or city guard, who have arrived on the scene after the circus patrons fled and reported what had happened.

He will also give the party his scepter, a sapphire, worth 2,000 gp, and sadly remark that perhaps he could have been nicer to Don, and how he may be on some level responsible for the loss of his circus.

If Don is alive and the party shattered the jewel prior to defeating him, Don will apologize tearfully to Morty and the party, and thank them for destroying the Jewel, but will ask for no leniency. He will offer the party his magic Trident in thanks, and be willingly led away by the authorities.

The party leaves the ship and returns to dry land, just as daylight breaks across the scene. They turn and give a final look back as Morty Viper's Sinking Circus slowly disappears from view. A ruin, collapsing to its final home beneath the waves.

data.name: Honest to Goblins
entries: Honest to Goblins is an adventure for four level 4 characters, featuring a mix of roleplay, combat, and strategic decision making that impacts how the story and combat unfolds. Decisions have lethal consequences in this no holds barred prison escape!

entries.name: Premise
entries: {@i The party have been captured by goblins! Don't worry, every adventurer has a story or two like this...}

The adventurers awake from an ambush that knocked them {@condition unconscious}, and find themselves in goblin jail on the peak of a mountain. Any races with a fly speed will find their wings wounded in the ambush. It is nothing permanent, but they will need at least 24 hours to recover in a safe location before flying again ({@adventure Map 1|HonestToGoblins|1|Adventure Map 1}).

They are not alone. The four of them are in a single, large cage. Around them they see three other cages, two of which contain other prisoners. Two sleeping {@creature Goblin||Goblins} are in one cage, and the third houses a well dressed elven woman, quietly weeping. The final cage lies empty, its door open.

A {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal signs of something heavy dragged through the dirt, away from this cage, and signs of a scuffle. It appears as though the one taken from this cage attempted to resist, and claw their way back inside.
Piles of equipment scatter the area, including the party's gear. The goblins seemingly have no interest or need for it. There are no guards at the peak.

entries.name: Jailbreak!
entries: To break out of the cage one character may attempt a {@dc 16} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. If a character can teleport out of the cage and pick up a weapon from one of the piles of equipment, they can try to destroy the cage. It has an AC 12 and 40 hp; only a character with a Strength score of 18 or higher can damage the cage with unarmed strikes.

If questioned, the weeping elf will introduce themselves as Honest, a wealthy merchant from a local town. She speaks through intermittent tears, explaining that the tribe of goblins and ogres occupies the mountaintop, collecting prisoners and feeding them to some terrible creature that slumbers deep in the mountain.

If the party escapes their cage and free her, she will request their protection as they progress down the mountainside. In exchange, she will pledge to do as they please, and pick up a {@item longbow} and {@item arrow||arrows} from the equipment lying there. She wields the bow with a practised air about her, and moves with unnatural stealth.

The friendly goblins are less communicative. They each jabber in broken {@language Common}, requesting the adventurers free them and pledging to lay down their lives in thanks for their rescue. They tell the party they are familiar with the mountain and can guide them past its many traps. They also make scattered, terrified references to "The Mawesome", some type of creature that slumbers nearby.

If released, they will charge forward and set upon the weapons, digging around until each is equipped with a {@item shortsword||short sword} and {@item shield}. They are loud and undisciplined, but appear enthusiastic to fight whatever faces them.

entries.name: The Bridge
entries: The only way down the mountain is to cross the goblin's bridge ({@adventure Map 2|HonestToGoblins|1|Adventure Map 2}). The party enters from the right side of the map.

From a distance, the party can see that the bridge is defended by four {@creature goblin||goblins}, two on each of the platforms, an {@creature ogre} on the bridge and a {@creature Goblin Shaman|DMSecretWeapon|goblin shaman} at the far side of the bridge.
If the party freed Honest or the two goblins, they can command them to take action in preparation for the fight.

A {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal a small gap in the mountain face that lies beyond the bridge, obscured by bushes. If Honest or the Goblins were to take up a post there, they may be able to distract or attack them on the bridge.

items: If the party sends Honest to the mountain gap, she will shoot down one of the goblins the moment the fight begins before retreating to safety.

If the party sends the Goblins to the mountain gap, they will create enough noise to draw the attention of the Ogre, who will lumber off to investigate. It will return 5 rounds after the combat is over, having killed the Goblins.

entries: Whoever the party sends to the mountain pass, the other prisoner will stay back to cover them should reinforcements arrive.
After the combat is over, if they are alive, Honest and the Goblins will rejoin the party.

entries.name: A Sinking Feeling
entries: Moving past the Goblin's Bridge, the adventurers make their way down the mountain, unknowingly drawing closer to a deadly trap.

Establish a marching order, including Honest and the Friendly Goblins if they are with the party. The path is 10 feet wide with the mountain wall on the right and a sheer drop to certain death on the left. A pit of quicksand constructed by the goblins and enhanced by their shamans lies hidden on the path; it is 10 feet wide and 20 feet long.

It has been well disguised and requires a {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to detect, although Goblins can see it clearly. Only the character leading the group will have an opportunity to see it before moving into its area.

entries.name: In the Sandtrap
entries: If the leader fails this Perception check they walk straight into it and sink to their waist immediately. The sand restricts their movement enough that they can no longer cast spells requiring Somatic or Material components.

The character in the sand can then make a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. On a failed check they sink up to their head and can no longer free themselves, sinking below the surface. They are {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, and suffocating.

A character outside the pit can throw a rope to their sinking comrade and make a {@dc 16} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to pull the trapped character up. If they fail, they are also pulled in, and must make their own Athletics check to avoid being submerged.

items: If Honest is leading the party, she will automatically fail any checks to free herself from the pit, lacking the physical strength to do so.
If the Friendly Goblins are leading the party, they will identify the Sandtrap immediately and guide the party around it.

entries: Once all the surviving party members are safe from the quicksand trap, the illusion is shattered and they can move around it safely.

entries.name: Brief Respite
entries: On the other side the party finds three {@spell Aid||Potions of Aid}. Ingesting one of these potions will give the drinker an additional 10 hit points for the next hour.
If Honest or the Goblins are with the party, they will tentatively ask if they can drink the potions, as they are weaker than the party and may need the additional protection.

items: If the party gives the potions to the other prisoners, they drink them immediately, and offer their thanks.
If the party holds onto the potions, the other prisoners nod understandingly, and prepare to move onward.

entries: While here, the group can take a short rest.
Moving on, the group continue until the path leads them to a large open clearing that seems as if it has been carved into the mountainside.

entries.name: The Mawesome
entries: The first thing they notice is the colossal gaping maw that sits at the centre of the area, taking up most of its space ({@adventure Map 3|HonestToGoblins|1|Adventure Map 3}).
Two {@creature ogre||ogres} stand nearby and can be seen holding a prisoner, who is struggling. Just as the party comes upon the scene, they release him, laughing, as he turns tail and sprints away.
As he runs, a tendril emerges from the maw and lashes at the prisoner, coiling around him and pulling him into its depths in a matter of moments.
Several goblins are scattered around the area and can be observed moving slower than would be expected of them, taking careful steps.

If Honest or the Goblins are with the party, they will infer from the scene that the Mawesome seems able to detect rapid movement, and they must be slow as they fight across the area to avoid its detection.

entries.name: Fight and Flight
entries: The adventurers emerge on the left of the map. There are the two ogres that stand on either side of the maw and 6 goblins scattered around, patrolling the area. The goblins and ogres are aware of the need to move slowly. The party must reach the other side of the map to escape.

items: Should a creature move more than 20 feet in a round, The Mawesome will {@condition grapple||grapple} them with a tendril. It has a reach of 100 feet. If {@condition grappled}, a creature must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save they are lifted 5 ft. into the air and {@condition incapacitated} unless someone uses an action to tear them free. On their next turn, they can attempt the save again. Should they fail, they are pulled into The Mawesome and instantly devoured.
The Mawesome can grapple up to 8 creatures at once. It is immune to all damage and effects.

entries: The party must make their way past The Mawesome and enemies to escape down the mountainside.
During this combat roll a {@dice d6} at initiative count 20 every round to determine what creatures arrive as reinforcements:
If the Friendly Goblins or Honest are with the party, they will engage the first two waves of reinforcements as they arrive, preventing them from reaching the scene to stop the party's escape.

entries.name: Escape!
entries: The party flees the scene, The Mawesome roaring and flailing its tendrils wildly.
If the party gave the Potions of Aid to the other prisoners, they will join them in the descent, running for their lives.
If the other prisoners did not receive the Potions of Aid, they do not join the party, having fallen protecting the party from the reinforcements.
Upon reaching the foot of the mountain the party is safe.

items: If the Goblins are alive, they will thank the party, and give each of them a Goblinoid Trinket|. It is a small locket, worn around the neck, that imbues the wearer with the cunning swiftness of a goblin. Once per dawn, the wearer can take the {@action Disengage} or {@action Hide} action as a bonus action.
If Honest is still alive, she will thank the party, and give them her bow. It is a {@item Bow of Blasting|DMSecretWeapon}.

entries: Free of the Goblin jail, the party continue on their adventure, now armed with a fresh, fireside tale of Goblins, Ogres, and a slumbering, mountain dwelling monster: The Mawesome.
It's pretty awesome.

data.name: Into the Mist
entries: Into the Mist is an adventure of mystery and challenging combat for a group of four level 5 adventurers.

entries.name: Premise: Mist-erious Tidings
entries: Tragedy has befallen the village of Pinewood! Crops have withered, livestock have gone missing, and rumours have spread of a creature stalking the woods.
The party arrive in the town ({@adventure Map 1|IntoTheMist|1|Adventure Map 1}) and learn of the recent troubles from the village elder, Evelyn Silverwood.

It all began after two Half-Orc brothers, Migen and Adarn, entered the ancient forest near the village and vanished. Two days later, a dense mist descended upon the forest and village, and Adarn returned alone soon after, staggering out of the forest and collapsing, a large wound along his brow.
Evelyn Silverwood has commissioned notices in nearby settlements calling for adventurers to find the source of the village's woes and put an end to them. She is offering 3,000 gold as a reward.

If the party seek out Adarn in the local tavern, he will tell them more of his tale. He is a green-skinned Half-Orc. His bandaged head has clearly suffered a dreadful wound; the bandages are stained green with his blood, his skull misshapen from the impact of the injury.

As Adarn tells it, he and Migen were foraging when Migen disappeared. He was simply there one moment, gone the next. Adarn then fled the scene upon hearing a terrible howling of some monstrous origin, falling several times while running through the undergrowth and injuring himself.

A successful {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check will reveal Adarn is not being completely truthful. Even if confronted on the matter, Adarn will not reveal any more information, and insist he is telling the truth.

As the party leaves the town, Migen's fiancé Rosalin approaches them with tears in her eyes. She shows them a necklace that bears half of a heart with Migen's name engraved on the back. She tells the party that Migen possesses the other half, bearing her name, and he will be wearing it should they find him.

She begs that the party save Migen from whatever creature is stalking in the fog, suggesting that they seek out the Old Windmill in the forest. She believes Migen would go there for protection; it is an ancient dwelling of magic.

entries.name: Into the Mist
entries: As the party ventures deeper into the forest, they find themselves struggling to move through the dense undergrowth. The trees grow thick and tall, blocking out much of the sunlight and casting deep shadows over the forest floor.

The foliage and fog are so thick that the party can barely see more than 30 feet in front of them, making it easy to get turned around or lost. They must choose one of their number as a guide; that player must make a {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to successfully navigate the dense forest.
If they fail, the party takes 1 level of {@condition exhaustion} as they spend hours walking in circles before stumbling onto the correct path.

entries.name: Rock and Blood
entries: After some time forging their way ahead, the party come across a stream of mist that runs along the forest floor like a path guiding their way. A {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will allow any players to catch a glimpse of shadowy figures, formed from mist, stalking them.
The path opens onto a clearing ({@adventure Map 2|IntoTheMist|1|Adventure Map 2}) containing a large pond and several ruined structures.

5 {@creature Mistling|DMSecretWeapon|mistlings} stand around, silently. They exist only as shades. They are immune to all damage and conditions, and cannot be interacted with. They stand around a small rock. Investigating the rock reveals dried, green blood.
As soon as the party finishes investigating the rock, the mistlings materialise into corporeal forms and attack.
Roll initiative.
Once all the mistlings are defeated, the mist making up the path they had been following dissipates, revealing a trail of dried blood that leads further into the forest. This blood is a deep crimson.

entries.name: The Mistwalker's Lair
entries: The party cautiously follows the trail, the air thick with an eerie silence broken only by the sound of their footsteps. As they navigate the twisted branches, they sense movement in the shadows. They catch glimpses of huge antlers, a humanoid form, too many eyes, and flashes of bright light, ever shrinking back into the mist.
Any investigation into the area reveals nothing; there are no tracks left by the mistwalker.

At the end of the path lies another clearing ({@adventure Map 3|IntoTheMist|1|Adventure Map 3}). Puddles and streams of waist deep water litter the area, making movement difficult. These bog-like pools are {@quickref difficult terrain||3}.
Two 20-foot radius spheres of dense mist are already present in the clearing.

The trail of blood leads to the ruins of an old windmill, within which a pool of dark crimson blood can be found. There is no body. Painted in the blood on the side of the windmill is a single word: "Betrayed". A curious sigil is marked below it, also in blood. A successful {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals this to be some crude attempt at a curse.

The moment the party finishes investigating the writing, a deep, terrible howl sounds within the clearing. {@creature Mistwalker|DMSecretWeapon|The Mistwalker} appears from a dense cloud of mist, thundering towards the party in a terrifying frenzy, determined to kill.
Roll Initiative!

Upon defeat, the mistwalker slowly dissipates, shrinking down until the corpse of a crimson skinned half-orc male lies before the party. A dagger protrudes from his back, and a necklace that bears half a heart with the name Rosalin upon it.
The blood, pooled on the floor of the windmill and on its walls, has also vanished. The mist clears.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The party have defeated the creature that plagued the forest and village, and have recovered Migen's body. However, there is a mystery at play that the party may be able to uncover.
A {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check on Migen's corpse reveals that the dagger was stuck in his back with force and precision, most likely the result of a surprise attack.

Cuts and bruises on Migen's torso and hands seem to imply he dragged himself through the forest on his chest, likely while wounded. There is also a small amount of green blood on the tips of Migen's fingers.
With this information, the party may be able to put together what happened:

items: Adarn stabbed Migen in the back but failed to kill him outright.
Migen then struck him with a rock before crawling away into the forest.

Migen dragged himself to the old windmill where he used his final words to curse his brother. He used his own blood for the spell, unintentionally turning himself into a mistwalker, a savage beast seeking revenge.

entries: If the party confronts Adarn, the dagger pulled from Migen's back is sufficient evidence for Evelyn Silverwood to convict him of murder. The dagger was Adarn's own blade.
As thanks, Evelyn allows them to keep Adarn's weapon (a {@item +1 Dagger||+1 dagger}).

Even if the party fails to solve the mystery, they are thanked by Rosalin and Evelyn (and Adarn, if they did not convict him), and given a reward of 3,000 gold pieces for returning Migen's body for burial and ridding the village of the mist.

data.name: The Canyon of Shadows
entries: The Canyon of Shadows is a Dungeons and Dragons one-shot adventure set in a vast and treacherous desert canyon. This adventure is designed for a group of four level 6 player characters, and it should take approximately three hours to complete.

One ending to this adventure grants each party member access to a single piece of fabulous loot. GMs may wish to construct their own loot tables to suit the power level of their campaign, or they can use the {@adventure table provided|TheCanyonOfShadows|0|Conclusion}.

entries.name: Premise
entries: This adventure begins as the party's travels bring them to the edge of a large canyon. The sun is beating down, the dirt sizzles beneath their feet, and the air is hot and dry.
Suddenly, the ground beneath the party gives way, sending them tumbling into the canyon below.

When the players regain their senses, they find themselves in a dark, shadowy canyon ({@adventure Map 1|TheCanyonOfShadows|1|Adventure Map 1}). The walls are steep and rocky, and a successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will reveal strange markings etched into the stone. Somehow, the magic in these carvings prevents the party from scaling the walls. Even those adept at climbing fail to find purchase on the rock, as if the stone turns to water in their hands. Those who attempt to fly find an invisible barrier blocking their escape about 30 feet in the air.

entries.name: The Shadow Cabal
entries: As the party ventures into the canyon, they come to an area of unnatural darkness. Three pockets of shadow magic cloak the canyon path ahead; they are 15-foot-diameter spheres of magical darkness.

As the party approaches the first pocket of shadow they can make a group {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. On a success, they notice several winged demons clinging to the canyon wall overhead. If they fail, they do not anticipate the ambush the Shadow Cabal has prepared for them and are {@condition surprised} as they are attacked.
The party are assaulted by three {@creature Cabal Beast|DMSecretWeapon|Cabal Beasts} and three {@creature Shadow Cabal Sorcerer|DMSecretWeapon|Shadow Cabal Sorcerers}.
Roll initiative.

Each of the pockets of shadow harbours one Shadow Cabal Sorcerer. On initiative count 20, a cabal beast will be summoned from the centre of each sphere. The spheres of darkness can be destroyed by defeating the Shadow Cabal Sorcerer lurking inside it, or by disrupting the shadow with a source of magical light capable of breaking the {@spell darkness} spell.

entries.name: Beyond the Shadow
entries: After surviving the onslaught, the party stumble upon a hidden cave, its entrance obscured by the final sphere of darkness they vanquish. As the party cautiously enters the cave, they feel a sense of creeping unease snake its way up their spines.

As they proceed deeper into the cave, they begin to see signs of habitation. Rusty weapons and discarded scraps of clothing are scattered on the ground, and the walls are etched with strange symbols and runic carvings.

The markings suggest that deep in the canyon lie ancient ruins, home to vast holds of treasure. A character proficient in {@skill History} can make a {@dc 14} check to recall an additional piece of information. There is said to be a powerful guardian protecting the treasure, one that does not allow anything to be taken lightly.

entries.name: The Djinn's Lair
entries: The cave leads out to the other side of the canyon. As the party make their way onward, they occasionally catch glimpses of cabal beasts flying high overhead, out of reach but always watching.

It isn't long before the party sees the entrance to the ruins hinted at in the carvings on the wall ({@adventure Map 2|TheCanyonOfShadows|1|Adventure Map 2}). As the party enter, they see a colossal statue looming above them, hewn from solid stone. It depicts a blue skinned god with eight arms adorned in golden trinkets.

The entrance is guarded by a {@creature Shadow Cabal Archon|DMSecretWeapon}, a {@creature Shadow Cabal Sorcerer|DMSecretWeapon|Cabal Sorcerer} and 3 {@creature Cabal Beast|DMSecretWeapon|Cabal Beasts}. They will attack on sight, not wanting any other group to access the ruins and claim the treasure within.
Roll initiative.
Upon defeating the Cabal guardians, silence falls once more.

The statue's eyes follow the party as they approach; its expression is one of cold indifference. Scorched earth marks the path leading to the statue, along with the bones of those who have tried to take treasure from the ruins. At the base of the statue is a door, opening into a vast chamber filled with untold riches.

As the party move through the door, before they can take any treasure, they are plunged into darkness. The world fades away to nothing, and out of the void emerges a gargantuan figure. It stands before them, a great {@creature djinn}, as vast as the night sky ({@adventure Map 3|TheCanyonOfShadows|1|Adventure Map 3}).
"Greetings, mortals."
The djinn intones, its voice echoing through the chamber like the rumble of thunder.
"You trespass upon my lair, you must pay the price."

"I am a fair being, and I will offer you a choice. I will break the seal on this canyon, and you shall be allowed to leave. You will be free to continue on with your short, mortal lives, and treasure the memory of my power."

"Alternatively, you may stay and face the challenge of wit that lies ahead. If you make this choice and fail my test, you will be cursed. You will be robbed of all memory of this place, left to wander without knowledge of what deed wrought misery upon you. You will be forever pained, not knowing your crime, but bearing a terrible punishment all the same. Choose!"

items: If the party chooses to leave without disturbing the treasure, the djinn will commend their wisdom. They will each receive 2,000 gold pieces, and a blessing to one weapon or piece of armour they own, granting it a +1 bonus. The darkness fades, and the party find themselves standing on the firm earth beside the canyon, where the adventure began.

If the party try to attack the djinn, it will teleport them all 200 ft. above the entrance to the canyon, where the adventure began. If they survive the fall, they will have no memory of the encounter, be unable to enter the canyon again, and will age at 10 times the normal rate for their species. This curse can only be broken by a {@spell Remove Curse} spell cast at 7th level or above, or by the {@spell Wish} spell.
If the party choose to face the Djinn's challenge, it will ask them three riddles:

entries.name: The Djinn's Riddles
entries: The Djinn will only accept the first answer given to it for each riddle; it doesn't care whether the party agreed upon the answer or not.

If a player guesses incorrectly, the character who voiced the answer is instantly transformed into a golden statue with gemstone eyes. They cannot be moved by force or magic and can no longer participate in the trial.

If all the party members are turned to statues, they awake by the side of the canyon with five levels of {@condition exhaustion}, no possessions, and no memory of any events after the moment they fell. Henceforth, they are cursed to age at 10 times the normal rate for their species, and are physically unable to enter the canyon again. This curse can only be broken by a {@spell Remove Curse} spell cast at 7th level or above, or by the {@spell Wish} spell.

entries.name: Riddle 1

entries: I am not alive, yet I grow;
I don't have lungs, yet I need air;
I do not breathe, yet I can drown.
What am I?
{@b Answer:} Fire

entries.name: Riddle 2

entries: I am a weapon of ancient times, crafted from the body of giants.
I fly faster than a hawk and as quietly as an owl. What am I?
{@b Answer:} An Arrow

entries.name: Riddle 3

entries: I will always speak back in the language you spoke.
The louder you cry, the louder am I.
What am I?
{@b Answer:} An Echo

If the party answer all the riddles correctly the djinn restores any party member that gave an incorrect answer to their true form. It gives the party a final warning before allowing them to claim the treasure:

"Be warned, mortals. The treasure that I offer is not without a cost. You may take one item. Every coin has its price, and every boon is a curse. Think carefully before you make your choice, for once you have claimed your prize, there is no going back.
Do not fall to greed. Take one item."

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The adventurers have passed all trials and are free to pick anything they want from the Djinn's treasure horde. The moment they are done collecting treasures, they rematerialise by the side of the canyon, where the adventure began.
The items in the horde are all powerful magic items. At the GM's discretion, there may be different objects here, or others beyond those listed in the Djinn's Horde Loot Table.
{@b Curses.} If any individual takes more than one piece of treasure, all treasure that they possess becomes cursed.
Those objects lose all their magical properties, and gain the following magical effects:

items: Any creature possessing cursed treasure will suffer {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage at the start of each turn if the item is more than 10 feet away from them.
In addition, while within 10 feet of the cursed item, they age at 10 times the rate they normally would.

entries: These curses can be ended by a {@spell Wish} spell, or by a {@spell Remove Curse} spell cast at 7th level or above.

entries.caption: Djinn's Horde Loot Table
rows: {@item Figurine of Wondrous Power, Obsidian Steed||Obsidian Steed Figurine of Wondrous Power}
{@item +2 Wand of the War Mage||Wand of the War Mage (Rare)}
{@item Horn of Valhalla, Bronze||Bronze Horn of Valhalla}
5 × {@item Potion of Giant Strength, Stone||Potion of Stone Giant Strength}

data.name: Temple of the Moon
entries: Temple of the Moon is an adventure for four level 8 adventurers, featuring branching paths players can choose that impact the final encounter!

The party arrive in the market town of Oakwood, a bustling tourist trap on the shoreline of Avestros ({@adventure Map 1|TempleOfTheMoon|1|Adventure Map 1}). As they walk down the cobbled streets, surrounded by the sounds of merchants pandering goods and artisans practising their craft, they come to a local chapel.

It is a small, rustic building, dedicated to the Moon Goddess, with stained glass windows depicting verdant forests and star strewn skies. Here, they are hailed by a young halfling in priest's clothes who introduces himself as Brother Matthew. He is short, even by halfling standards, with unkempt brown hair and blue eyes that sparkle with warmth.

Matthew tells the party about his chapel's sister temple, a much larger building that sits in a glade at the centre of the nearby Silvershade forest. His temple has not received the regular dispatches from Chandrila, the high priestess of the Moon goddess who dwells there, for several weeks. The last communication he received from the temple was for a delivery of silver, including a rare silver blade.
Matthew asks the party to journey to the temple and find out the cause of the silence.

He also explains that local trappers and hunters have refused to take his quest, fearing rumours of dangerous beasts moving in the forest. Matthew promises the church will reward the party handsomely upon completion of the quest.
The journey to the Temple of the Moon takes the best part of the day; the path to the temple is narrow and uneven. The stream babbles and gurgles beside the party as they hike.

A short while down the path they find the first signs of the supplies intended for Oakwood. Overturned carts and broken crates lie scattered at the side of the river, their contents nowhere to be found. Peculiarly, there is no sign of struggle.

A successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check will reveal footprints that head down the path toward the Temple, as well as large paw prints that zig-zag across the area before leading deeper into the woods.

At that moment, a loud howl sounds from deeper within the forest, soon joined by several others in discordant unison. Suddenly, they are silenced by a colossal, snarling roar, loud enough to shake the trees. No creature in the forest makes a sound for several minutes after the roar.

items: Should the party follow the pawprints that lead into the forest, proceed to {@adventure 1.3|TempleOfTheMoon|0|1.3}.
Should the party follow the footprints that lead to the temple, proceed to {@adventure 2.1|TempleOfTheMoon|0|2.1}.

entries: Following the pawprints leads the party off the beaten path. They come to a cunningly disguised trap: two logs suspended among the leaves overhead. There is a trip wire that activates the trap requiring a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 17 to detect.

If the character first in marching order does not detect the trip wire, they set off the trap, causing the logs to slam into the character second in the marching order. The trap deals {@damage 4d10} Bludgeoning damage.

Whether the trap goes off or not, the party will immediately be assaulted by a gang of four {@creature Cursed Werewolf|DMSecretWeapon|cursed werewolves}, in bestial form ({@adventure Map 2|TempleOfTheMoon|1|Adventure Map 2}).
After defeating the werewolves, the party can search their bodies to find a pure, silver {@item dagger|PHB}.
After coming to the end of the paw tracks, the party can pick up the trail that leads to the temple.

The party finally arrives at the Temple of the Moon. It stands in the centre of a serene glade bathed in moonlight and populated with lush, green grass and glowing wildflowers. A crystal-clear pool reflects the moon's light, and the cool air carries the scent of pine and earth. The only sounds are the rustling of leaves and the trickle of water.

A woman approaches the party cautiously from the entrance to the Temple, emanating an aura of otherworldly grace and serenity. She meets the party in the temple courtyard ({@adventure Map 3|TempleOfTheMoon|1|Adventure Map 3}).
She introduces herself as Chandrila and beckons the party inside, quickly sharing the tale of recent events at the Temple.

A man arrived in need of help, calling himself Xanthir, claiming to be cursed. Despite their best efforts, no treatment or spell the temple clerics could muster was able to ease his suffering. Then, at the height of the last full moon, Xanthir transformed into a great {@creature Werewolf} and fled in a bestial rampage. At least a dozen of the temple staff were bitten while attempting to restrain him before he escaped. Lycanthropy swiftly claimed their minds and flesh, sending them howling into the forest.
After days of praying to the goddess, Chandrila received a vision of a ritual which she believes can break the curse.
It requires the following steps to be performed:

items: One character of any good alignment must lead the ritual, reciting a prayer to the moon deity. They must use a bonus action each turn to hold concentration on the ritual for three full rounds.
The one afflicted with lycanthropy must inhale smoke of the wolfsbane plant and be weakened by a blow from a pure, silver blade.
Finally, the cursed one must stand within a sacred circle of holy water as they are reduced to 0 hit points.

entries: Performing the ritual will break the lycanthropy on Xanthir and any other werewolves he has infected. Alternatively, killing Xanthir will end his suffering, but not save the other werewolves. They will need to be hunted down and slaughtered at a later time.

Chandrila informs the party that the wolfsbane plant can be harvested from the very courtyard in which they stand; it grows freely under the blessings of the Moon. However, plucking the weed from this sacred earth comes with a price of its own.
She does not possess a pure, silver blade, but she did call for one to be sent. Alas, the merchants who were delivering that cargo never arrived.

Finally, she will give the party 5 vials of {@item Holy Water (flask)||holy water}. A player can use an action to spread the water on the ground. All 5 vials must be poured out to create a circle with a 15-foot radius.

items: If the party goes to seek the wolfsbane, proceed to {@adventure 2.3|TempleOfTheMoon|0|2.3}.
If the party goes to hunt for the silver blade, return to {@adventure 1.3|TempleOfTheMoon|0|1.3}.
When the party are ready to confront Xanthir, proceed to {@adventure 3.1|TempleOfTheMoon|0|3.1}.

entries: Wolfsbane is a sacred, magical plant, and plucking it from holy earth is not without consequence.

Each player within 60 feet of the plant as it is gathered must succeed on a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw as fungal spores are released. Any character that fails the save takes {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage and is unable to regain hit points for the next 24 hours.

The wolfsbane can be burned by any character that uses an action to do so. When burned, any lycanthropes within 120 feet of the plant take {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage and lose any legendary resistances.

Xanthir's den lies in the graveyard less than 500 feet from the temple ({@adventure Map 4|TempleOfTheMoon|1|Adventure Map 4}). As soon as the party gets within 60 feet of him, {@creature Xanthir|DMSecretWeapon|he} will strike. He is accompanied by three {@creature werewolf||werewolves}.
If the conditions of the ritual are met, Xanthir and the other lycanthropes will transform back into humanoids, {@condition unconscious} but alive.
If Xanthir is killed, the other werewolves will flee, scattering deep into the woods.

No matter the outcome, Chandrila thanks the party for ending the werewolf scourge and gives them 500 gp worth of diamond dust, a 300 gp diamond, 5 {@item Potion of Greater Healing||potions of greater healing} and 1,000 gp worth of incense.
If Xanthir survived, he will awaken at the temple and give the party a {@item +1 Heavy Crossbow||+1 heavy crossbow} which bears a Rune of the Mighty and Rune of the Swift.

data.name: The Court of the Rat Emperor
entries: The Court of the Rat Emperor is a whimsical adventure for four level 4 characters, where player choices, roleplay, and behavior impact the encounters along the way!

entries.name: The Offer
entries: The adventurers find a crudely hewn noticeboard erected in the centre of town. It stands a few feet from an open sewer grate, and reads thus:

The sewer grate nearby is just large enough for one person to enter at a time. Descending the rickety ladder steadily plunges the party into darkness. Those with {@sense darkvision} can see a very tight passage, blocked off to the right, with a stone wall to the left.

As soon as all members of the party are in the sewer, and have removed their helmets, the sewer grate above is dragged shut, and with a loud "bonk" each character is simultaneously knocked {@condition unconscious} by a blow to the head from an unseen creature. The adventure has begun!

entries.name: Rat Jail
entries: The party wake shortly afterwards in a dark, damp cell ({@adventure Map 1|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|1|Adventure Map 1}). The room is dimly lit and empty, save for the chains that shackle the party to the walls by their wrists and ankles. There is blood and bones on the ground, though a successful {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check reveals them to be the remains of beasts, not humanoids.
The party are missing all of their equipment save for their armour and clothing.
There is a door at the end of the room, barred shut. The party must work together to escape the prison and work out what has happened.

entries.name: Escape!
entries: A {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation} or {@skill Arcana}) check will reveal that the chains that bind the party have been enchanted to counter attempts to teleport away. Any character that attempts to teleport while bound must succeed on a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw or fail to escape. If they attempt to use a spell to teleport, the spell slot is consumed whether they succeed or fail. The chains can be broken with a {@dc 16} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or picked with the jagged edge of one of the bones on the floor using a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check.

At the exact moment the last character is freed, two {@creature Ratsecutioner|DMSecretWeapon|ratsecutioners} enter the room, opening the barred door. They are clearly rats, but humanoid in size and clad in simple armour and weaponry. Startled to find the party free, the rats raise their weapons and demand the players reimprison themselves.

entries.name: Negotiations
entries: The ratsecutioners are stupid, distrustful, and nervous. They are swift to suspect betrayal, and ready to attack. The party may attempt to argue for their freedom, avoiding bloodshed. At the GM's discretion, if the party can offer a convincing argument backed up with a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check, the ratsecutioners will allow them to pass.

entries.name: Aggressive Negotiations
entries: If the party fails to convince the jail wardens to let them pass, or choose to attack, the {@creature Ratsecutioner|DMSecretWeapon|ratsecutioners} will meet them with combat.

Each ratsecutioner has a bardiche and a {@item light crossbow}. Players can attempt to disarm a ratsecutioner by using an action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check contested against the ratsecutioner's {@skill Athletics}. On a success, the player wrestles one of the ratsecutioner's weapons free, and can wield it themselves.

entries.name: The Four Chests
entries: After defeating or placating the rats, the party can progress through the door the guards opened, coming to a large chamber with four doors and four chests.

items: Chest 1 is filled with noxious gas that, when opened, fills the room, dealing {@damage 2d10} Poison damage to all creatures.

Chest 2 is filled with a curious map that appears to mark a path to a great treasure hoard through Door 2. Players who make a successful {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check on the map detect a secret code in the etchings, indicating a hidden trapdoor in the room it charts.
Chest 3 contains the party's equipment.

Chest 4 is filled with a simple, sentimental etching of a family of humanoid rats, a proud father and three children. It appears to have no monetary value, and has clearly been placed here for safekeeping.

entries.name: The Four Doors
entries: Each of the doorways in the room leads to a different location within the warren.

items: Door 1 leads back to the jail cell, where the party came from.
Door 2 leads to the treasure room, as marked by the treasure map from Chest 2. If the party takes this doorway, proceed to {@adventure 3.1|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|0|Door 2: The "Treasure" Room}.
Door 3 leads to a pathway littered with traps and humming with magic. If the party takes this doorway, proceed to {@adventure 3.2|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|0|Door 3: Rat Traps}.

Door 4 is initially barred. A successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check made at the door will reveal a gentle breeze of fresh air passing through the cracks in the frame. This doorway leads to the Rat Emperor's Court, and the exit. It will open after the party has explored at least one other door. If the party takes this doorway, proceed to {@adventure 4.1|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|0|Door 4: Court of the Rat Emperor}.

entries.name: Door 2: The "Treasure" Room
entries: Doorway two opens into a twisting maze of passages and shifting doors. Players with the treasure map can make their way through without issue. Otherwise, the party must make a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check or lose their way in the maze, returning to the central chamber after 30 minutes of wandering.

If the players pass through the maze, they reach the "treasure" room ({@adventure Map 2|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|1|Adventure Map 2}). It is in a sorry state. What once must have been a fabulously stacked larder is barren; a few crumbs of cheese and mouldy bread are all that remains of the stock. Curiously, despite the emptiness of the room, the scent of cheese is thick in the air. The party also finds 500 gp worth of herbs and spices scattered around, but little else of interest.
Players who identified the secret message on the treasure map, or who succeed on a {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, find a trapdoor cunningly hidden in the centre of the room.

Lifting the trapdoor reveals a chamber below, almost as large as the room above, stuffed with fabulous cheeses of all types. The room glows gold with light bouncing from wheel to slice to crumb. A startled, large squirrel with a protruding belly lets out a shriek as the party opens the trapdoor and pounces towards them.
Roll initiative! ({@creature Pot-Bellied Thief|DMSecretWeapon})

The pot-bellied squirrel will attempt to surrender upon reaching less than 20 hit points (no action required). If the party accepts his surrender, he will confess to finding the trapdoor in the cheese room of the warren, and steadily stealing all the cheese for himself, living in a paradise of hibernation and dairy below the warren.
He will request the party let him go. Alternatively, there are ropes nearby the party could use to restrain him to await justice from the rest of the warren.
After dealing with the thief, the party can return through the doorway to enter the central chamber once again.

entries.name: Door 3: Rat Traps
entries: Beyond Door 3 lies a curious, tiled pathway and a heavy set trap. There is an iron scent of blood in the air; those who have attempted to pass this room before have been rebuffed painfully.

Each tile of the floor acts as a pressure switch, and the trapdoor to the next chamber lies at the far end of the room, in the centre of a giant rat trap. The rules for passing this trap are as follows:

items: Players can deactivate the rat trap by stepping on each tile only once, ending their pathway at the trapdoor.

If they fail to step on every tile before reaching the exit, or step on the same tile more than once, the spring will activate when they reach the trapdoor, closing on the party, dealing {@damage 5d4} Slashing damage and locking the door below.
Tiles marked with a rock do not need to be stepped on.
Due to a potent graviturgy magic in the room, players cannot fly or leap over tiles.

The party must progress one tile at a time moving either up, down, left, or right, and must all take the same route. Due to the instability of the trap, it will activate if they split up to cover multiple tiles at once.

entries: The first trapdoor leads to another chamber, more complex than the last:
Through the final trapdoor, the party finds a small, dusty chest. It has clearly gone unopened for years. Inside, they find an ornate, ceremonial crown.
Upon retrieving the crown, the party can return safely past the deactivated traps to the central chamber once more.

entries.name: Door 4: Court of the Rat Emperor
entries: Stepping through the final door, the party find themselves in a large courtroom, populated with dozens of rats similar to the ones that were guarding them in the jail cell ({@adventure Map 3|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|1|Adventure Map 3}). As they enter, every eye turns to them, and a nasal, imperious tone cries out:
"Finally, the accused have arrived!"
The {@creature Rat Emperor|DMSecretWeapon} stands high on a raised platform at the back of the room. He continues to speak:

"Before us stands the source of all our woe! Outsiders! Those who have laid unpassable traps and stolen our precious food reserves! With their execution, we officially declare war on the surface dwellers! We will show that none may harm us. Our hand has been forced. We will defend ourselves to the last!"
The rat emperor decrees that:

items: All the cheese from the treasure room has been stolen.
The pathway to the royal crown has been forever sealed by the placement of vicious traps.
Outsiders must be to blame, and the party is to be killed in retribution.

entries: The party will be given an opportunity to plead their case. If they are to be spared, they must pass a {@dc 35} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. Lower the DC of this check by 5 for each of the following actions the party took while moving through the warren:

items: The party found the cheese hidden in the basement of the "treasure" room.
The party restrained or killed the Pot-Bellied Thief rather than letting him go.
The party did not kill the ratsecutioner guards.
The party persuaded the ratsecutioner guards to let them go, rather than fighting them at all.
The party deactivated the traps that barred the way to the crown.
The party did not steal the sentimental picture from Chest 4.

entries: If the party succeed on their Persuasion check, proceed to {@adventure 4.3|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|0|Paragons of Ratkind}.
If the party does not attempt to plead their innocence, fails the Persuasion check, or decide to attack, proceed to {@adventure 4.2|TheCourtOfTheRatEmperor|0|Battle!}.

entries.name: Battle!
entries: {@creature The Rat Emperor|DMSecretWeapon} insists the party are executed immediately. He draws a sceptre, and the party are surrounded by four {@creature Ratsecutioner|DMSecretWeapon|ratsecutioners}. Roll initiative!
Upon defeating the Rat Emperor, the other rats in the room scatter, terrified. The party can take his sceptre, a heavy and cumbersome object worth 2,000 gold pieces.
There is daylight visible from the door at the back of the courtroom, and by following it, the party emerges in the sewers once again. From here it is a simple matter to make their way above ground.
With the Rat Emperor defeated, there is no chance of the surface world being troubled by the warrens again!

entries.name: Paragons of Ratkind
entries: On a successful Persuasion check, the Rat Emperor will declare the party free to leave. If the party passed the check by 10 or more, the Emperor will declare them heroes, and offer them 4,000 gold pieces to take on their way. The party are guided to the surface by an entourage of rats, emerging from the very sewer gate they clambered down earlier that day.

With the rats befriended, they will not trouble the surface world again. Perhaps the actions of the party that day mark the first step in a friendship between the surface races and rats who dwell below.

data.name: The Edge of Eternity
entries: The Edge of Eternity is a fun, one-shot adventure of mini-games, gambling, and combat for four level 7 player characters, featuring two endings and boss fights, depending on player choices.

entries.name: Journey to Eternity
entries: As the party gathers for the night in a cosy tavern, a sudden gust of wind sweeps through the room, extinguishing all candles and sources of natural light, plunging the players into darkness.
After the darkness is lifted, each player finds an elegantly crafted envelope sitting before them, each bearing that character's name in twirling script.
A {@spell Detect Magic} spell will reveal transmutation magic has been cast on the parchment.
Each letter addresses the character by name and says:
"Seekers of fortune and of the unknown, The Eternity's Edge Casino awaits you. A night of gambling, riches, and love are just a nod of the head away!
Fulfil your curiosity, seekers of fate. Embrace the unknown, and be lucky!"
Players who nod their head while holding the invitation vanish instantly in a plume of scarlet smoke, transported directly to The Eternity's Edge Casino.

entries.name: Welcome to Eternity
entries: The adventurers who consented to attend Eternity appear through a pair of double doors at the top of a dimly-lit casino ({@adventure Map 1|TheEdgeOfEternity|1|Adventure Map 1}). From this vantage point they can see other adventuring types crowded around tables, laughing, drinking, and gambling. Players with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 19 or above notice that the croupiers managing each table have eyes that gleam crimson.

The players are immediately greeted by an elegant, armour clad figure enveloped in shifting shadow. Their eyes sparkle with a whimsical, otherworldly glow, and shimmering silver motes of light cascade from their hair, evoking the image of starlight in motion. They introduce themself as Vesper, "house security", and guide the adventurers into the casino. If the party inquire as to why they are here, Vesper will respond that nobody enters or leaves the casino without a direct invitation from The Boss, but is unable to elaborate further.

Vesper explains several of the games, which the party can play to their heart's content. They are kind, genuine, and polite to the party, and give each player 20 gold pieces to gamble with, if they so choose. The full rules to three of the games available are described in the RPG {@variantrule Gambling Mini-Games|DMSecretWeapon} section. Traditional gambling games such as poker and blackjack are played on the smaller tables at the back of the room.

entries.name: The Activities!
entries: There are many games available at the casino, including Fireball, Golden Rollies, and Stacked Dice.

You may also wish to offer games to your players here too. Classic card games like Blackjack or Crazy Eights would be appropriate, as would other games, from Tic-Tac-Toe to Hangman. Feel free to explore and incorporate different types of mini-games to the casino, letting your players play (or attempt to cheat) in character! Players may gamble with any gold they have.

Players can interact with other patrons of the casino, and will also be approached by a random patron of the casino at the end of each game. When the party interacts with a patron, roll {@dice 1d4} on the following table to determine the behaviour of the person they interact with.

rows: The patron is actively hostile. They will attack the player with very little provocation, or accuse them of thievery and cheating in the games. If the players end up fighting a patron, use the {@creature Hostile Adventurer|DMSecretWeapon} stat block.

The patron is slippery and duplicitous. They will attempt to steal from the players while they talk. Request a {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check from the player over the course of the conversation. On a success, the players catch the patron attempting to steal from them. If the players end up fighting the patron, use the {@creature Hostile Adventurer|DMSecretWeapon} stat block.
The patron is warm and friendly. They will tip the player 1 gold piece, and tell them a rumour that the casino is operated by a shadowy figure known only as The Boss.

The patron is fearful. They will confess that something is not right in the casino, but before they can say anymore, two croupiers will appear at their side and kindly lead them away, consoling the distressed patron and offering a free drink. The patron acquiesces to being led from the party's view, and is not seen again.

entries: Players may also buy alcohol from roaming waiters at the casino. Each drink costs 3 gold pieces.

A player who buys a drink for another patron or croupier gains a +4 bonus to all Charisma checks they make to interact with that character. If a croupier running a game becomes inebriated as a result of consuming the drinks offered to them by the party, they make any checks to detect cheating, should the players try it, at Disadvantage.

entries.name: Moving On
entries: Once the party have met all four NPCs, or if they make a scene by fighting another patron or by getting caught cheating, stealing, or otherwise making a disturbance, three croupiers will appear and tell them they have been requested to attend a private party by The Boss. If the party goes with them, they are led to a door which teleports them into The Boss's lair.

If they attack the croupiers, or perform any hostile action in their presence, each one sheds their humanoid appearance and transforms into a {@creature Gambling Voidling|DMSecretWeapon}. They attack the party at once.
Roll Initiative.
After the Gambling Voidlings are defeated, the players feel a powerful pull at their feet, and vanish in a puff of scarlet smoke, reappearing in The Boss's lair.

entries.name: Meet The Boss
entries: The party find themselves in a fiery room, with a high backed chair at the far end, in which sits The Boss ({@adventure Map 2|TheEdgeOfEternity|1|Adventure Map 2}).
She appears humanoid in stature, with six, bat-like wings protruding from her back, addressing the party with exaggerated friendliness and a grin glowing with vicious, sharp teeth.

Impressed with the adventurers' obvious strength, The Boss offers them a deal. She wishes for them to assassinate Vesper, her lieutenant in the casino who has grown popular and powerful enough to threaten her. In exchange, she offers the party 8,000 gold pieces.
If they refuse, she assures them they will die on the spot.

items: If the party accepts The Boss's offer, proceed to {@adventure 3.1|TheEdgeOfEternity|0|Deal with The Devil}.
If the party refuses The Boss's offer, proceed to {@adventure 3.2|TheEdgeOfEternity|0|No Deal}.

entries.name: Deal with The Devil
entries: The Boss teleports the party back into the casino, which is now totally empty save for {@creature Vesper|DMSecretWeapon}. Clearly anticipating an attack by The Boss, Vesper launches themself at the party immediately, aiming to kill them and escape.
Roll initiative.
If the party does not kill Vesper after defeating them, The Boss appears and envelops Vesper in flames. They die instantly in a swirling vortex of heat.

Without a word, The Boss then claps her hands, and the players vanish in scarlet smoke, reappearing in their cosy tavern rooms where the invitations first arrived, with 8,000 gold in a briefcase and a thank you note that reads:
"You make for good murderers!
With love,
The Boss xx"

entries.name: No Deal
entries: If the party refuses The Boss's offer, she lets out an audible sigh of irritation before extending her wings, spiralling into the air, and diving towards the party.
Roll initiative ({@creature The Boss|DMSecretWeapon}).
If the party does not kill The Boss after defeating her, Vesper appears in a flash of white light and decapitates her.

The moment the Boss dies, the world around the party begins to shake and crumble. Vesper claps their hands together, and the players vanish in a flash of white light, reappearing in their cosy tavern rooms where the invitations first arrived, with 10,000 gold in a silver chalice and a thank you note that reads:
"Thanks for saving me a hard job! Let's grab a drink sometime! Here's a little reward, on the house.
Vesper"

data.name: The Hart of the Forest
entries: The Hart of the Forest is a challenging adventure for a party of four level 6–7 player characters. It features moral choices and multiple endings depending on the path the players choose.

entries.name: Welcome to Eisenholz
entries: The party arrive in Eisenholz, an industrious town bordering a vast and verdant forest. Eisenholz is well known in the region, the forest famous for its endless supply of timber and large deposits of adamantine. The forges of Eisenholz ever crackle and burn, plumes of smoke belch thick and pungent over the cobbled streets, and the workers of the town have long since grown wealthy and famous for their craft.

The townspeople of Eisenholz are proud of their work in their ability to produce enormous quantities of high-quality weapons and armour. The party will likely be able to find shopkeepers here selling many powerful and wondrous armaments. If they find themselves in the mood to shop, they will not be alone; the town is a hub of activity, with merchants and traders coming from far and wide to barter for the famous Eisenholz goods.
However, all is not well.
Immediately upon entering the town, the party find a large sign nailed to the village notice board. It reads:

Attention adventurers! Eisenholz needs your aid! Malevolent forces have chased our workers from the forests and attacked our guards. Our stockpile of resources is shrinking by the day, and each expedition into the forest costs more lives.
