We need you to clear this evil from the forest so that our work can resume. It is imperative we continue to supply the region with the goods it needs to thrive! There will be a handsome compensation.
Enquire with The Mayor for details.

entries.name: Meeting The Mayor
entries: The Mayor, Thomas Smile, is a young, handsome man with a sharp face and arrogant air. He walks with the obnoxious swagger of one born into immense wealth, and speaks in a lazy, confident tone. His eyes are sharp and observant, and his demeanour is fiercely pragmatic. Smile is not easily swayed by sentimentality or emotional appeals. However, should the party ask around the town, or make a successful {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check upon meeting Smile, they will find that he is not evil or cruel, and is widely regarded as a good mayor, despite being both entitled and arrogant. He greets the party dispassionately.

Smile gives the same information as the sign, but adds that the malevolent forces seem to be centred around a Great Tree deep in the forest. His soldiers believe this tree is key to their power, and he demands the party destroy it.

He goes on to explain that while his soldiers could simply burn the forest to the ground, the bountiful timber and other raw materials that would be destroyed could be better put to use, providing jobs and economic opportunity for the hard working citizens of Eisenholz.
It would be far more efficient to cut the source of this dark magic off at its roots.
The offered reward for destroying the tree is 10,000 gp.

If questioned further about the nature of the "malevolent forces" that are troubling those who enter the forest, Smile's answers are vague. If pushed, he will reveal he has not seen the creatures himself, only the shredded corpses of those who have had the misfortune of running into them. He gives the party a map that leads to the Great Tree, but warns them to be on guard.

entries.name: The Forest
entries: The forest is a wonderland of life and beauty, every turn revealing a spectacular new image of verdant tranquillity. The air is cool and fresh, scented with the fragrance of wildflowers and pine needles. The canopy of trees overhead forms a dappled shade, casting patterns of light and shadow on the forest floor. Rays of sunlight filter through the leaves, creating a natural kaleidoscope of colours. It is hard to believe any evil could dwell here.

After about an hour of the party moving through the forest, they come upon a clearing. The trees have been felled, leaving only stumps and barren ground behind and the air is thick with the smell of smoke. The peace of the forest has been slain, the timber harvested, and the earth ripped open by Eisenholz's resource extraction efforts.

At the far side of the clearing, the party see a logging camp ({@adventure Map 1|TheHartOfTheForest|1|Adventure Map 1}) and a successful {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal a subtle sound of movement from within. It does not appear to be the sound of humanoids moving around.

Entering the camp, the party find a group of wild cats. They are bloodstained but unharmed, and appear tranquil. There is blood smeared across the earthen floor, as if corpses have been dragged through the undergrowth.

The cats appear serene as the party first enter the camp, but become aggravated and pace up and down as soon as they notice them. Their eyes glow with an intense, otherworldly radiance, and their fur seems to shimmer and shift in the dappled sunlight. As the party watch on, the cats grow in size, their features becoming more angular, transforming into vicious monstrosities: {@creature Nightclaw|DMSecretWeapon|Nightclaws}.
Once transformed, they leap towards the party, howling with fury and bestial malice.
Roll initiative!
Once defeated, each Nightclaw shrinks back to its normal size as whatever power that had enhanced them retreats back into the forest.

entries.name: The Tree
entries: Beyond the camp is a path that leads to the centre of the forest. As the party follow it, a grand and enchanting presence emerges—the Great Tree. It looms tall, its ancient trunk bathed in an ethereal glow, as if infused with the very essence of magic. Delicate, luminescent leaves adorn its branches, shimmering with otherworldly hues that dance in mesmerising patterns. Wisps of mist and gentle whispers in ancient tongues emanate from its boughs; a beautiful, radiant magic that has persisted across millennia dwells here.

A character that succeeds on a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will find a gap in the trunk of the tree large enough to enter. Within, they find a concealed passage leading to a chamber. Moss-covered walls guide the way as soft light illuminates the path down into the fertile earth and on into calm waters. The chamber opens upon a shimmering fountain, its crystal-clear waters singing with vitality, bursting with an aura of magic and life that rejuvenates the spirit ({@adventure Map 2|TheHartOfTheForest|1|Adventure Map 2}).

The moment the party enter the chamber a radiant transformation begins. From the depths of the fountain's waters, a magnificent deer of pure light emerges, its form ethereal and majestic. The radiant glow envelops the chamber, casting cascades of shimmering luminescence over the walls.

entries.name: The Hart of the Forest
entries: As the stag emerges, two {@creature Nightclaw|DMSecretWeapon|Nightclaws} descend from the chamber's walls. Their eyes gleam and fur glows in the light as they join the scene. Standing beside the stag, the Nightclaws seem less vicious and feral, instead radiating an aura of untamed elegance and stark beauty.

The stag will attempt to communicate with the party in {@language Sylvan}, its piercing gaze filled with ancient wisdom and sorrow. As it speaks, its voice resonates with a melodic timbre, carrying the weight of centuries.
If the party can understand it, it poses them a question: Why they have chosen to aid in the destruction of the forest?

Despite the sorrow in its eyes, there is a glimmer of hope, a desire for understanding as to why the people of Eisenholz have plundered and destroyed so much of its ancient home. The Hart of the Forest's demeanour remains composed, yet there is an undeniable air of authority and patience as it awaits the party's response, hopeful for an explanation that it might understand.
If the party does not understand {@language Sylvan}, they can make no sense of the creature's words. However, they still must make a decision.

Either they must finish the task they were hired to do and destroy the tree, or turn back, and betray the interests of their employer and the town of Eisenholz. No matter what explanation the party give, the stag will not allow the pillage of its forest to continue.

items: If the party chooses to attack and destroy the Great Tree, proceed to {@adventure 3.1|TheHartOfTheForest|0|The End of Magic}.
If the party chooses to protect the Great Tree and the forest, proceed to {@adventure 3.2|TheHartOfTheForest|0|One with the Forest}.

entries.name: The End of Magic
entries: If the party decide to attack the Great Tree, {@creature The Hart of the Forest|DMSecretWeapon} and the two {@creature Nightclaw|DMSecretWeapon|Nightclaws} will attack at once.
Roll Initiative.

Upon defeating the Hart, the Great Tree rots in a matter of minutes, its dancing, playful magic silenced forever. The forest becomes mundane, and the people of Eisenholz are free to plunder it without reproach. The Mayor and the town celebrate the party, their intervention having saved countless lives and jobs. The party receives 10,000 gold pieces.
However, the forest's resources are finite, and without magic to rejuvenate itself, everything of value and beauty is depleted by the people of Eisenholz within a decade.

entries.name: One with the Forest
entries: If the party choose not to attack the Great Tree and leave, they must face the mayor and a full squadron of soldiers who are waiting for their report in the abandoned logging camp. Thomas Smile has ten soldiers with him, many of whom are helplessly embittered with grief at the loss of loved ones in the forest.

An attempt to peacefully convince the mayor to stop destroying the forest will require a successful {@dc 21} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check, made at Disadvantage. If the check fails, the mayor will brand the party as traitors, and will order his soldiers to attack. If the mayor detects any spell being cast on him or his soldiers, the squadron will attack.

If the party defeat the mayor's soldiers and leave him alive, he will return with them to Eisenholz a broken and bitter man. Should the party kill him, the end result is much the same. The forest's defences grow even more vicious, and the town of Eisenholz crumbles, unable to sustain its great forges and industry without access to the natural resources it requires. The life within the forest blooms however. Magic sings, the verdant pastures spread, and long after Eisenholz has fallen, life and joy continues to spring from the Great Tree.

If the party convince the mayor to stand down and leave the forest alone, he will return with them to Eisenholz furious but compliant. At the party's recommendation, he allows small teams to enter the forest to harvest resources in a non-destructive way. The town of Eisenholz struggles desperately to sustain itself on a lower supply of materials, but survives.

However, the forest swiftly begins to grow and replenish at a far faster rate than before, allowing increasingly more to be taken in a way that does no harm to those that dwell there. The party's reputation quickly spreads, and they are soon lauded as heroes by the people of Eisenholz. All the while, life springs anew in the forest.

Although initially not compensated, after {@dice 1d6} weeks the party receive 13,000 gold pieces from the mayor. At the DM's discretion, they may also receive a blessing from the Hart of the Forest in the form of a permanent +1 to their base Wisdom, Charisma, or Intelligence scores (their choice).

data.name: The Job at Peckle's Port
entries: The Job at Peckle's Port is an adventure for four level 5 player characters, with four different possible outcomes. A night of betrayal, mystery, and danger awaits!

entries.name: Welcome to Town
entries: The party have arrived in Peckle's Port ({@adventure Map 1|TheJobAtPecklesPort|1|Adventure Map 1}), a bustling coastal town built around its thriving harbour. It is a hub of commerce and trade, both above and below the eyes of the law, with merchants, sailors, pirates, and smugglers constantly passing through its waters.
Immediately, the party's attention is drawn by a large sign calling to adventurers:
"Help needed! Strong, burly, ideally handsome adventurers!
Significant gold reward.
Get in touch!
Meet here at 8pm tonight.
Arrrgh!"
Should the party answer the call, they are met under the gathering twilight by Plumbus Gumpy, a gruff-voiced seadog, who explains the mission.

Gumpy explains how his captain, Horatio, recently acquired a valuable and rare artefact, a Kraken Egg, but rumours have spread that a group of seafaring thieves, led by the Pirate Bandit Maukle, are planning to steal it. The heist is rumoured to be taking place this very night.

He requests the help of adventurers to protect the artefact and prevent it from falling into the wrong hands, explaining how his own crew cannot handle it themselves, for fear of drawing attention to the Egg's secret location. Gumpy also explains that upon retrieving the Egg, Horatio intends to sell it to the Royal Navy, who will likely harness its power and strengthen the defences of the nation, alongside the iron fist of the crown.

At present, the Egg has been hidden in the clocktower on the outskirts of Peckle's Port. The party must go there and ensure the Egg's protection through the night. Gumpy offers the party 4,000 gold pieces, to be delivered the following morning if the Egg is kept safe and sound.

entries.name: Ambush!
entries: On the way to the clocktower, the party is ambushed in the streets by the band of brigands and poultry thieves known as the Pigeon Boys, led by the swashbuckling simian pirate {@creature Hank Flag|DMSecretWeapon}.
The Pigeon Boys consist of three {@creature Pigeon Boy Bandit|DMSecretWeapon|Pigeon Boy Bandits} and {@creature Hank Flag|DMSecretWeapon}.
Roll initiative!

Upon defeating Hank and his bandits, Hank informs the party of his troop's aim to reach the Kraken Egg and destroy it before Maukle can steal it, or the Navy can use its power to put down the local criminals. He offers the party 6,000 gold pieces to destroy the egg, and another 1,000 for defeating Maukle and turning him in to the authorities should the party encounter him.

entries.name: The Clocktower
entries: Upon reaching the clocktower ({@adventure Map 2|TheJobAtPecklesPort|1|Adventure Map 2}), the party find the Egg resting inside, at the very centre of the room. A {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal that the Egg has thus far gone undisturbed. A Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check of 20 or above will also reveal that the Egg appears to tremble slightly as the party enters.

Immediately after looking around, the windows shatter as Maukle and his pirate gang, the Unjolly Rogers, burst through them and strike at the party. Simultaneously, the Egg cracks, and four large tentacles protrude from the shell, writhing wildly in the air.
The Unjolly Rogers consist of {@creature Pirate King Maukle|DMSecretWeapon} and three {@creature Brigand of the Unjolly Roger|DMSecretWeapon|Unjolly Rogers Brigands}.
Roll Initiative.

On initiative count 20 of each turn, the Egg will strike out with a tentacle at a random creature within 30 feet of it. That creature must make a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d8} Bludgeoning damage and be {@condition restrained} until the end of its next turn.

The Egg has an AC of 15 and 20 hit points. Destroying the Egg will stop the tentacles from striking. A successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check will coax the tentacles back into the Egg, which will then fall dormant.

After defeating Maukle, if the Egg is not destroyed, he will offer the party 8,000 gold pieces to walk away and leave his troop to their spoils. If the Egg is destroyed, he will offer them 2,000 gold to allow his troop to flee before the authorities arrive. Maukle does not have this money on his person; he will need to leave and have the party meet him later to retrieve it. Famously, Maukle's bond is his word, and he can be trusted to give the party what he owes them.
At this point, the party have four options. Depending on what they choose, proceed to the following sections:

items: {@b Option 1.} Destroy Egg and collect payment from Hank. See {@adventure Conclusion 1|TheJobAtPecklesPort|0|Conclusion 1}.
{@b Option 2.} Walk away and leave the Egg for Maukle and the Unjolly Rogers. See {@adventure Conclusion 2|TheJobAtPecklesPort|0|Conclusion 2}.
{@b Option 3.} Return the Egg to Plumbus and collect their payment. See {@adventure Conclusion 3|TheJobAtPecklesPort|0|Conclusion 3}.
{@b Option 4.} Keep the Egg for themselves. See {@adventure Conclusion 4|TheJobAtPecklesPort|0|Conclusion 4}.

entries.name: Conclusion 1
entries: {@i Destroy Egg and collect earnings from Hank.}

The party destroy the Egg (or the Egg is destroyed in the battle with Maukle) and meet Hank soon after. He gratefully hands over the reward as promised. If the party also killed Maukle or handed him over to the authorities, he will give them an additional 1,000 gold pieces.

The Pigeon Boys take further power in the port, stripping away territory and wealth from what remains of the Unjolly Rogers. The more vicious gangs are curbed, and a restless truce is formed between the underbelly and rulers of Peckle's Port. It becomes a town of infinite opportunity for those willing to bend the rules, and the people there who know how to keep their heads down are rewarded with the protection of multiple, powerful armadas that keep each other in check.

entries.name: Conclusion 2
entries: {@i Walk away and leave the Egg for Maukle and the Unjolly Rogers.}

The party walk away 8,000 gold richer, leaving Maukle and his gang with the Egg. Over the following year, the Unjolly Rogers syphon power from the Egg to enhance themselves with bizarre and powerful mutations, spewing additional limbs, fins, teeth, and gills. They overrun the other gangs, but are held back from complete control by the Royal Navy. Under the influence of the Egg, the Unjolly Rogers grow more vicious and brutal in their work, and their new, aggressive form of piracy makes life hard for those who live in Peckle's Port.

entries.name: Conclusion 3
entries: {@i Return the Egg to Plumbus.}

The party stand guard over the egg until the authorities arrive. Having protected it, they receive their 4,000 gold reward from Plumbus, and the gratitude of the crown. Over the following year, the Royal Navy enhances their fleet with mysterious, crude, tentacled creatures of unknown origin. These monstrosities lurk in the depths of the bay around Peckle's Port, and strike out at vessels the Navy finds suspicious. Piracy is halted in the area, although there are many lawful merchant ships that suffer a grim fate at the hands of the creatures, which appear difficult to control. The Navy's authority over Peckle's Port is unchallenged; taxes are raised, and huge incentives push many young people into the service of the Navy. The port becomes a stronghold of military force and pride of the nation, though the people living there fear to step near the waters, having learned to fear that which lies below.

entries.name: Conclusion 4
entries: {@i Keep the Egg for themselves.}

The party chooses to keep the Egg, and word spreads swiftly of their theft. With the Egg in their possession, they are a target of both local bandits and the crown. However, it is possible they might find a way to use its magic to their benefit. Their first step should be seeking out a powerful druid or wizard knowledgeable on sea creatures should they wish to harness the Egg's power.

If the party choose to release the Egg back into the ocean, it swiftly sinks beneath the waves. That night, they all receive a strange dream of darkness and rushing water. Upon waking up, they each gain a new feat: {@feat Conduit of the Kraken|DMSecretWeapon} (first published in DM's Secret Weapon Issue #17).

entries.name: Conduit of the Kraken
entries: The rumbling power of the Kraken surges through you, granting the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength or Wisdom score by 1.
You can breathe in air and water.
When a hostile creature moves out of your reach, you can use your reaction to attempt to grapple the provoking creature. This grapple occurs right before the creature leaves your reach.

data.name: Welcome to Ravenswood
entries: Welcome to Ravenswood is an adventure of puzzles and combat for four level 4 characters.

entries.name: The Story So Far...
entries: The village of Ravenswood has come to be plagued by Nyxarath, the Winged Terror. The three, immortal ravens who eternally sit atop the single gateway into the walled village have fled, a terrible omen for the fate of Ravenswood.
Nyxarath moves in a cloak of shadow, has plunged Ravenswood into perpetual darkness, burned buildings, and slaughtered livestock.
Desperate refugees who escaped the town have put out a call for brave adventurers to venture into the darkness, find the ravens that guard the village, and vanquish the winged demon.

entries.name: An Unhappy Landing
entries: The party arrives at the gate that marks entrance to Ravenswood just after midday. However, with every step closer to the walled village they take, the sky darkens unnaturally. Looking through the gate shows a town in shadow, illuminated only by lanterns and the light of the moon, despite the blazing sun outside. Since Nyxarath arrived, it is always night time in Ravenswood.
There are three perches carved into the gate. Each one is empty.

As they enter the town ({@adventure Map 1|WelcomeToRavenswood|2|Adventure Map 1}), the party are accosted by the mayor of Ravenswood, Gideon Silvermane, a lean and unusually tall dwarf. He is clearly exhausted and afraid. He explains that the three ravens who guard the village have vanished, and Nyxarath has been terrorising the town for weeks. Without the ravens to help, any hope of fighting the demon is out of the question. He offers a reward of 3,000 gold coins to anyone who can defeat Nyxarath and save the town.

As he speaks, a shadow passes overhead. A character with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 16 or higher will notice a large pair of black leathery wings, high above in the sky, the form of its body obscured by a limp corpse clutched in its talons.

At this point, the player character stood closest to Gideon must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 5d6} Bludgeoning damage on a failed save, as the corpse is dropped from the sky directly on top of them. If the party spotted Nyxarath beforehand, this save is made at Advantage. By the time the characters have recovered from the shock, the shadow is gone.
An Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check made on the body will reveal words carved into its flesh:
hunted ravens, there are three
hunted ravens, too proud to flee,
hunted ravens, can't hide forever,
you'll find your ravens in death, together

entries.name: Raven Quest
entries: From this riddle, the party may be able to intuit that the ravens have not fled Ravenswood, but are somewhere in the town. Gideon will speak up to help the party reach this conclusion if they are struggling. He will then point them to areas it is whispered the ravens have been seen. There are three:

items: {@b Blackwing, the Brazen} — Last seen in the Executioner's Square ({@adventure Chapter 2.1|WelcomeToRavenswood|0|Blackwing, the Brazen})
{@b Quillfeather, the Lost} — Last seen in the Forgotten Chapel Gardens ({@adventure Chapter 2.2|WelcomeToRavenswood|0|Quillfeather, the Lost})
{@b Keeneye, the Collector} — Last seen at the Old Apothecary ({@adventure Chapter 2.3|WelcomeToRavenswood|0|Keeneye, the Collector})

entries: The party can search for the ravens in any order they wish. Once all three have been found, proceed to {@adventure Chapter 3.1|WelcomeToRavenswood|0|Nyxarath}.

entries.name: Blackwing, the Brazen
entries: The journey through the village to the Executioner's Square is silent and foreboding. The square is at the very back of Ravenswood, the high, oak walls of the village barring any path onward. There stands a guillotine, and as the party approaches, a raven appears perched atop it.
It speaks thus:
O', bloody battles, O', endless strife,
A futile struggle, a waste of life,
But what good could come from hero's last hour?
A feast, a corpse, that ravens devour
But good, kind magic, with ravens does fly,
And heed this well, we cannot lie,
And as we feasted, blood and flesh,
So life we gave, to those in death
Returned from grave, no wounds did bear
Heroes healthy, strong, and fair,
The time has come, yes, strength we need,
Do you dare trust, to let us feed?

Blackwing will say no more, unless asked to repeat the riddle. The solution requires a party member to die, or fall to 0 hit points, at which point Blackwing will flutter down and feast on their body. As he does so, their wounds will knit, their hit points will be restored, any missing limbs will vanish and materialise back on their body, and they will return to life if dead, none the worse for wear.
The character Blackwing ate from also gains {@dice 1d10} hit points, and has their hit point total increased by the same amount.

After eating, Blackwing will speak with the party. He will tell them how his power has been depleted by the demon's darkness, and how it threatened to transform him into a terrible beast. He declares he will aid the party in their battle with Nyxarath, and entreats them to find his kin. He then flutters away into the darkness.

entries.name: Quillfeather, the Lost
entries: The Chapel Gardens ({@adventure Map 2|WelcomeToRavenswood|2|Adventure Map 2}) are large and foreboding in the dark. As the party moves through them, they see no sign of Quillfeather. Then, suddenly, a whistling screech pierces the darkness, and a huge, snarling beast of shadow lunges toward them.
Roll Initiative.
The party are fighting one {@creature Demonic Ravenbeast|DMSecretWeapon}.

Upon defeating the Ravenbeast, it bursts in a cascade of shadow and silver. In the wake of the demonic force, a fluttering raven remains—Quillfeather. She thanks the party earnestly, apologising for her aggression. Her powers have been weakened by Nyxarath's presence, allowing his corrupting force to overcome her utterly. She pledges allegiance to the party when they come to fight Nyxarath, and begs their help in finding Blackwing and Keeneye, the two other immortal ravens. She then flies off into the darkness.

entries.name: Keeneye, the Collector
entries: The old apothecary was once the jewel of Ravenswood—a place of potent potions and incredible alchemical experiments. Now, it is a ramshackle ruin, home to little more than dust and rot. Within, the party finds Keeneye. He pays them no heed, staring intently at a ring held within a translucent tube. Several bottles rest beside the tube.
This is {@adventure The Ring|WelcomeToRavenswood|1|The Ring} puzzle; see the appendix for the rules, solution, and hints.

Upon retrieving the ring, Keeneye flutters down. "I knew you could do it!" he declares triumphantly. Keeneye has been guarding the ring, awaiting adventurers with enough power to challenge Nyxarath. He offers it to them (it is a {@item Ring of the Ram}) and declares he will aid the party in their battle with Nyxarath. He also requests they seek out his brother and sister, Blackwing and Quillfeather, before flying out of the apothecary through a shattered window and vanishing into the darkness.

entries.name: Nyxarath
entries: Immediately after this happens, the party hears a howling, terrified scream from the center of the village. Upon arriving there ({@adventure Map 1|WelcomeToRavenswood|2|Adventure Map 1}), they see Gideon, helpless and held aloft by Nyxarath. The winged demon leers down at the party, his humanoid form a vortex of shadow and flame. He drops Gideon, who falls heavily to the earth and is knocked {@condition unconscious}. Simultaneously, each party member feels something appear in their hand: an {@item Immortal Raven's Feather|DMSecretWeaponAdventures}.
Roll Initiative.
The party is fighting {@creature Nyxarath the Winged Evil|DMSecretWeapon|Nyxarath, the Winged Demon}.

Upon defeating Nyxarath, he vanishes in a whirlwind of darkness and crimson fire. The sun bursts through the sky, a pleasant afternoon breeze ruffles over the party, and with a fluttering of charcoal feathers, the three immortal ravens return to their posts atop the gate that leads to the village.

Gideon wakes up with a start, and instantly begins to weep with gratitude. Villagers begin pouring out of their homes, cheering, dancing, and celebrating. The three ravens thank the party personally, and grant them each one additional {@item Immortal Raven's Feather|DMSecretWeapon}. Keeneye also lets the party keep the ring they found, and Gideon hands the party the promised 3,000 gold. Ravenswood is safe; the party will always have friends and free lodging here.

data.name: Puzzles of the Raven
entries: We're just past the spooky season, but no matter the time of year, there's always room to TERRIFY players with PUZZLES! Powergamers beware, no amount of Paladin/Sorcerer/Warlock multiclass shenanigans can help you here.

The following two puzzles are great ways to add a little variety to your game. The first is a real test of bravery, with a spooky theme. It is the puzzle of Blackwing, the Brazen, one of the magic ravens of Ravenswood.
O', bloody battles, O', endless strife,
A futile struggle, a waste of life,
But what good could come from hero's last hour?
A feast, a corpse, that ravens devour
But good, kind magic, with ravens does fly,
And heed this well, we cannot lie,
And as we feasted, blood and flesh,
So life we gave, to those in death
Returned from grave, no wounds did bear
Heroes healthy, strong, and fair,
The time has come, yes, strength we need,
Do you dare trust, to let us feed?

entries.name: The Answer
entries: The player must reduce themselves to 0 hit points, at which point Blackwing will feast on their body. As he does so, their wounds will knit, their hit points will be restored, and they will return to life if dead, none the worse for wear.

entries.name: Hint
entries: Blackwing, the Brazen is perched upon a guillotine.

entries.name: Reward
entries: A character restored to life by Blackwing has their maximum hit point total increased by {@dice 1d10}. A creature can gain this benefit only once.

entries.name: The Ring
entries: This puzzle was found by Keeneye, the Collector, another immortal raven of Ravenswood. The Ring puzzle is simple, in theory. Players must fill a tube with liquid to access a magic ring that lies at the bottom.

entries.name: The Rules
entries: A beautiful ring is secured by powerful, tar adhesive, and sits at the bottom of a long, thin, translucent tube of force. This tube is magic. It cannot be bent, shattered, or moved, and the opening is covered by a one way anti-magic field. Anything entering the tube ceases to be magical, and any magic that enters the tube is dispelled. The antimagic field will also repel anything other than liquid that might enter it; any attempt to place one's hand into the tube, for instance, is utterly impossible.

Any liquid poured into the tube vanishes immediately, with the exception of the liquid contained within four glass bottles that sit beside the tube. If one of these bottles, or the contents therein, is moved more than 5 feet away from the tube, it vanishes, and reappears back beside the tube.

items: Bottle 1 contains {@item Universal Solvent}, an orange chemical with the power to dissolve any adhesive. It is dense and viscous, and will sink through other liquids. It will lose its properties and morph into a potent adhesive immediately if it comes in contact with an acidic or alkaline chemical.
Bottle 2 contains Red Acid of equal potency to the Green Alkali.
Bottle 3 contains Red Acid of equal potency to the Green Alkali.
Bottle 4 contains Green Alkali of equal potency to the Red Acid.
All four bottles must be poured into the tube. If done in the correct order, the ring will rise to the top.

entries: There is also a hat with the words "I'm With Stupid" written on it. Placing this hat upon one's head will cause the entire puzzle to reset.

entries.name: The Answer
entries: The players must find a way to get the {@item Universal Solvent} to the bottom of the tube to free the ring from the glue. They must also pour every bottle of liquid into the tube so the ring can float to the top. However, if they start with the Universal Solvent, and then pour the acid or alkali on top of it, it will immediately lose its properties and become {@item Sovereign Glue}, locking the ring in place.

The solution is to begin with a bottle of Red Acid, then Green Alkali. These two chemicals of equal potency will neutralise the solution. The Universal Solvent can then be added, which will sink to the bottom and free the ring. The ring will then float to the top. From here, the final Red Acid vial can be added, and the ring will float to the top of the tube and can be taken.
In short, the correct order of bottles is as follows:
{@b Bottle 2, Bottle 4, Bottle 1, Bottle 3.}

entries.name: Hint
entries: Mixing acids and alkali neutralises the solution.

entries.name: Reward: What Is The Ring?
entries: You can make the ring in the tube a magic item appropriate to the power level of your campaign. Here are some suggestions on the ring to give your players, relative to their average level.

data.name: Rudolf, the Red-Blooded Paindeer
entries: Rudolf, the Red-Blooded Paindeer is a wintery adventure of roleplay, puzzles, and combat for a party of four level 6–7 characters.

entries.name: Premise
entries: Every year, on the night of the winter solstice, Sleigh, the Great Sky Ship, sets forth on a global voyage. Manned by the industrious and crafty Winter Elves, Sleigh tours every nation, every city, every home, and delivers unto the people of the world gifts of humble magic.
This year, something is wrong.

Word of the sky ship's departure from The Great Pole was met with delight by those in northern Avestros, knowing that very soon their gifts would come raining down from on high. But the ship never arrived. What is worse, a blizzard, the likes of which not seen since the Endless Winter, is bearing down upon the land.

There is only one hope. A single, one-way portal has appeared in the centre of Bearwick, the most northerly town in Avestros. Such portals are known handiwork of the Winter Elves, and only used in times of great need. A handful of adventurers may step through and be teleported to the Elves' location. Once they go however, there will be no way back. The portal appears to be a desperate attempt for the Winter Elves to summon aid. However, without a guaranteed way back home, only the bravest adventurers (or the most foolish) would dare attempt a rescue.

entries.name: The Crash
entries: Should the party accept the call to adventure, the portal will close after the final player character steps through. The party emerges in a desolate landscape of featureless white ({@adventure Map 1|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|2|Adventure Map 1}). The noon sun above offers no hug of warmth, but reflects a painful glare from the velvet snow surrounding them. Beside the party is the wreck of Sleigh, the Great Skyship, its noble bow shattered on the vicious ice.

The party hears a gentle belch from behind them, and turn to find Plumpkin, a Winter Elf. He is very short and deathly pale, and is carrying a bottle of whisky in one hand and a carton of eggs in the other.
"Eggnog!" he declares, before inserting a whole egg into his small mouth and swallowing it with a hearty gulp of whisky. "So, are you the ones here to save us?"

Plumpkin will explain the situation to the party. Sleigh was grounded in a flash blizzard which tore the enchanted sails from the vessel, causing it to fall from the sky. With no sail, the ship cannot fly, and the gifts of the annual solstice cannot be delivered.

What is worse, most of the elves' supplies were lost in the crash. They will surely not survive the night unless they can get the ship airborne once again. The last of their magic was used to open the one-way portal to bring help to them.

The only hope they have is to seek out the legendary beast of savagery who dwells somewhere in the tundra—Rudolf, the Red-Blooded Paindeer. With its powers of flight and incredible strength, Rudolf might be able to pull Sleigh free and allow the elves (and the adventurers) to escape.
Alas, with the blizzard bearing down upon them, even if they escape, it seems impossible for the winter solstice gifts to be delivered on time.
The gravity of the situation clearly weighs heavily on Plumpkin; he has found solace in homemade eggnog, and seems a little drunk.

entries.name: Landing Party
entries: There are four Winter Elves beside the crashed Sleigh: Plumpkin, Stumbles, Pitterfoot, and Craig. Each one knows something about the area. Each is attempting to patch up the Sky Ship, although it is a lost cause in its present state. These activities are listed in the table below. Should the party wish to help, they can attempt a skill check. On a success, the task is successful. After helping an Elf, they will offer a tip on finding and conscripting Rudolf.

entries.caption: Sleigh Chores
rows: {@dc 18} Charisma check to cheer him up.
Rudolf respects those who can defeat him in battle, or earn his favour somehow. He has aided Humanoids before, but only if they were able to survive his savage attempt to feast on their flesh, first.
Crafting winter gear from the fragments of Sleigh's broken sail.
Rudolf, the Red-Blooded Paindeer is said to favour the taste of Frost Wormlings. They can be found to the north of here.
Building a shelter to weather the storm.
Rudolf is rumoured to enjoy the drink Eggnog.
Rudolf is said to like carrots, but they are rare in these lands.

entries: Plumpkin can be convinced to part with his "eggnog" with a {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. Alternatively, a party member can challenge him to a drinking contest for it. They must succeed on a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw to win the contest, taking a bottle of "eggnog" on a victory. The GM may also choose to give a player who attempts this contest the {@condition Inebriated|DMSecretWeapon|inebriated} condition (see DM's Secret Weapon Issue #19).

entries.name: Snow Attack
entries: Just as the party are about to set off, the blizzard picks up. A gale of blinding ice surges over the landscape towards the ship, encasing the party, the elves, and Sleigh in a vortex of freezing snow. From within the blizzard, two humanoid figures emerge. {@creature Snow Elemental|DMSecretWeapon|Snow Elementals} are attacking. They appear as traditional snowmen—their eyes charcoal black buttons, their carrot noses wrinkled in sadistic, grim leers.
Roll Initiative.
Upon defeating the Snow Elementals, they collapse into inanimate snow. Their carrot noses and button eyes are free to be plundered. The carrots and buttons are ordinary and nonmagical.

If the party want to leave to find Rudolf, proceed to {@adventure 2.2|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|0|Rudolf, the Red-Blooded}. If the party first want to find frost wormlings after speaking with Stumbles, proceed to {@adventure 2.1|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|0|To Catch a Wormling}, and then go to {@adventure 2.2|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|0|Rudolf, the Red-Blooded}.

entries.name: To Catch a Wormling
entries: Frost Wormlings swim beneath frozen lakes, visible from above but shielded by a wall of translucent ice. They are small and swift, but can be trapped by cunning hunters. Players can attempt to catch a wormling by stepping carefully over the ice of a lake, cracking it as they go.
You can use the {@adventure Ice Puzzle rules|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|1} to set up this challenge.
There are three Frost Wormlings the players can catch.

entries.name: Rudolf, the Red-Blooded
entries: The journey to Rudolf's lair is arduous; the winds are biting and the snow is deep. Each player who attempts the journey must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or gain the {@condition Freezing|DMSecretWeapon} condition (see DM's Secret Weapon Issue #20). If you don't have DMSW #20, the GM can give one point of {@condition exhaustion} instead.

The lair itself is a frigid wasteland, and at its heart stands Rudolf ({@adventure Map 2|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|2|Adventure Map 2}). He is huge. His rough coat is blanketed in snow, his heavy, black hooves hover an inch over the snow, leaving no hoofprint as he moves, and his antlers rise to the heavens like jagged, twisting stalagmites. Hot steam rises as a thick, white vapour from his nose, which is stained eternally red with blood. It takes incredible power to act as sovereign in this eternal tundra, and Rudolf is unmatched among beasts. His eyes glint red as the party approach—should anyone wish to attempt any diplomacy, they have only seconds to do so before he attacks.

Rudolf cannot speak, but he understands {@language Common} and is intelligent enough to understand a plea for help. Should the party attempt to persuade him to lend assistance, they must succeed on a {@dc 21} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. They can enhance this check with offerings Rudolf might like:

items: An offering of eggnog adds +3 to the check.
An offering of carrots adds +3 to the check.
An offering of a Frost Wormling adds +1 to the check, to a total of +3.

entries: On a successful check, Rudolf will aid the party and the Winter Elves. On a fail, the party must prove themselves to Rudolf by defeating him in battle.
Roll Initiative.
The party are fighting {@creature Rudolf, the Red-Blooded Paindeer|DMSecretWeapon}.

After defeating or successfully bargaining with Rudolf, his demeanour changes. He bows his head and nuzzles the player nearest to him affectionately. He will then stand at the front of the group and use his powerful form to beat an effortless, safe pathway through the snow. The journey back to Sleigh is uneventful, although the howling winds and blizzard seem to be growing ever stronger as darkness begins to fall.

entries.name: Jack Frost Strikes
entries: If the Winter Elves are cheered at the sight of the party returning with Rudolf, they do little to show it. The blizzard has reached its apex, and the vicious cold and foreboding darkness dull all spirits ({@adventure Map 3|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|2|Adventure Map 3}). Were it not for Rudolf's nose, which glows a deep crimson even in darkness, it's unlikely the party would have found their way back.
Plumpkin hurries forward to greet the party upon their return. He shouts over the storm:
"Move quickly! I'll get Rudolf on the reins, he can tow us free and fly us out of here! Get inside the ship!"

Rudolf understands, and proudly steps forward, the only being present unbothered by the furious snowstorm. As he is drawn away by the elves, the light from his nose fades and the world grows dark once more. Then, over the shrill howl of the wind, an icy voice cries out.
From the darkness emerges a being clad in ornate fur, sat atop a deathly, black horse of ice. It raises a trembling, pale hand and points toward Sleigh.
"YOU CANNOT ESCAPE!"

"EVERY YEAR YOU FLY OVER MY DOMAIN, BRINGING GIFTS TO ALL. ALL EXCEPT ME, THAT IS. NOBODY CARES FOR JACK FROST. SO I WILL TAKE YOUR PRECIOUS CARGO, AND ALL THE GIFTS SHALL BE MINE. THERE WILL BE NO SOLSTICE CHEER THIS YEAR, ONLY YOUR ICY DEATH!"
At his final word, a {@creature Snow Elemental|DMSecretWeapon} rises from the ice beside the party. Roll Initiative.

The party are fighting {@creature Jack Frost|DMSecretWeapon} and a {@creature Snow Elemental|DMSecretWeapon}. The Winter Elves are readying Rudolf to pull Sleigh free, and they cannot help. The storm heavily obscures any area beyond 20 feet for all non-Elemental creatures.

When Jack Frost falls to zero hit points, all Snow Elementals disintegrate back into snow. The party may choose to kill Jack Frost, which will end the blizzard. Alternatively, they can speak with him to attempt to resolve the situation without further bloodshed.

items: If the party kill Jack Frost, proceed to {@adventure 3.2|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|0|The Death of the Blizzard}.
If the party choose to spare Jack Frost, proceed to {@adventure 3.3|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|0|A Solstice Miracle}.

entries.name: The Death of the Blizzard
entries: Jack Frost lets out a piercing cry that is snatched away in the wind. His body, and that of his steed, morph into snow, and collapse to the ground. With his disappearance, the blizzard lifts swiftly.

The party are free to leave, with Rudolf pulling Sleigh free of the ice, up into the air, and away from the arctic tundra. Through the night the ship sails, reaching Bearwick in the early morning hours of the following day. Here Rudolf brings the ship to land, before swiftly departing back to his home.

The party and Winter Elves are met with delight by the citizens of the town. Sadly, it is too late to deliver the gifts of the Elves this solstice, but who has need of such trinkets in times of merriment? All have survived, and all is now well. Next year will be a solstice grander than any before it, and word swiftly spreads across the kingdom of what transpired in the north.

A great feast is held in Bearwick, where all are welcome. With great food, drink, and company, the party and Elves rejoice, knowing they have saved all future solstice celebrations from the dark machinations of the thieving Jack Frost.

entries.name: A Solstice Miracle
entries: Jack Frost lets out a piercing cry that is snatched away in the wind. His fury swiftly turns to despair, as the blizzard around him dies, and he is left sobbing, pitifully, in the darkness.

"All I wanted was a solstice gift of my own. Is it really wrong to steal a kingdom's worth of gifts and murder a handful of Elves to get what I want? Nobody's ever nice to me, why should I be nice to them?"

Pathetic as he is, Jack Frost no longer poses any threat to the party or the flight of Sleigh. Should the party choose to leave him here in his despair, move to {@adventure 3.2|RudolfTheRedBloodedPaindeer|0|The Death of the Blizzard}.

If the party choose to offer Jack Frost a gift, his spirits will be lifted by an astonishing margin. Giddy with joy, he will thank them repeatedly. The quality of the gift matters little; it is the very act of receiving anything that delights Jack.
Jack will then apologise for his actions, and vow to do right by the Elves, Rudolf, and the party. With his storm magic, he conjures another mighty wind, but this time, it is in the ship's favour.

With Rudolf pulling Sleigh, and Jack Frost howling mighty words of magic to conjure a mighty storm that bears them onward, Sleigh goes dashing above the snow. At an incredible speed, the ship arrives over the town of Bearwick, illuminated by the rising moon. The people there celebrate and cheer, as the Elves hurl gifts manically over the side of the vessel. If Rudolf, Jack Frost, and the party aid them through the night, it will be possible to deliver every gift before sunrise.
After a gruelling flight over the entirety of Avestros, dawn breaks as the party return to Bearwick. The Solstice has been saved by Rudolf, Jack Frost, and the party.

Their return is met with delight by the citizens of the town. The Elves are rescued, the gifts delivered, and all is now well. Jack Frost pledges to aid the Elves every year, beginning with the construction of a new sail to fly their ship, letting Rudolf roam free once more. Word swiftly spreads across the kingdom of what transpired in the north, and the party and Rudolf are hailed as heroes across the land.

A great feast is held in Bearwick, where all are welcome. With great food, drink, and company, the party and Elves rejoice, knowing they have saved the solstice, and brought warmth to the heart of Jack Frost, who had long given up on hope and friendship. In the bleak darkness of winter months, a ray of hope shines, and the actions of the party have shown that through friendship and forgiveness, even those who believe themselves lost can find a way back to happiness and joy.

data.name: Ice Puzzles: Frost Wormling Hunt
entries: Frost Wormlings swim beneath frozen lakes. In order to catch one, a creature must walk over the treacherous ice and corner it. This puzzle uses the mini-maps given below, and has the following rules:

items: The ice is only strong enough to support one creature moving on it at a time.

A player can begin on any tile of ice they choose, but once they start, they must not leave the ice minimap until they have captured the wormling. Doing so forfeits the challenge as the wormling escapes.
Once a player steps on a tile of ice, that tile cracks.
Tiles with rocks on do not need to be cracked, and cannot be walked on. Players cannot move diagonally between tiles of ice.
If a player steps on a cracked tile of ice, the tile breaks, and the player falls into the freezing waters below. They take {@damage 2d8} Cold damage.

The wormling will always hide below an uncracked tile. Once a player has cracked every tile of ice by walking over each one, they will be able to plunge their hand through the final tile and seize the wormling. Ultimately, the aim of the puzzle is to step on every ice tile only once.

entries: There are three frozen ponds, each home to a Frost Wormling. The puzzles grow increasingly difficult.

data.name: Festival of the Hunt
entries: The Festival of the Hunt is a ticking clock one-shot of adventure and combat designed for four level 11 player characters.

entries.name: The Festival of the Hunt
entries: The ancient walled city of Vivile is hosting its annual Festival of the Hunt. The centre of the city is evacuated and locked down; shop windows have been boarded shut, and monsters are let loose to rampage through the empty streets. Criminals from the city's dungeon are forcibly entered into the Festival to battle these monsters for their freedom, alongside brave or foolhardy adventurers who willingly compete for glory and riches. Many warriors fight, and many die. Whoever accrues the greatest number of points for slaying the monsters is crowned victorious.

This year, the reward offered to the victor is a fabled {@item Superior Ring of Spell Storing|DMSecretWeaponAdventures|Ring of Superior Spell Storing}, an incredible piece of equipment capable of housing spells up to 9th level. If you are integrating this adventure into your campaign, you can instead choose an object that ties into the arcing narrative of your players, such as a vial of precious antidote they need to save a treasured loved one, or a mighty weapon they must obtain to battle an ultimate foe. In any case, the players have set their sights on victory, and must compete in the Festival to win the prize.

entries.name: Base Camp
entries: Before the hunt begins, all participants gather in the great cathedral at the very centre of Vivile ({@adventure Map 1|FestivalOfTheHunt|1|Adventure Map 1}). The civilians have long since evacuated, and they, along with the Regent and various nobles and spectators from neighbouring settlements, watch the events of the festival unfold from a huge scrying lake outside the city.

While in the cathedral, the party are able to wander freely, interact with other adventurers, and prepare for the upcoming hunt. The party are also free to consult Guard Captain Harrow for information on the rules of the hunt (see {@adventure 1.2 Rules & Regulations|FestivalOfTheHunt|0|Rules & Regulations}). The table below shows the various NPCs present.

entries.caption: Base Camp
rows: Human, lawful neutral. Harrow stands watch, clad in fabulous armour and weaponry, but does not participate in the hunt.
The party can ask Harrow to clarify the rules of the hunt, which are given in full in section 1.2. Aside from quoting the rules of the festival, Harrow is forbidden from offering advice or guidance.
Halfling, chaotic good. Merchant Willie stands beside a snail caravan that carries simple adventuring potions, food, and alcoholic drinks.
The party can purchase alcoholic drinks for 1 sp per serving. They can also purchase {@item Potion of Greater Healing||Greater Healing Potions} for 200 gp.
Elf, true neutral. Last year's champion of the hunt. He is clad entirely in black, and uses a scythe as his spellcasting focus.

The Harvester will say nothing should the party attempt to speak with him. If a party member buys him a drink from Merchant Willie, he will take it, and offer a single {@item Potion of Speed} in exchange.
Orcs, chaotic evil. A group of five orcs competing in the hunt. They wear no armour, but carry heavy weapons.

The Brood boast openly of their inevitable victory. If the party buys them drinks, the Brood will consume them. After 3 drinks a piece, the Brood will become drunk, and will die in the Festival as a result. Consequently, they will not earn points and won't challenge the players' score for victory.
Human, lawful evil. A bounty hunter, caught by the city after an assassination, competing for her freedom.

Lania will insult the party with words infused with vicious magic if they attempt to speak with her. The party member she directs this insult toward must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or suffer a {@dice d4} penalty to all saving throws until they finish a long rest. You can explain this debuff to the player, but the character is unaware of the curse on a failed save.
Hag, chaotic evil. A cackling witch who does as she pleases in the city, including disrupting the hunt.

entries: Agnis will offer a bargain to any party member who chooses to take it. She will reduce their maximum hit points by half until they finish a long rest, in exchange for one boon from the following:

items: Your attack rolls score a critical hit on an 18–20 until you finish a long rest.
The first spell you cast before your next long rest does not expend a spell slot.
After a party member makes a deal with Agnis, all other NPCs in the building will refuse drinks from them, fearful of their intentions.

rows: Human, chaotic neutral. Eagato runs the gambling circuit across the city.
Speaking with Eagato will unveil an optional quest. Hidden somewhere in the city is a Golden Hairpin. Finding it will double all points scored by the team or individual that bear it.

entries: When the party are done interacting with others in the cathedral, they can declare their readiness to Guard Captain Harrow. At his word, the great gates will open, the timer will begin, and the party and their competitors spill onto the streets of Vivile as the monsters are released.

entries.name: Rules & Regulations
entries: The following are the full rules of the Festival of the Hunt. You should familiarise yourself with these rules before beginning the adventure, and communicate the rules to the players before the festival begins. Players can speak to Harrow, the Guard Captain for a refresher on the rules at any time.

items: The Festival of the Hunt takes place in the city of Vivile ({@adventure Map 2|FestivalOfTheHunt|1|Adventure Map 2}, and {@adventure Map 3|FestivalOfTheHunt|1|Adventure Map 3}).
The aim of the Festival of the Hunt is to score as many points as possible by defeating monsters.
The festival uses real life time. You might choose to place a stopwatch or timer on the table so players can see their time remaining to score points!
After one hour, the party or individual with the most points is declared the winner. The player characters compete as a team, sharing points.
Points are rewarded equal to the CR of the mobs defeated. For example, defeating a mob of three CR 3 {@creature Owlbear||Owlbears} will grant the party 9 points.

If a player character scores a critical hit they are awarded one gold star. At the end of the hunt, the party receives bonus points equal to the number of gold stars they earned divided by 3 (rounded down).
The GM should keep track of the total number of points the party has gained across the Festival.

Every 5 minutes of real-life time two mobs will spawn in random locations in the city. Roll twice on the {@adventure Festival Monster Mobs|FestivalOfTheHunt|0|Monster Mobs Table} table to determine the enemies that appear. The enemies will appear on the map the players are currently on. If there are no mobs remaining on the map, the players can travel to another area of the city to find some. Any time the players travel to a new section of the city (moving from Map 2 to Map 3, or vice-versa), they will emerge at the new location to find two mobs ready to fight (roll on the Festival Monster Mobs table when the players arrive).

While players are engaging one mob, if the other is far away on the map, it can be removed from the map at the GM's discretion. This represents a fellow competitor defeating that mob and claiming the points. In this way, you can ensure the number of mobs never grows too unwieldy on a single map.
Mobs the players aren't fighting move 30 feet in a random direction on initiative count 0. Mobs composed of multiple creatures move together.

As the party earns points, so too will their competitors: The Harvester, The Brood, and Lania. These competitors are fighting monsters elsewhere in the city, but periodically their scores are broadcast across the map by the Regent via a communal {@spell sending} spell.

{@b Ongoing Initiative.} The players should roll for initiative at the start of the festival. This will be their initiative order for the duration of the game. Mobs spawn in with an initiative score of 0, the only exception being the creature which appears in {@adventure 2.3|FestivalOfTheHunt|0|Complication: 55 Minutes: Intruder}. If a mob contains multiple creatures, they all move on initiative 0.

Various Complications will arise across the festival. See {@adventure 2.1|FestivalOfTheHunt|0|Complication: 20 Minutes: Lania's Fall}, {@adventure 2.2|FestivalOfTheHunt|0|Complication: 35 Minutes: An Innocent Lost}, and {@adventure 2.3|FestivalOfTheHunt|0|Complication: 55 Minutes: Intruder} for these complications, which occur at the 20 minute, 35 minute, and 55 minute marks.

entries.name: GM Guidance: A Compelling Competition
entries: Depending on how you run games, the points players earn will vary. Optimised player groups who move swiftly will accrue points far faster than a casual playgroup who take the game at a measured pace. As such, in order to ensure a competitive game, enemy teams will earn points relative to the number of mobs the players defeat. This way, their points will scale alongside the players.
Every time the party earns points for defeating a mob, their competitors will earn points as well:

items: The Brood will earn {@dice 1d10} points
Lania will earn {@dice 2d6} points
The Harvester will earn {@dice 2d8} points.

entries: Feel free to adapt the number of points competitors are earning to craft a compelling narrative. Ideally, your players should feel pushed to seek battles quickly and rack up points. As a GM, your concern should be crafting an enthralling narrative, rather than meticulously calculating the points of the NPCs; feel free to estimate!

entries.name: GM Guidance: Keeping It Quick!
entries: When controlling mobs, aim to take your turn as swiftly as possible. Consider using fixed damage for attacks, for example an Owlbear attacks twice, and on each hit, always deals 12 damage. This will allow you to take your turns faster and save rolling for damage. To find the fixed damage for an attack, simply average the result of the damage dice—usually this average damage number is given in the stat block.

You can also help yourself out by preparing tokens for the different mobs in advance. If you are using a VTT, you may choose to have the mob tokens prepared on a separate page you can quickly navigate to, allowing you to copy and paste them onto the battle map for the players to fight across the festival.

entries.name: Complication: 20 Minutes: Lania's Fall
entries: Roughly 25 minutes into the hunt, the party will see Lania fall and be swarmed by 5 {@creature Owlbear||Owlbears}. The party is free to engage the mob, or let them savage the bounty hunter.

If the party retreat and let the mob savage Lania, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a result of 10 or below, Lania is killed and removed from the competition. On a result of 11 or above, Lania survives, and gains a bonus of 15 points to her final score.

If the party chooses to intervene, Lania survives (the party receives all the points for defeating the mob). Lania will curtly thank the party, remove any curse she placed on player characters in the cathedral, and then cast {@spell bless} on the group, giving player characters a bonus of {@dice 1d4} to all attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws for the next 10 minutes.

entries.name: Complication: 35 Minutes: An Innocent Lost
entries: Roughly 35 minutes into the hunt, the party will hear the cry of a child from an abandoned building in the city. Should they investigate, they will find a young dwarven girl cowering in the rubble, wounded, and left behind in the evacuation. She will request the party escort her to the cathedral for safety, a task that will take 10 minutes with her current condition. Alternatively, the party can leave her here in the hope she will not be found by the monsters.

If the party escorts her to the cathedral, it takes 10 minutes, and they do not earn points during this time. Over the course of this escort mission, the other competitors in the hunt each earn 6 points. Upon reaching the cathedral, the girl tearfully thanks them as they hand her over to Guard Captain Harrow, and offers them a Golden Hairpin she found in the building. While possessing the Golden Hairpin, all subsequent points the party earns are doubled.

If the party chooses to leave the girl in the rubble to keep fighting, she remains hidden in the rubble and is killed instantly by falling debris when the gigan scythemaw attacks ({@adventure 2.3|FestivalOfTheHunt|0|Complication: 55 Minutes: Intruder}).

entries.name: Complication: 55 Minutes: Intruder
entries: 55 minutes into the hunt, the earth beneath the party's feet trembles. In an unoccupied space, across the city from their current location, a {@creature Gigan Scythemaw|DMSecretWeapon|gigan scythemaw} wrenches itself from the earth, drawn by the wanton slaughter and blood of the festival. The scythemaw is not a part of the hunt, and magical sirens begin blaring across the city as it rampages through the streets, shattering buildings and devouring monsters and warriors whole.
Should the party choose to engage the gigan scythemaw, the festival will not end until its defeat, or their death at its claws.
Roll initiative.
Upon defeating the gigan scythemaw, the Festival of the Hunt ends. The party are now free to retreat from the lockdown via a portal back at the cathedral.

Should the party choose to flee instead of fighting the gigan scythemaw, they can escape back to the cathedral and be teleported to freedom. The Festival ends upon their exit, and the monster descends back underground after destroying the city centre.

entries.name: Closing Ceremonies
entries: Upon escaping the Festival, the party's score is tallied against the scores of their surviving competitors. If the party defeated the gigan scythemaw, they earn an additional 15 points.

If victorious in the hunt, the party will receive the {@item Superior Ring of Spell Storing|DMSecretWeapon}. It functions as a normal {@item Ring of Spell Storing}, but is able to hold up to 9 levels worth of spells. If the party saved the dwarven girl, saved Lania, accepted Agnis, the Watcher's deal, purchased The Harvester a drink, and defeated the gigan scythemaw, the ring comes bearing the 9th level spell {@spell time stop}. Otherwise, it is empty.
If the party does not win the festival, they instead receive 10,000 gold pieces.

With the festival's conclusion, the party are now celebrities among the citizens of Vivile, who watched the events unfold anxiously through the scrying lake. A great feast is held outside the town, while the guards begin clearing the city of debris, corpses, and the remains of defeated monsters. Over the coming days the city centre will reopen, and the party can expect to find many opportunities for work and gold with their newfound fame as survivors of the hunt.

data.name: The Heist at Blanka's Palace
entries: A non-linear, roleplay focused one-shot of thievery, player choices, and deadly combat designed for a party of 4–5 level 5 player characters.

entries.name: I Cast Guidance on the GM
entries: This is a non-linear adventure, meaning players are free to roam about the palace and take multiple paths to achieve their goals. I recommend you read the one-shot in full before running the game. Familiarise yourself with the layout of the palace, the locations of key NPCs and objects, and potential combat encounters. All important areas and objects are marked on the DM's Treasure Map ({@adventure Map Pack|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1}) for quick reference.

Before the session begins, give each party member an object they seek to claim from the table below, or have them invent an object they are seeking to claim for themselves. The objects sought are flexible, but at least one party member must seek the Demon Head Crown, and at least one party member must seek the Ancient Map. If you are running this adventure for more players, feel free to invent additional objects and place them about the palace to be stolen!

The table below also contains the location of each object, and the recommended method of obtaining it. The party will need to discover these locations and methods by exploring the palace and interacting with NPCs. Their choices and interactions across the adventure will impact how the narrative unfolds. As always, feel free to adapt the adventure as it progresses to reward your players' creativity and dice rolls.

entries.caption: Desired Objects Table
rows: Worn by Gilgard in the Higher Hall (Floor 2)
Trade for the flame-tongue rapier, or receive as payment for completing Gilgard's Quest.
Defeat Blanka or convince him to leave his quarters and take the map from the wall.
When the lounge is empty, shrink the Enchanted Piano with the Wand of Enlarge/Reduce and pocket it.
Carried by The Chef in the Kitchen (Floor 1)
Take from the chef after forcibly subduing him, or get the chef fired by tampering with the dish prepared for Colonel Zidane.
Take from displayed celestial corpse upon placating its restless spirit or defeating it.

items.name: General Blanka
items.entry: The owner of the palace, and the host of the feast that is being held.

items.name: Colonel Zidane
items.entry: A prodigious warrior and Blanka's right hand man. He has an extremely sensitive stomach.

items.name: Gilgard
items.entry: A mysterious half-beast warrior, well known amongst his kin for his furious ambition and burning hatred of General Blanka.

entries.name: GM's Treasure Maps
entries: In the {@adventure Map Pack|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1}, you'll find quick reference maps for GM use. They show the locations of each object the party is seeking and the names of each key room, along with unmarked player versions.

{@adventure Chapter 2.0|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|0|Significant Locations} details the various rooms of the palace and the key NPCs at each one. Read through this chapter in advance, and refer to each room as the party explores the palace to describe the various interactions within them.

entries.name: Premise
entries: Looming over the surrounding landscape is the titanic palace of General Blanka. A former soldier turned war profiteer, Blanka is renowned for his arrogance and hedonism. His palace is a hive of elites; a melting pot of nobles, politicians, wealthy merchants, and celebrities, each with their own entourage of servants and bodyguards. Today, on the anniversary of a victorious battle, General Blanka is hosting a fabulous feast—a swaggering display of wealth and power. The party intends to infiltrate this event and make off with some treasured loot. They arrive at the palace beneath a mid-afternoon sun. The festivities have already begun, and the air is buzzing with the excited chatter of crowds.

entries.name: Reconnaissance and Recreation
entries: As players explore and loot their way through Blanka's Palace, they will have opportunities to interact with guests, staff, and guards. You can use the following NPC table for these social encounters, taking the opportunity to drop hints that point to the locations of desired objects and significant NPCs.
A halfling bard, dressed in an old but well maintained patchwork suit. He carries a lute and a forlorn expression.

{@b Busking.} Zat-Zun periodically bursts into song, attempting to pry a coin or two from the wealthy guests. A player may choose to join in this endeavour with a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check. A result of 16 or above will garner a positive response from the crowd, and Zat-Zun and the player will each receive 10 gold pieces,

rows: I'd love to take a gander at the Enchanted Piano in the Lounge, but I can't stand Colonel Zidane. He stinks to high heaven and spends all his time gambling or boasting of his battle prowess and challenging strangers to duels.

entries: A female elven noble, dressed in an achingly exquisite emerald ball gown and an obnoxious sneer.
She will refuse to speak to any party member wearing Staff Clothes (see {@adventure 2.4 Storage Room|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|0|Storage Room}), other than to demand wine.

rows: Colonel Zidane is desperately allergic to most foods. He demands an incredibly specific diet, and his fury falls fast and cruel on any chef who fails to deliver to his high standards.

entries: An attractive human noble dressed from head-to-toe in gilded crimson velvet.
Emmaline has an impressively low Intelligence score of 6. She will readily believe almost anything a player tells her without question.

rows: General Blanka is handsome AND wealthy. Sadly, he never interacts with his guests. He stays hidden away in his quarters on the 3rd floor; is he secretly a tortured, lonely soul?

entries: A minotaur merchant, carrying various simple wares and trinkets.
Rathstag will offer the party the following for 500 gold pieces: 1 {@item potion of healing}, 1 scroll of {@spell disguise self}, 1 {@item clockwork amulet|XGE}.

rows: I'm getting out of here soon, fellas. I saw {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} upstairs; he's a powerful warrior, and it's long been rumoured he despises the General. I don't want to be around if something kicks off.
An elderly human noble and academic. He walks with a limp and carries a poodle puppy in a dragonhide handbag, which occasionally emits shrill barks.
The Ancient Map is a spectacular piece of nautical history. It is a tragedy that it now hangs in General Blanka's Quarters, where none save he can see it.
A gloriously fat centaur, dressed in a toga. He is surrounded by a number of servants bearing platters of food and wine with a euphoric expression on his face.
If you want more food, just take any dish you're enjoying to the Kitchen. The Chef will be able to use The Wand of Enlarge/Reduce to magically increase your portion size!
A young goblin wearing Staff Uniform. She carries a silver platter of glasses filled with red wine very unsteadily, lurching from pillar to post under its weight.
I'm terrified I'm going to drop these and ruin everything. Luckily, there are plenty of Staff Outfits held in the Storage Room on the 2nd floor in case I get spilled on.
A portly human wearing Staff Uniform. He seems to be successfully avoiding work by pouring wine from one glass into another and back repeatedly with a stern, focussed expression on his face.
Blanka's famous Vault is on the 2nd floor, and can be reached via the Lounge. It holds many curiosities, including the preserved corpse of a Celestial.

entries.name: Significant Locations
entries: The following chapter contains significant locations, NPCs, and objects. It also includes a series of interactions that can occur in those locations. As always, reward your players for their ideas and approach to problem solving. The given solutions to acquiring each object across this chapter are only a suggested path.

entries.name: The Main Hall
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 1}. The Main Hall is the largest room on floor 1. It is the primary reception area of the feast, where the bulk of the guests and food can be found.

The party enters General Blanka's palace via the Main Hall. They are surrounded by party goers, with servants in elegant tuxedos weaving through the crowd bearing platters of delicious food on silver plates.

The stage along the north wall of the Main Hall is occupied by a pair of magical entertainers: a pyromancer and cryomancer. As guests eat, drink, and chatter, the pair weave an elegant display of elemental magic; a quartet of roaring snow, flame, ice, and lightning.

From this point onwards, the party's actions will dictate the flow of the adventure. They must interact with the guests at the feast and explore the castle to find the objects they seek and engineer opportunities to steal them safely.

entries.name: Kitchen
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 1}. The Kitchen is on floor 1, to the right of the Main Hall. The Wand of Enlarge/Reduce is in this room, carried by The Chef.

The kitchen is a circus of sizzling pans, boiling pots, and scintillating aromas. It is manned by a single orc, The Chef, who is wearing a pink apron and a comically large, floppy white chef's hat. He bustles back and forth manically, preparing exquisite dish after exquisite dish. Once completed, he places each meal on the tabletop counter, before drawing The Wand of Enlarge/Reduce from beneath his apron and enlarging the dish. In this way, a delicate suckling pig is transformed into a huge roasted boar, fit to feed two dozen at least.

If engaged, The Chef will bark furiously that he is understaffed and overwhelmed with the preparation of Colonel Zidane's personal meal. His reputation is on the line, and if a single spice or seasoning is out of place, the Colonel will certainly fire him immediately.

items: The Chef is a regular humanoid with a +0 to all saving throws, an AC of 10, and 4 hit points. If he is incapacitated (such as by a {@spell Sleep} spell) the party can take The Wand of Enlarge/Reduce from his person.
If a party member succeeds on a {@dc 11} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check, they can steal some Super Spice Powder from the kitchen.

If a party member is wearing a Staff Uniform (found in the {@adventure Storage Room|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|0|Storage Room} on the 2nd floor), The Chef will allow them to deliver a special prepared meal to Colonel Zidane.
If The Chef has been fired, the kitchen will be empty, and The Wand of Enlarge/Reduce will be sitting on the countertop.

entries.name: Wand of Enlarge/Reduce
entries: This wand has 9 charges. A creature holding the wand can expend 1 charge to cast the spell {@spell Enlarge/Reduce}, targeting an object (it cannot target a creature). If cast in this way, the spell lasts for 1 hour, without concentration.

entries.name: The Lounge
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 1}. The Lounge is on floor 1, in the top left of the building. The Enchanted Piano is in this room, alongside Colonel Zidane, who carries a {@item Flame Tongue Rapier||flame-tongue rapier}.

The Lounge is a hazy room of smoke and quiet conversation. A gentle tinkle of music flutters over all in attendance, performed by an unmanned Enchanted Piano. The attention of most in the room falls on Colonel Zidane—a lithe, middle-aged human carrying a fabulous rapier.

Colonel Zidane is sharp witted. If engaged, he will remark upon the player's evident skill as a warrior and challenge them to a fencing match. He will arrogantly offer his fabulous {@item Flame Tongue Rapier||flame-tongue rapier} if they can touch him.

items: Colonel Zidane is awaiting his special meal. If a player is wearing Staff Clothes (found in the {@adventure Storage Room|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|0|Storage Room} on the 2nd floor), he will tersely demand they return to the kitchen and bring his food to him.

If Colonel Zidane is offered a meal that has been tampered with in any way by the party, such as by the addition of Super Spice Powder or through a spell like {@spell Prestidigitation}, the Colonel will vomit immediately, and demand The Chef be fired at once. His personal guard will act on this order, and the party will hear the furious proclamations of The Chef echo through the building as he is forcibly removed from his post.

A player can choose to fence Zidane. They must battle him one-on-one, although other players may be able to subtly aid them through magic (such as the {@spell Bless} spell). If a fencing match occurs, the Colonel will lead the player out into the courtyard, followed by the guests in The Lounge, leaving the room empty.

While fencing, the player and Zidane each take turns making a single melee attack roll against each other. Colonel Zidane will always go first. Zidane has a natural AC of 22, and a +9 modifier to hit. The first duelist to strike the other twice wins.
If Colonel Zidane recently ingested a meal that was tampered with, he has Disadvantage on attack rolls.

If Zidane loses the fencing match, he will throw down his flame-tongue rapier in disgust and leave the palace in shame. The other guests will rejoin the party in the Main Hall, leaving the Lounge empty.
If The Lounge is empty, a player can use The Wand of Enlarge/Reduce on the Enchanted Piano, which shrinks to the size of an apple. It can now be pocketed for easy extraction.

entries.name: Storage Room
entries: {@adventure Map 2|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 2}. The Storage Room is on floor 2, above the Kitchen and to the right of the Higher Hall.
The Storage Room is empty. Along the north wall, there are dozens of Staff Uniforms of all sizes.

entries.name: The Higher Hall
entries: {@adventure Map 2|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 2}. The Higher Hall is on floor 2, directly above the Main Hall. The Demon Head Crown is in this room, worn by {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon}.

The Higher Hall is every bit as opulent as the Main Hall directly below it, but void of explosive entertainers, harried servants, and chattering crowds; the dazzling excess of gilded drapery and jewelled furniture garnishing the quiet room creates a stifling air. In this room, more than any other, the true intent of General Blanka's palace is evident: to humiliate and intimidate any who would question him.

There are very few guests in this room, though the party's eyes are at once drawn to a hulking, bestial warrior, upon whose head sits The Demon Head Crown. This man is {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon}.

items: {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} sits alone in contemplative silence. Should the party inquire about The Demon Head Crown, he will offer to trade it in exchange for Colonel Zidane's {@item Flame Tongue Rapier||flame-tongue rapier}. Colonel Zidane is in the Lounge.

Alternatively, if the party ingratiates themselves to {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon}, he will offer The Demon Head Crown in exchange for a simple favour: the party must get rid of General Blanka, by any means necessary. {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} will not say it directly, but his intent is clear. Should the party assassinate the General, The Demon Head Crown will be theirs.

entries.name: Fateful Decision
entries: The party's interactions with {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} will have a significant impact on the conclusion of this story.

items: If the party gives {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} the flame-tongue rapier, he will gladly hand them The Demon Head Crown. He will then instruct the party not to follow him under any circumstances, and leave the room via the stairs, ascending towards General Blanka's Quarters.

After he does so, use {@adventure Chapter 2.8 General Blanka's Quarters (After Gilgard's Trade)|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|0|General Blanka's Quarters (After Gilgard's Trade)} when the party visits General Blanka's Quarters.

entries.name: The Vault
entries: {@adventure Map 2|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 2}. The Vault is on floor 2, directly above The Lounge. The Celestial Skull is in this room, as a part of the displayed celestial corpse.

The Vault is empty of people. It is a stuffy, claustrophobic room containing various curiosities and trinkets that shine despite a layer of dust. The party's attention is immediately drawn to a crystal coffin, within which sits a preserved celestial corpse.
If a player steps within 5 feet of the celestial coffin, a delicate, disembodied voice will whisper the following riddle:
It comes from heaven,
