and fears the flames of hell,
It cloaks the earth for a fleeting spell,
It can be a man or an angel,
but devil? Never
Bring me an offering of this,
if you think you are clever.
{@b GM Only:} The answer to the riddle is snow.

items: If a player makes an offering of snow to the celestial corpse (they may create some via a spell such as {@spell Sleet Storm}, or request some from the cryomancer in the Main Hall), the voice will thank them, and allow them to take the Celestial Skull.

If a player attempts to take the Celestial Skull without offering snow, a {@creature Celestial Spirit|DMSecretWeapon|celestial spirit} will appear and attack. After defeating the spirit, the Celestial Skull can be taken.

entries.name: General Blanka's Quarters
GM Guidance
entries: If the party gave {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} the flame-tongue rapier, disregard this chapter, and proceed to {@adventure 2.8|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|0|General Blanka's Quarters (After Gilgard's Trade)} instead.

{@adventure Map 3|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 3}. General Blanka's Quarters is the only room on floor 3, above The Higher Hall. The Ancient Map is in this room, as is General Blanka himself.
At the height of the palace, General Blanka sits alone in his quarters, drunk. The room is tidy and surprisingly bare. The Ancient Map hangs along the north wall.

items: Should the party enter while in Staff Uniform, the General will believe them to be servants. He will explode in a tirade of abuse and fire them immediately for entering uninvited, and attack the party with lethal intent if they do not leave at once ({@creature General Blanka|DMSecretWeapon}).

Should the party enter in normal clothes, the General will furiously demand that they leave his quarters immediately. He will attack the party with lethal intent if they do not leave at once ({@creature General Blanka|DMSecretWeapon}).

If the party previously accepted {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon}'s offer to eliminate Blanka, they can inform Blanka of the proposition. If they do so, they must make a {@dc 16} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check to convince General Blanka of their honesty. The party have Disadvantage on this check if they are visibly carrying any of the General's possessions, such as The Celestial Skull, Wand of Enlarge/Reduce, or Enchanted Piano.
On a successful check, the General leaps from the room, roaring for his personal guard, and descends the stairs to the Higher Hall, intending to murder {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon}.
If Blanka is defeated, or has left the room, the party is free to take The Ancient Map from the wall.

entries.name: General Blanka's Quarters (After Gilgard's Trade)
entries: {@adventure Map 4|TheHeistAtBlankasPalace|1|Adventure Map 4}. General Blanka's Quarters is the only room on floor 3, above The Higher Hall. The Ancient Map is in this room, as is {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon}.

At the height of the palace, General Blanka's Quarters wait in darkness. Blood is splattered across the room, from floor to ceiling, staining The Ancient Map which hangs along the north wall. The General is dead; his decapitated head sits on his desk. His face is twisted into a hateful grimace, the wound at his neck cauterised by the heat of a flame-tongue blade.
{@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} stands silently in the room, breathing heavily.

entries.name: Interactions
entries: The moment the party enters the room, {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} will roar that he instructed the party not to follow him, and ready himself to attack.

items: If the party attempts to defuse the situation, they can attempt a {@dc 21} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Deception}) check to convince {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} they will not speak of the murder. Showing {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} evidence of their thievery, such as The Celestial Skull or Enchanted Piano, will aid the party's reassurances of silence, conferring a {@dice 1d4} bonus to the check. On a success, {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} will bundle past them, fleeing the palace and leaving the room empty.
If {@creature Gilgard|DMSecretWeapon} is defeated, or has left the room, the party is free to take The Ancient Map from the wall.

entries.name: Escape
entries: Once the party has acquired the objects they seek, they are free to depart from the castle as dusk begins to fall. The nature of their escape may vary depending on the actions they took, but beneath the cover of the festivities and bustle of the crowds, vanishing into the encroaching darkness is among the easier tasks the party have attempted that night. It is doubtless their activities today will not go unnoticed for long, and consequences are sure to follow, but in the present, with loot in hand and freedom in sight, the heist has come to a victorious close.

data.name: The Red Tyrant
entries: The Red Tyrant is an action packed one-shot of adventure, combat, and fabulous treasures designed for four level 12 player characters.

entries.name: The Airship and The Statue
entries: Airship technology is among the great marvels of the modern age. Steam billows, engines roar, pistons pump, and the air dances with the steady clank and chuckle of magic and science entwined, propelling passengers through the heavens. The party are among the first humanoids to embark on a voyage upon an airship, traveling alongside the famous treasure hoard of dwarven explorer Amron Thudrim. Amron, after a long life of plundering treasures from all over the world, has nobly decided to return all his treasures to the countries where he initially found them.

This voyage does not promise danger however, merely the exhilaration of soaring through the skies; the party have been hired to escort Amron's treasure hoard, and no trouble is expected. After all, this is a largely diplomatic mission, and what dangers are the players to fear up here in the skies?
{@adventure Map 1 (Amron's Airship)|TheRedTyrant|1|Adventure Map 1}

Amron's treasure hoard is vast, with all manner of magical trinkets and weapons stored in the airship's hold. Chief prize among the collection is a colossal dragon, hewn from a ruby mountain and bearing a gem encrusted crown. Worth more than the airship and all its other contents together, it is the value of this statue that warrants the party's involvement as its guard.

entries.name: Eruption
entries: Fourteen hours into the flight, at a time when the dizzying thrill of air travel has just begun to wane, the party are disturbed from their activities by a distant rumble. Suddenly, a plume of ash bursts from below them, followed almost immediately by a deafening roar. The earth below the airship shatters as a distant mountain top explodes, hurling molten rock, lava and choking fumes of ash into the air. The force of the shockwave strikes the airship before anyone can react, causing it to list dangerously to the starboard side.
Roll initiative.

For three rounds, in initiative order, each player must succeed on a {@dc 18} Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone}. A prone creature falls to the starboard side of the ship and ends their turn. If a creature on the starboard side of the ship fails a second Dexterity saving throw, they are thrown from the airship, falling 500 feet and landing on the outskirts of Fertilemound below. Unless a creature does something to mitigate the impact of this fall, they will take {@damage 20d6} damage when they land.

A creature that succeeds their Dexterity saving throw may take one action. A creature can use this action to secure themselves to the deck (no check required), or attempt to secure an ally within reach to the deck with a {@dc 11} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check, or take any other action.

After three rounds, a tortuous, bestial roar reverberates through the air, and the ship engulfs in flame. Cloaked by the raining ash, a gargantuan creature slams into the ship, sending it spiraling out of the skies and crashing with a scream of splintered wood and strangled metal in the farming town of Fertilemound. Creatures aboard the ship when it crash lands take {@damage 10d6} Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Fertilemound
entries: {@adventure Map 2 (Fertilemound)|TheRedTyrant|1|Adventure Map 2}

Fertilemound is a simple farming village. It reaps the benefits of loamy, volcanic soil to grow fine agricultural produce. Life here is, by all accounts, as ordinary a life as one could imagine... Until an airship falls on your head.
Pieces of the burning ship have landed across the town, setting many buildings on fire. Players thrown from the airship can reach the crashed ship in time to meet those on board disembarking.

If the party chooses to help put out the fires, the town will survive the blaze, and the party will earn the town's gratitude. If the fire is left it will spread and destroy the surrounding buildings.

Upon inspecting the crashed ship, the party will discover much of the treasure destroyed. Any non-magical gold has melted, and only a few magical pieces remain. The Ruby Dragon Statue is missing. A huge hole has been torn in the side of the ship, through which the statue was stolen from the hold by whatever creature attacked.
The party can attempt a collaborative Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to recover treasure. They recover the following items depending on their roll.

rows: {@item Boots of Elvenkind}, {@item Elven Chain}, 1,000 gold worth of gems
{@item Plate Armor of Etherealness||Plate Armour of Etherealness}, a {@item Frost Brand} weapon
{@item Belt of Fire Giant Strength}, {@item +2 Armor||+2 Armour}

entries: No sooner have the party finished gathering what treasure remains than a droning warhorn echoes through the air. Three {@creature Gladiator|DMSecretWeapon|orc gladiators}, one of whom is mounted on a {@creature Wyvern||red wyvern}, move toward the village.
The trio of orcs come to a stop before the party, and their leader speaks in a gruff voice:
"Amarezen, the Great, demands tribute. She is risen, and your treasure and food are forfeit. Hand everything over, or we shall kill you and take it!"

These orcs are fanatical worshippers of Amarezen, the Great. Any questions the party asks regarding Amarezen will be met with raucous laughter. The orcs will not be persuaded to leave by any non-magical means, and unless the party surrenders all their treasure and the villagers' food, they will attack.
If the party attacks the orcs, or refuses their demands, roll initiative.
The party are fighting three {@creature Gladiator|DMSecretWeapon|orc gladiators} and one {@creature Wyvern||red wyvern}.

entries.name: The Approach
entries: Upon defeating the orcs or submitting to their demands, the party will be able to question the townspeople of Fertilemound. The villagers will share the legend of Amarezen, the Great, a winged tyrant said to slumber deep within the mountains that surround the village. Certainly, it is this creature that attacked the airship and stole the Ruby Dragon.

Getting to the volcano that Amarezen, the Great calls home will take half a day on foot. If the party has the townspeople's gratitude, they will be gifted a {@item Potion of Speed} and two {@item Potion of Superior Healing||Potions of Superior Healing} before setting off.

Upon reaching the volcano the party will need to find a way in. There is an ornate and ancient iron gate at the foot of the mountain. It is unlocked, but guarded by three {@creature Gladiator||orc gladiators}. The players can pass them unnoticed with a {@dc 17} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check. Should the party be discovered, or attack the orcs, they must defeat them before being able to continue into the volcano.

Alternatively, a player that succeeds on a {@dc 21} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will notice a strange rock formation about 30 feet up the mountain. This formation is an ancient path the players can take to bypass the orcs and the main gate. The path is treacherous; a creature without a climb speed must succeed on a {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to clamber over the rocks safely. On a fail, the creature falls 30 feet and lands directly on top of one of the orc gladiators guarding the main gate. Both the player and the orc take {@damage 3d6} Bludgeoning damage, and the orcs are alerted to the party's presence.

If the players take the hidden path, they will enter a storage room before moving into the main cavern of the volcano. If the party surrendered their magic items to the orcs in {@adventure chapter 2.1|TheRedTyrant|0|Fertilemound}, those magic items can be reclaimed here.

entries.name: Into the Fire?
entries: {@adventure Map 3 (Volcano Heart)|TheRedTyrant|1|Adventure Map 3}

The path into the volcano leads to a large chamber containing ruined dwarven structures and half-collapsed statues of ancient, lost heroes. A steady stream of magma divides the chamber, and the Ruby Statue sits atop a plinth on the far bank of the molten river.
The magma is incredibly hot; any creature that touches it takes {@damage 8d6} Fire damage. A creature submerged in the lava takes {@damage 20d6} Fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

The party have only moments to take all this in before a low, guttural rumble echoes through the chamber. Stepping forth from the shadows is a gargantuan red dragon. The air before the dragon quivers under the heat of its breath. The dragon growls, and then launches into the air towards the party.
Roll Initiative.

The party is fighting an {@creature Illusory Red Dragon|DMSecretWeapon}. A creature that scores a critical hit against the dragon or uses an action to examine it can attempt a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check. On a success, they discern the nature of the creature and identify it as an illusion. Creatures with {@sense truesight}, {@sense tremorsense}, or {@sense blindsight} can identify the creature as an illusion upon sight.
If a creature has identified the Illusory Red Dragon as fake, they automatically succeed on saving throws against its Frightful Presence, and resist all damage it deals.

entries.name: Amarezen, The "Great"
entries: Once the dragon is defeated, the illusion dissipates into smoke and retreats into a magical Illusory Staff at the rear of the cavern. There, covered in sweat and carrying the staff, cowers Amron Thudrim.

Amron is no threat now the staff's magic has been depleted. Under questioning from the party, he will reveal he didn't wish to surrender his treasures, and so hired the help of orc mercenaries to stage the capture of his hoard by a red dragon. He played upon the local myths of Amarezen, the Great, and used some of the magical artifacts he stole across his life to simulate the presence of the mythical beast.

The party can do as they wish with Amron; his reputation lies in shatters once they reveal his plot to the world. They are free to keep the treasures they recovered from the crashed airship to themselves, and to oversee the delivery of the Ruby Dragon statue to its rightful home.
With Amron dealt with, his gold used to rebuild the devastated town of Fertilemound, and the return of the Ruby Dragon, the party are heralded as heroes across the land.

data.name: The Sea Queen's Tears
entries: If nautical nonsense be something you wish, this adventure be for ye! (And four level 4 adventurers).

entries.name: Premise
entries: The renowned elven bard Aria Nightingale has long sought a powerful artefact, the Sea Queen's Tears. It is a beautiful sapphire necklace, once belonging to Aria's great grandmother, who took it on the maiden voyage of the galleon Leviathan's Fury. Tragically, the vessel vanished in a terrible storm. All souls on board were believed forever claimed by the icy deep, along with the necklace, and no shipwreck was ever found. However, after decades of searching, Aria claims to know the location of the galleon wreck on the ocean floor, and has offered to take the party to the ship. They will be allowed to keep all they can plunder from the sunken vessel, as long as they retrieve the Sea Queen's Tears for Aria.

entries.name: The Voyage
entries: The adventure begins with the adventurers boarding Aria's private yacht, Songbird, and making their way into the open ocean. The journey to Leviathan's Fury is long, and the party will need to make themselves useful aboard Songbird to ensure the trip goes smoothly. For each job the party succeeds at, they gain 1 point of favour with Aria:

items: One party member must act as a lookout. Over the course of the voyage, they must make a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to guide Songbird out of the path of an oncoming storm. On a successful check, they gain 1 point of favour.

One party member must act as a gunner. Over the course of the voyage, they must make five attack rolls with the ship's mounted harpoon to spear fish for the crew to eat. The mounted harpoon is a ranged, martial weapon that uses Dexterity for attack rolls. A player who scores an attack roll of 13 or above successfully spears a fish. Spearing 3 or more fish earns the player 1 point of favour.

One party member must act as sailing master. Over the course of the voyage, they must make a {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to handle the heavy mast and ensure the sails are catching the wind. On a successful check, they gain 1 point of favour.

One party member must act as navigator. Over the course of the voyage, they must make a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to guide Songbird to the coordinates of the sunken Leviathan's Fury as swiftly as possible. On a successful check, they gain 1 point of favour.

entries: Upon reaching the coordinates of Leviathan's Fury, Aria brings Songbird to a halt. She then offers gifts to the party to aid them in their search below the waters. Depending on how many party members earned her favour, she may offer additional gifts, as shown in the table below:

rows: A {@item Potion of Water Breathing||Potion of 24 Hour Water Breathing} for each member of the party.
A {@spell Darkvision||Potion of 24 Hour Darkvision} for each member of the party.

entries.name: The Descent
entries: Songbird is equipped with a diving bell that will lower the party into the depths of the sea. The diving bell will remain where it lands on the ocean floor until a button is pushed inside which will lift the bell back to the surface. When the party is ready, they can step into the diving bell and be lowered into the ocean. The descent takes 1 hour.

A lurching bump signals the party has reached the ocean bed. They step out into total darkness; no light from the sun touches this landscape of eternal, freezing night. Creatures with {@sense darkvision} are greeted by a rocky, alien landscape of bizarre, twisting plants and perforated rock ({@adventure Map 1|TheSeaQueensTears|1|Adventure Map 1}).

Immediately upon stepping from the diving bell, the party hears a rush of water approaching them. A {@creature Spectral Killer Whale|DMSecretWeapon} barrels into the diving bell, almost knocking it over, and lunges at the party. It is joined by a number of {@creature Giant Octopus||Giant Octopuses} equal to half the total players in the party (rounded down).
Roll Initiative.

Upon falling to 0 hit points, the Spectral Killer Whale bursts into blinding, green light. Any remaining Giant Octopuses scatter, and the glow of the departing whale spirit illuminates the sea bed for a clean mile. By this light, at a distance of no less than 500 metres, the party see a rotting ship's carcass: Leviathan's Fury. The light slowly fades over the course of the next minute.

entries.name: Inside The Leviathan
entries: Upon reaching the vessel ({@adventure Map 2|TheSeaQueensTears|1|Adventure Map 2}), the party find the words Leviathan's Fury proudly displayed on the ancient, ruined hull. Exploring the wreck of the ship is challenging for those without {@sense darkvision}; players who can see can attempt a {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to uncover any objects. While exploring the inside of the ship, use {@adventure Map 3|TheSeaQueensTears|1|Adventure Map 3}.

No matter the result of the players' Investigation check, they find 3,000 gold pieces worth of gems and gold. On a successful check they also find a {@item Cloak of the Manta Ray} and a {@item Folding Boat}. On an unsuccessful check, they are ambushed by 2 {@creature Giant Octopus||Giant Octopuses}.
After exploring the inside of the ship, the party find no trace of The Sea Queen's Tears. No corpses or bones can be found either; some tattered remains of clothing are scattered across the ship.

entries.name: Kismet's Choice
entries: Upon completing their initial investigation and returning to the deck, the party feels a rumble deep inside the galleon. Slowly, the ship begins to glow with a sinister green light. It also begins to move, as if plucked from the ocean's bed by a curious giant, slowly rising from the sea bed ({@adventure Map 4|TheSeaQueensTears|1|Adventure Map 4}).

Players standing on the deck must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone} by the ship's sudden movement. At the same time, a figure emerges on the deck, appearing at first in the form of pure, green light, then solidifying into the shape of a towering, bearded merfolk.
The merfolk is well armed, but does not appear to be seeking a fight. The Sea Queen's Tears is strung about his neck. He addresses the party in a quiet, but rasping voice:
"Will You Please Listen?"

If the party chooses to listen to the merfolk, he will reveal himself to be {@creature Kismet|DMSecretWeapon}, captain of the Leviathan's Fury. He will explain that when the ship went down in the storm, there was a terrible scramble as passengers fought one another for the legendary Sea Queen's Tears, hoping its magic would save them. As friend, crewmate, and family turned on one another, he too fought to the death aboard the sinking ship, ultimately emerging victorious and taking the necklace for himself. He placed it about his neck as Leviathan's Fury slipped below the crushing waves and howling gale of the storm.

The Sea Queen's Tears has allowed him to exist on the ocean's floor with Leviathan's Fury. It has transformed him into a being able to thrive and hunt below the waters—a half-merfolk, half-spirit creature.

Kismet gave each crew member and passenger an honourable burial, and now roams the ocean floor, afraid to die alone in the dark, and forever bound to The Sea Queen's Tears about his neck. He is forever battling with shame and guilt for his failure as captain.

entries.name: Outcomes
entries: The party can reason with Kismet, leave him with the necklace, or attempt to kill him and take it.

items: If the party speak with Kismet and meet his tale with empathy and understanding, he may be persuaded to offer them the Sea Queen's Tears willingly. Convincing him to do so requires a {@dc 21} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. On a failed check, he will become enraged at the suggestion of willingly ending his existence and attack.
If the party leave Kismet alone, they can return to the diving bell and be hauled to the surface without The Sea Queen's Tears and without provoking combat.
If the party attempt to trick Kismet or attack him, he will fight to the death.

entries: If the party leave Kismet with the necklace they return to the surface with only the treasures they recovered from the ship. Kismet will slowly fade into the darkness once more, a forlorn longing on his face. Upon reaching the surface, the party are met with a bitterly disappointed Aria. The trip back to land is a quiet one, the party grimly carrying the knowledge of what happened aboard Leviathan's Fury, and the tale of one man's endless, lonely reward for surviving its destruction.

If the party persuade Kismet to depart to the afterlife willingly, or kill him and take the necklace, they return to the surface with the Sea Queen's Tears. Aria will take it from them greedily, and then thank them with heartfelt fervour. She will give each party member an additional 500 gold pieces, and return Songbird to the nearest port, eager to hear the tale of what occurred below.

data.name: Catch The Goblin!
entries: Catch The Goblin! is an adventure for a party of four level 1 player characters with moral choices and multiple endings.

entries.name: Premise
entries: For the past ten days the town of Denan has been plagued by a cunning goblin thief. Weapons, food, and magical potions have been stolen! The party has been hired by Denan's mayor, Finnegan Fubster, to capture the goblin and retrieve all the stolen items.

entries.name: The Town of Denan
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|CatchTheGoblin|1|Adventure Map 1}) Denan is a quaint and charming town divided in two by the Archon river. Three stores have been stolen from over the past ten days—The Apothecary, Fubster's Foods, and The Place Where You Can Buy Stuff To Murder People With.
Details of each store and its owner can be found in the following table. Should a party member attempt to haggle after returning a stolen item, they have Advantage on that Haggle Check.

items: {@item Potion of Healing} — 50 gp
{@item Potion of Speed} — 300 gp
{@item Alchemist's Fire (flask)||Alchemist's Fire} — 100 gp
{@item Acid (vial)||Vial of Acid} — 50 gp

entries: Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) ({@dc 15})
{@actSaveSuccess} 10% discount

rows: Finnegan Fubster, a halfling who is also the mayor of the town.

items: {@item Hunting Trap||Hunter's Trap} — 10 gp
{@item Rations (1 day)||10 Days Rations} — 5 gp
{@item Antitoxin (vial)||Antitoxin} — 10 gp
{@item Poison, Basic (vial)||Poison, Basic} — 30 gp

entries: Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) ({@dc 13})
{@actSaveSuccess} 10% discount

rows: The Place Where You Can Buy Stuff To Murder People With

items: {@item Spear} — 1 gp
{@item Dagger} — 2 gp
{@item Greatsword} — 50 gp
{@item Rapier} — 25 gp
{@item Longbow} — 50 gp
{@item Shield} — 200 gp
Silvered Weapon (any) — 100 gp
{@item +1 Ammunition} — 500 gp
{@item +1 Weapon} (any) — 1,000 gp

entries: Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) ({@dc 17})
{@actSaveSuccess} 10% discount

entries.name: Goblin Chase!
entries: Upon visiting the final store, have the party roll a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. On a success, they see a {@creature goblin} attempting to sneak out of the store holding several items and can immediately give chase. On a failed check, the goblin gets an additional 30-foot head start for the chase.
Roll Initiative.

The party are chasing a fleeing goblin through the streets of Denan. The goblin starts 30 feet ahead of them (60 feet if they failed the Perception check), goes first in initiative order, has an AC of 14, and moves 50 feet each turn by taking the {@action Dash} action using its bonus action.
Track how far away the goblin is from the nearest player at the end of each turn.

The goblin uses its action each turn to lay traps for the party. Narrate how the goblin knocks over carts of fruit and vegetables to clutter the road, weaves between carts and caravans causing traffic obstructions, and releases livestock from their pens as it sprints through the bustling town.
If the fleeing goblin is hit by an attack roll, its speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

Each party member takes their turn in initiative. Players can take the {@action Dash} action, cast spells, make ranged attacks, or use any other means at their disposal to attempt to catch the goblin. A player who chases the goblin through the streets must succeed on a {@dc 9} Dexterity saving throw at the start of their turn to avoid falling amidst the chaos the goblin leaves behind. A player who falls must use half their movement speed to stand back up.
After three rounds, if the goblin is not caught, it vanishes below ground via a manhole cover. If this happens, proceed to {@adventure 2.1 Into The Nest|CatchTheGoblin|0|Into the Nest}.
If the party catch up to the goblin, it is captured. If this happens, proceed to {@adventure 1.3 Gottem!|CatchTheGoblin|0|Gottem!}.

entries.name: Gottem!
entries: The captured goblin wails and wriggles desperately, but to no avail.
"No hurt Crook! Crook mean no harm! Let Crook go home!"
The goblin's name is Crook. He speaks in an aggravating voice and will explain that he must return to his nest to feed his family.

A party member can attempt a {@dc 11} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check to uncover information on the stolen goods. On a successful check, Crook will confess the stolen goods are hidden at his nest. On a fail, he will refuse to answer the question, playing dumb.
If the party chooses to allow Crook to go to his family, they can follow him to his nest.
If they return Crook to Finnegan, Crook will be held in the town jail, and Finnegan will request the party investigate the goblin nest to retrieve the stolen goods.

entries.name: Into the Nest
entries: ({@adventure Map 2|CatchTheGoblin|1|Adventure Map 2})

Crook's Nest is below a manhole cover on the outskirts of the city. It is a dank and smelly cavern, little more than a mossy hole in the ground. Inside, there are 4 {@creature Goblin Soldier|DMSecretWeapon|goblin soldiers}, 1 {@creature Goblin Shaman|DMSecretWeapon|goblin shaman}, and at least twelve infant goblins.
If the party is accompanied by Crook, they can enter safely.

If they enter alone, they can attempt a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check (at least half the party must pass for a success) to reach the nest unnoticed. On a failed check, the goblin soldiers will spot them and attempt to arrest them for trespassing.
Should the party choose to question the goblins, proceed to {@adventure 2.2 Goblin Tales|CatchTheGoblin|0|Goblin Tales}.
Should the party choose to start a fight, proceed to {@adventure 2.3 Goblin Horde|CatchTheGoblin|0|Goblin Horde}.

entries.name: Goblin Tales
entries: The party have made themselves known to the goblins in their nest. A {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check will convince them to return the stolen goods to the party without resistance. Alternatively, a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check made while at the nest will allow a player to spot the stolen potion and {@item +1 shortsword}, which can then be stolen back from the goblins with a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check.

If questioned about their presence, the goblins will explain that they needed to find a new nest after being thrown out of their old one in the mountains by a chromatic dragon wyrmling. Crook has been stealing food to keep them alive, while also stealing weapons and potions to arm himself and attempt to slay the dragon and reclaim their land. Two goblins, Crook's sister and father, have already died attempting to drive off the wyrmling.

If the party returns to the surface, they can turn over the goblins to Finnegan who will have them removed from the town by force. The burglaries come to an end, and the grateful merchants hail the party as heroes.

Alternatively, the players can offer to deal with the dragon for the goblins personally. If they do so, the goblins will gladly offer them the {@item Potion of Speed} and the {@item +1 Shortsword} to aid them in the upcoming battle. Proceed to {@adventure 3.1 Draconic Encounter|CatchTheGoblin|0|Draconic Encounter}.

entries.name: Goblin Horde
entries: The party are fighting the goblins in their nest below the town of Denan. Immediately when combat starts, one of the {@creature Goblin Soldier|DMSecretWeapon|Goblin Soldiers} will usher the children away, out through a secret tunnel and into the wilderness.

The party are fighting 3 {@creature Goblin Soldier|DMSecretWeapon|goblin soldiers} and 1 {@creature Goblin Shaman|DMSecretWeapon|goblin shaman}. If Crook is present and the party have been neutral or unkind to him, he will fight on the goblins' side.
If the party have been kind to Crook, he will attempt to defuse the situation. If the party ignore him and initiate combat anyway, he will ruefully fight on the goblins' side.
Roll Initiative.
Upon defeating the goblins, the party can search the nest to recover the stolen items. A small amount of food has been eaten, but otherwise everything is free to be returned to its rightful owners.
With the nest destroyed and the goblin soldiers killed or imprisoned by the party, the burglaries come to an end, and the grateful merchants hail the party as heroes.
The End.

entries.name: Draconic Encounter
entries: {@adventure Map 3|CatchTheGoblin|1|Adventure Map 3}
The wyrmling has settled in the old goblin nest in the mountains north of Denan. The goblins will give the party instructions on how to reach it.

The nest is in a crag on the west face of the mountain. There are many boulders, crevices, and tight corners to hide behind. Should the party wish to lay a trap, allow them to do so and narrate how they might ambush the dragon. If their plot is reasonable, they can initiate combat and {@condition surprised||surprise} the wyrmling, meaning it will take no actions on its first turn in combat.
If the party brazenly rolls into the nest without caution the dragon spots them and roars.
Roll Initiative.

Upon defeating the wyrmling, the goblins can return to their old stomping ground. With plenty of food and space in the mountain, they have no need to steal from Denan. Both the goblins and the merchants of the town hail the party as heroes, and allow them to keep any of the goblins' stolen goods as a reward for their good deeds.
The End.

data.name: The Dunedien Dungeon
entries: The Dunedien Dungeon is a challenging adventure of exploration, puzzles, mystery, and combat for a party of four level 7 adventurers.

entries.name: Running the Adventure
entries: The Dunedien Dungeon is a ruined, ancient temple buried beneath desert sands. Players will explore the dungeon across the adventure, encountering various puzzles, monsters, and key items.

A "GM Version" of each map can be found in the {@adventure Map Pack|TheDunedienDungeon|1}. These GM Maps are labelled with figures which correlate to objects, encounters, and puzzles referenced across the adventure. When an object, encounter, or puzzle is referenced in the text, you can refer to the GM Maps to see where it appears physically in the dungeon.

The adventure also challenges players to identify missing adventurers from their corpses strewn throughout the dungeon. The list of missing adventurers can be found in {@adventure 1.2 Ol' Man Glumpkin|TheDunedienDungeon|0|Ol' Man Glumpkin}. At the end of the adventure, ask the party to list the identity of the dead bodies they found and how each one died. The more corpses they find and identify correctly, the more gold they will receive as a reward.
{@b It is recommended you read through this adventure at least once in full before running it for your players.}

entries.name: The Dunedien Dungeon
entries: Ancient songs tell of rivers of gold that crisscross and spiral like veins beneath the desert sands of Dunedien. Many a foolhardy adventurer has wandered into the maw of the desert in pursuit of these riches. None have returned, until now.

A small party of adventurers uncovered a ruin in the desert; an ancient well that acts as a gateway to beneath the desert. Word swiftly spread of the vast riches they found there. Unfortunately, they have not returned from their latest expedition below the sands. The party have been hired to descend into the well and explore the dungeon that lies below Dunedien, and uncover the mystery that lies in wait.

entries.name: Ol' Man Glumpkin
entries: At the outskirts of the ruin the party meet Ol' Man Glumpkin, an eccentric Cleric blessed with unorthodox magic. He has the power to call spirits back from beyond the grave, but only if he knows their true identity and exact cause of death. If the lost adventurers are indeed dead, finding and correctly identifying each corpse and their cause of death will allow Ol' Man Glumpkin to commune with their spirits, and reveal the location of their lost gold.
There are 6 members of the lost adventuring party, presumed dead:

entries.name: Dunedien Level -1: The Antechamber Doors
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|TheDunedienDungeon|1|Adventure Map 1})

The first floor of the Dunedien Dungeon is an arid and stifling antechamber. Ever-burning torches eternally wash the floor and walls in dim light. The party enter by the descending staircase in the center of the room (Fig. 1).
Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 are shining, golden doors. They are identical. Inscribed above each door are the following words:
If a spellcaster dares, place your hands upon this door, and offer a tribute of magic.
If a warrior dares, place your hands upon this door, and offer a tribute of blood.

If a creature with the Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature places their hands on the door, have them roll {@dice 1d6+1}. They lose spell slots of a combined level equal to the result on the dice, and the door swings open. If they do not have sufficient unspent spell slots to offer, nothing happens.
If a creature without the Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature places their hands on the door, have them roll {@dice 6d6}. They take Necrotic damage equal to the result, and the door swings open.

entries.name: Dunedien Level -1: The Golden Golem
entries: In the room immediately behind the open door waits a {@creature Golden Golem|DMSecretWeapon}, which attacks immediately. It is magically bound to this room, and cannot leave of its own accord.

If the party opened the antechamber door with an offer of spell slots, the golem gains its Spellcasting trait. If the party opened the antechamber door with an offer of blood, the golem gains its Necrotic Blows trait.
Roll initiative.

If the party destroys the golem, the character who offered a tribute of magic or blood to the door regains a number of spell slots equal to the level they sacrificed to enter, or gains a number of temporary hit points equal to the Necrotic damage they took to enter.

entries.name: Golem's Room Corpse
entries: In the golem room there is also an adventurer's corpse. Its body has been totally crushed; beside it lies a small, bloody rock and pristine {@item hide armor|PHB|hide armour}. The armour appears undamaged. The corpse lies next to a tiny crack in the right-hand wall of the chamber.

{@b GM Note.} This is the corpse of Loveday, the Druid. She was crushed while in her wild shape by the thrown rock after sneaking into the chamber through the tiny crack in the wall. In death, she reverted back to her humanoid form, her armour de-merging from her crushed form.
Beyond the antechamber door and the golem room, the passageway leads to a stairwell that descends deeper into the dungeon. Beside this stairwell is an open, plundered treasure chest (Fig. 4).

entries.name: Spike Trap Corpse
entries: Beside the open treasure chest is an exposed spiked pitfall trap; an adventurer's corpse lies within. The gold-tipped spikes drip with a visible, green poison, and have penetrated the corpse's heavy armour and helmet.
{@b GM Note.} This is the corpse of Kenrith, the Paladin.

A player can attempt a {@dc 11} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check to harvest one vial of poison from one of the spikes of the open pitfall trap. The poison can be applied to a weapon or piece of ammunition as a bonus action. Once applied, the first time that weapon or piece of ammunition hits a creature or an object within the next minute, it deals an additional {@damage 2d8} Poison damage.

entries.name: Dunedien Level -2: The Grand Tomb's Prismatic Door
entries: {@adventure Map 2|TheDunedienDungeon|1|Adventure Map 2}
Descending the stairwell leads the party to a cool, clammy room. There is a barred iron door ahead (Fig. 7). There are two lanterns either side of the door which are unlit.
The door bears the following inscription:
Complete The Prismatic Lock To Move Forward

The room splits into six small chambers, each housing a shrine (Fig. 1–Fig. 6). Each shrine radiates a different colour of light in a 10-foot radius. A creature that steps into the light of a shrine must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or suffer a negative effect, as shown in the Prismatic Shrines table below. A creature that succeeds this saving throw is aware of the effect that they avoided.

entries.name: Yellow Shrine Corpse
entries: In the Yellow Shrine room (Fig. 3) there is an adventurer's corpse. It is wearing no armour, and its flesh has been blackened and charred. Its robes, however, appear undamaged. Beside it lies a book, which bears a curious, magically shifting script that requires a {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check to decipher.

{@b GM Note.} This is the corpse of Samag, the Wizard, who died as a result of the Lightning damage from the yellow shrine. The severe electrical energy that burned through her body has charred her corpse beyond recognition.

A {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals the book beside the corpse to be a wizard's spellbook. Almost all of its pages have been destroyed; only one page at the far end remains intact: it details the effects and behaviour of the 9th level spell {@spell prismatic wall}.

{@b Opening the Door.} The door lanterns must be lit to complete the prismatic seal. The only missing colour is green, which relates to Poison damage (as per the spell {@spell prismatic wall}). Dealing any amount of Poison damage to the lanterns either side of the door will cause them to light, and the iron doors will melt into nothingness.
{@b GM Note:} The party will be aware that poison can be recovered from the poison spike trap on the floor above.

entries.name: Dunedien Level -2: The Grand Tomb
entries: Beyond the Prismatic Door sits an {@creature Abyssphinx|DMSecretWeapon|abyssphinx}; a mighty, cruel monstrosity (Fig. 8). As the party approach, it speaks in a hissing, arrogant whisper:
I can race, but not run,
I can break without tearing,
You have only one,
But you hope for a pairing.
I can beat, I can thump,
But can't punch or pummel,
I can skip, but not jump,
And if I stop you're in trouble.
{@b GM Note:} The answer to this riddle is heart.

The abyssphinx will wait for an answer while the party discuss the riddle amongst themselves, and will repeat the riddle if asked. It will say nothing more. If the players fail to answer the riddle correctly or attack, the abyssphinx will attack them.
If the players correctly answer the riddle, or destroy the abyssphinx, a paving slab at the center of the chamber will open, revealing a path down to the depths of the dungeon.

entries.name: Grand Tomb Corpse
entries: In the room to the right of the Grand Tomb there is an adventurer's corpse (Fig. 9). A cruel slash of claws has torn the torso almost in two. The corpse is wearing no armour. A character that succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will discover that the knuckles on the corpse's hand appear dusted with gold, identical in colour to the Gold Golem on the floor above.

{@b GM Note.} This is the corpse of Knel, the Monk, who died at the hands of the Abyssphinx. The gold on his knuckles is residue from attacks he made against the Golem on the higher floor of the dungeon.

entries.name: Dunedien Level -3: Road to the Golden River
entries: {@adventure Map 3|TheDunedienDungeon|1|Adventure Map 3}

The 3rd floor of the Dunedien Dungeon is wet and sweltering. A sickly sweet, powerful aroma wafts through the earthy tunnels, tinged with a sharp metallic edge that seems to burrow through the nose and mouth and linger on the tongue. Golden webbing is strewn about the tunnels, exuding natural light.

The webbing looks flexible, but is in fact hard as steel. It requires a {@dc 22} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to break. Alternatively, dealing 15 points of Acid damage to it will cause the webbing within 5 ft. of that point to melt.
The party enter the floor via a 10-foot drop from the room above, landing at the bottom of the map (Fig. 1).

entries.name: Headless Corpse
entries: At Fig. 2 lies an adventurer's corpse. Its head is missing. The body wears light armour, and by its side are a wizard's scrying gem, a golden locket bearing a holy sigil, three {@item Vial of Biting Acid|DMSecretWeapon|Vials of Biting Acid}, and a {@item +1 Dagger||+1 mythril dagger}.
{@b GM Note.} This is the corpse of Helena, the Rogue, who pilfered some trinkets from her fallen allies.

entries.name: Golden Statue
entries: At Fig. 3 stands a spectacular, life size statue of a roaring barbarian; it is rendered in stunning detail seemingly from pure gold.
{@b GM Note.} This is the corpse of Beau, the Barbarian, killed by a Goldwyrm's Vomiting Greed attack.

At Fig. 4 there is a hole in the earth, which leads to a running river of molten gold. The heat from the river is unbearable, causing the air above it to shimmer and dance. The moment the party peer into the hole, a {@creature Goldwyrm|DMSecretWeapon} bursts from the molten river with a terrifying shriek and attacks.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Epilogue
entries: Upon defeating the goldwyrm, the party are free to return to the surface. There they will find Ol' Man Glumpkin awaiting them. For every corpse they successfully identify, a spirit will ascend from the desert sands and leave a gift of 2,000 gold pieces.

With the grim fate of the previous adventurers in mind, and a first-hand knowledge of the monsters that lurk beneath the desert, the question of what is to be done now lies with the party. Should they pursue more adventures below Dunedien in search of greater treasures? Or turn their back on the deadly pursuit of gold, and drown this ancient dungeon in sand, along with all the dangers that dwell within?

data.name: The Watchtower Descent
entries: The Watchtower Descent is a challenging adventure of combat, puzzles, curses, and treasure for a party of four level 8 player characters.

entries.name: The Watchtower
entries: The Watchtower sits at the edge of the Shimmering Veil, a magical fortress built aeons ago to observe the infinite planes of the multiverse and guard against those who would cross the boundaries into this one. The magic here is ancient and weighty, and the dangers mysterious and bizarre. The Watchtower has long since been abandoned, but rumours still swirl of treasure lying unclaimed within, guarded by an unknown and ancient force. Only the most brazen and foolish adventurers would ever dare to plunder such a place, and yet that is the task the party have set themselves.

entries.name: GM Note
entries: The treasure offered at the end of this dungeon is only a suggestion—feel free to adapt the reward to suit your players' backstories and integrate this adventure into a longer campaign. For example, the treasure might take the form of an antidote to an ancient curse tormenting a family member, or a magical signet that will solidify an allied warchief's claim to the throne.

entries.name: Cliffs of the Veil
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheWatchtowerDescent|1|Adventure Map 1}

The entrance to The Watchtower sits at the apex of the Cliffs of the Veil. Arriving at the peak, the party find a cracked, stone doorway wreathed in flame. A {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will reveal the gateway to be dangerous and magical. Only upon dousing the flames can the doorway be passed. A creature that attempts to move through the doorway while it is ignited takes {@damage 4d10} Fire damage, and is pushed backwards 10 feet.
As the party approach the doorway, read the following aloud:

As you approach the doorway, you feel a swirling gust of icy magic tear over the crumbling stone pathway at your feet. Four creatures, as pitch black as a starless night sky, materialise before you, blocking the path to the door. The shadow creatures move toward you with a sinister hiss, their icy magical aura extinguishing the flames on the torches that burn beside the gateway as they pass by.
The party are fighting 4 {@creature Voidling|DMSecretWeapon|voidlings}. Roll Initiative.

If a voidling is pushed into the flaming gateway, it takes {@damage 4d10} Fire damage and the flames within the door diminish. Each subsequent voidling that touches the flames takes {@damage 1d10} less damage than the last, until the flames are fully quelled. Pushing the corpse of a voidling into the flames has the same effect.
Once the flames of the gateway are quenched, the party can pass through the door safely to enter The Watchtower. Any surviving voidlings will not follow.

entries.name: The Stairwell
entries: {@adventure Map 2|TheWatchtowerDescent|1|Adventure Map 2}

Passing through the Veil door transports the party to The Stairwell, the long, winding, vertical descent to the heart of The Watchtower. The walls are lined with endless faces—the faces of those foolish enough to enter uninvited.
As soon as the party begin descending the stairs, each face in the room speaks simultaneously in screeching, deafening unison:
"BODY, MIND, HEART, OR SOUL?"

The question echoes endlessly inside the tight, vertical chamber. Each character is {@condition incapacitated} and cannot move; they must each answer with one of the four choices before they can regain control of themselves. The outcome of this trap depends on the answer they offer, and if they pass a {@dc 15} saving throw.

items.name: BODY
items.entry: The character must make a Constitution saving throw as painful, sapping energy courses through their being. On a failed save, a creature's hit point maximum is halved until they leave The Watchtower.

items.name: MIND
items.entry: The character must make an Intelligence saving throw as a stabbing, needling pain bursts in their skull. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 3d10} Psychic damage and is cursed until they leave The Watchtower. While cursed, whenever the creature casts a spell using a spell slot or pact magic slot, they take {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage for each level of the spell slot they expend.

items.name: HEART
items.entry: The character must make a Wisdom saving throw as deadening, numbing chill grasps at their insides. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 3d10} Necrotic damage and is cursed until they leave The Watchtower. Roll {@dice 1d4}. While cursed, the creature subtracts the result from every attack roll and saving throw they make.

items.name: SOUL
items.entry: The character must make a Charisma saving throw as blistering, stinging fire writhes through their body. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 3d10} Force damage and is cursed until they leave The Watchtower. While cursed, the creature loses one racial trait of the GM's choosing. For example, a dragonborn may lose their ability to use their Dragon's Breath, a variant human might lose their feat, or a gnoll might lose their Rampage trait. The GM should choose carefully to ensure this loss doesn't render a character completely unplayable.

entries: Once the party have given an answer and made their saving throws, they are free to continue the descent. At the bottom of The Stairwell, they can pass into the lower chambers of The Watchtower.

entries.name: The Gravity Chamber
entries: {@adventure Map 3|TheWatchtowerDescent|1|Adventure Map 3}

To step into the Gravity Chamber is to be met with a sickening, lurching sensation, as if being plunged into churning water. In this magical demiplane, the familiar laws of time and space do not apply. Although eerily tranquil and stunningly beautiful, the Gravity Chamber is a lethal trap.
The players enter the chamber through the green doorway at the bottom left of the map.

In this room, gravity is flighty and changeable. Players can move freely in three dimensions even without a flying speed. There is a glyph on each of the four walls in the chamber, forming the letters N, E, S, and W. These letters represent the directions of a compass.

entries.name: Surviving the Gravity Chamber
entries: Upon entering the Gravity Chamber, have the players roll initiative.

On initiative count 20 and 10 one of the glyphs will activate, changing the direction of the gravity in the room. Immediately, when the gravity shifts, all players fall 40 feet in that direction. The same glyph cannot activate twice in a row.
If a player falls off the map, they take {@damage 3d8} Force damage and reappear through the last doorway they entered.
The glyphs are sentient, and aim to kill the party by causing them to fall off the map, and keep them away from the exit door in the north-west quadrant of the map.
The glyphs each have 100 hit points, and an AC of 18. Hitting a glyph with an attack roll causes it to activate, changing the direction of gravity in the chamber.
To escape the room, players must exit through the green door directly opposite the door they entered, in the north-west quadrant of the map.
If a player uses their movement on their turn to move in any direction other than the direction gravity is currently flowing, they must expend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot they move.

The green door close to the centre of the chamber is a broken gateway. A creature can identify that it is malfunctioning with a {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. Any creature that enters it is teleported 60 feet in a random direction.
A creature that passes through the exit door in the north-western quadrant of the map is teleported to the Watchtower Base.

entries.name: The Watchtower Treasure
entries: {@adventure Map 4|TheWatchtowerDescent|1|Adventure Map 4}

The party fall out of The Gravity Chamber, landing in the shadow of a colossal {@creature Fossilised Angel|DMSecretWeapon}. The Gravity Chamber is behind them—the seemingly infinite demiplane now the size of a simple crate.
At the heart of the Fossilised Angel lies a gaping maw, stretched open. Within it is a simple treasure chest.
A creature that places its hand on the treasure chest is enveloped in blinding, silver light, which swiftly spreads to each party member. A deep, powerful voice speaks telepathically:
"BODY, MIND, HEART, OR SOUL?"

Each character is {@condition incapacitated} and cannot move; they must each answer with one of the four choices before they can regain control of themselves. The treasure they will receive depends on the answer they offer.

items.name: BODY
items.entry: The character gains the {@feat Survivor|DMSecretWeapon} feat.

items.name: MIND
items.entry: The character gains three 1st level spell slots, which recharge upon finishing a long rest. The character also gains the Furious Smite feature: when they hit a creature with an attack roll, they can expend one spell slot to deal {@damage 2d8} Radiant damage to that creature, in addition to the attack's usual damage.

items.name: HEART
items.entry: The character can add their proficiency bonus to saving throws using one ability of their choice, which they choose immediately (for example, Wisdom saving throws).

items.name: SOUL
items.entry: The character learns the spells {@spell disguise self}, {@spell alter self}, and {@spell polymorph}. They can cast each spell, targeting themselves only, once per long rest without expending a spell slot. They can also cast each spell with any spell slots they might have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is the spellcasting modifier they use for these spells.

entries.name: The Watchtower Guardian
entries: Immediately upon receiving their treasure, the angel lets loose a terrible, earthy roar. The gust of wind echoing out from its core pushes any creatures currently inside its mouth 40 feet back, where they land {@condition prone} in the center of the map.
The colossal guardian lifts its many arms to the heavens, and prepares to smite the party.
Roll initiative.

Upon reducing the {@creature Fossilised Angel|DMSecretWeapon|fossilised angel} to 0 hit points, it returns to its dormant state, and the doorway at its base opens. The party can now ascend The Watchtower safely and return to the corporeal world with their plundered treasures in tow.

data.name: Plants Vs. Zombies: A D&D Adventure
entries: Plants Vs. Zombies: A D&D Adventure is a one-shot for a party of four level 2 characters, featuring a mix of puzzles and combat.

entries.name: Welcome to Rattock
entries: The gentle farming village of Rattock is known for its fine artisanal cheese, breathtaking nature hikes, and zombies.

Zombies are a way of life in Rattock, standing proud as equals in society. Thanks to the magic of Zimboom, the local Wizard, an enchantment placed over the village renders all undead good-natured and free from their innate urge to feast on flesh. In Rattock, zombies have jobs, families, and sports teams. Unfortunately, however, something has gone wrong.

A zombie, Brian, has gone missing, lost in the Deep Woods beside the village. Outside the influence of Zimboom's magic, Brian's murderous instincts will soon return. And if there's one thing bad for a village's reputation, it's letting a flesh-eating zombie loose on the neighboring towns.
The adventure begins in Rattock ({@adventure Map 1|PlantsVsZombiesADDAdventure|2|Adventure Map 1}), where Zimboom meets the party and explains their mission.

items: The party must venture into the Deep Woods to retrieve the missing zombie, Brian.
The Deep Woods are known for their beautiful plants, some of which are potentially dangerous, so caution is advised.
Brian has a habit of losing limbs; the party should keep an eye out for any missing hands, feet, fingers, etc. that he may have dropped along the way.

If the party cannot find Brian and return within 24 hours, the magic of Rattock will leave him and he will regress into a normal zombie. Should this happen, they have to kill Brian, and will receive no payment.
Zimboom is willing to pay a 500 gp reward for the successful delivery of Brian the zombie within the next 24 hours.

entries: Alongside this information, Zimboom hands each character a vial of {@item Alchemist's Fire (flask)||Alchemist's Fire} and a {@item potion of healing}, and points them in the direction of the Deep Woods. The adventure has begun!

entries.name: The Deep Woods
entries: The deep woods are aptly named. The air is heavy with moisture, the verdant pathway springy underfoot, and the towering trees shelter the floor in dim light, even at the height of day.

Upon entering the forest, a player who succeeds on a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check can identify the tracks of a lumbering, humanoid figure that has passed through the area.

Following these tracks puts the party directly on Brian's trail, leading them through a meadow of {@spell goodberry||goodberries}. Though most of the berries have been scavenged by local wildlife, each player is able to harvest four berries each. A goodberry can be eaten, or fed to an ally, as an action, and restores 1 hit point when consumed. Brian's trail then leads into an open clearing...
Should the players fail to pick up on Brian's trail immediately, they instead stumble around the forest aimlessly for a time, before reaching an open clearing...

entries.name: The Plant Traps
entries: {@adventure Map 2|PlantsVsZombiesADDAdventure|2|Adventure Map 2}

In the clearing is a pleasant, hazy scent, like that of warm butter and honey. There are four beautiful, closed pods in the clearing, each roughly the size of a person and surrounded by flowers and vines. While inactive, the plant pods are resistant to all damage and appear non-magical.

Upon entering the clearing, each player must make a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw. Characters that cannot smell or who are resistant to the {@condition Charmed} or {@condition Poisoned} conditions have Advantage on this saving throw. On a failed save, a character hears a noise coming from inside the closed plant pods. It sounds like a scratching, as if a creature inside is attempting to escape.

Moving within 5 feet of a plant pod causes it to spring to life. The vines on the forest floor immediately animate, attempting to seize that creature, and each pod splits open to reveal a gaping maw of bubbling acid hungrily snapping open and shut. The triggering creature must succeed on a {@dc 12} Strength saving throw or be {@condition grappled}. At the same time, each other pod bursts to life. Roll Initiative.
The party is fighting four {@creature Plant Pod|DMSecretWeapon|plant pods}.

Upon defeating the final plant pod, it withers away to nothing, leaving behind a grim gift. The arm of a zombie, burned by the acid of the plant pod but not yet digested, flops out of the dying flora. It seems Brian ran afoul of these plants and lost a limb.
Brian's tracks continue deeper into the woods, leading to an old, ruined temple.

entries.name: The Temple Floor
entries: This temple contains two rooms: a guarded antechamber and The Divine Room, a sacred place where purified, holy water nurtures beautiful, ancient wildflowers.

The first room is protected by a floor puzzle. This is {@adventure The Rook's Impasse|PlantsVsZombiesADDAdventure|1|The Rook's Impasse}. Refer to the appendix for the rules and map of this puzzle, which will stop the party from crossing the checkered floor unless they move as a Knight would in chess.

entries.name: Briiiiaaaaaaan
entries: {@adventure Map 3|PlantsVsZombiesADDAdventure|2|Adventure Map 3}

After passing the enchanted floor of the antechamber, the party moves into The Divine Room. Here, the architecture is beautifully integrated into the forest. Here, also, is Brian, standing aimlessly in the pool of {@item Holy Water (flask)||Holy Water} at the center. Upon hearing the party approach, he turns, and his face cracks into a broad, gormless smile. He raises his shoulder as if to wave hello, a gesture rendered ineffective by his lack of an arm. He then calls out, but rather than the common speech known by the zombies of Rattock, he can only manage a low rumble.
"Briiiiaaaaaaan"
It seems the magic of Rattock is already wearing thin.
Any attempt to question Brian is met with the same, groaning response. It seems all he can do is repeat his own name. Still, Brian has been found, and the party is free to take him home.

However, there is a new problem. The wound from Brian's missing arm is gently trickling blood into the Holy Water below. This is the water that feeds the ancient wildflowers that grow throughout the temple.

As soon as the players make a move towards Brian, a shrill rustling noise writhes and skitters throughout the temple. The flowers about the room begin shaking violently, their leaves staining blood red. From the depths of the chamber a gurgling, alien hiss echoes forth, and a lumbering {@creature Necrotic Shrub|DMSecretWeapon} lunges towards the party—its blood red flowers glistening, its fierce thorns hungry for flesh.
Roll Initiative.

entries.name: Back to Rattock
entries: Upon defeating the Necrotic Shrub, the party is free to take Brian home. Zimboom meets them delightedly, and listens with great interest as they speak of their adventure, and the effect of Brian's blood on the plants of the forest.

Although troubled by the effect Brian had on the forest, Zimboom is relieved at his safe return. He gives the party their promised 500 gold pieces, and assures them no zombie will ever again escape the borders of Rattock. He then hastily begins work sewing Brian's arm back on, and scolds him gently for wandering too far from the village.
For now, it seems all is well, but time will soon tell if the ramifications of Brian's escape, and the necrotic blood that seeped into the forest, have yet to be fully revealed...

data.name: The King's Puzzles
entries: Below are two chess-themed puzzles for your players (although I recommend not telling them they're chess themed before presenting them. It somewhat gives the game away).

The first is a traditional riddle, perhaps one that needs answering before the players can pass through a guarded door or sealed chest. The second is a floor puzzle, best used as a non-combat encounter to challenge players' wits as they navigate a dungeon.

entries.name: Riddle of the Kings

entries: A battlefield of warring armies,
Equal in stature, talents, and might,
Alike as reflections, one-to-one,
But as apart as darkness is to light,
Where holy men draw swords and battle,
With steeds by side and men ahead,
A battlefield of death and glory,
Where not a drop of blood is shed.
Where are we?
{@b Answer:} A chessboard

entries.name: The Rook's Impasse
entries: Rook's Impasse is a simple dungeon floor puzzle. The tiles on the ground are coloured black and white in a 6x8 grid. Players must move from one side to the other. You can use the map below to represent this puzzle.
Scrawled on an archway on the far side of the floor are the following words:
Move Onward With Chivalry

There are also two 8 ft. tall stone statues of birds on the grid. The two birds start in the far left and far right corner respectively. A player who succeeds on a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check will know the birds to be rooks.
{@b The rules:}

items: Players roll initiative, and take their turns moving across the grid.
A player must move in an "L" shape, like a Knight in chess (two squares vertically, one square horizontally, or two squares horizontally, one square vertically).

If a character moves in any other fashion, or exceeds the movement of a knight on their turn, a furious gust of magical wind barrels into them. Roll {@dice 1d6}. The character is pushed backwards a number of tiles equal to the result, and takes Bludgeoning damage equal to twice their character level.
The rooks move on initiative count 0. They move as a rook does in chess (any number of squares horizontally, or any number of squares vertically).
The rooks aim to move onto squares occupied by a character. If they do, that character takes Bludgeoning damage equal to twice their character level and is teleported back to the start of the puzzle.

If a player moves as a knight, and lands on a square occupied by a rook, they make a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. On a success, the rook is destroyed. On a fail, they are pushed diagonally backwards to the nearest unoccupied square on the grid.
The puzzle is complete when all players have successfully made it to the other side of the grid.

entries: {@b Optional rules:}

items: An extremely powerful gravity enchantment lingers over the magical floor.
Clerics and paladins only are allowed to move any number of squares diagonally across the grid in a straight line on their turn without punishment, rather than moving as a knight.
A player Wild Shaped or otherwise transformed into a horse can move across the grid in any fashion without punishment.

data.name: Night of the Living Bones
entries: An adventure for 4–5 5th-level characters.
{@b Content Warnings:} Mind Control, Necromancy

entries.name: Synopsis
entries: Field researchers at the University of Brightbarrow have just unearthed the discovery of the century: the most complete ancient dragon skeleton known to humanity. For days the scientists have been carefully moving the bones into carts so the skeleton can be transported to a research facility, but droves of kobolds keep mounting attacks while they work. To make matters worse, every night someone—or something—places the packaged bones back in the dirt, undoing all the work of the previous day.

What the researchers don't know is that this ancient dragon was once a powerful necromancer named Necrux. Though it could not preserve itself forever, its corpse still drips with rotten magic. By digging it up, the archaeologists have unknowingly released a curse in the area that controls all dragons and dragon-like creatures.

entries.name: Necrux's Curse
entries: Familiarize yourself with the rules of this curse before running this adventure. The ancient dragon Necrux implanted a curse in his skeleton, which controls the wills of dragons and creatures related to them (such as kobolds) within one mile of the bones. Any living creature with a biological connection to dragons is compelled to congregate at the site of the skeleton and viciously protect it from disturbance. At night, the flesh of dead draconic creatures melts off their corpses, and the resulting skeletons reanimate to continue this work.

A cursed creature remains that way until they fall {@condition unconscious} or their corpse is destroyed. An individual can also be freed from the curse immediately via the {@spell remove curse} spell or similar magic. Once a cursed individual loses the curse, they can't be affected again until the next dawn.

{@b Breaking the Curse.} The curse has three sources of power within the skeleton—the skull, the third rib, and the last tailbone. When all three of these bones are destroyed or neutralized, the curse ends. Any mind-controlled creature regains their faculties, and any reanimated bones drop to the ground, inert. Each bone has an AC of 16, 30 HP, resistance to Slashing and Piercing damage, and vulnerability to Bludgeoning damage. A {@spell dispel magic} spell, {@spell remove curse} spell, or similar magic automatically neutralizes the bone.

entries.name: Draconic Heroes?
entries: If one or more of your party members has ancestral or sorcerous connections to a dragon, the fiction dictates that they would be affected by Necrux's curse as well. However mind control is a difficult thing to make fun at the table. With your players' consent, you can use this optional rule:

{@b Heroic Falter.} Heroic characters are able to resist the call of the curse better than most. At the start of each of their turns, a character who is connected to dragons in some way must make a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the character must immediately use their action to attack the closest creature, friend or foe. If no creatures are in range, the character uses their movement to get in range. Once a creature has succeeded on this saving throw, they automatically succeed on saving throws to resist the curse until the next dawn.

entries.name: Kobold Attack!
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|NightOfTheLivingBones|1|Adventure Map 1})
The characters are traveling when they stumble upon the dig site. Read or paraphrase the following:

You hear frenzied hisses, the clatter of weapons, and desperate screams for help. Just ahead is an opening in the crags that hosts several makeshift tents. Digging supplies are strewn about, and the area is abuzz with small, dragon-like creatures using slings and knives to threaten unarmed people in lab coats. A young red wyrmling exhales a burst of fire from overhead. Several of the offending creatures have hidden themselves in the giant hole below, where the gargantuan bones of a long-dead dragon slumber.

Six {@creature kobold||kobolds} and one {@creature red dragon wyrmling} are attacking the dig site. The wyrmling and three of the kobolds are chasing the dig staff around the campsite. The remaining three kobolds have taken up residence beneath the massive ribcage of the dragon fossil and use their sling attack to strike the party from afar.

The six members of the dig team are {@creature commoner||commoners} who spend their turns running and hiding. Once the kobolds see the player characters, they leave the dig team alone and go after what they perceive is the larger threat. The kobolds and wyrmling do not respond if spoken to. On a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check, a character gets the sense that these creatures are being magically controlled.

entries.name: Environmental Conditions
entries: The following conditions are true for the dig site:

items.name: Steep Hole
items.entry: The hole that houses the skeleton is 10 feet deep. A creature who falls in takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage.

items.name: Bone Shield
items.entry: While underneath the ribcage or the skull, creatures enjoy both {@quickref cover||3||half cover} and shade that negates the effects of the Sunlight Sensitivity trait.

items.name: Desert Terrain
items.entry: The sandy environment of the dig site is {@quickref difficult terrain||3} for creatures not native to the area. The kobolds, having lived their entire life among the dunes of the desert, are not affected by this.

entries.name: Development
entries: Once the characters neutralize the kobolds, the dig team emerges from their hiding places and thank the characters profusely. The chief archaeologist on the expedition, a human {@creature commoner} named Edwin Proudmoon, explains the situation: his team has been loading the bones onto their wagons every day, and the bones magically reappear back in the dirt the next morning. This, however, was the first time they've been attacked.
Edwin asks the heroes to guard them from future attacks while they load up the bones, and help uncover the mystery of why the skeleton seems so averse to being transported.
Any enemies who were knocked out during combat come to after two hours, no longer affected by the curse.

entries.name: Investigation
entries: While the dig team loads the bones on their wagons, the characters are welcome to investigate the dig site, help out, or take a rest. They have limited time before the sun goes down. To simulate this, each character may attempt two actions (e.g., investigate the bones, cast a spell, speak with any captured kobolds). If a character chooses to take a short rest, they instead get one action before sunset.

entries.name: Investigation Leads
entries: The following are leads the characters can follow up on to learn more about the curse.

entries.name: Captured Attackers
entries: Any captured attackers who were knocked out regain consciousness after an hour. They don't remember much, and they don't appreciate being tied up. A character can make a Charisma ({@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, or {@skill Persuasion}) check to question them. The character has Advantage on the check if the captured attacker is not bound.
The check's roll determines how much the characters learn:

items: {@b 11 or below:} The enemy says they live here and don't recognize the authority of the characters. They don't appreciate being questioned like a common criminal.
{@b 12–16:} The enemy admits they don't remember much beyond losing consciousness, although they claim even now they feel an uneasy affinity for the bones in the site, like they need to be near them.
{@b 17 or above:} The enemy vaguely remembers an overwhelming desire to protect something called "The Dread Lord Necrux."

entries: A character may take another action to make a {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill History}) check on the name "Dread Lord Necrux." On a success, they learn that Necrux was a necromantic black dragon who lived over a thousand years ago. He drank the life force from other dragons to consolidate his power and grant himself eternal life. Those he couldn't subdue, he cursed. Ancient heroes whose names are lost to time vanquished the monster.

entries.name: Enemy Corpses
entries: Characters can investigate any enemy corpses they find. They can also take an action to destroy the corpses, which removes them from the nighttime encounter in the following chapter.
Characters can take an action to search the corpses. They find 5 gp for each corpse they search, but nothing that links them to the phenomenon.
If characters cast {@spell speak with dead} on an enemy corpse, the body rises and shouts "Dread Lord Necrux reclaims his cursed own at Dusk" before returning to its repose permanently.

entries.name: Detecting for Magic
entries: Casting {@spell detect magic} reveals that the entire skeleton is bathed in necromantic magic. Any corpses from the encounter are also covered in that same magic. A character who casts {@spell detect magic} can make an additional {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to notice the three strongest points that the magic is flowing from: the skull, the third rib, and the last point on the tail.
Casting a spell to remove the magic from a bone, or attempting to break one, requires another action. Edwin begs the characters not to destroy the bones unless absolutely necessary.

entries.name: Investigate the Bones
entries: With a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, characters who investigate the dig site find it's littered with countless other smaller bones, kobold-sized. A success by 5 or more reveals that these bones are all of varying ages, meaning things keep dying and decomposing here at this dig site.

entries.name: Speaking with Archaeologists
entries: Characters who wish to speak with the archaeologists while they work may get some information out of them. Edwin and his staff are very busy. To learn anything from Edwin, characters must succeed on a {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check, or offer to help them move the bones with a successful {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

Edwin then reveals that his team uncovered a stela with a curious inscription, written in {@language Draconic}. Ironically, none of the archaeologists can read {@language Draconic}. The inscription reads:
Let Your Breath be My Breath
Let Your Bones be My Bones
Let the Curse Reach All
To Retribute Necrux's Fall

Any character proficient in {@skill Arcana} recognises that this is a curse. They can use an action to make a {@dc 22} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check to understand the curse. On a success, they learn everything in the "{@adventure Necrux's Curse|NightOfTheLivingBones|0|Necrux's Curse}" section above.

entries.name: Too Good?
entries: It's possible your characters may discover how to break the curse and then break it before the nighttime encounter, if their rolls and choices are really good. If that's the case, and you still want to cap this adventure with an encounter, let seven {@creature Kobold Skeleton|DMSecretWeapon|kobold skeletons} and a {@creature Dead Dragon Wyrmling|DMSecretWeapon|dead dragon wyrmling} rise immediately, the curse's desperate, dying gasp before Necrux is removed completely from this world.

entries.name: Bones at Dusk
entries: ({@adventure Map 2|NightOfTheLivingBones|1|Adventure Map 2})

The moment the sun is set completely, and the dig site bathed in the inky blackness of night, a commotion stirs from the backs of the wagons. The gigantic bones rattle and shake, limned in a ghastly green light. They rise and return to the picture-perfect spots in which they were laying this morning. Smaller skeletons that look like the beasts from this afternoon rise from the pit and begin their attack. You see three bones glowing more brilliantly and dreadfully than all the rest: the skull, the third rib, and the tip of the tail.
"We are truly cursed!" cries Edwin. "Please, stop it if you can—by any means necessary!"

Two {@creature Kobold Skeleton|DMSecretWeapon|kobold skeletons}, plus the skeletons of any of the enemies the characters killed earlier today, rise and attack. Use the {@creature Kobold Skeleton|DMSecretWeapon|kobold skeleton} and {@creature Dead Dragon Wyrmling|DMSecretWeapon|dead dragon wyrmling} stat blocks for the defeated kobolds and wyrmling.

For the duration of combat, on initiative count 0, {@dice 1d4} {@creature Kobold Skeleton|DMSecretWeapon|kobold skeletons} rise from inside the dig site and join the fight. This lair action does not trigger if there are currently six or more kobold skeletons in play.

To end combat, the heroes must end the curse by destroying or neutralizing the three bones. Otherwise, the skeletons will endlessly rise.
