If the players are struggling to identify the victory condition, Edwin suggests doing something about the three bones that are glowing the brightest. See the {@adventure Necrux's Curse|NightOfTheLivingBones|0|Necrux's Curse} heading at the beginning of this adventure for more details.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Edwin pays each character 250 gp for defending his team. If they lifted the curse without destroying any of Necrux's skeleton, he doubles the reward. In addition, the party gains favor with Edwin and the University of Brightbarrow. They may write to Edwin in the future and ask about any historical thing they're curious about, and Edwin can respond with what he knows, acting in much the same way as a {@spell legend lore} spell that takes a few days.

data.name: Mahomare's Jailbirds
entries: If you're looking for an exciting way to bring new heroes together, why not have them accidentally break a villain out of jail?

Mahomare's Jailbirds is a starting adventure for a party of 4–5 level 1 heroes that twists the players' expectations and provides the GM with two enemy factions they can flesh out over the course of a full campaign.
To my Shining Hero,
I was captured and taken to The Old Rook
Beware the Wyrm Wardens
Help me! I don't know what will happen next
Or when

entries.name: Background
entries: The Wyrm Wardens are a sect of dragonborn knights with a twisted sense of justice. They raid towns, kidnapping criminals and innocents alike, unconvinced that the "miscreants" were being punished enough for their crimes. All of their victims are held at a fortress in the North Valley known as The Old Rook, the magic scarred bastion of a long forgotten royal family before the Wyrm Wardens took it over.

Despite their terrible ideals of law and order, the Wyrm Wardens were able to successfully (if inadvertently) imprison a powerful witch named Mahomare. For centuries, she laid waste to entire kingdoms and took their magical heirlooms. Mahomare wagered her powers in a card game with the Wyrm Wardens and lost, and they incarcerated her for gambling.

The witch is near powerless and trapped inside The Old Rook, but she has set a few plans into motion in order to make her escape and find her revenge. First, she has taken on a low profile disguise among the prisoners, known as the Jailbirds, so they might befriend her. Second, she slipped hundreds of letters out on the winds, written vaguely enough to catch the attention of some foolish heroes looking to save the day.

entries.name: Setup
entries: Each hero has been sent a letter from someone special to them, saying they had been taken into custody by the Wyrm Wardens. These special someones can be the same person or all different people, as long as they tie into their heroes' backgrounds. The heroes run into each other by chance, meeting on a hill overlooking The Old Rook. As the sun sets, they have an opportunity to coordinate their efforts and find a way inside.

entries.name: Into The Old Rook

items: Old Rook Exterior — {@adventure Map 1|MahomaresJailbirds|1|Adventure Map 1}
Old Rook Interior — {@adventure Map 2|MahomaresJailbirds|1|Adventure Map 2}

entries: The front gate is guarded by two {@creature Wyrm Warden Guard|DMSecretWeapon|Wyrm Warden guards} while the perimeter is patrolled by one {@creature Wyrm Warden Guard|DMSecretWeapon} and one {@creature blink dog} every 10 minutes. A hero needs to succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to sneak past the guards. Otherwise, the guards will call for the Highwarden and attempt to apprehend anyone suspicious lurking about.

The heroes may try to rappel up The Old Rook's walls if they have the right equipment. The walls are 50 feet tall and require a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check to reach the top. From the roof, they can reach either the cafeteria, the highwarden's office, or the center battle platform.

entries.name: Magic Suppression
entries: Magic inside the fortress doesn't work as well as outside of it. 2nd-level spells or higher fizzle out before they can be completed, and uncommon or rarer magic items have their durations, range, and damage dealt halved.

One of the few reliable sources of magic are the wards placed on the cells. If a prisoner is out of their cell for 1 minute or longer without the highwarden speaking the contingency password, a shrill alarm sounds across the entire complex.

entries.name: General Encounters
entries: The Old Rook's roster is light while the heroes haven't made contact with the jailbirds. Whenever the heroes enter a room that isn't the cafeteria, the highwarden's office, the center battle platform, or the jail cells, roll a {@dice d4}:

rows: 1 {@creature Wyrm Warden Guard|DMSecretWeapon} and 1 {@creature blink dog}

entries: The heroes can attempt to sneak by enemies or engage with them. If they raise enough noise, roll another {@dice d4} and have more enemies answer the call. If the heroes dispatch the enemies within a room, the next room they enter will be empty.

entries.name: Cafeteria
entries: The Old Rook's mess hall is empty, only featuring the remains of a big dinner that will surely spoil if left out overnight. The heroes can take up to 3 portions and use them like they were {@item Potion of Healing||potions of healing}.

entries.name: Highwarden's Office
entries: The office's impressive desk looks out over the center battle platform whenever it isn't flooded with stacks of forms and contracts. {@creature Highwarden Ragna|DMSecretWeapon}, a knight, is asleep at the desk before the heroes reach the jailbirds.

A hero can search the office with a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to find a {@item deck of illusions} and a tattered witch's hat. There are also a number of sheets of parchment that resemble the letters the heroes received.

entries.name: Center Battle Platform
entries: Blood, scorch marks, and divots scar the round platform. It rests above a dusty 30-foot pit filled with {@dice 1d6} {@creature swarm of spiders||swarms of spiders}.

At the far end of the platform is a cage with a sleeping {@creature copper dragon wyrmling} inside. If the wyrmling wakes, it will scream until it is let out and proceed to attack anyone that gets close.

entries.name: Jail Cells
entries: The cells are unlit and dirty, completely unfit for people to stay in for a night, let alone indefinitely. 2 {@creature Wyrm Warden Guard|DMSecretWeapon|Wyrm Warden guards} and a {@creature blink dog} carry the keys to the cells while they stand watch.

The bars are made of iron, requiring a {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to bend wide enough for someone to pass through. The bars whine under enough pressure, ringing throughout the fortress and alerting all Wyrm Wardens.

entries.name: The Jailbirds
entries: There are currently 6 prisoners in The Old Rook, one of which is Mahomare in disguise. Roll a {@dice d6} before introducing the jailbirds to the heroes:

rows: Dirk Dirk, a goblin roughneck in red with a 5 o'clock shadow and a bad attitude. He was caught writing obscenities on the mayor's house.
Juujubee, a young {@creature doppelganger} in blue that wants to go home to their family. They were taken while lost and alone just outside of a town.

Appel, an early adult {@creature commoner} in green that never lets her identical twin sister Anan out of her sight. Appel was captured waiting for Anan to finish her work at the library on suspicion of "stalking."
Anan, a put together {@creature commoner} in green that watches over her identical twin sister Appel like a hawk. Anan was taken in after punching the Wyrm Warden that took her sister.
Baltasar, a halfling hedge mage in yellow that idolizes the magical prowess of "The Mighty Mahomare." He was falsely blamed and arrested for setting the oldest tree in his town on fire.
One of the heroes' special someones in purple. Use the {@creature commoner} stat block unless better fitting statistics match the person. They don't have any memory of how they got to The Old Rook.

entries: None of the jailbirds know anything about the letters the heroes received; Dirk Dirk even suggests that the Wyrm Wardens might write the letters to lure "vigilantes" here and save them the trouble of staking out more prisoners. Nonetheless, they plead with the heroes to free them from The Old Rook.

entries.name: Break Out
entries: The moment the cells open and the ward sounds the alarm, it's a race to escape the Wyrm Wardens and Highwarden Ragna. The encounters that the heroes face change, and hints to Mahomare's identity emerge to anyone who stops long enough to notice them.

entries.name: Jailbird Oddities
entries: As the heroes make their escape, have the last person to leave each room make a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. On success, they notice the next oddity on the following list until all oddities have been revealed:

rows: The hero hears one of the Wyrm Wardens call out "be careful of the monster!"
The fortress walls glow whenever a person with magical energy passes near them.
A charred skeleton in the corner is wearing similarly colored clothing to the jailbird that Mahomare replaced.

entries: Each oddity might paint a target on an innocent jailbird separately, but together, the heroes can deduce the true villain as they escape.

entries.name: New Encounters
entries: The jailbirds aren't prepared to join combat and try to stay out of harm's way. Whenever the heroes enter a room, roll a {@dice d4}:

rows: 2 {@creature Wyrm Warden Guard|DMSecretWeapon|Wyrm Warden guards} and 1 {@creature blink dog}
1 {@creature Wyrm Warden Guard|DMSecretWeapond} and 2 {@creature blink dog||blink dogs}
{@creature Highwarden Ragna|DMSecretWeapon} ({@creature knight}) at full hit points. He retreats whenever he is reduced to half his hit points.

entries: If the heroes linger in a room longer than 1 minute, roll another {@dice d4} and have more enemies enter the room. If the heroes dispatch the enemies (or cause them to retreat) within a room, that encounter is removed from the dice roll for the next two rooms. If a hero can cause a successful distraction, such as opening the cage at the center battle platform, the next two rooms are guaranteed to be empty.

Once outside, the heroes are met with Highwarden Ragna, 3 {@creature Wyrm Warden Guard|DMSecretWeapon|Wyrm Warden guards}, and 2 {@creature blink dog||blink dogs} as a final stand. However, if Mahomare is outside the walls of The Old Rook, she regains a fraction of her powers and joins the heroes in the fight. She uses the {@creature Mage} stat block, but has no 3rd-, 4th-, or 5th-level spell slots. Even if Ragna is reduced to 0 hit points, he survives and retreats, vowing that his "justice will overcome Mahomare and her evil goons."

entries.name: To My Shining Heroes
entries: After fending off the Wyrm Wardens, Mahomare disappears cackling into a green storm cloud. She leaves the heroes and any freed prisoners with one final letter:
To my Shining Heroes,
At last I am free to reclaim my power
You answered my call
This wretched world will soon be plunged into darkness
Thank you

data.name: A Hellish Escape
entries: A 1–3 session adventure for five 10th-level characters.

entries.name: Synopsis
entries: Gilly Gnoll is a clavichord player renowned the world over. Unfortunately his singing voice and magic behind the keys has attracted the notice of forces beyond mortal comprehension. Recently, he signed a fiendish contract to play a show at the house of Pergozal, a mighty devil who runs a fiendish cocktail bar in hell. Gilly needed the money, so he signed without reading and has only recently discovered that he signed a deal to play at Pergozal's in perpetuity.

Gilly knows the characters well enough to ask for help. He might be an old friend, or the party may have met him while he was playing in a tavern. Whatever the case, he sends the party complimentary tickets to his next show at Pergozal's and encloses a letter. The letter is delivered by an {@creature imp} who, upon completion of its duties, explodes in a puff of smoke and ash. The letter reads:

Hello, friends! Even though we are far, you are always near to my heart. Let's meet up again soon! Please come to my show next evening at Pergozal's in Hell. My employer was kind enough to supply these comped tickets, which come with transportation to hell and one drink coupon. Excited to see you, but don't forget that dress is black tie.

Any character who has spent more than 10 minutes speaking with Gilly can tell something is off about the contents of this message. A character who knows {@language Thieves' Cant} can automatically tell there is a message hidden in this letter. In truth, the first letter of each sentence spells out "HELP ME." Characters who succeed on a {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check decipher this hidden message.

entries.name: Many Enemies?
entries: This adventure introduces the players to a kaleidoscope of devils, monstrosities, hags, and other fantastical creatures. Original, named creatures have stat blocks present in the bestiary. Other creatures, such as the {@creature imp} above, have stat blocks freely available as part of the D&D 5e Creative Commons online you can easily find, should you need them.

entries.name: Cocktails and Conspiracies
entries: Speaking the name "Pergozal's" while holding onto one of the tickets opens up a gate that leads directly into hell, right outside the door of the night club. This information is printed on each ticket. When the characters step through, read or paraphrase the following:

It is a hot night in hell, where you now stand. You are outside a chic-looking building made of marble. Multicolored lights stream out from the windows. In front of the door is a bored-looking devil clad in chains, confiscating weapons from dressed-up partygoers at the front of a line that winds around the building.

Aziza, the {@creature chain devil} at the door, demands the characters leave their weapons, armor, and arcane focuses with her before they enter Pergozal's. Characters can conceal a small weapon (such as a {@item dagger}) or focus on their person with a successful {@dc 20} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check. The bouncer places the characters' personal items in a {@item bag of holding} she keeps on her person and gives them a ticket so they can retrieve them upon exiting. She then takes their tickets and welcomes them inside.

{@b Aziza's Plight.} Aziza hates working here, but she's contractually bound to do so. She's underpaid and sarcastic about it, and this attitude is no secret. If characters wish to keep or regain their weapons, they can offer to free Aziza like they plan to free Gilly.

entries.name: Inside Pergozal's
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|AHellishEscape|1|Adventure Map 1})

The light of hellfire streaks through the windows of this otherwise dimly-lit hall of silk and velvet and other materials I'd rather not name. Red-painted gargoyles sit atop pedestals, staring down at the patrons of Pergozal's: humanoids and fiends and fey, creatures from across worlds, here with or without shame to dance, drink, gamble, and consort. Above it all on the raised stage sits Gilly Gnoll with his clavichord. He sings, and the music is magically amplified to fill the space around him.

entries.name: Cocktail Bars
entries: Several {@creature imp||imps} flit about the two bars, taking orders for cocktails both familiar and novel. Characters can order a drink, but the prices are hefty. A regular drink costs 1 gp, a specialty cocktail costs 5 gp, and a round for the entire room is 250 gp.

entries.name: Card Tables
entries: Tuxedoed {@creature imp||imps} run card tables, simple games of chance that mortals are especially drawn to. The house accepts bets in intervals of 50 gp, and the rules of the game are simple: draw a higher card than the house's. (Have both the player and the DM roll a {@dice d100}; the highest is the winner. If a player succeeds, they receive their initial 50 gp plus an additional 45 gp).

entries.name: The Stage
entries: Gilly Gnoll (uses the {@creature gnoll} stat block) sits on the stage with his clavichord. If the characters approach, he wraps up his song and takes his allotted ten-minute break so he can converse with them. Gilly is grateful that the characters are here and provides the following information on how they can help:

"Pergozal's got me, forever, through this infernal contract. On my breaks I've been charming the guests and learning some interesting stuff. Pergozal's got a whole dungeon down below—that's where he keeps me when I'm not playin'. Not sure how to get there without his permission. But he keeps his contracts down there too. If we can destroy my contract before he catches you, I'll be free to go. Maybe some of the other folks around here would know more. But be careful—they play with forces guys like us can barely fathom. And look, once you get my contract, I can get us out of here, no problem."

entries.name: The Investigation
entries: In this section, the characters must learn how to enter the dungeon below and destroy the contract. They can speak with many characters who might offer several solutions. Many of these characters ask for things in return.

entries.name: Pergozal
entries: The lounge's owner, Pergozal, is a greedy {@creature horned devil} wearing a bow tie (and nothing else). He is amicable as a rule, because happy people spend more. He can be found wandering the hall, sharing a laugh with patrons, and encouraging them to spend more. Characters cannot speak with him until they have spent at least 500 gp here, which they can do easily at the bar or the card tables. The more money they spend, the friendlier the devil becomes. Use the Pergozal Friendship Table to determine what Pergozal will say to a high-spending character.
"Gilly is the best addition I've added to my place in an epoch. I'm never gettin' rid of that silly little guy!"
Pergozal answers surface-level questions the characters ask him.
"Heh, you guys are fun. You meet the other whales yet?"
Pergozal introduces the characters to Valheira or Stasya of the Coven of Nightsong if they haven't met.
"Half of those poor saps playing cards are gonna lose everything. That's when I swoop in and offer a deal for their soul so they can keep playin'. They can always get it back. For a price!"
Pergozal's guard drops around the characters. Spells the characters cast are not affected by his Magic Resistance trait.
"You're adventurers, right? You look a little naked. I can fix that. Just don't cause any trouble, OK?"
Pergozal allows the characters to hold onto their checked weapons.
"You guys must love it here! You want a private tour of downstairs?"
Pergozal requests two {@creature chain devil||chain devils} take the characters downstairs and show them around.

entries.name: Valheira
entries: Valheira is an {@creature erinyes}, a soldier in the eternal wars of hell. When she's not risking her life for an archdevil master who does not know her name, she's here wasting the money she earns just to feel something. The characters can find her at the bar. Valheira won't open up to the characters without a successful {@dc 30} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. Each drink the characters buy her reduces the DC by 2. She's not getting drunker; no matter how much she drinks, it doesn't seem to affect her at all.
Valheira knows the following information:

items: Pergozal is constantly making petty contracts with mortal patrons. When they lose money, he encourages them to offer their soul as collateral. He will then magically annul the contract if they can pay back what he gave them twofold (they often can't).
To be so flippant about breaking contracts, Pergozal must have an Infurnace, a device that creates magical nullifying flames. Placing a contract inside one destroys the magic that binds both parties.

entries: Valheira longs for a better magic weapon to protect her while on the front lines. The characters may have one checked right now. If the characters promise to give her that magic weapon, she offers to convince Aziza to let them hold onto their weapons.

entries.name: The Coven of Nightsong
entries: The Coven of Nightsong is a trio of {@creature night hag||night hags} who employ powerful magic to trade in mortal souls. They're here to purchase some from Pergozal, although his prices have gone up lately. Stasya, the leader of the coven, argues with her sisters about taking their business elsewhere. Characters who succeed on a {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check can tell the sisters three are terrified for their future and desperate to find a way to get back at Pergozal. The hags know the following and share with characters they're friendly with:

items: They have been to the dungeon below and know its approximate layout. (Show the characters the un-annotated {@adventure map|AHellishEscape|1|Adventure Map 2}).

The dungeon below is 200 feet directly beneath the club. A {@spell dimension door} spell or similar magic will get the characters safely there. Alternatively, they can jump through the fiery pit in the north of the cocktail bar to get there (but that might harm them).

entries: The coven can employ magic to aid the characters, including the {@spell locate object} spell to find the contracts and the Infurnace. The coven is willing to cooperate with the heroes if the following conditions are satisfied:

items: They want souls, which the heroes can find in the dungeon below. For each spell they cast for the characters, they expect to be brought 5 souls.

The coven can protect any character from being harmed by "Pergozal or any magic wielded in his name" if they pledge their eternal service to the coven. Mechanically, the character promises that they will become a Warlock on their next level up, with the coven serving as their patron. When the character kills a creature with a soul, the soul immediately enters the grasp of the coven. The coven cannot extend this agreement to characters who are already Warlocks.

entries.name: Asking Too Much?
entries: The NPCs in this section are asking a lot of the players: spend all their money, give up their precious items, or pledge eternal service. This is a tenth-level adventure, so the stakes reflect this! If your heroes don't have the means, you can adjust the requirements. For example, scale back Pergozal's prices so they're more in line with how much gold your players have. Have Valheira ask for any kind of magic item, not just a weapon. Let Stasya ask for one favor, not a lifetime of them.
That said, big choices are interesting. Don't be afraid to use them.

entries.name: Entering the Dungeon
entries: Characters will most likely enter the dungeon through the flaming pit in the northmost, topmost part of the club. This brings the characters directly to the Entryway (Area D1). This pit is a 200-foot-long tunnel whose walls shoot non-magical fire into the center. Characters who jump take 35 ({@damage 10d6}) Fire damage from traveling through and 35 ({@damage 10d6}) Bludgeoning damage from the landing. They will likely want to mitigate this through any means available.

entries.name: The Dungeon Below
entries: ({@adventure Map 2|AHellishEscape|1|Adventure Map 2})
There is an annotated {@adventure map|AHellishEscape|1|Adventure Map 2} for your reference in the Map Pack.
Once the characters enter the dungeon below, they must find Gilly's contract and cast it into the Infurnace. The following features are true of the dungeon:

items.name: Hellfire and Brimstone
items.entry: The entire area is brightly lit unless otherwise stated. Additionally, because of the magical properties of this area, all magical Fire damage is more impactful. Resistances are ignored, weaknesses are doubled, and creatures immune to Fire now take half damage.

items.name: Lava
items.entry: Most areas are situated atop an endless pool of hellfire lava. A creature takes 42 ({@damage 12d6}) magical Fire damage when they touch the lava, and every six seconds they continue to touch the lava.

items.name: Big Dungeon
items.entry: 1 square of the map equals 10 feet.

items.name: Overworked, Underpaid
items.entry: All of the devils in this dungeon are here because they're contractually obligated to be. If a character finds an employee's contract in Area D4 and promises to cast it into the Infurnace, the employee becomes friendly to the characters and assists them. If a character reneges on this promise, that employee joins the fight during {@adventure Final Confrontation|AHellishEscape|0|Final Confrontation}.

entries.name: D1. Entryway

entries: The temperature shoots up considerably. You stand on a hexagonal platform overlooking a sea of lava. Stone statues of Pergozal adorn the walls, each one holding out a top hat like a collection basket. Halls stretch out to the west and east, and large stone steps descend to the south. Infernal runes have been carved into the floor at the center of the platform.
Though the statues of Pergozal are mostly for decoration, characters who donate at least 10 gp to a statue gain a temporary +1 to their AC, which lasts until the next time they take a short rest.

{@b Runes.} These runes are the making of a teleportation circle. Activating the circle requires an action, after which it takes 30 seconds (5 rounds of combat) to charge up. The circle takes characters to center stage in the cocktail lounge.

entries.name: D2. Barracks

entries: Torchlight flickers against the wall adorned with used armaments and uniforms—for both combat and cocktails. Scrolls written in hasty Infernal are pinned to the sides of shelving units. Two spiny-looking devils sit at a table playing cards, muttering softly. A hell hound rests at their feet.

Two {@creature barbed devil||barbed devils} and one {@creature hell hound} are in this room, though they are distracted. So long as characters don't make any noise, they can easily {@condition surprised||surprise} the group. The devils only understand {@language Infernal} and can't negotiate with characters who don't speak it.

The guards attack as soon as they notice intruders. They are only underpaid employees, after all, and can be convinced to give up once they all possess less than half their hit points with a successful {@dc 25} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check. The guards know the layout of the dungeon and share it with characters who spare them.

{@b Infernal Scrolls.} Most of the scrolls are shift schedules, work protocol, and guidelines for how to heat up your lunch in the lava sifter. A character who can read {@language Infernal} can make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. On a success, they find a scroll of {@spell planar ally} attached to a note that reads, "Use In Case Of Absent Coworker."

entries.name: D3. Storeroom

entries: South of the barracks is a hall that leads to a storeroom. A large chunk of the hallway has been destroyed, leaving a 20-foot gap that plunges into the pool of lava below. Most of the employees here can't actually reach the storeroom anymore, so it's full of items confiscated from patrons and summarily forgotten.

{@b Treasure.} Along with the dust and expired food, characters who spend 5 minutes searching this place find a {@item +2 weapon||+2 magic weapon} of the GM's choice (ideally one matching what the characters gave to Valheira if they did so). They also find 200 gp worth of diamonds and an old, ornate hand mirror with inset rubies worth 500 gp.

entries.name: D4. Contract Library

entries: No torches adorn the walls of these two rooms, though the glow of the lava outside dimly shines through the windows. The space is filled with shelves upon shelves, each one crammed with crates and boxes stuffed with scrolls.

This is the library where Pergozal keeps the contracts he makes with clients and employees. Characters can search for Gilly's contract here. If the characters used a {@spell locate object} spell or similar magic to find the contract, they know automatically where it is. Otherwise, they'll have to search.

{@b Searching for a Contract.} A character can locate any contract with a minute of searching and a successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check. A character can gain a +2 bonus on this check for any of the following reasons:

items: The character can read {@language Infernal} (the language the contracts are in).
The character has already spent at least a minute searching in this area.
The character's background involves libraries, academia, or similar work.
The character has made a contract with a supernatural being before.
An employee of the cocktail bar is helping them look.

entries: These bonuses stack. On a success, the character finds the contract they're looking for. It could be Gilly's, Aziza's, or any other contract. After every 2 attempts, a {@creature barbed devil} and a {@creature hell hound} arrive while patrolling the area and attack.

entries.name: D5. Kitchens

entries: A cacophony of metal against metal, the roar of flame, and sizzling of meat in oil swells in this cramped, greasy kitchen that would violate any health code. Tiny devils fly through the air shouting in Infernal as they pass each other. One stuffs a plate full of still-wriggling food into a tube and slams the door shut. The tube whooshes, the door reopens, and the food is no more.

Six {@creature imp||imps} flurry about the kitchen rushing to fulfill the orders of the patrons upstairs. They don't care about anything but their work. Characters can sneak by them with a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, but one failure alerts the imps to all the characters. The imps move to call two {@creature barbed devil||barbed devils} to appear from the north and apprehend the characters, but they can be persuaded to look the other way with a successful {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. If it comes to combat, the imps flee.

{@b Food Tube.} The food tube is a magical device that sends one Small creature or object (or up to 5 Tiny creatures or objects) at a time to the upper floor, where they are received by the staff behind the bar. This is a potential exit for characters if they're small enough.

entries.name: D6. Soul Extraction Chambers

entries: Agonizing screams fill these chambers. Fetid corpses are stacked up against walls as devils work various instruments of torture against mortals of varying degrees of aliveness. The shelves are lined with jars of various make and material, each one glowing a unique eerie shade.

Each of these three chambers has two {@creature barbed devil||barbed devils} extracting the soul from one {@creature commoner}. Characters can easily sneak past these gruesome scenes with a successful {@dc 15} group Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check. However, if left alone the commoners die within 18 seconds (or 3 combat rounds). Once all three commoners die, their flesh magically combines with the corpses against the walls to become a {@creature Vengeful Amalgam|DMSecretWeapon|vengeful amalgam} that attacks hero and devil alike. This monster cannot be reasoned with.

{@b Rescuing the Victims.} The victims here are all contract holders. They can't leave unless their contracts are destroyed. They are tottering on the brink of death—{@condition unconscious} with 1 hit point remaining. Each one offers the heroes 500 gp for getting them out of the place alive.

{@b Treasure.} The jars on the shelves are full of souls. Searching the shelves costs an action, and each character can do it once for free. A character can roll {@dice 1d6} to determine how many souls they find. If a character would like to search a second time, they take 13 ({@damage 2d12}) Psychic damage. These souls can be traded to the hags in the Nightsong Coven. If they have any excess, the hags buy them for 100 gp apiece.

entries.name: D7. Justice's Divine Gate

entries: Standing at the center of this room is a muscular, winged man clad in golden robes. He is motionless, expressionless, and glows a malevolent red. Behind him are steps that lead upwards to a giant iron furnace.

The creature in this room is {@creature Armistician|DMSecretWeapon}, a fallen deva. He is a celestial whose impartiality Pergozal relies upon to be the last line of defense against misuse of his Infurnace. Pergozal and Armistician do not have a contract. Rather, Armistician renders this service for free, as part of his misguided belief that Pergozal is the pinnacle of justice, a belief Pergozal himself has falsely cultivated.
Armistician's job is to read all contracts and determine whether they deserve to be voided by the Infurnace. The only person who is allowed to overrule the deva's judgment is Pergozal himself.
When characters enter the room, Armistician demands they state their purpose and bring the contracts to him for inspection. The characters have options available to them:

items.name: Lie
items.entry: Characters can convince Armistician they are authorized to use the Infurnace with a successful {@dc 30} Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check. On a success, Armistician lets them pass freely. On a failure, he attacks.

items.name: Reason
items.entry: Characters can convince Armistician his pursuit of justice is misguided here. To do so, the characters must make at least three convincing and true arguments about Pergozal's nature. Bringing up his greed, his treatment of employees, or his misleading contracts count as evidence. If the characters have other employees with them, these employees can testify to this. Finally, the characters must succeed on a {@dc 30} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Performance}) check. Each employee they have with them provides a +2 bonus to this check. If the characters succeed, Armistician joins the heroes. If they fail, he attacks.

items.name: Fight
items.entry: At the beginning of his first turn in combat, Armistician summons a {@creature nightmare} to fight with him.

entries.name: D8. The Infurnace

entries: The Infurnace is an iron box shaped to look like the maw of a ravenous beast. Skulls and carrion hug the contraption's feet. Every step closer raises the temperature another unbearable degree.

The Infurnace does exactly what it says on the tin. When a character puts an infernal contract into the maws, the contract burns away and all creatures bound by that contract are bound no longer. The creatures bound by the contract know immediately that this is the case (meaning Pergozal is now aware of the characters' meddling, if he wasn't already). Putting any living thing inside the Infurnace immediately destroys that thing and any soul residing in it.

entries.name: Final Confrontation
entries: Just before the characters make their exit, they are caught red-handed by the man of the hour. If the characters are leaving via the teleportation circle in area D1, run this section once they reach that area. Otherwise, run this section wherever the characters decide to stage their getaway.

"So," rasps the voice of Pergozal. "You didn't enjoy the show, I take it." In a burst of brimstone and green hellflame, the devil appears flanked by two of his hellish hounds. "Listen up, kids. You never take from the house, or it'll take all of it back—and more."

{@creature Pergozal|DMSecretWeapon} and two {@creature hell hound||hell hounds} appear and attack the characters. Pergozal also summons any NPC the characters may have screwed over and goads them into fighting. This has the potential to be a very deadly encounter if the characters did some backstabbing!

The heroes don't have to defeat Pergozal (although they can if they like). They just have to escape. Activating the teleportation circle takes 5 rounds. As long as one character per round uses their bonus action to maintain the circle, they can escape at the end of the 5th round.

entries.name: Escaping Hell
entries: When the characters return to the cocktail bar, everyone but Gilly is blissfully ignorant of what transpired downstairs. Gilly meets the characters and uses a cowbell—a magical artifact that helps him get to gigs on time—to return himself and the characters to their home plane. Once there, Pergozal can't touch them ("Devil Law," says Gilly with a noncommittal shrug).

entries.name: Rewards
entries: Gilly pays the characters 500 gp for rescuing him. Additionally, he tells the characters he owes them "big-time." Once during the campaign, if the characters need a performance for any reason, they can contact Gilly. He'll arrive within the hour and automatically succeed a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check on his clavichord.

data.name: Secrets of Mycelia Grove
entries: An adventure for 4–5 3rd-level characters.

entries.name: Background
entries: The tiny farming village of Tuckertout sits on the edge of a largely unexplored valley. Lately, townsfolk have been disappearing in the night, never to return. What they don't know is that deep within the depths of the valley lies a colony of mushroom monsters who control minds with their spores. They seek to grow their numbers using the townsfolk. Recently, the colony managed to infect the druid who guards the valley, who now acts as a guardian and mistakenly believes the mushrooms to be innocent.

The characters begin in Tuckertout, where they learn of the disappearances and investigate the town to discover where the missing townsfolk have gone. Following the evidence trail, they travel into the misty valley and discover the grove, where they must face the mushroom colony while protecting the infected as much as they can.

entries.name: Story Hooks
entries: You can use the following hooks to place this adventure in your campaign:

items.name: Passing Through
items.entry: The characters arrive in Tuckertout en route to their next destination. When they stop for a rest or supplies, the townsfolk beg the heroes for help.

items.name: Missing Merchant
items.entry: Aloisius Gumm (he/him, human {@creature commoner}) of Gummworks Trading has gone missing. He was last seen traveling on the road that runs through Tuckertout. The heroes discover there is a 200 gp reward for anyone who can find him.

items.name: A Family Matter
items.entry: One of the heroes is from Tuckertout (or, perhaps, another small farming town of their invention). Their younger sibling or other family member has gone missing, and they receive a message urging them to return home.

entries.name: Tuckertout
entries: Tuckertout isn't so much a town as it is a collection of buildings placed around a dirt trading road, surrounded by farmland. There are only a few places in town worth seeing: the Horsehogg Inn, the mayor's office, and Idira Farms. This section outlines the major players and locations in Tuckertout as well as how the characters can learn the path to the hidden grove.

The dirt road stretches across the flat, grassy land. A handful of houses made of brick and wood and whatever other available materials sit on either side, and the surrounding fields are tilled and rich with crops. There is precious little activity in the sad excuse for a town, although most of it is concentrated outside the largest building. This old, wooden wreck shudders with each passing breeze. Outside is a painted sign (decades newer than the building it advertises) that reads: Ol' Horsehogg Inn.

entries.name: Horsehogg Inn
entries: This sad inn has a pub downstairs and an inn upstairs. It mainly makes its money from merchants and other travelers who need a night's rest between destinations. Right now, there is only one guest, Eban the mayor. When the heroes arrive, the inn's owner, a human {@creature commoner} named Barty, stands behind the bar. He says he can serve drink, but no food. The cook's gone missing.
{@b What Barty Knows.} If the characters speak with Barty, he can impart the following:

items: The cook, a halfling {@creature commoner} named Tassle, went missing in the middle of the night, after her shift.
Tassle gets most of her ingredients from the surrounding farms. She has an especially good deal with Idira Farms. She'll also trade with the occasional traveler for rarer spices.
There was only one person who rented a room last night: Aloisius Gumm. His caravan and horse are still out back, and he hasn't yet come down from his room.
Barty is happy to let the characters search the area if they mean to investigate Tassle's disappearance.

entries: {@b Mayor Eban.} Mayor Eban is an elderly human {@creature commoner}, looking gaunt and miserable. He's nursing a stout when the characters arrive. If the characters indicate their status as adventurers or their interest in the disappearances, Eban approaches them and begs them to help. His daughter Neeza has gone missing. The last place she was seen was Idira Farms, where she works the fields.

{@b The Kitchen.} Inside Tassle's kitchen, characters can find a few clues: a basket of half-used mushrooms on the counter, a recipe for mushroom stew, and a few written-down orders (one of which includes said mushroom stew). Any character who succeeds on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check recognizes that these mushrooms are not typically found around here. A success by 5 or more reveals the mushrooms resemble those found in the Feywild.

{@b Aloisius's Room.} Characters can knock on Aloisius's room all they want; he isn't in. They can ask Barty for the key, pick the lock with a successful {@dc 13} Dexterity check, or break it down with a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. The latter causes Barty to demand recompense in the form of 5 gp. There is a cold, half-eaten bowl of mushroom stew on the wooden desk.

entries.name: Spore Problems
entries: The characters are safe from the spores so long as they aren't ingested. A character who eats a mushroom must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, that character is infected. An infected creature instinctively knows the way to the mushroom portal and follows the call of Celica towards it. When in range of Celica, an infected creature follows her orders without question. The character can repeat the saving throw every time they take damage.

entries.name: Idira Farms
entries: {@adventure Map 1|SecretsOfMyceliaGrove|1|Adventure Map 1}

At the edge of town, where the farmland stretches to the very edge of the forest, one farm boasts the most land and the most profits: Idira Farms. They specialize in crops, but there are a few horses, a coop of chickens, and one cow.

The farm's owner is Elspeth Idira, an orc {@creature commoner} who is always thinking about five things at once. Today she is stressed—her farmhand Neeza didn't show up for work today, so she's short-staffed, and the farm is facing a crisis. Elspeth doesn't know the characters, so she's not inclined to answer their questions unless they either succeed on a {@dc 18} Charisma check or offer to fill in for Neeza for a few hours.
{@b What Elspeth Knows.} Elspeth can tell the characters the following:

items: The farm's crisis is an invasion of sorts. For the last few days, weird fungi have been sprouting up all over her farm. She squashes one, and ten more take its place by the next light.
Neeza knows a thing or two about mushrooms, so Elspeth had her sorting through them to see if any could be sold.

entries: {@b Exploring the Farm.} If the characters explore the farm, they find baskets of mushrooms just like the ones in Tassle's kitchen. The basket is the same as well; Neeza likely sold or gave one to the cook in the last few days. While exploring, they hear a ruckus in the barn. Two {@creature Fungal Abomination|DMSecretWeapon|fungal abominations} are trying to capture Annie, the cow.

The fungal abominations are unable to speak or communicate, but upon defeating them, players can perform an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check on their bodies (if alive and {@condition restrained}) or corpses (if not). A result of 18 or above will reveal that these large plant folk were once humanoid, but the grotesque transformation is irreversible. At this late stage of corruption, there is no way to identify who these people once were, but the process likely took some time.

entries.name: Development
entries: After investigating the town, the characters should conclude that the strange mushrooms in town have something to do with the disappearances. Any character who spends 10 minutes searching for mushrooms finds a small patch of them close to the valley path. The characters should take this as a sign to descend into the damp, misty valley to continue their search.

If the players aren't picking up the thread of adventure, have Mayor Eban request an update on the characters' investigation. When they mention mushrooms, Eban remembers that his daughter loves collecting mushrooms in the valley.

entries.name: Searching For the Grove
entries: {@adventure Map 2|SecretsOfMyceliaGrove|1|Adventure Map 2}

When the characters set out, it is daytime unless they helped out Elspeth on the farm; then it is night. If the characters would prefer to spend the night in Tuckertout and search the valley in the morning, then two of the townsfolk in the final encounter (GM's choice) completed their transformation and appear as {@creature Fungal Abomination|DMSecretWeapon|fungal abominations}. They cannot change back; they can only be subdued.

The forest is lush and green, with a large canopy that shades the ground below: the perfect environment for mushrooms to develop. The heroes need only follow the mushrooms to find their destination. Have the characters make a group {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check. On a success, they advance. On a failure, they are discovered by one {@creature Fungal Abomination|DMSecretWeapon|fungal abomination} and two {@creature wolf||wolves} who look to be infected with spores. Once they deal with the raiding party, they automatically succeed on any future checks made to advance.

entries.name: Guards at the Portal
entries: The base of the valley is misty and humid, with damp, springy undergrowth that winds through long, mushroom-lined corridors. They lead up to a brown fungal altar, raised with steps like the caps of oyster mushrooms. The altar supports a massive orb of rainbow light, which twinkles and shines and teases of worlds beyond. Standing in front of this altar are two mushroom people with spears.

Two {@creature Fungal Abomination|DMSecretWeapon|fungal abominations} stand guard at the altar. Near them, on either side of the path, are two {@creature violet fungus||violet fungi} and two {@creature shrieker||shriekers}. Characters who succeed on a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) check can identify them; otherwise, the mushrooms lie in wait for unsuspecting travelers. Any creature who gets within 30 feet of a shrieker triggers its Shriek ability, alerting the guards immediately.

{@b Light at the Altar.} The light at the altar is a portal to Celica's pocket dimension. It does not hurt the characters to pass through, though it does feel as though characters are swimming underwater.

entries.name: Infecting Mushrooms
entries: {@adventure Map 3|SecretsOfMyceliaGrove|1|Adventure Map 3}

The portal in the grove leads to a clearing in a pocket dimension where Celica the spore-infected druid works her old magic. She gives life to the mushrooms and sends them out through the mirror pool in the center of the map to bolster their numbers. The characters emerge from this very same mirror pool and find themselves face-to-face with Celica.

You surface from a well, surrounded by moss-covered stones. Ancient mushrooms, larger than oaks, tower over you. Surrounding this well and its tiny, moss-covered altar, is a bog full of noxious-smelling green water. All is green and brown, life and death. An ancient woman, adorned with decaying antlers and caked in dirt, stands over you with an accusing glare. "Interlopers!" she croaks. "Destroy them!"

Celica is infected by the cursed spores herself, too far gone to be reasoned with. When the heroes arrive, she rouses her troops to expel or exterminate the intruders. Three {@creature Fungal Abomination|DMSecretWeapon|fungal abominations} and four of the townsfolk (use {@creature commoner} stats) emerge from the bog water and attack. Celica uses the {@creature Fungal Druid|DMSecretWeapon} stat block.
{@b Bog Water.} The bog water is {@quickref difficult terrain||3} for characters with no swim speed. Any character who begins their turn in bog water takes 2 Poison damage.

{@b Civilians.} All of the missing townsfolk mentioned in Part 1 are here, with a body full of mind-control spores. They attack the characters at Celica's instruction, but none of them have actually begun to physically transform into fungal abominations. It isn't too late to save them. A character can get rid of their condition with the {@spell dispel magic} spell, or similar magic. Killing Celica also ends the effect.

{@b Destroying Celica.} When Celica dies, the pocket dimension grows weaker until it collapses. Any character with knowledge of magic realizes they have 30 seconds (5 rounds of combat) to escape through the well before the place implodes on itself. Players who fail to make it out in time are thrown, painfully, back into their home dimension, landing {@condition unconscious} with 0 hit points (but stable) at a random location within 20 miles of the valley. Non-player characters who do not escape die as the dimension collapses.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The townsfolk are grateful for the characters removing the druid, but their monetary reward depends on how many civilians were saved. If their loved ones die, they need the money for burial costs. Mayor Eban gives the characters 300 gold for stopping the druid, and an extra 50 for each civilian who returns to Tuckertout safely.

data.name: Pixies in the Sticks
entries: The fey have rules, and guests to their world would do well to abide by them. Yes, these rules are different from the mundane world's rules. Sure, the fey have nigh endless generations of customs that come in conflict with one another. And yes, the magical consequences of breaking their rules can be as severe as your tongue bleeding whenever you speak out of turn.

This adventure offers level 1 heroes (3–6 players) a chance to learn and navigate these rules as they are hired as security for a fey celebration in the material plane. They'll be asked to keep the event safe and free of uninvited guests without offending the unpredictable fey.

entries.name: Background
entries: Haute and Rhost Cocoacup are {@creature pixie} sisters from a small noble family (just the two of them, in fact!) whose bickering causes anyone within a mile of them to start sweating. Haute wants to expand their domain and garner the adoration of both the fey and mundane worlds, while Rhost wants to keep their presence to the fairy realm, and keep her younger sister safe.

Haute is celebrating. She has molted into new wings and wants to host the celebration in the material plane to the dismay of her big sister. In response, Rhost has gathered enough mundane money to hire a few heroes to ensure Haute and the other fey nobles have a good time undisturbed by uninvited bugaboos.

The celebration is set to take place in the Leafy Scent Woods, the unspoken domain of the Valentine circle of witches. They have long cut off the woods from outsiders, including those who live at the nearby Briar Town; typically, none can enter the woods save the witches themselves. The Valentine circle will take claim of any power that they can get their hands on, whether it originates from the material plane or the fairy realm.

entries.name: Setup
entries: While looking at a job board in Briar Town, either individually or as a group, the heroes notice a very, very tiny posting in {@language Common} that reads
PLEASE PROTECT MY SISTER
LEAFY SCENT WOODS
50 GOLD EACH

stamped with a cocoa bean insignia. The woods are about an hour outside of town, where Rhost Cocoacup, a {@creature pixie} in pied clothing and red butterfly wings, hides in wait. When the heroes arrive, she reveals herself as the client and guides them to the party.

Rhost explains to the heroes that they will be guarding her sister's party from outsiders and kicking out anyone already inside who was not invited. She is unaware exactly who Haute invited, but she knows for certain she invited Auntie Yuvee, and there are five official guests; 10 gold pieces will be removed from the reward for each guest not in attendance when Haute makes her grand appearance, and 10 will be removed for each uninvited guest that stays at the party. She'll pay at sundown as long as her sister Haute has a good time.

entries.name: Every Witch Way You Look
entries: A hero with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 15 or higher will notice that they're being watched from every corner of the woods. The Valentine circle of witches are using {@spell arcane eye||arcane eyes} to spy on the intruders, seeking the right moment to strike. If this information is brought up to Rhost, she pleads with the heroes to deal with them discreetly to prevent an inter-realm incident (or worse, ruin Haute's party).

entries.name: Rules of the Fey
entries: Before splitting off from the heroes to go help Haute get ready, Rhost gives them several common rules of the fey that they'll need to observe both to avoid offending the nobles and to avoid getting hurt:

items: The fey must leave if they were not invited—do not invite them yourself. Auntie Yuvee was invited for certain. There are 5 official guests.
Never thank the fey—be grateful. If you say thank you to a fey, you are magically bound to give them something in return.
If a fey asks to have something—turn them down. They will keep something offered no matter how intangible it is.
Steady your hand and sheath thy blade—invite blood and, in turn, blood will be paid.
The older and far-traveled fey may have other rules they abide by. If you break their rules, apologize and cover your mouth. They will look past a transgression once.

entries: After reviewing the rules, she wishes the heroes luck and flitters off.

entries.name: Haute's Party
entries: {@adventure Map 1|PixiesInTheSticks|1|Adventure Map 1}

The party is hosted in a cool, canopy-covered glade in the Leafy Scent Woods, protected by a thick underbrush surrounding the area. A pool of water burbles on the top of a stone ridge in the back of the glade. It flows down the side of the ridge and forms a stream that bends three times before trickling deeper into the woods.

Airy music dances along the stream and the leaves of the trees slowly shift colors. Several groups of partygoers congregate along the bends of the water sharing gossip about one another and the Cocoacup Sisters. Once in a while, a patron breaks from their conversation to dip their glass under the falling water and sip the wine they caught.

entries.name: Atop the Ridge
entries: Rhost and Haute, a {@creature pixie} in striped clothing and yellow wings, flutter in and out of the hollow behind the pool of water as they prepare for the main ceremony. Whenever one of the sisters raises her voice, everyone in the party starts to sweat. This seems to occur about every 20 minutes. Rhost and Haute are extremely busy and aren't paying attention to the guests right now—it will be up to the heroes to maintain order without their guidance as the sisters prepare.

A huge pane of glass lays flat near the side of the water. If a hero examines it, Haute will call out to them to help stand it up at the front of the ridge which requires a {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. When lifted, it acts like a magnifying glass for the upcoming ceremony.

entries.name: Guess the Guests
entries: Two of the seven guests of the party aren't supposed to be here. By speaking with the guests, heroes can learn gossip and piece together who does not belong. They must be careful, however—many of the guests are tricksy, even those who have been invited. A hero can attempt a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check during a conversation to figure out if a guest is trying to play a trick on them. If the heroes insult an invited patron, they will leave in a huff:

rows: A jolly, fatherly brownie (use the {@creature deep gnome} stat block) adorned with shells and colored glass. He enjoys stories of adventure both heroic and tragic.
Trey and Shorewill were invited at the same time.
Trey will ask a hero for their father's name, claiming to be their new father if they give it.
A gruff {@creature satyr} clad in animal pelts and covered in mud. While terse and off putting, they're interested in peoples' bonds and what motivates them to be who they are.
Jihn was the second to last guest to be invited.
Jihn will pretend to pick up a gold coin off the ground and attempt to give it back to a hero in hopes of getting them to say thank you.
An adonis of a {@creature dryad} in a mix of autumn and spring colors who loves everything beautiful. He loves to talk about the trinkets and mementos that people cherish.
Puttup was the second guest to arrive at the party.
Puttup will compliment a hero up and down about their looks to get them to say thank you. He will then demand an invite, which the hero who thanked him is obligated to give.
A demure {@creature merfolk} that mainly stays in the stream throughout the party. She shares tales of her people's conquest in wars with a deadpan delivery.
Shorewill was the third guest to be invited after Yuvee.
Shorewill will ask a hero "to give her a five" holding out her hand for a high five. A hero that claps her hand has all 5's that they roll on their dice from now on count as 0's.

A loud and proud {@creature green hag} who wears a Victorian upper class outfit. She likes to talk about humans she's tricked, marriages she's ruined, and stray pets she's taken into her hut and now treats like her children.
Yuvee recommended Snug should be invited last so he would be more likely to accept.
Yuvee knows what the heroes are doing and will directly ask them to let her into the party. If any of them fall for it, she laughs at them, and all Insight DCs go up by 1.
An elegant {@creature harpy} with long flowing robes that looks down her nose all the time. She shares stories about the Cocoacup Sisters' childhoods that aren't true.
Mai-Mai was the first guest to be invited.
After sharing her gossip, Mai-Mai will ask a hero to "let me in [pause] tell me a secret" to get an invite.
Snug is a motley dressed {@creature bugbear} that is nervous around the heroes. This is his first time in the mundane world.
Snug was invited after Puttup showed up.
Snug doesn't play tricks, but if a hero is nice to him, he'll point out another guest's trick.

entries.name: Optional Encounter: Witch Hunt
entries: If you feel like the pace of the adventure invites combat during the party, have a guest point out the curious behaviour of a quartet of {@creature deer} just outside the clearing. If the party goes to investigate, the animals will reveal themselves to be disguised Valentine witches (use the {@creature Coven Acolyte|DMSecretWeapon} stat block) and move to attack the party.

The heroes will either need to drive the Valentines away, defeat them non-lethally, or slay them at a place away from the event. If a witch manages to make it past them and into the event, the party must expel her swiftly and without troubling the other guests. If the witch causes sufficient ruckus, an invited guest may leave in disgust (at the GM's discretion).

entries.name: Ceremony of Wings
entries: When the party reaches its peak, Rhost calls for everyone's attention. On top of the ridge, Haute proceeds to molt her yellow wings for cyan ones in a brilliant display of color filling the entire glade. If the magnifying glass on the ridge was set up, each hero watching the ceremony feels warm and gains Inspiration.

entries.name: The Valentine Witches Attack!
entries: As the ceremony concludes, dark clouds seep out of the ridges in the rock and coalesce in front of the first stream and bend into the form of a tall witch wearing dark purple robes.

The witch introduces herself as Lady Brew Wary of the Valentines (use the {@creature Coven Elder|DMSecretWeapon} stat block) and calls upon her fellow witches to take their territory back. She is joined by 6 witches (use the {@creature Coven Acolyte|DMSecretWeapon} stat block), minus any witches the party defeated if they fought in the optional {@adventure Witch Hunt|PixiesInTheSticks|0|Optional Encounter: Witch Hunt} chapter.

In the event that a hero invites Brew Wary to the party, it's possible for the heroes to talk the Valentine witches down with a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. However, Rhost will refuse to pay the heroes for breaking the rules.

entries.name: Fairy Well Then
entries: The heroes must protect Haute and the guests from the Valentines. If Haute, Rhost, or a guest is killed, it sparks an invasion of fey creatures into the forest and beyond, which doubtless will impact the local kingdoms and principalities.

Otherwise, if the heroes manage to fend off the Valentines and keep the peace, Haute is overjoyed by her party and Rhost invites the heroes to join them in the fairy realm as their royal guards for life. If the heroes accept, they live a life of comfort and luxury as royal guards in the fairy realm. If not, they receive their agreed upon reward as the fairies and their guests depart back to their home.

data.name: Colosseum of Hags
entries: Sometimes you make a small mistake, you miss a little lie, or you blink at the precise wrong moment. Sometimes your lapse of judgement leads you into the employ of a hag, and not even a particularly powerful one. And sometimes the fate of a region rests in you championing this hag against the champions of other hags in gladiatorial combat.

The Colosseum of Hags is an adventure for 4–5 level 4 heroes who compete in a high stakes tournament against several other teams in a magically changing arena. They will aid a hag in defeating her peers and becoming the next High Nona of the Haglauf games.

entries.name: Background
entries: Among hags, there is one individual among them who has the title of High Nona that gets to dictate what is 'good manners' when dealing with common people. Every 300 years, hags and high witches from across the land meet in secret to conjure a massive arena and compete for the title. The hags (normally) don't fight themselves, but have their familiars and thralls compete as a show of their unmistakable power and experience.

This has gone on for thousands of years with hags living in relative comfort on the outskirts of mundane society. But within the last 300 years, so called "heroes" have been aggrieving hags in their own homes for little cause, treating them like monsters, and there's been a rally cry among the hags to change good manners around proactively conquering towns in response.
That's fine and dandy for the powerful aunties or iron bound covens, but one craven hag has no intent on giving people more of a reason to take her head.

entries.name: Setup
entries: The heroes wake up groggy and fully armed in a straw hut, where Madam Eileen, a basic witch with one horn and a long, pointy nose, is preparing bowls of stew for them. Eileen is in possession of each of their souls. Eileen is under the protection of a powerful enchantment that is not of her own design. Whenever a hero attempts to attack Eileen, they must succeed on a {@dc 29} Charisma saving throw. On failure, the hero is overwhelmed by a magical compulsion to ask Madam Eileen for forgiveness. Should a player overcome this enchantment, or should Eileen be forced to fight across the adventure, she uses the {@creature Basic Witch|DMSecretWeapon|basic witch} stat block.

The heroes don't remember much—the players should each take turns recalling what happened to their hero the night before and how Madam Eileen got ahold of their soul. This is an opportunity for players to construct their own backstory to the adventure; consider ways to tie their choices and explanations into Madam Eileen's behaviour (or even the behaviour of other hags).
The timid Madam Eileen relies on disguises and cunning to get what she wants, and only threatens violence when it's absolutely necessary.

Eileen has full intention of giving back the heroes' souls after they compete in the Haglauf for her, where they will be pitted against other hags in a giant arena. If any hero wants a bigger reward or does not care for their soul, they can make a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check to convince her to offer them either an uncommon magic item of their choice or knowledge of where to find a rare magic item they desire.

entries.name: Outside the Hut
entries: The straw hut sits among several little huts belonging to other hags in the middle of a tall wood forest. A dirt path leads a short hike away from the huts to a towering stone colosseum resting on two green dragon legs. A handful of hags cackle and fly overhead towards the colosseum, while other small travel huts trot from out of the woods to roost near Eileen's hut.

entries.name: Let's Haglauf!
entries: {@adventure Map 1|ColosseumOfHags|1|Adventure Map 1}

When the heroes are ready, Eileen leads them to the arena. The stands are filled with hags and witches from all over the world clamoring amongst themselves and shooting bolts of fire and lightning over the arena. Overlooking the colosseum from a throne is Miss Orthat, the current High Nona who has taken on the shape of an elderly {@creature androsphinx}. Orthat waits patiently for all competitors to enter the arena before calling for the games to begin.

The heroes will have to win three out of four games to secure the title for Madam Eileen. The game type, colosseum state, and their opponent are all determined on the following tables. Reroll if the heroes have already competed in the resulting game type or against the resulting opponent:

entries.caption: Game Type
rows: The teams are directly pitted against each other. Last competitor standing wins. You can find each team's party composition in the Opponent table below.

Each team's hag is positioned at the opposite side of the arena. The team that first grapples the opposing team's hag for one full round wins. (Have one player control Eileen in addition to their character). If no one has won after 3 rounds, a klaxon blares; the first team to grapple the opponent's hag wins immediately.

7 {@creature dust mephit||dust mephits}, 7 {@creature magma mephit||magma mephits}, and 7 {@creature ice mephit||ice mephits} are released into the arena. They take their turns on initiative count 20, 15, and 10 respectively. The party must defeat as many mephits as possible in 2 full rounds. The GM controls the mephits, who attack randomly. While the party bust mephits, an enemy team is doing the same, off-screen (they do not roll initiative or take turns). After 3 rounds, any remaining mephits are considered killed by the opposing team. If the party kills 11 or more mephits, they win. Any less, and the opposing side wins.

Hags swarm the arena, combining and taking on the shape of 1 {@creature adult red dragon} and 1 {@creature adult green dragon}. The team with the most competitors standing after three rounds wins. Lethal damage in this game does not result in death, and heroes do not die as a result of failed death saving throws. If all competitors on one side drop, the other team wins. Any competitor that flees the arena is disqualified.

entries.caption: Colosseum State
rows: {@adventure Map 3|ColosseumOfHags|1|Adventure Map 3} (A creature that enters the area of a flame jet for the first time on their turn or starts their turn there takes {@damage 1d12} Fire damage)
{@adventure Map 4|ColosseumOfHags|1|Adventure Map 4} ({@quickref difficult terrain||3} for creatures without a swim speed)

entries.caption: Opponent
rows: Aunt Tazel (Use the {@creature Green Hag} stat block)
A bubbly green hag wearing a blood smeared apron who always talks about how tasty her present audience looks. She wants to make eating people in broad daylight more acceptable.
2 {@creature black pudding||black puddings}, 4 {@creature ochre jelly||ochre jellies}
Mother Martuche (Use the {@creature Oni} stat block)
A menacing, muscular hag with a short temper. She wants to become High Nona so that it becomes good manners to turn people into furniture.
Granny Sniftly (Use the {@creature Medusa} stat block)
A heavyset poison hag that can't speak or hear. She can tell what's going on in a person's heart by the way they smell. She's only competing for the thrill of the competition.
Lady Hearshell (Use the {@creature Sea Hag} stat block)
A stunning sea hag that is always accompanied by string music playing from seemingly nowhere. Her goal as High Nona is to make it impolite not to sing while talking to others.
Miss Sienna (Use the {@creature Night Hag} stat block)
Madam Eileen's older, more imposing night hag sister. She's stern, dismissive, and ready to plunge the world into darkness so hags never have to look upon disappointment ever again.
Bibi Bernadead (Use the {@creature Vampire Spawn} stat block)
A gaunt blue hag (use the {@creature vampire spawn} stat block) that wants to enlist all people and hags into her coven. (And by coven, she means her undead army.)

entries.name: Between Games
entries: The colosseum needs to be cleaned and reset after each game, providing the heroes an opportunity to take a short rest and explore the premises. If a hero left a strong impression on an NPC, they might be sought out before getting a chance to explore.

entries.name: Opponent
entries: Whether they accuse the heroes of cheating, attempt to recruit a hero to their own team, or attempt to sabotage the heroes with a baked good, the opponent will usually be out to weaken Madam Eileen's team. It's important to note that a hag won't directly attack another hag or a team member outside of a game they are participating in, but they might try one of the following tricks.

entries.caption: Hag Tricks
rows: A hag attempts to pass a poisoned drink to a player, either directly or by interfering with the catering.
A player who drinks a poisoned goblet must succeed on a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} Poison damage.
A hag attempts to weave a beguiling enchantment over a hero disguised as innocent conversation.
The hero must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or have a {@dice 1d4} penalty to attack rolls and saving throws until the end of the next game in the colosseum.
A hag attempts to cast Delayed Polymorph on a hero.
The hero must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or be polymorphed into a {@creature baboon} the moment they next roll initiative.
A hag attempts to distract the party whilst sneaking in some reinforcements.

The party all roll Wisdom ({@skill Perception}). If anyone scores a result of 20 or above, they spot the reinforcements entering the barracks, who swiftly flee. If they fail to spot them, the next game of Head to Head Battle, Capture the Hag, or Survive sees 4 {@creature ghoul||ghouls} join the side against the party.

entries.name: Miss Orthat
entries: Miss Orthat (the current High Nona) is tired and ready to give up her title. She passes no judgement on the intentions of the next High Nona as this tradition has gone on for centuries without issue. She'll meet any attempt to convince her otherwise with the threat of being turned into a potted plant.

The current High Nona knows the history of each creature that has entered the colosseum. She's willing to answer questions in exchange for taking a part of the inquirer's history for herself—if the individual was knighted by a queen, Miss Orthat would now have that title instead.

entries.name: Fan in the Crowd
entries: One of the heroes may gain a fan for their performance in the games, at the GM's discretion. This might occur if they score a critical success, engage in a particularly daring or outlandish activity, or earn victory without taking a point of damage. Once in between each game, a hero can meet their fan and gain a Witch's Kiss. Whenever the hero fails a D20 Test, they can use a Witch's Kiss to roll a {@dice d10} and add the number rolled to the d20.

entries.name: The Colosseum
entries: The heroes can interact with the colosseum from the outside by scratching its legs. It doesn't get much recognition as an animated being and generally appreciates the attention. If the heroes form a bond with the colosseum, they can choose the state of the colosseum during the next game.

entries.name: A Hag Above
entries: If the heroes lose at Haglauf, Madam Eileen will violently call for a Hag Royale, pitting all opponents and hags against each other in a furious battle to the death. This will almost certainly result in the death of all in attendance, but it's also a fantastic opportunity for the heroes to escape while everyone is preoccupied with the outburst.

If Eileen becomes the next High Nona, she makes good on all the rewards she promised the heroes and then asks each hero for a hug before they leave. If all heroes accept her hug, they each pass out a few moments later and wake up in a nearby town with no memory of the colosseum or the hag games.

data.name: The Last Sacrifice
entries: An adventure for 4–5 8th-level characters. Expected length: 2–3 play sessions.
{@b Content Warnings:} Human Sacrifice

entries.name: Synopsis
entries: For one hundred years, the city of Verlanis has enjoyed a rich and bountiful relationship to the massive Loch Balen, the lake it sits upon. Verlanis has made its fortune in the fishing and trading industries. The town never floods or wants for potable water. It is, the locals say, like magic. But Verlanis hides a dark secret: the lord of Loch Balen, the dreaded water deity Ochtore, grants them these gifts in exchange for human sacrifice. Every ten years a young, unmarried woman must climb to the top of the Balen Dam and wait for Ochtore's waves to take her. The people of Verlanis then honor her, and Ochtore, during the local Festival of Water ten days afterward. This year, the village offered no sacrifice. Furious, Ochtore called back the waters of Loch Balen and plunged Verlanis into a terrible drought.

entries.name: Story Hooks
entries: Use one of the following to hook your characters into this story:

items: The heroes arrive just in time for Verlanis's Festival of Water to find the city completely dried up.
A merchant pays the heroes to investigate why they're no longer receiving fish shipments from their contact in Verlanis.

The heroes arrive in response to a public summons by Priest Set, high cleric of Verlanis. Riders speak of a great fortune promised to those who can provide an answer to the priest's mysterious problem.

entries.name: Verlanis
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|TheLastSacrifice|1|Adventure Map 1})

The city of Verlanis, built into the cliffs overlooking Loch Balen, stands still; its ancient stone buildings with their brightly-colored roofs show no sign of life. The great Balen Dam, a marvel of modern architecture, towers over the city, casting shadows over not a glimmering lake, but a dry and dusty gulch. No water—not so much as a drop—trickles down from the dam's mouth, though the floodgates gape open. Circling gulls cry out overhead, desperate for relief from the drought.

Two teenage boys play at the base of the dam, picking through dried-out corpses of aquatic life. They do not notice as the wind kicks up around them, and the dust coalesces into two humanoid and vaguely threatening forms.

The boys (two {@creature commoner||commoners} named Ross and Kenney) are being terrorized by two {@creature air elemental||air elementals}. The monsters only want to cause destruction, not to kill, so they only knock the children out. If the characters don't intervene, the elementals attack them once they're finished with the children. After two rounds of combat, or the elementals are dealt with (whichever comes first), an old man exits his home and urges the characters to bring the children inside.

entries.name: Mayor's Home
entries: The old man is Tamhas, the mayor of Verlanis. He tends to the wounded children and thanks the characters for their help. Kenney is his grandson, and if the boy is awake he serves his grandfather and guests tea before Tamhas dismisses him to his bedroom.

Tamhas tells the heroes of Verlanis's troubles with Ochtore and the drought. If the characters ask why the city has chosen this year to refuse to cooperate with Ochtore, Tamhas offers very little explanation besides, "there was no woman who fit the requirements."

A character who succeeds on a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check understands that Tamhas is hiding something (see "{@adventure The Truth About Kenney|TheLastSacrifice|0|The Truth About Kenney}" below). Characters can attempt a {@dc 25} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check to get Tamhas to tell the truth. Mentioning the name 'Moira' reduces the DC by 10.
When the conversation draws to a close, Tamhas asks the characters to escort the other boy, Ross, back to his home.

entries.name: Exploring Verlanis
entries: Most of the homes are shut up tight to avoid the terror of the elementals raging outside. A few stores are open, however. Every time the characters leave the indoors to venture into Verlanis, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a 5 or higher, they are accosted by another {@creature air elemental}.

entries.name: Apothecary
entries: Auntie Claire runs the apothecary in town. Many of her plants have withered in the drought. Her stock is low and her resources few. She does, however, have six {@item Potion of Water Breathing||potions of water breathing} in stock. The characters may need these to confront Ochtore. She sells them for 300 gold apiece, higher than the usual asking price of 200. If characters can magically make her plants grow, such as with the {@spell Plant Growth} spell, she reduces the price to 150 each.

{@b What Auntie Knows.} Auntie Claire laments the drought but knows nothing "could be done." Most of the children born lately have been boys, except, she mentions, "Mayor Tamhas's sweet granddaughter Moira. We lost her a few months after the last sacrifice. Such sorrow in this town. That's probably why he took in that orphan boy Kenney. They look about the same age."

entries.name: Cathedral of the Falling Rain
entries: Priest Set sits in residence as the clergyman in the Cathedral of Falling Rain. Despite its grandiose name, the cathedral appears little different to the many other ancient stone buildings that flank Verlanis' cobbled streets. If the party is here in response to Set's summons, he welcomes them gladly and speaks at length of great jewels and gold that he can offer them. He requests the party meet him later that afternoon, by the port bastion (see {@adventure Map 2|TheLastSacrifice|1|Adventure Map 2}), but offers no further information about their quest. If questioned about the drought, Set says little, other than that he will stop at nothing to save the city. A successful {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check will reveal that despite his stoic exterior, he is a man broken by grief and fear. He says little else on the matter, but does, however, quiz the heroes on their combat capabilities, taking particular interest in any women among them.

While at the cathedral, heroes can request the cleric's services.
