For 500 gold pieces, Priest Set will cast one of the following spells: {@spell death ward}, {@spell greater restoration}, {@spell heroes' feast}, or {@spell reincarnate}. If Set casts {@spell death ward} over a party member, he will subtly alter the spell to ensure it fails, leaving the target unaware of any subterfuge. A hero with {@spell death ward} in their spell list can identify this interference with a successful {@dc 23} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. If a hero confronts Set on this matter, he will apologize for his error and cast the spell successfully.

{@b Priest Set's Plan.} Unbeknownst to the heroes, Priest Set has a desperate plan. With no sacrifice among the townspeople, he intends to kill or capture the party and offer them to Ochtore in the hope of saving Verlanis.

entries.name: Ross's Home
entries: Ross lives with his parents Sandra and Louis on one of the higher cliffs. Ross's parents thank the characters for keeping their son safe and invite them inside for a meal. They have nothing to offer the characters except what they know about Ochtore and his legend:

items: Ochtore lives in an underwater palace at the center of the lake.
The gate to Ochtore's palace only opens when he wishes it to—sacrifices and allies can enter, but no one else has seen the inside.
The last sacrifice was ten years ago: Sandra's sister, Isabel.
Kenney is Tamhas's adopted grandson. Tamhas adopted the boy a few months after Isabel was sacrificed.

entries.name: At the Port Bastion
entries: ({@adventure Map 2|TheLastSacrifice|1|Adventure Map 2})

After the heroes finish exploring the town, their route will naturally lead them to the port bastion. Here, Priest Set has laid a trap. In a burst of radiance and flame he confronts the party accompanied by a divine golem, demanding they lay down their arms and consent to be sacrificed to Ochtore. The priest is a desperate man, driven beyond rationality by fear of the starvation and death soon to be wrought upon Verlanis by the endless drought. The party may attempt to talk him down. Should they do so, they will require a {@dc 24} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check to succeed. In any other outcome, Set attacks mercilessly, but with a sorrowful heart. Roll Initiative.
The heroes are fighting {@creature Priest Set|DMSecretWeapon} and a {@creature Divine Golem|DMSecretWeapon|divine golem}.
Should the heroes kill Set, he will implore them in his dying breath to do what they must to bring water back to Verlanis. If they keep him alive, he can be chained in the Cathedral to await trial.

The heroes may try to sacrifice Set to Ochtore. Doing so will require them to descend into the dam, continuing the adventure as outlined in the following chapters. Attempting to sacrifice Set will kill him, but not placate Ochtore, unless the cruel god can be deceived into believing Set is an unmarried woman.

entries.name: The Truth About Kenney
entries: News of Set's death or capture spreads swiftly through Verlanis. Tamhas, the mayor, brings the heroes to his home before asking them to explain the situation. Upon understanding the series of events, he thanks the party and apologises, once again articulating the hopeless predicament of the town. During this conversation with the mayor, a hero who succeeds on a {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check notices Tamhas' grandson, Kenney, eavesdropping from outside the door.

In reality, Kenney isn't Tamhas's grandson; she's his granddaughter. As an eighteen-year-old girl, Kenney (or Moira as she's actually called) is the Verlanis resident who best fits the description of the sacrifice. Tamhas has hidden her these last ten years to prevent her from becoming the sacrifice. Moira, sheltered and protected, does not learn about Ochtore until she overhears her grandfather speaking of it. She believes it is her duty to turn herself in to Ochtore and will stop at nothing to do so. If she gets the opportunity to speak to characters away from her grandfather, she begs them to take her with them to Ochtore's subnautic palace. She knows the way, and she knows the gates will not open without a sacrifice who fits the description. "You need me," she insists. "Verlanis needs me."

Nobody, not even a subdued Set if the party kept him alive, asks the heroes to confront Ochtore. They view him as a deity, someone who can be defied but not subdued. The heroes must choose to make this journey themselves. If the heroes do not escort Moira or decide to journey to the center of the lake, Moira runs away on her own to fulfill her duty. Distraught, Tamhas pleads with the characters to bring her home safely. He offers as a reward every resource Verlanis has available, including the 4,000 gold in the town's coffers. He would rather destroy Verlanis than give up his granddaughter.

entries.name: A Dangerous Drought
entries: The characters must climb down the other side of the dam and head to the center of Loch Balen, where Ochtore resides. The lake is twenty miles wide, meaning the characters must traverse about ten miles to get from Verlanis to the lake center. When the heroes make it to the top of the dam, read or paraphrase the following:

The dry basin of Loch Balen stretches for miles, its dirt cracked and dusty as though it hasn't seen water for generations. Forest life at the edges has already begun to thirst and wither. In the center of the basin, far below and away, stands a massive cylindrical structure made entirely of water: the Subnautic Throne, where Ochtore waits for the city of Verlanis to correct their mistake.

entries.name: Elemental Hazards
entries: Getting to the lake center requires about six hours of travel, and the characters' enemy Ochtore controls the weather. For each hour, roll on the Elemental Hazards table below to determine what happens. If you'd like to use a grid map while running these hazards, use {@adventure Map 2|TheLastSacrifice|1|Adventure Map 2}.

entries.name: Corpsenado
entries: Wind kicks up a minor tornado, picking up all the surrounding fish corpses. All characters, including Moira, must succeed on a {@dc 13} Strength saving throw or take 10 Bludgeoning damage. A character can give themselves Disadvantage on this test to protect Moira from the damage.

entries.name: Lightning Strike
entries: Lightning strikes at the exact area the characters travel in. All characters must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 10 Lightning damage. A character can give themselves Disadvantage on this test to protect Moira from the damage.

entries.name: Spontaneous Combustion
entries: The wind and dryness collude to create a spontaneous fire in the gulch. Everything around the characters ignites and burns, from the corpses to the characters themselves, in a 60-foot square. So long as characters are in this area, they are on fire. A creature takes {@damage 1d6} Fire damage when they end their turn inside the fire area. Additionally, a creature must choose one nonmagical item they wear or carry. That item begins to burn up. Use the burn table to determine what happens to that item based on its item type. An item can only be chosen once for this purpose. A burned item can be repaired by a professional (such as a blacksmith) or through magic such as the {@spell Mending} cantrip.
A character can put out the fire with 1 gallon of water per 5-foot square.

entries.name: Stony Encounter
entries: Two {@creature earth elemental||earth elementals} rise from the dirt and question the characters. Why do they trespass upon Emperor Ochtore's land? If they have a sacrifice to bring, such as Moira, the elementals insist on bringing the sacrifice themselves. Characters must succeed on a {@dc 20} Charisma check to convince the elementals that they must bring the sacrifice to Ochtore themselves. On a failure, the elementals attack.
If the heroes have no sacrifice to bring, they must make some other excuse with a {@dc 25} Charisma check. On a success, the elementals let the characters pass. On a failure, they attack.

entries.name: Moira's Meddling
entries: If the characters brought Moira along, they must protect her. Stubborn and scrappy, Moira refuses to sit on the sidelines. But with {@creature commoner} stats, Moira is more of a liability than an asset.

If the characters did not bring Moira along but did nothing to discourage her in the previous chapter, she follows along behind them at a distance of 50 feet. For each hour of travel, have Moira roll a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check with Advantage (she's been hiding for most of her life). Any character whose passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) beats the result spots her immediately. If caught, she begs the characters to let her come along. They can only convince her not to tag along on a successful {@dc 25} Charisma ({@skill Deception}, {@skill Intimidation}, or {@skill Persuasion}) check.

If the characters are chasing after Moira, they can catch up to her if they push themselves to travel faster. Each character takes on one level of {@condition exhaustion} but catches up with her without delay. Additionally, characters who push themselves only roll 3 times on the hazards table instead of 6.

entries.name: Development
entries: Once the characters traverse the lake, they must find a way to enter the water sphere and confront Ochtore on the Subnautic Throne.

entries.name: The Subnautic Throne
entries: Ochtore, King of the Elements, Master of Thunder and Rain, sits in his palace at the centermost point of the dried-up lake. The palace is an open concept, with no walls or ceilings to speak of. It sits encased in a watery sphere with a magical seal that lets only those Ochtore desires cross.

entries.name: Crossing the Threshold
entries: The massive sphere of water towers overhead, protecting the fissure within—the long, deep, dark trench that leads where not even the sun dares go, where Ochtore waits for his sacrifice. The sphere's surface is calm and still, unperturbed by wind or creature.

When a creature touches the water sphere, it ripples outward from the point of contact. No creature can pass without express permission. The characters do not have magic powerful enough to defy the sphere. The only way in is to obtain permission—and the only ones Ochtore wants to let through are those who have brought his sacrifice.

Characters who have Moira in tow can walk in without issue. If the players brought Set as an attempted sacrifice, Ochtore does not accept him. Set dies upon touching the seal; the fluid is drained from his body as he shrieks and writhes before falling to the dirt as a dehydrated husk.

Heroes without any sacrifice may need to get creative. Any unmarried adult woman in their party can pass for a sacrifice. However, there is nothing inherently magical about an unmarried woman; the demand for one is Ochtore's own, based on mistaken ideals of purity.

His magic barrier cannot actually detect a creature's sex or marital status; it simply prevents creatures of Ochtore's choice from entering his domain. As such, the sphere can be bypassed by trickery. Heroes may use spells and disguises to dress up as a suitable sacrifice, or disguise Set as one. Characters who wish to deceive the sphere must succeed on a {@dc 22} Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check, which they make with Advantage if they use tools such as a {@item Disguise Kit} or magic such as the {@spell Alter Self} spell.
Once given permission, the characters can pass freely through the water sphere. The interior is made up of water, but those who pass with Ochtore's permission can breathe and speak freely here.

entries.name: Confronting Ochtore
entries: ({@adventure Map 3|TheLastSacrifice|1|Adventure Map 3})

Stone steps descend further into the trench until they reach a long bridge made of petrified wood and pearlescent shell. The bridge extends out to a throne made of prehistoric, multicolored coral, on a raised dais so high it could be considered a balcony at this point. Sitting in a wrought-iron chair, arms crossed, is a humongous man with long white hair couching a coral crown, his chest and arms exposed to reveal bright colored elemental tattoos on his blue skin that glow with magic. He sneers at the intrusion.

{@creature Ochtore|DMSecretWeapon} gives the characters one simple choice: leave the sacrifice or die. If they choose death, combat begins immediately. This combat encounter takes place underwater, so the map is considered {@quickref difficult terrain||3||Difficult Terrain} for creatures without a swim speed.

entries.name: Killing Ochtore
entries: If the characters kill Ochtore, the aftermath is immediate. His control over the weather dies with him, and the watery sphere erupts, sending water flowing into all corners of the lake. The sky that Ochtore had been holding up for days opens up, and the rain comes. The heroes must swim to safety. Those granted the ability to breathe and speak underwater lose this boon upon Ochtore's death.

{@b Rewards.} If the heroes loot Ochtore's throne, they can take his regalia (crown and clothing) worth 500 gp. They also find a collection of rare shells and corals worth 200 gp. If they return to Verlanis having saved Moira, Tamhas insists they stay for the Water Festival in ten days' time. He and the villagers of Verlanis repair any equipment that was damaged in this adventure.

entries.name: Sacrificing to Ochtore
entries: If the characters leave a sacrifice to Ochtore, he acknowledges that they did not need to meddle in the affairs of an unknown village and offers as thanks a collection of rare shells and corals worth 1,000 gp. He asks the characters to leave him to his meal. Once the characters exit the watery sphere, Ochtore undoes the drought, leaving them to find a way to the surface themselves. If the characters return to Verlanis, the townsfolk regard them with suspicion, though secretly all but Tamhas believe they performed a necessary evil to save the town. In ten years, who knows if future heroes will have the courage to do the same?

data.name: Night on Gnoll Mountain
entries: How does a hero deal with the inevitable? If your world is doomed if you don't take action, but you're personally doomed if you do take action, do you still have what it takes to climb the mountain to your death? Would you climb the mountain alongside someone else who had to make that choice? And can you reach the top of the mountain with gnolls biting at your heels?

Night on Gnoll Mountain invites 4–6 heroes at level 4 to race against the clock and trek up a treacherous cliffside. They will have to contend with ravenous hyenas, bloodthirsty gnolls, and a particularly cranky goat, all while protecting a young ward on the most important quest of his life.

entries.name: Background
entries: Centuries ago, a demon lord rampaged through the mundane world until they were imprisoned under a mountain by a powerful spellcaster. In an act of pettiness, the demon lord cursed the spellcaster's home city of Novel to be overrun by demons. The spellcaster then sacrificed their life to the demon lord in order to break the curse, but it was only enough to suspend the curse for 10 years.

Novel has trained mages in the years since to protect their way of life. The mages learn the Mountain Dance, scale the mountain, and perform the dance at its peak. The dance concludes with the death of the mage, and reinvigoration of the magical binds that restrain the demon lord below the mountain. However, Novel is little more than a village today, and the only mage they have left is a young half-elf.

Demons have already started appearing outside Novel. The mage has just finished learning the dance and is making preparations to climb the mountain. Time is of the essence, and the fate of the village (perhaps the fate of the entire region) rests on the youth's shoulders.

entries.name: Setup
entries: The heroes can begin the adventure in one of two ways:

items: The heroes are residents of Novel tasked by the village chief with being guardians to a young mage on his pilgrimage up the mountain. The chief is willing to pay every silver they have left to ensure his success (about 160 sp).

The heroes are traveling between towns when they meet the young mage on the side of the road surrounded by gnolls (see {@adventure Out of Gnollwhere|NightOnGnollMountain|0|Out of Gnollwhere} below). The bodies of two warriors lay dead at his feet.

entries: The mage (use the {@creature cult fanatic} stat block) is a 13-year-old half-elf named Camic. He is the last mage of Novel after his grandmother performed the dance 10 years ago. Camic is quiet and usually lost in thought over his present circumstances. When a situation starts to look bad, he nervously mutters to himself as he tries to work out a solution on his own.

The mountain is very close. It'll take a day's trip from Novel to reach the peak of the mountain without any setbacks. However, gnolls are starting to rise out of pools of blood along the road and across the mountain. More blood pools are appearing by the hour and could reach unstoppable numbers by tomorrow morning.

entries.name: Out of Gnollwhere
entries: {@adventure Map 1|NightOnGnollMountain|1|Adventure Map 1}

About a mile away from the village, Camic and his party are quickly surrounded by 8 {@creature gnoll||gnolls}. The gnolls primarily focus on killing the weakest creature, but are easily distracted by freshly open wounds. When half the gnolls are defeated, the remaining gnolls run in the direction of the village. Novel can defend itself from a gnoll or two, but will be destroyed before long at the rate that these demons are starting to appear.

Camic will plead with the heroes to help him scale the mountain as soon as possible to save his village. He willingly explains most of the history of his pilgrimage and the Mountain Dance, but leaves out what happens to the mage after the ritual. A hero must succeed on a {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check before he becomes forthcoming about sacrificing himself.

entries.name: The Ascent
entries: The mountain is treacherous and punishes bad decisions swiftly. The party won't have many opportunities to rest once they start climbing and will need to choose their battles if they want to reach the top in time.

The GM rolls on the following encounter tables. The party is tasked with bringing Camic safely from one end of the map to the other. They must complete three encounters before reaching the top. They can choose to back down from an encounter and find another way up a maximum of two times.

entries.name: Mountain Conditions
entries: While adventuring on the mountain, use the following adjustments to the rules:

items.name: Thin Air
items.entry: Each hero has a -2 penalty to all Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution ability checks unless they are acclimated to a mountain environment.

items.name: Rough Earth
items.entry: Attacks that deal non-psychic damage over an area of effect turn the ground under that area into {@quickref difficult terrain||3}.

items.name: Rock Slide
items.entry: A creature that takes damage while occupying {@quickref difficult terrain||3} slides {@dice 1d4} × 5 feet towards the nearest cliff edge. A creature falls {@condition prone} and hangs on the edge if this movement would cause them to fall off.

entries.caption: Encounter Complication
rows: 4 {@creature gnoll||gnolls} and 2 {@creature giant hyena||giant hyenas} appear from bloodpools and attack the party. Each time the party receives this complication add one more gnoll.

Rocks or stalactites are falling from above. The party must reach the other side of the map before they are crushed. On Initiative count 0 of each round, each character must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d10} Bludgeoning damage. At the start of Initiative count 0, a hero can increase the DC by 5 for themself to decrease the DC by 5 for another character they can see within 15 feet.

A goat appears near the center of the map and attacks anyone that comes close to them. The goat is fabled by the people of Novel as a spirit of the mountain who tests the resolve of their mages. In reality, this goat is Billie, the original spellcaster who bound the demon lord below the mountain. Her spirit won't rest until she finds a way to seal him forever, ending the curse that forces mages to sacrifice themselves to maintain the magical restraints that bind the demon lord. Billie uses the {@creature Billie, The Greatest of All Time|DMSecretWeapon} stat block.
2 + {@dice 1d4} {@creature Phantasm|DMSecretWeapon|phantasms} appear at random locations across the map. Camic has Disadvantage on checks made to identify the phantasms as illusory creatures.
The GM picks two of the above complications for the encounter.

entries.name: A Harried Ritual
entries: {@adventure Map 5|NightOnGnollMountain|1|Adventure Map 5}

A shallow pond and gnarled tree greet the party at the top of the mountain. The pond comes up to the heroes' ankles and makes no sound when it's disturbed. The tree is covered in faces that look carved into the bark.

If Camic hasn't changed his mind, he will tepidly walk out to the center of the pond to begin the Mountain Dance. He needs to spend his action each turn dancing in the water for 30 seconds (5 rounds) in order to complete the pilgrimage. Each time he takes damage, the ritual requires 6 more seconds.

As soon as Camic starts dancing, bloodpools appear along the edge of the mountaintop. 4 {@creature gnoll||gnolls} and 1 {@creature Blood Gnoll Alpha|DMSecretWeapon|blood gnoll alpha} arise from the bloodpools and attack. 1 more {@creature gnoll} and 2 {@creature hyena||hyenas} appear at the start of each subsequent round of combat. If all gnolls and hyenas are defeated before the end of a round, 1 {@creature giant hyena} also appears at the start of the following round.

Should Camic finish the ritual, all the gnolls and hyenas in the region are vaporised to dust and blown away by a fierce, warm wind. One gnoll remains, however. It stands in the middle of the pond where Camic was dancing; as the wind blows across the mountain, the creature lets loose a terrified cry and scuttles down the cliffside, vanishing into the wilderness. The tree features a new face in its bark and Camic's body is nowhere to be found. The demon lord is trapped below the mountain for another decade.

entries.name: Another Way?
entries: The players might not be satisfied with Camic being resigned to his fate. If the heroes resolve to find an alternative solution, there are several avenues you can explore to extend the adventure until everyone is saved.

entries.name: The Demon Lord
entries: The heroes can choose to travel deep below the mountain and eradicate the demon lord once and for all. Though the demon used to be way beyond the caliber of mortal men, their power has atrophied in the decades since being imprisoned. The heroes will be aware however that at present, it is likely out of their league. Perhaps upon travelling the world and advancing their skills they might return and vanquish it forever?

Should the heroes seek to challenge the demon lord, you should choose a fiend stat block of a sufficient CR for the demon lord to challenge the party whilst still being achievable. A {@creature Nalfeshnee}, {@creature Marilith}, or {@creature Balor} are all thematic and challenging options should the party return upon gaining more power. If the party immediately seeks to challenge the demon lord upon completing this quest, allow them to level up to level 5 and use the {@creature Hezrou} stat block, accompanied by 4 {@creature gnoll||gnolls}, for a very challenging encounter.

entries.name: Billie the Greatest
entries: The goat spirit the heroes can encounter during the ascent can be pacified and potentially communicated with through magic, such as a {@spell speak with animals} spell. As the original spellcaster, Billie's old equipment and notes may still exist on the mountain and hold the key to a new ritual that doesn't require a sacrifice.

entries.name: Another Mage
entries: If one of the heroes is a spellcaster, they can learn the Mountain Dance from Camic and take his place on the pilgrimage. Upon completing the ritual, the hero transforms into a gnoll but can continue earning class levels (if you have GM's Secret Weapon Issue #31, you can use the Avestrosian gnoll playable species for their new form, and its species traits replace their current ones). Their true face appears on the tree; until the curse is lifted, their original appearance is locked away on the mountain.

data.name: Bold Strategy, Heroes

entries: There are several ways of measuring your growth as a hero. We all enjoy the obvious method of going toe to toe with bigger and badder villains! However, we don't often share what we've learned on our adventures with fresh followers and watch them learn from our mistakes. We used to be in their shoes, and now, we can help them to fend for themselves and see how far we've come.

Bold Strategy, Heroes sees 3–5 heroes at level 4 take a family of {@creature kobold||kobolds} under their wing as they make their final stand in the face of the Greencap gnomes. They'll train the kobolds, learn combo moves, and lead them into battle against wave after wave of ruthless gnome forces.

entries.name: Background
entries: The Snapsnarl kobolds used to be a tough family of kobolds known for their ferocity and cunning. They were the first, and perhaps the only, kobolds to fend off a blue greatwyrm and take one of their scales as a trophy. In the generations since, the Snapsnarls have contended over their prized scale with the Greencap gnomes, an infamous coalition of mercenaries. The gnomes refuse to relent until the kobolds are routed and the scale falls into their hands.

These kobolds have been whittled down to their weakest platoon to date. One more push could be all it takes for the Greencaps to finally claim victory, especially now that they're led by the infamous conqueror Nylus Pinebeard.

The current Snapsnarl matriarch, Captain No, knows her family can rise to the occasion with the right training and support. She's scouted the trade routes for weeks in search of anyone that could help them... for free. Her tactics needed to change.
Desperate, Captain No resorts to family secrets, empty threats, and begging.

entries.name: Setup
entries: The heroes should be familiar with each other before starting the adventure. Bold Strategy, Heroes can fit into an existing campaign as they travel between towns, or kick off on the trail a day away from starting a big job in the next town over.

Take note of each hero's combat style. Ideally, the party should feature at least one of each of the following roles. The adventure will provide the heroes new features based on these roles and will be referring to them throughout the text:

items.name: Skirmishers
items.entry: Melee and defensive heroes

items.name: Artillery
items.entry: Ranged and offensive magic wielding heroes

items.name: Cavalry
items.entry: Mobility and supportive heroes

entries: The action kicks off with Captain No, an orange {@creature kobold} with an eyepatch and a large blue scale pendant around her neck, calling out to the heroes just off the side of the trail. She's carrying and shaking a beehive.

"Be you heroes?!" the orange kobold snaps in {@language Common}. She's just barely audible over the roar of excitement held between her hands. As she draws closer, you notice the nondescript roar crystalize into buzzing, and the excitement she holds come into focus as a swirling hive of bees.

Captain No threatens to throw the beehive at the heroes if they ignore her plea. If they call her bluff ({@dc 8} Wisdom) or threaten her in return ({@dc 5} Charisma), she drops the beehive and immediately starts to grovel for help instead.

The kobold wants to bring the heroes back to the Snapsnarl familial grove to ready her family for an invasion. She's certain they won't survive on their own, but doesn't have any coins to buy reinforcements. All she has to offer are family secret battle techniques if the kobolds are trained well enough to show how they work.

entries.name: To the Grove
entries: Captain No has traveled far in search of heroes; the trip back to the Snapsnarl grove is long. Captain No will gladly share any information she can regarding the Greencap gnomes, the Snapsnarl kobolds, and the history of the region if asked.

After about an hour's travel, the group come to the edge of the woods, within which the Snapsnarl grove is hidden ({@adventure Map 1|BoldStrategyHeroes|1|Adventure Map 1}). Before Captain No can usher the heroes along the secret path, however, they're met with a thunderous roar as a {@creature troll} lumbers out of the forest towards them. The troll speaks in a gravelly voice:
"Curse the rivalries of kobolds and gnomes,
Your battles and rivalry disrupt my home,
Ye must answer a riddle, and answer it quick,
Or I'll bash the lot of ye, with this 'ere stick.
You will be me, if you choose to flee,
But you might roast, fry, or grill me for your tea,
I've tools to fly, but can't touch the sky,
Tell me, heroes, what am I?"
Captain No quails behind the heroes as the troll speaks. She recommends they answer the riddle correctly, lest the troll attack. The troll uses the standard {@creature Troll} stat block.
{@b The answer to the riddle is:} Chicken
If the heroes guess wrong, attack the troll, or do not give an answer in due course, the troll will attack.
If the party guesses correctly, the troll will allow them to pass freely, requesting that they put an end to the conflict swiftly, and without mercy for any who disturb his lands.

Quivering, Captain No continues to lead the party onward, dipping into a roundabout underground tunnel that leads to the grove. The path there is lined with countless small, shallow graves, each marked by an orange scale. The 19 plots toward the end of the tunnel are empty.

The tunnel opens up to an idyllic glade ({@adventure Map 1|BoldStrategyHeroes|1|Adventure Map 1}). Crystal clear ponds sit perfectly still, while an ever present gentle breeze rocks the trees and grass. Birds perch on the roughshod training dummies and spears stationed on each islet.
A small crowd of kobolds sit in a circle passing around a sweet smelling jug of nectar near the tunnel mouth, all while their weapons and shields lay nearby in a heap.

The heroes arrive near the top of the map in front of the 18 kobolds, who snap to attention as soon as Captain No clears her throat. She introduces her guests as master warriors who will ensure every one of them will survive the war and then invites any hero to give some words of encouragement as a {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. On success, the kobolds are eager to get started and the heroes gain two rerolls anyone can use during the following montage.

entries.name: Training Montage
entries: The captain estimates that the gnomes will storm the grove from the South in 5 days' time. She splits the kobolds up into three squads of six: the Skirmishers, the Artillery, and the Cavalry (stat blocks in the bestiary: {@creature Kobold Squad|DMSecretWeapon}). Each hero is then invited to help train the squad that matches their combat role.
The players are encouraged to come up with names for each kobold in their hero's squad, as well as a squad name.
The training montage is a three-round skill challenge that spans the course of the next three days. Players roll initiative, and each round plays out in the following way:

items: On a hero's turn, they describe the type of training they're doing with their squad and a skill they have proficiency in that they're relying on. The hero can't use that skill again for the rest of the montage.
The GM determines the most appropriate ability score for the training, and whether the difficulty is easy ({@dc 8}), normal ({@dc 11}), or hard ({@dc 14}).
The hero makes a check at the set difficulty using the ability score and skill. On a success, the Kobold Squad learns something. On a failure, they fail to grasp the technique.
The next hero takes their turn, repeating the process.
At the end of the round, each Kobold Squad who succeeded in learning something receives a Technique Point.

entries: At the end of the montage, the GM checks how many Technique Points each squad has. For each technique point, the squad gains one of the following bonuses (let the heroes who trained them decide):

items: They gain a +1 bonus to their attack and damage rolls
They can take the {@action Dash}, {@action Dodge}, or {@action Disengage} actions as a bonus action
They can take the {@action Help} action as a bonus action
They can use an action to restore a number of hit points to an ally within 5 feet equal to {@dice 1d8 + 2}
They have Advantage on initiative rolls
They have Advantage on the first attack roll they make in a combat encounter
Their AC increases by 1
Their speed increases by 10 feet
Allies within 5 feet of the squad have Advantage on attack rolls made against enemies within 5 feet of the squad

entries.name: Returning the Favor
entries: On the fourth day, Captain No and the kobolds have practiced enough that they can teach the heroes the Snapsnarl family's secret battle techniques. These techniques allow the heroes to combine their efforts together as a Reaction and quickly turn the tide of battle. Each hero learns one technique based on their role:

rows: An enemy attacks an ally adjacent to you.
An enemy comes within reach of an ally within 50 feet of you.
An ally takes damage within 30 feet of you.

items.name: Eyes on Me!
items.entry: As a reaction to an enemy attacking an ally within 5 feet of you, you distract the enemy. The enemy can choose to change its attack to target you, but no matter who it targets, it has Disadvantage on the attack roll.

items.name: Lock On!
items.entry: As a reaction to an enemy moving within reach of an ally within 50 feet of you, you strike with a ranged weapon or cantrip! Make a single ranged weapon attack or spell attack with a cantrip against the target at Disadvantage.

items.name: Move In!
items.entry: As a reaction to an ally taking damage within 30 feet of you, you can move up to your speed. If you end this movement within 5 feet of the triggering ally, you reduce the damage they take by half.

entries.name: The Gnomes Attack!

entries: "YOUR LEGACY ENDS HERE, SNAPSNARLS!"
It's faint, but it's sharp enough to pierce through the morning silence. Day five suddenly opens with the sounds of fire, marching boots, and quivering kobolds. The Greencap gnomes have arrived.

The heroes have enough time to get themselves and their squads into position near the midpoint on the map. When players are ready, the first wave of troops (see {@adventure Waves of Gnomes|BoldStrategyHeroes|0|Waves of Gnomes}) round the bend of the southwestern part of the map and everyone rolls for initiative.

The kobold squads are commanded by their squad's trainer (use the {@creature Kobold Squad|DMSecretWeapon} stat blocks, remembering to add any bonuses accrued in the training montage). If a squad was trained by multiple heroes, the heroes take turns each round commanding a squad.

entries.name: Waves of Gnomes
entries: Each round of combat, more Greencaps arrive on the scene. Their ranks are composed of the following units:

items: {@b Garden Guards} (use the {@creature Guard} stat block, but its size is Small) dive headfirst into melee combat from the south and prefer to target kobolds.
{@b Fieldshots} (use the {@creature Scout} stat block, but its size is Small) enter from the western treetops and typically target the heroes with their arrows.
{@b Ballooners} (use the {@creature Darkmantle} stat block, but it is a Small humanoid) appear skyborne near the middle of the map and try to drop down upon the tallest targets first.
{@creature Nylus Pinebeard|DMSecretWeapon}

entries: Most of the kobolds must survive five rounds of combat or the heroes must defeat Nylus to force the gnomes to retreat. If two or more Kobold Squads die, the gnomes overwhelm the glade (see {@adventure Gnowhere to Go?|BoldStrategyHeroes|0|A Bold Future, or Gnowhere to Go?} below). The following table outlines the composition of each wave of Gnomes.
Roll initiative for each group in combat:

entries.name: A Bold Future, or Gnowhere to Go?
entries: Should the gnomes be driven back, the Snapsnarl kobolds celebrate over jugs of juice and use this momentum to continue their training until they reclaim their former glory. Whenever the heroes need backup in the future, the Snapsnarl squads will be available for them to call upon.

If the gnomes successfully take over by eliminating more than two kobold squads, Captain No will force the heroes and any surviving kobolds to flee while she buys them time. More waves of gnomes eventually arrive to take over the grove and claim the captain's blue scale pendant, killing No in the process.

The remaining kobolds will mourn their leader and scatter for the time being, but might be convinced in the future to regroup when the heroes have grown more powerful should the party wish to lead a troop to retake the blue scale pendant from the Greencaps in honor of those who have fallen on this day.

No matter the outcome of this adventure, the heroes have made an enemy of the Greencap gnomes. For future quests, it's possible they'll appear to make life harder for the heroes in matters pertaining to mercenary work and bounty hunting.

data.name: Pirates on the Azure Skies
entries: An adventure for 5–6 15th-level characters.
{@b Content Warnings:} Human Trafficking, Falling from Large Heights

entries.name: Synopsis
entries: The sky city of Vedrgard is a stunning metropolis and a paradise for dragons and their descendants. Lately, many in Vedrgard have reported missing persons, all dragons and dragonfolk. However, the city's Queen Sigrunn, a copper dragon so ancient she can barely move, only takes notice when her granddaughter is counted among the disappearances. She offers a great reward for anyone who can discover who is behind the disappearances and return her granddaughter to her alive.

Miles away is a much smaller floating island, a lair for the pirate crew of Admiral Viggo. The island stays in the air through the use of an eternal flame powered by kidnapped dragons and their descendants' breath weapons. The characters' search takes them to this lair, where they'll have to plan a daring escape, for to remove the kidnapped dragonfolk means extinguishing the very fire that keeps the island in the air!

entries.name: Vedrgard
entries: Vedrgard—Weather's Keep—is an island that floats among the clouds, large enough to rival most earthbound city-states. Its rocky geography boasts beautiful mountainous vistas where the palaces of the nobility reside, overlooking the busy streets where merchants conduct business and the docks where sky-sailors make their trade.

The city is gilded on top and rotting from the bottom. The nobility are all dragons, and the descendants of dragons, such as dragonborn and kobolds, typically enjoy upper-class life in some of the wealthier districts. Folks with no ties to dragons usually make up the working class and populate the geographically lower areas, including the island's cavernous, interconnected tunnels that accommodate smugglers, thieves, and other sorts of illicit activity.

This adventure begins in Vedrgard, where the characters first learn of these disappearances and must navigate this city to hunt down any information that might be relevant to solving the problem. The characters, as level 15 adventurers, have already earned the attention of Queen Sigrunn, who personally requests an audience with them.

entries.name: Meeting Sigrunn
entries: The most royal chamber of the most royal palace is a square room made of ancient stone, carved with runes that glow with ancient draconian magic. Long black banners coat the walls, each carrying the heraldry of the Vedrgard royal family: a golden dragon breathing a mote of hot-red fire. A plain stone throne that seats a human comfortably sits alone on a gargantuan raised dais. Sitting on this throne is an elderly human woman, her back hunched and her hair in two white braids.

This woman is Sigrunn, who is using her Change Shape ability to communicate in a form more palatable to the characters. While she is technically an {@creature ancient copper dragon}, Sigrunn is much too old and frail to maintain her dragon form for long—she can hold it for five minutes maximum, and even then she hasn't been able to produce her breath weapon in centuries.

Sigrunn explains that her adolescent granddaughter, the royal princess Astrid, disappeared five days ago. She offers the characters 5,000 gold up front and an additional 10,000 gp on the princess's return. She allows the characters to search Astrid's room to look for clues and implores them to not hesitate if there is anything that a queen can provide to aid in their task.

entries.name: Astrid's Room
entries: Characters can search Astrid's room and the surrounding areas for clues as to where Astrid may have gone. Depending on their methods, characters may get different information:

items: A character who searches Astrid's room finds multiple posters and flyers advertising the cage fighting matches of a pirate named "Vicious Viggo," which take place at a place called The Crater.

A character who succeeds on a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation} or {@skill Persuasion}) check while speaking with Astrid's attendants may learn that there's been a human girl around Astrid's age spotted in the princess's quarters. No one knows who she is. They're remiss to admit this indiscretion as they may be blamed for Astrid's disappearance.

entries: A character who succeeds on a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check finds Astrid's journal written in scratchy {@language Draconic}. The last entry is dated six days ago (just before she disappeared) and reads:

Can't believe it worked! They won't let Princess Astrid outside without a guard, but no one bats an eye when it's a little human servant girl. Saw the most amazing show last night. The tunnels are the REAL part of the city. Vicious Viggo. He's so cool. He told me to come back to the Crater tomorrow! We'll see if I can get away with it two nights in a row.

{@b Putting it Together.} How exactly did Astrid get kidnapped? Astrid has been practicing how to shapeshift into her human form, though her family and ladies-in-waiting do not yet know she can do this. Using this to her advantage, Astrid's been sneaking out of the palace and heading to the Crater, an underground fighting ring. She became taken with a strapping, invincible fighter named Vicious Viggo, who is in fact our pirate Admiral Viggo. After earning her admiration and trust he kidnapped her and brought her to Dragonsbane Fortress.

entries.name: Clash at the Crater
entries: {@adventure Map 1|PiratesOnTheAzureSkies|1|Adventure Map 1}

While no one at the palace is base enough to know the location of a hellhole like the Crater, most people on the streets of Vedrgard do know. A character can easily find someone to give them directions with a successful {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check.

The Crater is an underground fighting ring that sits in the deepest pit of the tunnels at the base of Vedrgard, so-named because at the first match there a {@creature stone giant} punched their opponent so hard it formed a crater. The man who runs the Crater is a powerful devil by the name of Denbaxyl who knows Viggo's trade and often aids in it for a cut of the profits. Denbaxyl isn't loyal to Viggo, though. When the characters come sniffing around, he smells an opportunity to make a lot of money by putting them in the ring.
Denbaxyl asks one of the characters to step in the ring against {@creature Little Danny|DMSecretWeapon}, a massive, muscular human known for taking a beating.
If a single character can bring Little Danny to 0 hit points in 2 rounds, Denbaxyl promises to tell them what they want to know about Vicious Viggo.

{@b Breaking the Rules is a Team Activity.} If the players don't catch on, remind them that they can get creative about this! How much damage can they do in one turn while also not getting caught? Encourage them to get creative about hiding how they assist their chosen champion, but remind them that a devil of Denbaxyl's rank is rather perceptive (passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) 14). If Denbaxyl catches them cheating, he ends the match and attacks the characters.

{@b What Denbaxyl Knows.} Denbaxyl says that Viggo's career as a crater clasher is only a side gig. He's truly Admiral Viggo, a dread pirate who has slain multiple dragons with his crew. He's considered somewhat of a hero by the downtrodden in Vedrgard's tunnels, and so most tend to look the other way when he's committing crimes. Denbaxyl points the characters to a specific section of the air docks that Viggo's men own and suggests they investigate there.

{@b Resorting to Violence.} If this encounter comes to blows, {@creature Denbaxyl|DMSecretWeapon} fights until he is down to 10 hit points or fewer. No one comes to his aid—no one at the Crater has love for its selfish bookie. Once Denbaxyl is defeated, he gives up what he knows. But once the characters leave, he calls up the docks via a {@item sending stone} and warns Viggo's crew in advance that the characters are coming.

entries.name: To Catch an Airship
entries: ({@adventure Map 2|PiratesOnTheAzureSkies|1|Adventure Map 2})

Moonlight filters in through the shabby rafters. Lit lanterns line the walls of this massive wooden dock. The place is disheveled from the day's worth of pulling in and shoving off—broken and discarded crates littering the floors, garbage everywhere but in the garbage barrels. The gentle creaking of the airship and the odd seagull's cry both echo through the hall. Wind whips past you, reminding you that beyond and below lies the wide-open air.

If the characters fought Denbaxyl in the previous section, the pirates here are already aware that the heroes are coming and are lying in wait to intercept them. One {@creature djinni}, two {@creature assassin||assassins}, and two {@creature Swashbuckling Bandit|DMSecretWeapon|swashbuckling bandits} hide amongst the refuse in this room and attack immediately when the characters arrive. Any character with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) lower than 15 begins the encounter {@condition surprised}.

If the heroes did not fight Denbaxyl in the previous section, the pirates are busy attempting to cram their unwilling passengers—three dragonborn {@creature commoner||commoners} who are bound and gagged—onto the ship so they can shove off and make for Dragonsbane Fortress. Add the following to the read-aloud text:
There's grunting and muffled yelling coming from near the ship, as well as scuffling and moving shadows. Someone else is here.

The heroes can get the drop on the pirates with a successful {@dc 18} group Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, meaning each pirate starts the combat {@condition surprised}. When combat begins, the djinni and assassins attempt to keep the characters away from the ship while the bandits flee to the ship and attempt to disembark. On the swashbuckling bandits' turn, they each roll a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. When the pair gets four successes, the airship disembarks.

{@b What the Pirates Know.} The pirates work for a man named Admiral Viggo, a demon pirate who captains a ship known as The Flametongue and leads operations at Dragonsbane Fortress. They were told the admiral placed a heavy bounty on "folk who breathe the elements," though they aren't sure why. The pirates willingly give this information, including directions to Dragonsbane Fortress.

{@b Stopping the Ship.} If the heroes stop the ship, they can save the three dragonborn on it and question the pirates to find the location of Dragonsbane Fortress. If they killed all the pirates, they can find all the information the pirates know written in the djinni captain's log in his quarters.

{@b Break In Case of Total Failure.} If the heroes fail to stop the ship and they kill off all the pirates who remained on the docks, they can't very well question the pirates! Or can they? Any of the pirates willingly answers questions under the power of a {@spell speak with dead} spell. If the heroes can't cast that one, they can ask Queen Sigrunn for a priestess who can.

{@b Development.} Once the heroes learn the location of Dragonsbane Fortress, they can charter a ship and hightail it there. Queen Sigrunn is more than happy to foot the bill for such an endeavour, or the characters can use the ship they captured in this section.

entries.name: Dragonsbane Fortress
entries: {@adventure Map 3|PiratesOnTheAzureSkies|1|Adventure Map 3}
Before this section begins, allow the characters to take a short rest. Once they get to the fortress, there will be little opportunity to catch their breath.

After a half-day of travel, the clouds part, and Dragonsbane Fortress comes into view. The skulls of twelve dragons are arranged in a twelve-pointed star, wooden docking points extending from each of their mouths. Atop it, the hulls of seven pirate ships are attached to each other through careful carpentry. Broken masts hold black sails and the blood red flags of Admiral Viggo's dread crew. As the island comes closer and closer into view, you can also make out black cylindrical figures, and they're pointed straight for your ship. One of them fires, and in seconds a cannonball whizzes past your starboard side.

entries.name: Landing the Ship
entries: The characters must land the ship (or at the very least get off of it) while the crew manning Dragonsbane Fortress attempts to blast it out of the sky. Run this encounter as a skill challenge, where the characters must succeed on 6 {@dc 18} ability checks before they fail 3 times.

During the skill challenge, the characters take turns making ability checks to attempt to solve this situation. A player determines which action they would like to take, and the GM determines which ability score and skill is most relevant. No character can act twice in a row, and once a skill is used, it can't be used again. At the GM's discretion, characters expending spell slots can lower the DC of a skill test or even cause an automatic success.
Examples of actions the characters can take include:

items: Grabbing the wheel and attempting to land the ship ({@skill Sleight of Hand})
Rallying any remaining crew to defend the ship ({@skill Performance}, {@skill Persuasion})
Lobbing the cannons back at Dragonsbane Fortress ({@skill Athletics})
Patching up the ship in real-time to keep it from falling out of the sky (Dexterity with {@item Tinker's Tools})
Using {@spell control weather} to disrupt the cannonballs' trajectory

entries: If the characters succeed, let them choose where on the island to land.
{@b Failures.} When the characters reach each of the three failures, they take a penalty:

items: On the first failure, each character takes 10 Force damage from the impact of the cannon.
On the second failure, the characters lose partial control over the ship—they'll need to land on the deck of the ship, not on one of the dragon skull docks.
On the third failure, the characters instantly crash onto the deck of the ship. Each character takes 20 Fire damage and starts the next combat encounter {@condition prone}.

entries: If the characters landed on the deck, proceed to "{@adventure Pirates On Deck|PiratesOnTheAzureSkies|0|Pirates On Deck}." Otherwise, proceed to "{@adventure Belly of the Dragonsbane|PiratesOnTheAzureSkies|0|Belly of the Dragonsbane}."

entries.name: Pirates On Deck
entries: There are two {@creature Swashbuckling Bandit|DMSecretWeapon|swashbuckling bandits} and one {@creature ice devil} on deck. They engage as soon as they see characters on the deck. The ice devil attempts to isolate the characters from each other with its Wall of Ice ability, and the swashbuckling bandits try to gang up and pick off characters one-by-one.
Once these pirates are dealt with, the characters can freely descend into the Belly of the Dragonsbane and search for the abductees.

entries.name: Belly of the Dragonsbane
entries: ({@adventure Map 4|PiratesOnTheAzureSkies|1|Adventure Map 4})

Each skeletal dragon maw and ladder from the decks leads into this circular chamber. In the center sits a gigantic mechanical apparatus made of glowing blue mithril that creaks and chugs and expels steam. In cages all lined up around the machine are dragons and dragonfolk of all ages and sizes—including a young copper dragon. As pirates crack whips through the bars, the captives cry out in pain, releasing their breath weapons towards the machine.

In this room there are ten captives, all young, emaciated, and incapable of defending themselves: dragonborn, young hatchling dragons, even the odd {@creature kobold} or two. They are imprisoned here, used for their breath weapons whose magic powers the mithril engine. There are three {@creature Swashbuckling Bandit|DMSecretWeapon|swashbuckling bandits} cracking the whip. These pirates are a trivial matter for the characters, and they know it. Any show of force from the heroes is sufficient to cause the three to beg for their lives.

If the characters aggress, the pirates urge them to think things through. They explain that when the mithril engine runs out of power, this entire island will cease to float and will drop down from the sky into the sea below. They also know that Viggo's men haven't been bringing in enough captives. The ones they have are running out of energy. It's only a matter of time before the fortress crashes anyway.

entries.name: Stopping the Mithril Engine
entries: The mithril engine requires a combination of 30 points of magical Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage every 6 seconds, or a single round of combat, to power Dragonsbane Fortress. The island falls for six rounds before crashing into the earth (and devastating whatever settlement lies below). The characters can power the engine with their own spells and abilities, and the engine takes damage as though it were a creature (meaning spells like {@spell fire storm} and {@spell wall of fire} work on it).

entries.name: Escaping the Fortress
entries: To run this encounter, decide which dock on the map leads out to the ship the characters are using to escape. (If the characters crashed their ship in the previous section, there are several ships docked on the island that they can hijack). Mark the dock on the opposite side of the map; this is where Viggo and his men will emerge.
When the characters begin to liberate the captives, read the following:

A dark shadow covers the island from above. The fortress shudders and groans under the new weight. Someone is docking their ship to the island. There's frantic shouting from above. The {@creature young copper dragon} who can only be Astrid scowls grimly and says, "Viggo's home."

Have the characters roll initiative. There are 10 noncombatant captives in all. At the beginning of the second round, {@creature Viggo, Demon Pirate Admiral|DMSecretWeapon|Viggo the demon pirate admiral} and two {@creature berserker||berserkers} arrive in the space determined above, and two more {@creature berserker||berserkers} arrive from a random dock on the map. The encounter ends when the characters have successfully transported all captives to the edge of their dock, where the ship is.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: {@b Crashing Fortress.} If the fortress crashes into the sea below before the party escape, the effects are devastating. The wreck kills all NPCs onboard but Viggo. All characters who suffer the crash must make a {@dc 20} Strength saving throw, taking 80 Bludgeoning damage on a failure or half as much on a success. Viggo spits at whomever manages to climb out of the rubble and float to the top of the sea; at least he'd never killed anybody he kidnapped.

{@b Escape.} If the characters manage to escape, they can safely navigate their airship back to Vedrgard as the fortress crashes into the sea below them. If they saved Astrid and the others, Queen Sigrunn rewards them handsomely, exactly as promised. Unbeknownst to the characters, Viggo survives the crash (assuming the party didn't kill him in combat), and makes it his mission to see to the characters' demise personally.
